docs/phase-0-prereg.md:1| # Tessera — Phase 0 Pre-Registration
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:2| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:3| > **What this document is.** A dated, GPG-signed, OpenTimestamps-anchored
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:4| > declaration of intent, made *before* the system it describes is built. Its
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:5| > credibility comes from the fact that it cannot be backdated: the Bitcoin
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:6| > anchor on the commit that introduces it fixes its existence in time. The
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:7| > build journal that follows will be measured *against* this document —
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:8| > including, honestly, where reality diverged from it.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:9| >
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:10| > **Why pre-register at all.** Anyone can write a flattering after-the-fact
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:11| > story. Pre-registration converts the build log from a highlight reel into
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:12| > evidence: the hypotheses, success criteria, and design commitments are on
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:13| > record before the outcomes are known, so the reader can check the work
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:14| > instead of trusting the narrator.

docs/phase-0-prereg.md:21| - **AI collaborator:** Tyst (`tessera@wamason.com`) — mechanics, drafting,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:22|   pushback. Division of labor is explicit and recorded; see §6.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:23| - **Integrity:** this commit is signed by the Tyst key (ed25519,

docs/phase-0-prereg.md:25|   is the WHO layer; the OTS anchor is the WHEN layer.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:26| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:27| An AWS native attestation service modeled on our work in Willay: a robust
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:28| demonstration of building, validating, observing, and deploying a

docs/phase-0-prereg.md:33| ## 1. Objective and the honest ranking
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:34| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:35| The function of an attestation service is to provide a neutral, third
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:36| party's cryptographic binding to a package of information delivered to
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:37| it.  Attestation in this usage is similar to SSL certificates that say
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:38| "this attestation says that the party in control of a website has
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:39| demonstrated this control and the following certificate validates it."
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:40| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:41| The distinction here is that a Tessera attestation is an attestation of
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:42| information at a fixed point in time, while an SSL certificate is an
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:43| attestation of website ownership with a fixed expiration.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:44| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:45| Why would you use an attestation:
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:46| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:47| 1. to demonstrate a tamper-resistant pre-registration, such as a hypothesis,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:48|    an experimental design, and a predicted outcome.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:49| 2. to record the findings of one or more third parties, such as an
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:50|    audit, regulatory policy, ontology, or citation.  Note: this is a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:51|    suggested but not exhaustive list.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:52| 3. to record agreements between parties, such as a contract, and
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:53|    signatures of parties to that contract, similar to the way a notary validates
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:54|    documents.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:55| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:56| The distinction here is that this attestation is over a _digital artifact_.  Thus,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:57| for example, the SHA256 hash value of a document, or a blockchain address, or
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:58| some other unique identifier, might be part of the digital artifact.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:59| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:60| This service provides a cryptographic signature and timestamp over the digital artifact
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:61| and that attestation receipt permits future parties to verify the attestation.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:62| The design is done in such a way that the receipt is verifiable independent
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:63| of the attestor, which ensures the ability of parties in the future to validate
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:64| the signed artifact.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:65| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:66| **The honest ranking.** Two objectives, strictly ranked, and the ranking is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:67| the discipline:
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:68| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:69| 1. **Primary — the demonstration.** Close the operational-envelope gap (§7):
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:70|    show that I can build, validate, observe, secure, and deploy an attestation
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:71|    service to a beta-quality bar, with the engineering rigor visible in the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:72|    repository itself. This is the objective. It succeeds or fails on its own,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:73|    independent of whether anyone ever pays for the service.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:74| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:75| 2. **Secondary — possible commercial service (upside, not premise).** Tessera
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:76|    may become a viable attestation-as-a-service. If it does, good — but the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:77|    revenue-bearing pieces (billing/payment integration, PCI *certification*,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:78|    customer acquisition, scaling for real traffic) are **deferred until
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:79|    validated paying demand exists**, and built no sooner. The product dream
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:80|    does not expand the demonstration's scope. Note the distinction the primary
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:81|    objective *does* honor: Tessera is architected **to the PCI standard**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:82|    (minimal cardholder-data environment, segmentation, key custody) as a matter
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:83|    of engineering discipline — designing to the bar is demonstration; obtaining
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:84|    the certificate is product, and waits.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:85| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:86| **Credibility line (non-negotiable):** every architecture decision here is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:87| the human author (Tony) in collaboration with AI agents. The purpose of
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:88| the AI agents is to accelerate the typing, push back on my decisions, clarify
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:89| them, but not to _make_ those decisions without consultation.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:90|

docs/phase-0-prereg.md:93| ## 2. Hypotheses (falsifiable, dated)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:94| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:95| A key aspect of designing this project is to identify the anticipated
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:96| criteria for evaluating the project itself.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:97| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:98| The work is decomposed into dependency-ordered bands. The bands matter because
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:99| they have different risk profiles, and the hypotheses are stated per band rather
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:100| than lumped into one figure. **Band 0 precedes all of them:**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:101| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:102| 0. **Band 0 — the formal foundation (H0).** Before any code, the central
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:103|    guarantee is established by a machine-checked formal model and proof (see
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:104|    H0). This is formal-methods work, not software engineering, and it gates
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:105|    everything: if the guarantee cannot be proven, there is nothing worth
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:106|    building. No time bound — a rushed proof is worse than none — and the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:107|    Phase 1 / H1b clock does not start until Band 0 is resolved.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:108| 1. **Band 1 — cloud-independent core.** The cryptographic guarantees, proven
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:109|    on a laptop with no AWS and no LocalStack. This is the invariant the later
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:110|    bands must not break. It has no irreducible wall-clock latency in its test
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:111|    path (OTS *confirmation* latency is deferred to band 3; band 1 tests use
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:112|    stamped-not-yet-confirmed proofs). Throughput-bound, fast.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:113| 2. **Band 2 — local vertical slice.** The same guarantees delivered through
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:114|    the LocalStack-emulated pipeline (S3/DynamoDB/SQS/Lambda/KMS), sustaining
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:115|    a steady issue rate. Cloud-*shaped* but free and local.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:116| 3. **Band 3 — real cloud.** The operated service on actual AWS: the attack
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:117|    surface, real KMS, observability, adversarial attack, cost/capacity claims.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:118|    Wall-clock-bound (terraform apply, GuardDuty population, OTS confirmation),
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:119|    slow and externally gated.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:120| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:121| - **H0 — the foundational claim (gates the entire project).** Tessera's central
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:122|   guarantee — that altering any part of a signed attestation package requires
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:123|   solving a computationally hard problem — is established by *formal proof of a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:124|   machine-checked model*, with one honestly-declared gap between model and code.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:125|   This is not software engineering; it is the precondition for Tessera being a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:126|   *commercial* offering rather than a demonstration of confidence. A party
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:127|   relying on an attestation in adjudication must be able to *depend* on the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:128|   guarantee, not trust an assertion of it.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:129| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:130|   *Two layers, kept distinct (so the claim cannot be accused of formal-methods
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:131|   theater):*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:132|   - **Layer 1 — symbolic composition invariant (what the checker proves).**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:133|     Assuming *idealized* signatures, hashes, canonicalization, and temporal
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:134|     anchors, a machine-checked model (TLA+ and/or Lean4) establishes that the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:135|     verifier accepts only packages satisfying the intended integrity and
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:136|     ordering properties — e.g. "no transition leads to an accepted receipt over
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:137|     altered bytes," "ordering/replay conditions hold." This is exactly what
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:138|     state-machine and proof tooling is good at.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:139|   - **Layer 2 — computational assumptions (what is depended on, not proven).**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:140|     The idealized primitives are justified by *external* assumptions we cite,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:141|     not discharge: signature unforgeability, SHA-256 collision/preimage
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:142|     resistance (only as actually needed), and Bitcoin/OpenTimestamps timestamp
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:143|     assumptions. The cryptographic claim "altering any part requires solving a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:144|     computationally hard problem" holds *under these stated assumptions and an
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:145|     explicit adversary model* — it is not proven from nothing.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:146| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:147|   *The verification chain, by trust source:*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:148|   1. **A machine-checked formal model** of the construction (Layer 1 above).
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:149|      The checker establishes that *the model* has the claimed properties — but
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:150|      **not** that the model is the *right* model. Model fidelity to intent is a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:151|      human judgment, not a checkable one. What is proven is **our own
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:152|      composition** (Layer 1) under the cited primitive assumptions (Layer 2);
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:153|      the document states crisply which is which.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:154|   2. **An agreement gate:** author and AI must each independently agree the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:155|      model faithfully captures the claim before it is handed onward — a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:156|      cross-model convergence, not a single nod, to catch "the checker proved the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:157|      wrong model."
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:158|   3. **An informal written proof** (not required for the proof obligation —
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:159|      the checked model carries that — but required as the H2 evidence for the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:160|      formal core). A passing checker is identical whether the human owns the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:161|      formalism or prompted an AI into it; the written, defend-it-cold prose is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:162|      the artifact that demonstrates the *author's understanding* of the core,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:163|      which is the primary objective (§1) and the deskilling defense (§6) at the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:164|      spot it is hardest and most tempting to skip.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:165| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:166|   *Human external review is NOT a resolution requirement — deliberately.* The
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:167|   gate is **machine-checked** (free, deterministic, repeatable, in CI, in our
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:168|   control). Requiring an *independent human* formal-methods reviewer would set
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:169|   the bar where it cannot be met under the pre-registered no-spend constraint
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:170|   (H3): a competent reviewer costs money, so a human-review gate would either
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:171|   stall the project indefinitely in Band 0 or force spend we committed against.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:172|   Therefore human external review is an **optional enhancement, gated on a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:173|   revenue stream (the secondary objective, §1)**. Its *absence is a declared
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:174|   residual risk:* a machine-checked proof and multi-model agreement reduce the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:175|   probability of an undetected flaw but do not eliminate it — no review,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:176|   machine or human, guarantees a future party will not find a hole. That
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:177|   residual risk is accepted and disclosed, not concealed. (Earlier drafts made
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:178|   human external review a hard gate; that was an over-tightening, removed.)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:179| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:180|   *The declared gap (what is attested, not proven):* the chain proves *the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:181|   model* sound. It does **not** prove that *the code implements the model* —
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:182|   that link is *attested, not proven*. When the code deviates from the model,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:183|   that is a *bug*, hunted by the H1a adversarial suite — the ordinary
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:184|   spec-to-implementation relationship, stated plainly rather than concealed.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:185|   Declaring this gap is the Tessera ethos applied to Tessera: declare what you
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:186|   cannot see.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:187| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:188|   *Resolved when:* the machine-checked model (1) holds under its stated
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:189|   assumptions, the agreement gate (2) has passed, and the informal written
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:190|   proof (3) is in the repository, with the model-to-code gap documented. Human
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:191|   external review is not required for resolution (see above); if later obtained
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:192|   under a revenue stream, its outcome is recorded. *Falsified if:* no such proof
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:193|   can be produced, or
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:194|   it shows the guarantee fails under realistic assumptions — **the project does
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:195|   not proceed to Phase 1 as designed.** The H1b clock does not start until H0
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:196|   is resolved.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:197| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:198| - **H1a (band 1 — crypto core):** The cloud-independent cryptographic core is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:199|   frozen *before* any LocalStack work begins, with adversarial evidence that
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:200|   the implementation conforms to the H0 model. (Tests do not *prove*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:201|   correctness — H0 is the proof gate; H1a is *implementation evidence* that the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:202|   code rejects the enumerated attacks and conforms to the model's expected
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:203|   verifier behavior.) *Falsified if:* there is not a public, adversarially-
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:204|   authored red-bar suite that, for each attack family — forge, tamper,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:205|   backdate, break-chain, strip-one-signature — and each degradation scenario,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:206|   shows the verifier emits the **correct explicit verification state** (see
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:207|   §4.6): `VALID_STRICT`, `VALID_DEGRADED(policy)`, `INVALID`, or `UNVERIFIABLE`.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:208|   Emitting the *right* state for every case is the criterion — including the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:209|   fail-open trap of returning `VALID` where the honest answer is `UNVERIFIABLE`.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:210| - **H1b (band 2 — vertical slice speed):** A local vertical slice (issue →
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:211|   verify → chain a receipt, all on LocalStack) sustaining **1 attestation/second**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:212|   lands within **7 calendar days** of the Band 1 freeze. The 1/sec figure is a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:213|   *functional throughput* check (the pipeline sustains a steady rate without
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:214|   deadlock or chain corruption), explicitly **not** a real-infrastructure
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:215|   performance claim — LocalStack's performance characteristics are not AWS's.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:216|   *Clock (as a state machine, no ambiguity):*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:217|   H0 resolved → Phase 1a implements the cloud-independent crypto core →
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:218|   **H1a freeze commit** (dated, signed; this both closes H1a and opens the H1b
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:219|   window) → Phase 1b builds the LocalStack slice → **H1b evidence commit** must
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:220|   land within 7 calendar days of the H1a freeze commit. Both endpoints live in
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:221|   the anchored git history; elapsed time is auditable from the timestamps, not
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:222|   asserted from memory.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:223|   *Falsified if:* no H1b evidence commit demonstrating 1/sec sustained on
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:224|   LocalStack lands within 7 calendar days of the H1a freeze commit.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:225| - **H2 (division of labor):** The architecture decisions are demonstrably
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:226|   mine; AI handled mechanics. *Falsified if:* the multi-model review panel (the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:227|   same ≥3 unrelated LLM models that adversarially review security in §5, here
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:228|   tasked to interrogate architecture ownership) finds a load-bearing decision I
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:229|   cannot justify without reconstructing it from the AI's reasoning. The panel is a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:230|   proxy for the only reviewer who matters: someone reading the repository to
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:231|   see what was actually done.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:232| - **H3 (cost discipline):** Three separate numbers, so none can be trivially
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:233|   contradicted by the pricing page:
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:234|   - **demo-cycle variable cost under $25** — a complete cycle (`terraform apply`
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:235|     → run the full red-bar + load suite → `terraform destroy`) at standard
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:236|     on-demand pricing;
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:237|   - **persistent monthly footprint under $5/month** — the intentional always-on
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:238|     pieces (each customer-managed KMS key ~$1/mo, a Route 53 hosted zone
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:239|     ~$0.50/mo, the ledger's S3 bucket) are low single-digit dollars, *not*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:240|     "cents";
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:241|   - **idle compute exactly $0** — nothing *runs* between demonstrations (no
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:242|     Fargate task, idle EC2, or provisioned capacity).
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:243| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:244|   Cost is measured against *standard* pricing, not free-tier: free-tier credits
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:245|   may cover actual spend, but H3 evidences cost *governance*, not subsidy.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:246|   *Falsified if:* a measured demo cycle exceeds $25 at standard rates, the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:247|   persistent footprint exceeds $5/month, or any idle compute persists between
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:248|   demonstrations.

docs/phase-0-prereg.md:251| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:252| ## 3. Architecture decisions (the part that is genuinely yours)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:253| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:254| ### 3.1 The signing-architecture decision — KMS vs. GPG vs. dual
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:255| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:256| The decision space, stated neutrally before the decision and its reasoning:
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:257| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:258| - **Willay's model (A):** local GPG signs; verification needs only the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:259|   pinned fingerprint and the bundle. Maximally portable, zero infrastructure.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:260|   Rejected for Tessera because it exercises no cloud-native services — it's
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:261|   "Willay with extra overhead."
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:262| - **KMS-native (B):** KMS signs the cloud receipt. This exercises real
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:263|   cloud-native key custody, and current KMS supports offline-verifiable
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:264|   asymmetric signatures — including `ECC_NIST_EDWARDS25519` (Ed25519) and
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:265|   post-quantum `ML-DSA` (FIPS 204) key specs; the private key remains in KMS
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:266|   while the public key downloads via `GetPublicKey` for verification outside
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:267|   AWS. B is therefore **technically viable** — the earlier belief that KMS
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:268|   could not sign Ed25519 was wrong (corrected against current AWS docs). It is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:269|   rejected as the *sole* trust mechanism not because KMS is incapable, but
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:270|   because it concentrates issuer custody, AWS account lifecycle, key-deletion
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:271|   risk, IAM/policy risk, and public-key-provenance risk in **one operational
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:272|   domain**.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:273| - **Dual-attestation (C), the chosen path:** KMS signs the cloud receipt to
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:274|   demonstrate cloud-native custody, **and** local GPG counter-signs to preserve
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:275|   a portable, independent WHO layer (Willay's). Public keys are published via
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:276|   DNS (`wamason.com`, DNSSEC), repositories, and the bundle. The justification
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:277|   is **not** that KMS is incapable; it is that a long-lived attestation should
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:278|   not rest on a single operational trust domain.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:279| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:280| **Decision: C.**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:281| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:282| **Why C, defended cold.** The threat model for an attestation is not "is this
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:283| signature valid today" — it is "will this signature adjudicate in fifty years,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:284| when the issuer may be gone." B is technically capable (it can even produce
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:285| offline-verifiable Ed25519 or post-quantum signatures), but it places the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:286| entire trust story in **one operational domain**: AWS account lifecycle, KMS
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:287| key-deletion policy, IAM, and the provenance of the published public key all
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:288| sit together. If that domain lapses — the account closes, the key is deleted,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:289| the policy changes, the published key's provenance becomes unclear — the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:290| attestation's verifiability is at risk, all at once, for correlated reasons.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:291| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:292| C signs the same canonical bytes with two keys from *independent failure
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:293| domains* — KMS (cloud-native custody) and local GPG (Willay's portable WHO
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:294| layer). They fail for *uncorrelated* reasons (AWS account/policy lapse vs. local
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:295| key disclosure), so the attestation's durability does not rest on any single
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:296| domain surviving. **Not replicating is what concentrates the risk**; the cost of
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:297| C over B is essentially nil, and the benefit is that attestations stand up to
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:298| adjudication even if one trust domain disappears entirely.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:299| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:300| **Key distribution is a separate axis from dual-signing.** Public keys are not
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:301| secret; they are published redundantly — via DNS (`wamason.com`, DNSSEC), in
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:302| public repositories, and in the attestation bundle itself. This defends against
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:303| any single distribution channel expiring. Note this redundancy could be applied
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:304| to B as well; it is *not* what justifies C. What only C provides is two
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:305| independent signatures whose validity does not share a failure domain.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:306| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:307| **Verification policy lives with the verifier, not frozen into the receipt.**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:308| The attestation carries a *set* of signatures (a JSON map of key-type →
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:309| signature), not an AND/OR rule. The default reference verifier requires **all
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:310| issue-time signatures to verify** — the strong guarantee a naive holder gets
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:311| without having to understand the policy.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:312| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:313| This fail-closed default is not a fragility to apologize for; it is the system
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:314| refusing to lie. If one signature can no longer be verified, we will **not**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:315| let a naive holder assume the attestation is still fully valid. A verifier
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:316| *may* override and accept a lower bar — but the act of overriding is itself an
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:317| informed-consent step: by relaxing the requirement, the verifier has
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:318| demonstrated they understand the tradeoff and have knowingly accepted a weaker
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:319| guarantee, thereby changing their own self-label from "naive" to "not naive."
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:320| The objection "but naive users will be misled by a relaxed check" therefore
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:321| cannot land: the category it worries about cannot exist, because relaxing the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:322| check is precisely the act that exits naivety. (Long-term, the wrapping model
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:323| below lets fresh assurance be re-anchored *before* old algorithms fail, so a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:324| fully-strict verification can remain available across decades — but that is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:325| additional assurance, not a rescue this default requires.)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:326| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:327| That argument is the *justification*; the *mechanism* that implements and tests
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:328| it is an explicit set of verifier states (this is what makes the policy
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:329| auditable rather than rhetorical, and it is the H1a acceptance criterion —
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:330| §4.6):
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:331| - `VALID_STRICT` — all issue-time signatures verify (the fail-closed default);
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:332| - `VALID_DEGRADED(policy=...)` — accepted under an explicit, recorded weaker
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:333|   policy the verifier chose (the informed-consent override);
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:334| - `INVALID` — a required check failed;
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:335| - `UNVERIFIABLE` — a check could not be performed (missing key, unsupported
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:336|   algorithm, expired trust root). Critically, this is **never** silently
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:337|   promoted to `VALID`.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:338| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:339| **Temporal upgrade by wrapping, not replacement.** Cryptographic strength
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:340| decays; post-quantum standards are still in flux, and the right time to choose
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:341| a PQ algorithm is when a customer needs that guarantee — it will be a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:342| *different* key algorithm, a real architectural choice encoded per-receipt.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:343| Rather than re-sign old payloads (which would require the original
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:344| canonicalization to remain byte-identical forever), a **superseding
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:345| attestation wraps the original package** and signs *that* with the new-algorithm
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:346| key. The inner attestation's bytes, signatures, and OTS proof are immutable;
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:347| the wrapper is a new layer with its own time-anchor. This (a) makes the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:348| upsigning *visible and ordered* rather than a silent mutation, (b) lets a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:349| customer add PQ assurance *while the original keys are still trusted* — the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:350| window in which bootstrapping new trust is actually sound — and (c) dissolves
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:351| the canonicalization-freeze problem into per-layer versioning: each layer
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:352| records which canonical form it used. Wrapping is a *paid* operation; nesting
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:353| depth is therefore bounded by willingness to pay (as PKI key sprawl is bounded
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:354| by storage budget), not by a protocol cap. It is for rare, high-value
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:355| supersession, not routine.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:356| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:357| **What the wrapper attests.** The base service wrapper attests *integrity of
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:358| the inner object* — "this 2026 package existed and is bit-for-bit unaltered,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:359| re-anchored under a 2030 algorithm." It commits to the inner package's **bytes**,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:360| **not** to the inner receipt's *verification result* at wrap time: the wrapper
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:361| does not assert "the inner receipt was VALID_STRICT when wrapped," because that
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:362| would be a form of re-evaluation. The inner receipt's validity stands on its own
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:363| signatures, verified independently whenever a relying party checks it. It does
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:364| **not** re-evaluate the original claim. Semantic re-attestation (a genuinely new inspection over the old
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:365| package, with its own losses and open questions) is a separate, priced business
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:366| offering, and — honestly declared — *may not be available years later*, because
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:367| the evaluator, context, and resolvable evidence degrade over time. (An expert
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:368| report written in 2021 can be updated in 2031, but not for free, and perhaps
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:369| not at all.)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:370| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:371| **The temporal anchor is an independent trust dimension that crypto advances
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:372| do not touch.** The *intended* argument: even total signature compromise should
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:373| not let a forger rewrite the *past*, because forging a Tessera attestation would
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:374| require breaking the signature algorithm(s) **and** producing a valid
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:375| OTS/Bitcoin anchor at the original time — i.e., forging Bitcoin's proof-of-work
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:376| history. Length is bound into the canonical bytes every signature commits to, so
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:377| length-extension / boundary-ambiguity attacks must also defeat both keys *and*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:378| the anchor.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:379| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:380| **This argument is not yet proven, and that gap gates the project (H0).** The
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:381| paragraph above states the guarantee we *believe* holds; it is an assertion, not
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:382| a formal result. Establishing it — a threat model, a machine-checked formal
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:383| model of the composition, and a proof that the model has the claimed invariants
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:384| — is **Band 0**, the precondition for building anything. Asserting it here
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:385| without proof would be exactly the theater this project exists to refute. See
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:386| H0.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:387| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:388| **Four distinct threat classes (do not conflate them).** The cryptographic
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:389| story above defends two of these; the other two need *operational* controls,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:390| and saying so plainly is part of declaring what we cannot see:
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:391| - **Cryptographic forgery** — an attacker produces an accepted receipt without
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:392|   authorized signing authority. *Mitigation:* the dual-signature + anchor
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:393|   construction (H0).
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:394| - **Tampering** — an attacker alters an issued package after the fact.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:395|   *Mitigation:* same construction; the signatures and anchor break.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:396| - **Misissuance** — an *authorized or compromised issuer path* signs content it
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:397|   should not. Dual signatures do **not** prevent this if the attacker can drive
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:398|   both signers through the legitimate issuance path. *Mitigation:* authorization
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:399|   controls and audit logs, **not** cryptography. Named here so it is not
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:400|   mistaken for something the signing construction solves.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:401| - **Key compromise** — an attacker obtains signing capability outside normal
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:402|   policy. *Mitigation:* KMS/GPG domain separation (§3.1) reduces correlated
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:403|   compromise; OpenTimestamps constrains backdating; the §4.2 threat model and
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:404|   TTL bound the local-key blast radius.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:405| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:406| **Open question (declared, deferred):** a *quantitative* forgery-cost analysis
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:407| of the combined construction (signature-set + length-bound canonicalization +
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:408| OTS anchor) is not yet done. The argument above is qualitative
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:409| (independent-failure-domains); the quantitative bound is unproven. Deferring it
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:410| is honest — and the scenario that would make it worth doing (a customer with
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:411| many supersessions) is itself the revenue signal that funds the analysis.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:412| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:413| **Hard invariants this decision incurs (see §4):** the `canonical(payload) →
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:414| bytes` function is the true root of trust and must be frozen and explicitly
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:415| versioned; the verification path must depend on *zero* service-side state.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:416| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:417| ### 3.2 The shared-core / forked-edge boundary
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:418| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:419| The prior spec proposed reusing Willay's `canonical.py`, signing, models,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:420| evaluators, and ledger logic unchanged, forking only the cloud edges (compute,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:421| key custody, storage, queue), with clean extractability as a goal.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:422| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:423| **Decision: the shared-core / forked-edge boundary is not a design priority
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:424| for Tessera.** Tessera is a demonstration of *building and operating the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:425| service*, not a reusable, detachable, re-deployable library — that
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:426| extractability goal belongs to Willay, not here. Code is reused from Willay
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:427| where convenient, but clean separation is not an architectural commitment, and
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:428| no effort is spent making the core independently redeployable. This is a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:429| deliberate *narrowing* of scope: optimizing for extractability we do not need
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:430| would be wasted work.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:431| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:432| (The one piece of Willay's core that *is* load-bearing — and therefore is a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:433| hard invariant, see §4 — is the canonicalization function, because the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:434| wrap/upgrade model in §3.1 depends on it being frozen and versioned. That is a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:435| property of the bytes, not of code extractability.)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:436| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:437| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:438| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:439| ## 4. Hard invariants
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:440| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:441| The five standard NFRs (security, reliability, observability, scalability,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:442| usability) are addressed operationally in §5 and the design spec. The items
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:443| below are *hard invariants* — not aspirations but rules with mechanical
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:444| enforcement, committed to before any implementation. They are the lines that,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:445| if crossed, mean the system has failed regardless of what else works.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:446| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:447| ### 4.1 Secure observability (hard rule)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:448| Key material is **unloggable by construction** — never logged, not private
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:449| keys, not passphrases, not "redacted-but-present," not in a debug branch, not
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:450| as a joke. Enforced *mechanically*: structured logging that cannot serialize
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:451| key types, plus a CI secret-scan gate that fails the build if signing material
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:452| reaches a log sink. Discipline is not the control; the type system and CI are.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:453| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:454| ### 4.2 Signing-key threat model (explicit, accepted)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:455| The commit-signing key (Tyst, ed25519, `...42C73835`) is **passphraseless**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:456| with a **6-month TTL** (expires 2026-12-07), residing on a firewalled
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:457| workstation. **Threat accepted:** host compromise lets an attacker sign as
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:458| the tessera committer. **Mitigation:** short TTL + revocation certificate
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:459| (already generated). **Deferred (deliberately, not by oversight):**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:460| higher-assurance signing (enclave/secure sandbox so the key never touches an
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:461| internet-facing system) until there is real demand for it. This is a defensible
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:462| demonstration-project tradeoff; it would NOT be acceptable for a production
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:463| root-of-trust, and the journal should say so.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:464| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:465| **TTL note.** 6 months is acceptable *for the demonstration* — a passphraseless
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:466| key on a firewalled box facing a low-probability, bounded-blast-radius threat.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:467| **Trigger to revisit:** if anyone relies on issued attestations, shorten the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:468| TTL toward monthly *and* move to the deferred enclave/HSM model so
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:469| passphraseless-ness stops being acceptable at all.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:470| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:471| **Hardware token (e.g. YubiKey) — considered, deferred.** A hardware token for
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:472| the local GPG layer would close the passphraseless vulnerability and read well
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:473| on a CV. It is declined *for now*, for two reasons that are on-thesis rather
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:474| than convenience: (1) it reintroduces interactive touch-to-sign, defeating the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:475| headless, non-interactive signing the project deliberately chose; (2) it
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:476| concentrates local-layer custody in a single hardware token — a step *toward*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:477| the single-domain concentration §3.1 rejects, not away from it. It sits in the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:478| same deferred enclave/HSM tier, gated on real reliance, not adopted as security
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:479| theater.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:480| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:481| **Security review (flagged).** This section is the one most worth an
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:482| independent adversarial pass. Per the project's method (§6), that review is a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:483| *different model's* job, not the model that authored this — it is a tracked
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:484| item, not a claim of completeness here.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:485| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:486| ### 4.3 Canonicalization is frozen and versioned (hard rule)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:487| `canonical(payload) → bytes` is the true root of trust — more than any key.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:488| The wrap/upgrade model (§3.1) requires that a signature added years later
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:489| commit to bytes reconstructible exactly as they were at issue time. Therefore
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:490| the canonical form is **frozen and explicitly versioned**: it never changes
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:491| silently; any change is a *new, versioned* canonical form, and every receipt
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:492| records which version it used. Length is bound into the canonical bytes (not a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:493| side field), so the encoding is **boundary-unambiguous** by construction (a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:494| parser cannot disagree about where the payload ends).
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:495| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:496| **Bind to an existing deterministic standard, not a hand-rolled function.**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:497| Canonicalization is the graveyard of cryptographic implementations: differing
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:498| language runtimes disagree on whitespace, key ordering, number precision, and
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:499| Unicode escaping, which silently breaks cross-platform verification. The
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:500| canonical form binds to **RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme, JCS)** rather
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:501| than a bespoke `canonical()`. JCS's one sharp edge — numbers must be exactly
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:502| representable as IEEE 754 doubles — is handled by an explicit invariant: **any
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:503| value not exactly a double (hashes, large/256-bit integers, blockchain
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:504| addresses, opaque identifiers) is string-encoded, never a JSON number.** (JCS is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:505| an Informational RFC, not IETF standards-track — cited as the deterministic
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:506| serialization we adopt, with the precision rule above closing its gap.)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:507| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:508| Operational commitments that make this checkable, not merely asserted:
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:509| 1. canonicalization **test vectors** are part of the public verifier
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:510|    conformance suite;
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:511| 2. every canonicalization **version has byte-for-byte golden examples**;
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:512| 3. **wrappers record both inner and outer** canonicalization versions.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:513| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:514| (We claim boundary-unambiguity, which is what the length-binding buys. We do
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:515| *not* make a blanket "length-extension-resistant" claim — that is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:516| construction-specific and would invite cryptographic nitpicking we have not
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:517| earned; the relevant property here is unambiguous framing, proven in Band 0.)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:518| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:519| ### 4.4 Verification path depends on zero service-side state (hard rule)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:520| An attestation must verify with the service **dead**. The verification path
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:521| touches no database, no live service, no cloud reachability. The operational
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:522| database exists to *run* the service (who may request an attestation, rate
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:523| limits, keys, later billing) and is **never** on the path that *verifies* one.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:524| If verifying ever requires service-side state, the verification-independence
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:525| guarantee is broken.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:526| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:527| **DNS and repositories are *discovery* mechanisms, not *verification*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:528| dependencies.** A public key sitting in the bundle proves little by itself — the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:529| future verifier needs to know that key was an *authorized issuer key at the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:530| relevant time*. Therefore the bundle carries an **issuer-key manifest**: the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:531| issuer public keys (or references) plus *timestamped evidence* that those keys
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:532| were authorized issuer keys at issue time, the manifest itself anchored. The
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:533| future verifier then has an archived trust path inside the bundle, rather than
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:534| needing live DNS or a reachable repository. DNS/repo remain useful for *finding*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:535| keys; they are not *required* to *verify*.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:536| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:537| **Revocation is time-relative.** A key revoked *after* issue does not retroactively
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:538| invalidate attestations made *while it was authorized* — the manifest's
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:539| timestamped authorization evidence, anchored, establishes the key was valid *at
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:540| issue time*, and an attestation signed then remains `VALID_STRICT`. The naive
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:541| reading ("the key is revoked now, therefore the receipt is invalid") is wrong and
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:542| is exactly the kind of error the verifier-state logic must get right: revocation
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:543| *after* the anchored issue time is irrelevant to that receipt; revocation
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:544| *effective before or at* issue time means the signature was never authorized
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:545| (`INVALID`). This is precisely why the temporal anchor (WHEN) is load-bearing
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:546| alongside the signature (WHO).
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:547| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:548| ### 4.5 Adversarial tests are authored by a different model (hard rule)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:549| The red-bar suite's attacks are authored by a *different* model (Codex) than
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:550| the one that wrote the implementation, so the implementer cannot unconsciously
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:551| shape attacks to what the code survives. This is not perfect (shared
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:552| training-distribution blind spots remain) but is a real, defensible separation,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:553| and stronger than self-authored tests. Test/code separation is CI-enforced.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:554| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:555| ### 4.6 The verifier returns an explicit typed state, never a bare boolean (hard rule)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:556| Verification yields one of `VALID_STRICT`, `VALID_DEGRADED(policy=...)`,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:557| `INVALID`, or `UNVERIFIABLE` (§3.1) — a typed result, never a bare `true`/`false`.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:558| A boolean collapses the load-bearing distinction between "this failed a check"
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:559| (`INVALID`) and "this check could not be performed" (`UNVERIFIABLE`), which is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:560| exactly where fail-open bugs hide. The typed state is what makes the fail-closed
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:561| policy *auditable and testable* rather than rhetorical, and it is the form H1a's
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:562| acceptance criteria assert against.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:563| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:564| ### 4.7 Review recency is itself attested (hard rule)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:565| This pre-registration's exit gate (§5) uses **multi-model adversarial review** —
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:566| not a professional human audit, and not claimed as one. A substantive human
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:567| audit requires a paid expert; anything less labelled "audit" would be theater. A
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:568| real system has a *recurring* review cycle, not a one-time blessing. So review
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:569| recency is made a verifiable property: the service attests *when it was last
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:570| adversarially reviewed* (signed, timestamped), and review staleness beyond a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:571| declared threshold fails the invariant. The system that attests artifacts
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:572| attests its own audit recency — dogfooding, not decoration.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:573| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:574| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:575| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:576| ## 5. Success criteria & kill criterion
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:577| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:578| Three gates, in order, not to be conflated:
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:579| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:580| - **The gate (§8 / H0)** comes first — the formal foundation. Nothing below
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:581|   begins until it is resolved.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:582| - **The initial-slice gate (H1 §2)** — Band 1 frozen, then the LocalStack
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:583|   vertical slice at 1/sec within 7 days of the declared Phase 1 start.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:584| - **The whole-project gate (§5 below)** — when Tessera is a credible **v1
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:585|   product**, not merely an impressive demonstration. This is a deliberately
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:586|   binary, checklist-able bar rather than a subjective "impressive enough"
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:587|   judgment, because a credibility artifact wants a done-line a reader can check.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:588| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:589| **Done when (v1 product):**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:590| - Sustains **10,000 attestations in a 24-hour period** (~0.116/sec sustained).
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:591| - Survives **multi-model adversarial review by at least three unrelated LLM
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:592|   models**, including the web-facing surface. (This is the demonstration-project
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:593|   adversarial-review mechanism — explicitly *not* a substitute for a professional
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:594|   human security audit, and not labelled "audit.")
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:595| - **Review recency is attested** (§4.7): the service publishes a signed,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:596|   timestamped record of when it was last adversarially reviewed, and treats
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:597|   staleness past a declared threshold as a failing invariant — encoding that
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:598|   review is a recurring cycle, not a one-time gate.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:599| - **Account lifecycle complete through sign-up and API-key management**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:600|   (creation, invalidation, usage-log access) — the security-relevant authn/authz
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:601|   surface, red-bar tested (forge a key? use a revoked one? escalate via the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:602|   usage log?), not merely features. **Billing/payment is deferred** (a known
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:603|   Stripe-shaped, SAQ-A-minimizing integration when paying demand is validated —
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:604|   not built for v1).
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:605| - **Architected to the PCI standard, not certified to it.** The cardholder-data
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:606|   environment is minimized *by design* (tokenize via a compliant processor so
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:607|   PCI scope is SAQ-A-shaped, not SAQ-D), evidencing segmentation, key-management,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:608|   and access-control judgment. Designing to the bar is the demonstration;
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:609|   obtaining the certificate is deferred product work.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:610| - The scaling question — *if promoted for AI-agent use (e.g. openclaw,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:611|   hermes-agent), could it scale to handle success?* — is answered by
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:612|   **architecture + load evidence** (a design-and-load-test claim, not a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:613|   production-traffic claim).
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:614| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:615| **Kill criterion (further work is vanity):** the v1 done-line above is green and
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:616| the scale-to-success path is demonstrated *on paper*. Past that point — tuning
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:617| for traffic that does not yet exist, polishing UI, chasing scale that has not
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:618| been sold — is vanity. Stop and ship the demonstration.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:619| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:620| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:621| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:622| ## 6. Method & division of labor (the meta-claim)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:623| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:624| The stance is contest-then-adopt: the prior design spec (a previous AI's work,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:625| in `docs/tessera-cloud-demo-spec.md`) is coherent and useful, but it is *not*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:626| ratified. Architecture decisions are re-derived or contested in the human
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:627| author's voice; the disagreements are part of the credibility evidence, because
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:628| a design merely executed from an AI's spec would demonstrate the deskilling
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:629| failure mode, not the healthy one. AI accelerates mechanics; the judgment is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:630| the author's.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:631| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:632| **Disagreements with the prior spec, on the record:**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:633| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:634| 1. **The prior spec's KMS-only signing fork (B) concentrates the trust story in
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:635|    one operational domain.** KMS is technically capable (it signs Ed25519 and
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:636|    even post-quantum ML-DSA, with offline-verifiable public keys) — so the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:637|    disagreement is *not* that KMS is incapable, as an earlier draft wrongly
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:638|    implied. It is that resting a long-lived attestation solely on KMS ties its
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:639|    verifiability to a single domain's account lifecycle, key-deletion policy,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:640|    IAM, and public-key provenance (§3.1). Rejected in favor of dual-signing (C)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:641|    across independent failure domains, with DNS/repo/bundle key publication and
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:642|    a bundled issuer-key manifest. This was the load-bearing architectural
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:643|    disagreement.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:644| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:645| 2. **The prior spec under-specified supersession.** It had no model for adding
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:646|    assurance (e.g. post-quantum) to existing attestations. The wrap-don't-
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:647|    replace model (§3.1) — which also dissolves the canonicalization-freeze into
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:648|    per-layer versioning — is a Tessera addition, not the spec's.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:649| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:650| 3. **The prior spec treated the cloud-independent core and the LocalStack slice
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:651|    as one phase.** They are separated here into bands (§2): the cryptographic
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:652|    guarantees are frozen on a laptop *before* any LocalStack work, so the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:653|    cloud-shaped layers cannot silently regress the invariant.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:654| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:655| 4. **The prior spec assumed the central guarantee, never demanded it be
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:656|    proven.** It described an attestation service as if "tamper-evident,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:657|    cryptographically secure" were established by construction. It is not. The
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:658|    guarantee that altering a signed package requires solving a hard problem is
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:659|    an *unproven claim* until a machine-checked formal model and proof exist
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:660|    (H0 / Band 0). Treating that as a gating precondition — building nothing
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:661|    until the foundation is proven — is the largest divergence from the prior
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:662|    spec, and the one most central to the difference between a commercial
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:663|    offering and theater. Formal verification is itself a capability the project
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:664|    demonstrates (§7).
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:665| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:666| (Further disagreements are expected as the build proceeds; the journal records
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:667| them as they arise.)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:668| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:669| *Right-sizing note (carried from the prior spec, and true): the documentation
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:670| layer is a dated markdown journal, not an attestation system. The cleverness
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:671| goes in the service, not the log.*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:672| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:673| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:674| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:675| ## 7. Capability-map rows targeted (the CV mechanics)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:676| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:677| The gap profile is coherent, not a random scatter, and it *is* the CV thesis
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:678| made concrete: **I have the infrastructure primitives but not the operational,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:679| security-posture, and observability envelope around them.** I have built the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:680| components services are made of; the market wants people who can *operate*
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:681| services. Tessera closes exactly that envelope. Stated honestly in three bands:
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:682| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:683| **Direct gaps being closed (the point of the project — the "operate it" layer,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:684| mostly the SRE / security-engineering cluster, hard to fake and hard to learn
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:685| from docs alone):**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:686| - ECS / Fargate
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:687| - KMS (key custody)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:688| - CloudTrail (audit)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:689| - GuardDuty / Security Hub (threat detection / posture)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:690| - S3 Object Lock (WORM / immutability)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:691| - OpenTelemetry / Prometheus / Grafana (observability)
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:692| - SLOs / error budgets / load testing / graceful degradation
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:693| - CDK / Terraform IaC
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:694| - FinOps / cost governance
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:695| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:696| **Reinforced (already have hands-on; this project evidences depth, not novelty):**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:697| Lambda, SQS, DynamoDB, EC2, EBS, S3 (basic — *not* Object Lock), and security
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:698| architecture generally.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:699| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:700| **Acknowledged stretch (a real edge of competence, named rather than hidden):**
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:701| web-facing systems. I do not typically build public-facing web surfaces; the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:702| API gateway and (v1) web surface are a deliberate stretch, not a strength I am
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:703| claiming. Declaring this edge is itself the point — the same "declare what you
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:704| cannot see" ethos the attestation service embodies, applied to my own CV. A
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:705| reviewer should trust the strong claims *more* because the weak edge is stated.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:706| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:707| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:708| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:709| ## 8. The gate — this project does not begin until these are true
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:710| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:711| A pre-registration is only honest if it can name the condition under which the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:712| project *does not proceed*. Tessera has one, and it is non-negotiable:
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:713| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:714| **Band 0 (H0) must be resolved before Phase 1 begins.** Concretely:
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:715| - a machine-checked formal model (TLA+ and/or Lean4) of the attestation
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:716|   construction and its claimed invariants exists, and the proof — resting on
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:717|   cited external hardness assumptions, proving *our own composition* — holds;
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:718| - the agreement gate has passed (author and AI each independently judge the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:719|   model faithful to the claim);
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:720| - the informal written proof (the author's defend-it-cold account) is in the
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:721|   repository.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:722| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:723| The gate is **machine-checked**, by design. Independent *human* formal-methods
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:724| review is *not* a resolution requirement under the no-spend constraint (H3) — it
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:725| is an optional enhancement gated on a revenue stream, and its absence is a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:726| declared residual risk (no review, machine or human, guarantees a future party
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:727| won't find a hole). This keeps the bar rigorous *and* achievable in our control,
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:728| rather than set where it can never be met.
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:729| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:730| Only then does **Phase 1a** begin (implementing the cloud-independent crypto
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:731| core), marked by an explicit, dated, signed commit declaring the build runway
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:732| open. The 7-day H1b window opens later, at the H1a freeze commit (§2).
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:733| 
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:734| **If H0 cannot be met, the project does not proceed as designed — and that is a
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:735| valid, honest outcome of this pre-registration, not a failure to conceal.** A
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:736| highlight reel cannot say "we stopped because the foundation did not hold." A
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:737| real pre-registration can, and that is precisely where its credibility comes
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:738| from. The central guarantee of an attestation service is not something to
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:739| assert and build around; it is something to prove, or to honestly report we
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:740| could not. Building on an unproven foundation would be theater — the one
docs/phase-0-prereg.md:741| outcome this project exists to refute.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:49| ## A1.0 Why amend before starting
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:50| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:51| The review found that the pre-registration, as signed, could be *passed by a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:52| proof that does not protect the project*. H0 pre-registered that a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:53| machine-checked proof would exist, but not **what it must prove**. That gap
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:54| is precisely the drift-vector formal-methods theater needs: months into the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:55| modeling, the provable-in-practice properties drift toward whatever the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:56| model makes easy, and "the proof holds" quietly becomes "the proof of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:57| whatever we managed to prove holds." The agreement gate, as written, would
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:58| judge fidelity only *after* any such drift, by the same parties who drifted.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:59| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:60| This amendment closes that gap by pre-registering the property list
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:61| (A1.2), the degraded-policy semantics (A1.2.1), the adversary model (A1.3),
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:62| and the tooling rationale and choice discipline (A1.4). It also resolves
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:63| one design hole the review surfaced (manifest authority, A1.5), states the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:64| temporal-anchor semantics precisely (A1.6), and hardens the agreement gate
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:65| from a confirmation task into a falsification task (A1.7). The original
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:66| objectives, bands, and invariants are not weakened; this amendment *adds*
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:67| resolution and evidence obligations (A1.8).
