docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:71| ## A1.1 Clarification of the H0 falsifier
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:72| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:73| The original's phrasing — "if the guarantee cannot be proven, there is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:74| nothing worth building" — could be misread as one-shot: first failed proof
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:75| attempt, project over. That is not the claim and never was. The method is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:76| iterative, as all modeling is: model, attempt proof, find the flaw, revise,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:77| re-prove — with each revision recorded in the journal.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:78| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:79| Iteration within scope is ordinary work. **Falsification is scope
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:80| reduction.** Precisely: H0 (as amended) is falsified if any A1.2 property
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:81| cannot be discharged without one of the following:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:82| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:83| - **weakening the property** as pre-registered;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:84| - **demoting** a property from `[model]`/`[proof]` to `[assumption]`;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:85| - **excluding** a declared A1.3 adversary capability;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:86| - **changing the construction so materially** that it no longer implements
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:87|   the dual-signature + temporal-anchor design of §3.1.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:88| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:89| Any such weakening requires a further signed, dated amendment stating what
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:90| was weakened and why; absent that amendment, Phase 1 does not begin. This
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:91| gives a future reader a concrete way to see whether Band 0 succeeded,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:92| failed, or changed scope — rather than an unfalsifiable "no model could be
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:93| built." Building the service on a foundation that required concealed
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:94| weakening would be theater; that, and only that, is what the original
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:95| sentence forbids.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:96| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:97| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:98| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:99| ## A1.2 The pre-registered properties (the theorem statements)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:100| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:101| These are the properties the Band 0 work must establish, stated in prose
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:102| *before* any modeling begins, so that "the proof holds" has a fixed
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:103| referent. Each names how it is discharged: **[model]** — proven in the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:104| machine-checked model under idealized primitives (Layer 1); **[proof]** —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:105| proven directly (not a state-machine claim); **[assumption]** — cited as an
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:106| explicit Layer 2 assumption, not proven. Restating a property here in
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:107| sharper form does not weaken the original's hard invariants; where an
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:108| invariant (§4.3, §4.6) and a property overlap, the property is the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:109| checkable form of the invariant.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:110| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:111| Temporal vocabulary used throughout (defined precisely in A1.6):
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:112| `declared_issue_time` is what the issuer claims; `anchor_time` is the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:113| Bitcoin block time of the OTS anchor, which establishes only that the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:114| anchored bytes existed *not after* that block.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:115| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:116| - **P1 — Integrity (the headline claim).** There is no reachable state in
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:117|   which the verifier returns `VALID_STRICT` or `VALID_DEGRADED` for a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:118|   package whose canonical bytes differ from bytes signed at issue time.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:119|   **[model]**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:120| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:121| - **P2 — Signature-set completeness (anti-stripping).** The canonical
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:122|   signed bytes commit to the required-signer manifest. A package presenting
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:123|   fewer signatures than its manifest requires yields `INVALID` — never
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:124|   `VALID_STRICT`, and `VALID_DEGRADED` only under an explicit, recorded
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:125|   policy within the waivable set of A1.2.1. Consequence: "issued with one
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:126|   signature" and "issued with two, one stripped" are distinguishable by
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:127|   construction, because the expected set is inside what every signature
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:128|   signs. **[model]**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:129| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:130| - **P3 — Key binding (anti-substitution).** Acceptance binds each
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:131|   signature to the issuer identity committed in the signed bytes. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:132|   adversary model (A1.3) explicitly includes key-substitution attacks
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:133|   (DSKS / exclusive-ownership failures: constructing a different keypair
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:134|   under which an existing message–signature pair verifies, then
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:135|   re-presenting the package under a substituted manifest). Idealized
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:136|   signatures assume this binding by fiat; Ed25519 signature verification
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:137|   alone does not provide protocol-level issuer binding or exclusive
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:138|   ownership — the verification equation is not, by itself, the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:139|   issuer-binding protocol. Discharge is split:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:140|   - the binding of identity into signed bytes — the signed bytes include,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:141|     at minimum: domain-separation tag, object type (per P7's enumeration),
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:142|     algorithm identifier, issuer identity, key fingerprint, manifest hash,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:143|     and canonicalization version — is **[model]**;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:144|   - the implementation's **verification profile** is **[assumption]**,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:145|     named in Layer 2 and discharged as H1a evidence: exact library and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:146|     version, accepted signature encodings, public-key validation behavior,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:147|     low-order-point handling, cofactor equation variant, and negative test
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:148|     vectors for each, all recorded in the repository.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:149| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:150|   This property may not fall between the layers.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:151| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:152| - **P4 — Fail-closed state logic.** The verifier's four states partition
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:153|   all outcomes. A required check that fails yields `INVALID`. A check that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:154|   cannot be performed yields `UNVERIFIABLE` — never any `VALID` state,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:155|   under any trace. `VALID_DEGRADED` arises only from an explicit, recorded
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:156|   policy within A1.2.1's waivable set, never as a default or a fallback.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:157|   (The checkable form of §4.6.) **[model]**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:158| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:159| - **P5 — Temporal soundness (two-sided).** The anchor is an upper bound on
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:160|   creation time, and only that (A1.6). Strict verification requires the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:161|   anchor to be consistent with the declared issue time **in both
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:162|   directions**:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:163| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:164|       declared_issue_time − ε  ≤  anchor_time  ≤  declared_issue_time + δ
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:165| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:166|   The δ side **bounds** *backdating*: a forger signing new bytes cannot
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:167|   obtain a conforming anchor for a claimed time more than δ in the past —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:168|   backdating within the tolerance window is not eliminated, only bounded.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:169|   The ε side **bounds** *post-dating*: an issuer cannot declare an issue
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:170|   time more than ε after the anchor and later present the receipt as
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:171|   fresh.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:172| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:173|   **δ and ε belong to the verifier, not the receipt.** A receipt records
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:174|   its issue-time policy version and the observed anchor delay; it may not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:175|   choose its own temporal tolerances — a receipt-controlled tolerance
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:176|   would let a malicious issuer write an enormous window into the signed
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:177|   bytes. The reference verifier's strict policy fixes the maxima: **δ =
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:178|   72 hours** (OTS aggregation-to-confirmation lag plus Bitcoin timestamp
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:179|   skew), **ε = 24 hours** (Bitcoin block timestamps may lag real time by
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:180|   hours under the median-time-past rule). A verifier may choose stricter
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:181|   bounds; no degraded policy may enlarge δ or ε beyond the strict maxima.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:182|   Both maxima are ratified (or revised, on the record) at Band 0 exit.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:183|   Temporal-anchor consistency is **non-waivable** (A1.2.1). **[model]**,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:184|   resting on the Bitcoin/OTS assumptions of A1.6 **[assumption]**.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:185| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:186|   *Issuance-protocol corollary (so honest receipts cannot rot):* issuance
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:187|   is not complete until the anchor is **confirmed** — buried at a minimum
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:188|   confirmation depth **k** on the Bitcoin chain (strict default **k = 6**,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:189|   ratified with δ and ε at Band 0 exit) — within δ of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:190|   `declared_issue_time`. Depth is what "confirmed" *means*: a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:191|   one-confirmation anchor orphaned by a transient reorganization would
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:192|   leave an already-shipped receipt permanently unverifiable, so a receipt
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:193|   never ships on a shallow anchor. If confirmation is delayed past δ for
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:194|   benign reasons (calendar outage, fee spikes, reorg), the receipt is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:195|   **re-issued** with a fresh declared time and re-anchored — the failed
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:196|   attempt is discarded, not shipped. Without this rule, honest-but-late
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:197|   anchoring would be permanently indistinguishable from backdating.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:198| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:199| - **P6 — Revocation time-relativity (evaluated over the uncertainty
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:200|   window).** The anchor proves only that the signed bytes existed *not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:201|   after* `anchor_time`; it cannot locate the signing moment inside
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:202|   [`declared_issue_time`, `anchor_time`]. Evaluating authorization only
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:203|   at `declared_issue_time` would therefore admit a revocation/backdating
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:204|   interaction: a key revoked inside the δ window could sign *after*
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:205|   revocation while declaring a time just before it, and pass both P5 and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:206|   a point-evaluated P6. Accordingly, `VALID_STRICT` requires
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:207|   authorization **throughout the uncertainty window**:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:208| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:209|       key_authorized(declared_issue_time)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:210|       ∧ no revocation effective at or before anchor_time
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:211| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:212|   Revocation effective *after* `anchor_time` does not retroactively
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:213|   change the verdict. Revocation effective at or before `anchor_time`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:214|   yields `INVALID`.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:215| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:216|   **Key lifecycle is monotonic, by design commitment.** Revocation is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:217|   terminal: a revoked key is never re-authorized; re-keying issues a *new*
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:218|   key with a new fingerprint and a new manifest entry. Without
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:219|   monotonicity, "no revocation effective at or before `anchor_time`"
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:220|   would be ambiguous across revoke–re-authorize cycles; with it, the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:221|   interval check is well-defined. This is an issuer key-management rule
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:222|   that the model *assumes* and operational policy *enforces* — a design
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:223|   commitment, not a cryptographic assumption, and deliberately not filed
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:224|   under Layer 2.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:225| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:226|   This interval evaluation is deliberately stricter than checking
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:227|   `declared_issue_time` alone, and it can fail honest receipts whose key
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:228|   was revoked between declaration and anchor confirmation — the correct
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:229|   fail-closed outcome: the system cannot honestly prove such a receipt
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:230|   was signed before the revocation, and the issuance protocol (P5
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:231|   corollary) already treats unconfirmed issuance as incomplete. (The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:232|   checkable form of §4.4's revocation paragraph, in A1.6's vocabulary.)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:233|   **[model]**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:234| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:235| - **P7 — Wrapper and object-type soundness.** Every signed object carries
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:236|   a domain-separation type tag *inside the signed bytes*, drawn from the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:237|   enumerated set: base attestation, wrapper, issuer-key manifest,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:238|   authority evidence, conformance vector, review-recency attestation
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:239|   (§4.7). No trace exists in which an object of one type is accepted as
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:240|   another (no cross-type confusion). A wrapper commits to the inner
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:241|   package's **exact bytes, embedded as an opaque byte string** (e.g.,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:242|   base64 of the inner package's framed bytes) — never as parsed JSON.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:243|   Outer canonicalization must be structurally unable to re-serialize,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:244|   re-escape, or otherwise touch the inner byte stream: a nested-JSON
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:245|   embedding would let a different outer canonicalization version silently
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:246|   alter the inner bytes and break the inner signatures and OTS proof.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:247|   (Hash-only commitment is rejected: the inner bytes must travel *inside*
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:248|   the bundle, or P9's self-containment fails.) The wrapper records both
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:249|   inner and outer canonicalization versions. Wrapping never alters the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:250|   inner package's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:251|   independently-computed verdict — the wrapper attests the inner *bytes*,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:252|   never the inner *verification result* (preserving §3.1's distinction
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:253|   exactly). **[model]**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:254| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:255| - **P8 — Canonicalization injectivity, framing, and rejection.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:256|   `canonical()` is injective on its **accepted payload domain**, and the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:257|   encoding is boundary-unambiguous. JCS (RFC 8785) itself carries no
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:258|   length header, so the frame supplies it: signatures and anchors commit
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:259|   to a **framed envelope** —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:260|   `type_tag || canonicalization_version || payload_length || payload` —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:261|   where `payload` is the JCS bytes. The *issuer* constructs the frame; the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:262|   *verifier* reconstructs it independently and rejects any mismatch; the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:263|   exact binary layout is fixed, with golden vectors, before the Band 1
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:264|   freeze. A parser cannot disagree about where the payload ends. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:265|   accepted domain is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:266|   closed by explicit *rejection*: anything outside it is refused, never
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:267|   "helpfully" normalized. Rejection is required, at minimum, for:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:268|   duplicate object names; `NaN`/`Infinity`; numbers not exactly
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:269|   representable as IEEE 754 doubles (per §4.3, such values must be
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:270|   string-encoded); `-0` and numeric edge cases; non-I-JSON strings;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:271|   inputs relying on Unicode normalization assumptions; unknown
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:272|   canonicalization versions; trailing bytes; type-tag mismatch;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:273|   length-prefix mismatch. Golden vectors (§4.3) evidence the positive
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:274|   domain; the rejection suite evidences the negative domain — both are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:275|   H1a obligations. Injectivity over the accepted domain is discharged by
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:276|   direct proof. **[proof]**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:277| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:278| - **P9 — Verification statelessness.** The verdict is a pure function of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:279|   the bundle and the verifier's declared policy — no service-side state,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:280|   no live network dependency, appears in the decision. (The checkable form
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:281|   of §4.4's hard rule.) **[model]**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:282| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:283| - **P10 — Manifest authority (external evidence plus possession).** The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:284|   issuer-key manifest carries **two independent, archived, time-anchored
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:285|   authority-publication evidences** — the DNSSEC snapshot and the anchored
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:286|   repository publication (A1.5) — **plus** a manifest self-signature by the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:287|   issuer keys. The self-signature proves *possession* and binds the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:288|   manifest bytes to the asserted keys; it is **not authority evidence and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:289|   is never counted as an authority channel** — an adversary substituting
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:290|   their own key self-signs trivially. `VALID_STRICT` requires **all**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:291|   external authority evidences to validate, plus proof-of-possession.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:292|   Property: an adversary controlling any proper subset of the external
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:293|   authority channels cannot cause a manifest asserting a non-authorized
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:294|   key to satisfy the `VALID_STRICT` evidence requirement. Missing or
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:295|   partially-validating evidence degrades by A1.2.1's explicit-policy
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:296|   logic, naming which authority evidence was waived and why — never
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:297|   silently. **[model]**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:298| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:299| **Change discipline.** This list may be amended before Band 0 exit only by
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:300| a further signed, dated amendment stating what changed and why — the same
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:301| rule as everything else in the pre-registration. Silent narrowing of the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:302| property list is the failure mode this section exists to prevent.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:303| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:304| ### A1.2.1 Degraded-policy semantics (the waiver lattice)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:305| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:306| `VALID_DEGRADED` exists so long-horizon verification does not collapse to
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:307| a boolean — not as a universal escape hatch. Its scope is fixed here:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:308| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:309| **Non-waivable checks.** No verifier policy may waive: canonical-byte
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:310| integrity (P1, P8); type/domain separation (P7); boundary framing (P8);
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:311| key-to-issuer binding for every accepted signature (P3); temporal-anchor
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:312| consistency (P5). A package failing any non-waivable check is `INVALID`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:313| under **every** policy — no degraded policy may promote it
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:314| (*monotonicity*). A non-waivable check that *cannot be performed* yields
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:315| `UNVERIFIABLE`, never any `VALID` state — the P4 partition applies inside
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:316| the lattice: performed-and-failed → `INVALID`; unperformable →
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:317| `UNVERIFIABLE`; neither is promotable.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:318| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:319| **Waivable checks (declared redundancy only).** Degraded policies may
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:320| weaken only declared redundancy requirements: accepting a subset of the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:321| issue-time signature set (P2); accepting fewer than all external
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:322| manifest-authority evidences (P10); accepting a signature whose trust root
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:323| is no longer independently recoverable, where the remaining checks pass.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:324| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:325| **Recording.** Every `VALID_DEGRADED` verdict records the precise waived
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:326| check set and the policy that authorized the waiver — the informed-consent
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:327| act of §3.1, made auditable.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:328| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:329| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:330| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:331| ## A1.3 The adversary model (explicit capabilities)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:332| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:333| The Band 0 adversary can, at minimum:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:334| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:335| 1. **Alter** any bytes of a package, receipt, manifest, or wrapper after
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:336|    issue.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:337| 2. **Strip, reorder, or duplicate** signatures within the signature set.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:338| 3. **Substitute keys** — including choosing keypairs *after* seeing valid
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:339|    signatures (the DSKS capability of P3) — and always self-sign with keys
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:340|    it holds (possession is free to the adversary; see P10).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:341| 4. **Replay** valid packages, receipts, or manifests in other contexts, and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:342|    re-frame objects across the P7 type boundaries.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:343| 5. **Craft manifests** freely, and anchor anything: anchoring proves
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:344|    existence at a time, not authority (A1.5, A1.6).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:345| 6. **Control any proper subset of the external manifest-authority
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:346|    channels** (P10).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:347| 7. **Drive the legitimate issuance path** with authorized credentials —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:348|    named to re-affirm the original's misissuance boundary: this adversary
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:349|    is *out of scope for the cryptographic construction* and is met by
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:350|    operational controls (§3.1, threat classes). The model documents the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:351|    boundary; it does not pretend to cover it.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:352| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:353| The adversary cannot break the idealized primitives — signature
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:354| unforgeability, hash collision/preimage resistance, or the temporal-anchor
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:355| assumptions — which are the cited Layer 2 assumptions (original H0; A1.6).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:356| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:357| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:358| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:359| ## A1.4 Tooling: the right tool per target, not the familiar tool
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:360| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:361| The original said "TLA+ and/or Lean4." That was reached for on familiarity,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:362| and the review contested it — recorded here in the §6
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:363| disagreements-on-the-record spirit:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:364| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:365| - **The verifier state machine and temporal logic (P1, P2, P4, P5, P6, P7,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:366|   P9, P10)** — TLA+. This *is* state-machine work, TLA+'s home turf, and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:367|   the author can read and defend TLA+ cold, which the agreement gate
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:368|   requires.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:369| - **The composition under an active adversary (P1–P3, P7 under A1.3)** —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:370|   a symbolic protocol verifier, **Tamarin or ProVerif**, whose built-in
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:371|   Dolev-Yao adversary derives, replays, and substitutes messages natively.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:372|   Hand-rolling an adversary inside TLA+ would make the proof's value rest
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:373|   on the fidelity of that hand-rolled adversary — reintroducing the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:374|   wrong-model risk at the exact spot it is hardest to review.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:375| - **Canonicalization injectivity (P8)** — direct proof over the encoding
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:376|   rules (Lean4 if warranted, rigorous prose proof plus the golden-vector
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:377|   and rejection suites if that is honest sufficiency), separate from the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:378|   state-machine work.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:379| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:380| **Tool-choice discipline (anti-tool-shopping).** "Tamarin or ProVerif"
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:381| must not become "whichever tool proves the desired result." The choice is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:382| fixed *before* theorem-proving begins: a bounded spike may compare the two
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:383| only on **expressiveness and author-readability** for P1–P3/P7 under A1.3
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:384| — not on which yields the proof. The choice, the rejected alternative, and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:385| the reason are committed before substantive proof work starts. Switching
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:386| tools later requires a signed amendment naming the blocker.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:387| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:388| **The readability trade-off, named.** The author reads TLA+ but not (yet)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:389| Tamarin's lemma language or ProVerif's applied pi calculus. A tool the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:390| author cannot audit weakens the human half of the agreement gate exactly
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:391| where it matters most. Mitigation, committed to here: every
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:392| symbolic-verifier lemma carries a **prose mapping** back to the A1.2
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:393| property it discharges, and the informal written proof (H0 requirement 3)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:394| covers the composition argument in the author's own words regardless of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:395| tool.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:396| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:397| **Cross-model correspondence (the two-formalisms risk, named).** The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:398| construction is formalized twice — a TLA+ state machine and a symbolic
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:399| protocol model — and two formalisms of "the same" system can quietly
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:400| describe two subtly different systems, each verified, neither wrong,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:401| jointly meaningless. The informal written proof must therefore include an
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:402| explicit **correspondence mapping** between the TLA+ transitions and the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:403| symbolic tool's rules/facts, arguing that both describe the same
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:404| construction; the model-derived conformance vectors (A1.7) test both
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:405| against the same implementation, which bounds — but does not eliminate —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:406| the divergence risk.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:407| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:408| Learning to read the symbolic tool's output well enough to contest
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:409| it is part of the capability H0 demonstrates — the deskilling defense
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:410| (§6), applied at the new edge.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:411| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:412| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:413| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:414| ## A1.5 Manifest authority: resolving the circularity
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:415| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:416| The review surfaced a hole in §4.4 as written: the bundle's issuer-key
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:417| manifest was to carry "timestamped evidence that those keys were authorized
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:418| issuer keys at issue time, the manifest itself anchored." But **anchoring
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:419| proves existence, not authority** — anyone can anchor a manifest claiming
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:420| anything. A manifest signed by the keys it authorizes is circular; a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:421| manifest signed by a separate root key reintroduces the single trust
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:422| domain §3.1 rejects.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:423| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:424| **Resolution (not deferral): apply §3.1's own argument recursively.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:425| Authority at issue time cannot be conjured from nothing — every PKI bottoms
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:426| out in trust anchors; the honest move is to make the anchors plural,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:427| independent, archived, and time-anchored. The manifest carries **two
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:428| external authority-publication evidences plus proof-of-possession**:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:429| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:430| 1. **DNSSEC chain snapshot** — the `wamason.com` records publishing the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:431|    issuer-key fingerprints, with the signature chain to the root as it
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:432|    existed at issue time, *archived in the bundle* (discovery channels stay
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:433|    discovery; the archived snapshot is what verification uses).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:434| 2. **Anchored repository publication** — the public git commit publishing
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:435|    the same fingerprints, with the commit object, its signature, the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:436|    relevant proof material, and the OTS proof **archived in the bundle**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:437|    (like the DNSSEC snapshot: verification uses the archive, never live
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:438|    repository availability — P9).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:439| 3. **Manifest self-signature** by the issuer keys — *proof of possession
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:440|    only*. It binds the manifest bytes to the asserted keys and is never
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:441|    counted as authority evidence (P10): an attacker's invented key
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:442|    self-signs for free.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:443| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:444| `VALID_STRICT` requires both external evidences plus possession. A future
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:445| verifier sees that at issue time, two channels with independent operational
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:446| failure modes asserted the same key authority, and the asserted keys were
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:447| demonstrably held. Subverting the process requires tampering with both
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:448| external channels, at or before issue time, consistently.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:449| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:450| **Declared residual risks (difficulty, not impossibility):**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:451| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:452| - **Correlated control.** Both external channels are ultimately operated by
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:453|   the same author — same registrar sphere, same person. Their independence
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:454|   is real against *channel failure* (registrar lapse vs. repository-host
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:455|   lapse) and against an attacker who compromises one channel; it is weaker
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:456|   against an adversary who owns the author's entire operational sphere at
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:457|   issue time. That adversary sits at the misissuance boundary (A1.3, item
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:458|   7) and is met operationally, not cryptographically.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:459| - **Trust-anchor recursion.** The archived DNSSEC chain validates against
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:460|   the root trust anchors *as they existed at issue time*. A verifier
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:461|   decades later needs trustworthy knowledge of those historical anchors —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:462|   which is itself a historical-authority question. Concretely, the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:463|   reference verifier maintains an **archived historical trust-anchor
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:464|   store** (DNS root keys and repository signing keys, by validity period),
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:465|   distributed *with the verifier* as trust configuration — not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:466|   service-side state, so P9 is not violated. The plural-evidence
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:467|   structure and the §3.1 wrapping model (re-anchoring under fresh trust
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:468|   *before* old roots decay) mitigate the remaining recursion; they do not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:469|   eliminate it.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:470| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:471| Not *perfect* — plural evidence is a difficulty argument, not an
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:472| impossibility proof, and it is declared as such — but *difficult*, and P10
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:473| makes the difficulty claim checkable.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:474| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:475| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:476| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:477| ## A1.6 Temporal anchor semantics, stated precisely
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:478| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:479| The original's forgery argument ("producing a valid OTS anchor at the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:480| original time") compressed what the anchor actually establishes. Precisely:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:481| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:482| - **Vocabulary.** `declared_issue_time` — the issue time the issuer claims,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:483|   committed inside the signed canonical bytes. `anchor_time` — the Bitcoin
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:484|   block time of the OTS anchor over those bytes.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:485| - **The anchor is an upper bound on creation time.** The anchor proves the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:486|   bytes existed *not after* `anchor_time` — nothing more. It provides **no
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:487|   lower bound**: old bytes can be stamped today, and a forger with
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:488|   compromised keys can sign new bytes today. What the anchor prevents is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:489|   *backdating* — obtaining a conforming anchor in the past for bytes
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:490|   created now. New forgeries dated honestly-now are the key-compromise /
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:491|   misissuance classes (§3.1), met operationally, not by the anchor.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:492| - **The verifier enforces a two-sided consistency check (P5).**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:493|   `declared_issue_time − ε ≤ anchor_time ≤ declared_issue_time + δ`, with
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:494|   strict defaults δ = 72 hours and ε = 24 hours, both declared per receipt
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:495|   and ratified (or revised, on the record) at Band 0 exit. Temporal
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:496|   consistency is non-waivable (A1.2.1). The issuance protocol treats
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:497|   anchor confirmation — at minimum depth k, strict default k = 6 (P5
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:498|   corollary) — within δ as part of successful issuance; late or reorged
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:499|   anchors force re-issue.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:500| - **Layer 2 assumptions, extended.** To the original's cited assumptions
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:501|   (signature unforgeability, SHA-256 resistance, OTS/Bitcoin timestamp
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:502|   assumptions) add, explicitly: Bitcoin block timestamps are inexact —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:503|   consensus rules (median-time-past, the two-hour future bound) bound but
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:504|   do not eliminate skew — absorbed into δ and ε; anchors at depth ≥ k are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:505|   treated as permanent (a reorganization deeper than k is out of model,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:506|   subsumed by the history assumption that follows); and **the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:507|   proof-of-work history remains intact and available over the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:508|   adjudication horizon**. A
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:509|   fifty-year adjudication story rests on Bitcoin's fifty-year survival;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:510|   stating that plainly is the declare-what-you-cannot-see ethos, applied
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:511|   to the anchor itself.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:512| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:513| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:514| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:515| ## A1.7 The agreement gate, hardened
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:516| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:517| The original gate asked author and AI to independently *agree* the model is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:518| faithful. Confirmation tasks produce weak evidence: a reviewer re-reads the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:519| author's framing and nods, because the framing is persuasive — that is why
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:520| the author chose it. And the AI collaborator that helped author the model
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:521| agreeing with it is close to self-review. Two changes, both consistent with
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:522| §4.5's different-model discipline, applied one level up:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:523| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:524| 1. **The fidelity review is a falsification task performed by non-author
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:525|    models.** Models that had no hand in authoring the formal model receive
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:526|    the A1.2 property list (prose) and the model itself, and are tasked
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:527|    adversarially: *construct a concrete trace the model accepts that the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:528|    properties say must be rejected, or a property the prose implies that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:529|    the model fails to state.* A reviewer who hunted for a counterexample
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:530|    and failed is evidence; a reviewer who agreed is a nod. The hunt's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:531|    artifacts are committed either way — found or not found — and each
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:532|    review records, for reproducibility: model, vendor, and date; the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:533|    prompts used; configuration where available; the hash of the exact
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:534|    input bundle; and whether the reviewer saw prior review transcripts.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:535| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:536| 2. **Model-derived conformance vectors.** The model checker's explored
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:537|    traces are mechanically extracted into concrete fixtures for the real
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:538|    verifier — each trace names inputs and the verdict the model requires
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:539|    (e.g., "manifest requires {KMS, GPG}, bundle carries only KMS →
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:540|    `INVALID`"). This narrows the declared model-to-code gap (the code is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:541|    tested against the model's exact predictions, not hand-written
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:542|    approximations of them) and doubles as a fidelity check: an unfaithful
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:543|    model, concretized into fixtures, produces *visibly absurd test cases*
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:544|    — far easier to catch than a subtle misstatement in temporal logic.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:545|    These vectors become part of the H1a suite, with a clean division of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:546|    labor: model-derived vectors *evidence* conformance to the model on the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:547|    extracted traces — testing, not proof of implementation/model
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:548|    equivalence, preserving the original's attested-not-proven discipline
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:549|    for the model-to-code gap; the adversarially-authored red-bar attacks
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:550|    (§4.5) hunt for what is *outside* the model. **Declared limitation:** the trace-to-fixture translation
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:551|    is itself a step with fidelity risk — abstract states must be
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:552|    concretized into real byte-level bundles. The concretizer is therefore
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:553|    reviewed under the same non-author discipline, and its output is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:554|    spot-audited by eye; the risk is named, not waved off.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:555| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:556| **Declared residual risk — self-adjudication.** Whether a reviewer's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:557| counterexample stands or is refuted is judged by the author. Independent
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:558| adjudication costs money the pre-registered no-spend constraint (H3)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:559| forbids; the softness is therefore declared rather than concealed, and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:560| every adjudication (counterexample accepted or refuted, with reasoning) is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:561| committed alongside the review artifacts, so a future reader can re-judge.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:562| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:563| H0's resolution criteria are amended accordingly: requirement (2) now
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:564| reads — the falsification-task review by non-author models has run, its
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:565| artifacts are committed, and no unrefuted counterexample stands; and the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:566| conformance-vector extraction is added to the H1a evidence obligations.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:567| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:568| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:569| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:570| ## A1.8 What did change, and what did not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:571| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:572| The ranked objectives (§1), the bands and the H1–H3 hypotheses as
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:573| originally registered, the hard invariants (§4), the success and kill
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:574| criteria (§5), and the division of labor (§6) are **not weakened** by this
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:575| amendment. This amendment **adds** obligations: pre-registered theorem
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:576| statements and a waiver lattice (A1.2, A1.2.1), an explicit adversary
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:577| model (A1.3), a tool-choice discipline (A1.4), a manifest-authority
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:578| mechanism with declared residual risks and a historical trust-anchor
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:579| store (A1.5), precise temporal semantics with new Layer 2 assumptions and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:580| a confirmation-depth rule (A1.6, P5), a key-lifecycle monotonicity
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:581| commitment (P6), an opaque-embedding rule for wrappers (P7), a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:582| framed-envelope specification (P8), a falsification-style agreement
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:583| gate with reproducibility requirements, new H1a evidence obligations
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:584| (conformance vectors, the P3 verification profile, the P8 rejection
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:585| suite), and an auditable H0 falsifier (A1.1). The gate (§8) is unchanged
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:586| in intent: Band 0 resolves before Phase 1 begins, and "the foundation did
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:587| not hold" remains a valid, honest outcome. What this amendment changes is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:588| that the gate can no longer be *passed by accident* — the theorems are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:589| named, the adversary is named, the tools fit the targets, and the fidelity
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:590| check tries to break the model instead of blessing it.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:30| ## A2.0 What the model surfaced, and a correction registered with it
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:31| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:32| The state machine did what pre-registering models is for: it made a prose
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:33| ambiguity mechanically undeniable. The author ratifies the **strict**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:34| reading — restated below on a chain-visible observable so that the issuer
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:35| and the verifier check the *same temporal conjuncts* (under the issuance
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:36| policy's tolerances; A2.1).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:37| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:38| One correction from the ratification dialogue is registered alongside,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:39| because leaving it implicit would invite a misreading of what the strict
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:40| rule protects. Consider the **abandoned-anchor artifact**: an issuance
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:41| attempt whose anchor lands in an in-window block but buries slowly; the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:42| strict issuer discards and re-issues, yet the discarded transaction
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:43| persists and typically confirms later, so a complete, chain-verifiable
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:44| (receipt, anchor) pair exists that was never shipped. Checked against the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:45| registered properties: this artifact violates **none of them** — none of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:46| the **pre-Amendment-2 registered set**; A2.2 below changes exactly that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:47| for the **chain-late subclass** (`confirmed_at > declared + δ`), which
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:48| it rejects. An operationally abandoned but **chain-valid** artifact
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:49| (predicate holds; no timely eligibility latch, so the attempt was
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:50| refused — possible under the A2.1 clock roles) is *not* rejected by
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:51| A2.2; it is governed by the A2.1/A2.4 standing rules: cryptographically
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:52| valid, evidentially admissible, no protocol standing. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:53| anchor's security content is the block time alone — backdating is bounded
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:54| because no forger can place bytes in a past block (P5), and P6's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:55| uncertainty window is bounded by `anchor_time` because signing precedes
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:56| block inclusion. *When* depth k was reached enters neither argument. What
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:57| the depth-k-within-δ rule actually protects is different: no shipped
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:58| receipt can be orphaned by a tolerated reorganization (the P5c
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:59| `NoShippedOrphan` invariant), and the issuer's evidence trail stays free
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:60| of receipts whose completion needs explaining. The residue the artifact
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:61| does create — two verifiable receipts for the same content with different
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:62| declared times — is **not closed by this amendment** (correction,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:63| 2026-07-21: an earlier draft claimed closure via A2.2 and A2.4; that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:64| argument silently assumed the fused clock, under which every discarded
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:65| attempt is chain-late. Under the ruled clock roles of A2.1 a discarded
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:66| attempt can be chain-valid, A2.2 rejects only late-burial artifacts, and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:67| A2.4 confines standing without deduplicating content). Closure — a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:68| lineage/equivocation-evidence mechanism or an explicit dedup rule — is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:69| registered as an Amendment 3 obligation.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:70| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:71| The ratified form strengthens P5 with a new verifier-side conjunct and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:72| adds obligations; under A1.2's change discipline that requires this
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:73| amendment. No A1.2 property is weakened; the A1.1 falsifier is not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:74| triggered (stated precisely in A2.6).
