docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:76| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:77| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:78| ## A2.1 "Confirmed within δ": one predicate, both sides
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:79| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:80| **Vocabulary.** The anchor transaction is included in the block at height
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:81| `h`. Confirmation count follows the Bitcoin convention: the including
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:82| block is the first confirmation, so `c = tip_height − h + 1`, and the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:83| block that grants the k-th confirmation has height `h + k − 1`. Define
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:84| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:85|     confirmed_at  :=  timestamp(block at height h + k − 1)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:86| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:87| **The rule.** Issuance is complete only if
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:88| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:89|     confirmed_at  ≤  declared_issue_time + δ
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:90| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:91| The issuer evaluates this conjunct **as part of the full three-conjunct
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:92| temporal predicate** (the P5 temporal test inside `VALID_STRICT`; all
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:93| three A2.2 conjuncts — not the whole verdict, which contains more than
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:94| the temporal test) before shipping: under
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:95| skewed, non-monotonic block timestamps the confirmation conjunct does
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:96| not imply the anchor-time conjunct, so shipping on this conjunct alone
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:97| could ship a receipt the verifier rejects (surfaced by the bridge model,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:98| `formal/tla/P5cP5P6_Bridge.tla`, 2026-07-21). The verifier evaluates the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:99| same conjuncts on the same chain observables at verification (A2.2),
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:100| **under the issuance policy's tolerances**: the verifier-owns-tolerances
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:101| discipline permits stricter verifier values of either tolerance (a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:102| stricter δ′ < δ, or a stricter ε′ on the anchor-time lower bound), and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:103| such a verifier may reject honestly-shipped receipts — the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:104| no-disagreement guarantee below is scoped to verification under the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:105| issuance policy's δ and ε.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:106| **Clock roles (ruling, 2026-07-21).** Chain time and wall time hold
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:107| separate, explicitly-ranked roles. **Chain time governs evidence:** the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:108| three-conjunct predicate above, evaluated identically by issuer and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:109| verifier on the designated blocks' timestamps. **Wall time governs the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:110| attempt lifecycle:** the service waits through `declared + δ + S` before
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:111| treating an attempt as expired, where S ≥ 0 is an **operational slack
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:112| constant** joining δ, ε, k, N for ratification at Band 0 exit (working
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:113| default S = 24 h, sized to the observation path — outages and polling,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:114| not timestamp skew alone). **No global bound on the backward observation
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:115| lag is assumed.** Writing C = `confirmed_at` and B = the service's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:116| wall-clock observation of the designated block: Bitcoin consensus
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:117| provides no finite bound on B − C (median-time-past and the two-hour
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:118| future rule bound the forward direction only), and B additionally
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:119| absorbs the entire observation path — network and header-store delay,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:120| polling, outage and recovery, wall-clock error. Registering a hard
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:121| bound would assert, at Phase 0, a property of an operational stack that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:122| does not yet exist. Instead the guarantee is registered **conditionally
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:123| on the observable antecedent**: *if B − C ≤ S for an attempt whose
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:124| predicate holds, that attempt has a live shipping opportunity at
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:125| eligibility* (slack-parameter analysis,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:126| `formal/tla/P5cP5P6_BridgeSlack.tla` and its `_Latch` variant;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:127| predictions-first record in
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:128| `docs/reviews/2026-07-21-claude-predictions-slack-bench.md`). Since B
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:129| and C are both observable, a violated antecedent is a detectable
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:130| operating-envelope event, not a silently failed assumption. Timeliness
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:131| is **latched at eligibility**: an attempt eligible within the envelope
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:132| cannot be expired by later packaging or scheduling delay —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:133| eligible/finalizing, shipped, and expired/refused are mutually
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:134| exclusive states (a construction obligation on the implementation,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:135| registered with the ruling). An attempt whose lag exceeds S may be
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:136| refused; a chain-valid artifact of such an attempt remains
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:137| cryptographically valid and evidentially admissible but carries **no
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:138| protocol standing** (A2.4; enforcing that distinction against later
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:139| publication is Amendment 3's lineage/standing obligation). If
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:140| operational evidence later supports an SLA-style hard bound, it may
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:141| enter a **deployment profile** with monitoring and an explicit
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:142| violation outcome — never this pre-registration's assumption set. What
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:143| the opportunity guarantee buys is opportunity, not outcome: "every
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:144| timely-eligible attempt ships" is a contract obligation on the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:145| implementation, the same proof-versus-contract split as A2.3's refusal.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:146| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:147| **Boundary ties, registered per clock.** The chain-side predicate is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:148| stateless: at exactly `confirmed_at = declared + δ` it holds, and holds
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:149| identically whenever evaluated — there is no chain-side race. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:150| wall-side boundary is **resolved by the latch, not raced** (round-3
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:151| repair, 2026-07-21: an earlier draft of this paragraph carried the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:152| fused-clock race forward; under latched eligibility there is none).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:153| Eligibility observed at exactly `B = declared + δ + S` is timely — the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:154| boundary is **inclusive and latch-winning**, matching the mechanized
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:155| form (`burialAtWall <= declared + Delta + Slack` in the `_Latch`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:156| companion) — so such an attempt latches eligible/finalizing and cannot
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:157| expire. Expiry (on the final attempt, refusal) applies only **strictly
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:158| after** the boundary, and only to attempts with no timely-latched
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:159| eligibility. Atomicity of the latch against the expiry transition is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:160| part of the mutual-exclusion construction obligation (A2.3). If the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:161| predicate fails at issuance time, the attempt is discarded and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:162| re-issued per the P5 corollary, subject to the attempt bound of A2.3.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:163| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:164| **Why chain time on both sides.** A wall-clock ship rule ("ship if depth k
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:165| by `now ≤ declared + δ`") and a block-timestamp verifier check can
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:166| disagree at the δ boundary by the consensus-bounded skew (block timestamps
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:167| may run up to about two hours ahead of network-adjusted time). Defining
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:168| the rule once, on the chain-visible quantity, removes the divergence: **no
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:169| honestly-shipped receipt can fail the verifier's confirmation conjunct
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:170| under the issuance policy's δ**, and the issuer's ship rule and the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:171| verifier predicate become the same intended statement about the same
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:172| observable under the declared abstractions — the correspondence A1.4
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:173| demands, asserted here and checked mechanically by the bridge model
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:174| (`formal/tla/P5cP5P6_Bridge.tla`; its own non-author review pending).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:175| P5c's fused-clock guard (`now ≤ declared + δ` at depth k) is a locally
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:176| *stronger* condition that implies the chain predicate under that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:177| module's single-clock abstraction; with the clocks decoupled, the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:178| bridge's `Ship` evaluates the chain quantities directly.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:179| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:180| **Named residuals.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:181| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:182| - *Adversarial timestamping.* A miner can set `timestamp(h + k − 1)`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:183|   forward within the consensus bound, pushing an honest issuance into the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:184|   tail case. This is a griefing surface bounded to hours against δ = 72
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:185|   hours; it can force a re-issue, never a false verdict.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:186| - *Non-monotonic timestamps.* Block timestamps are not monotonic;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:187|   `confirmed_at` may even precede `anchor_time`. The predicate is a single
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:188|   comparison on one designated block and is well-defined regardless; no
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:189|   monotonicity is assumed.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:190| - *`confirmed_at` is a proxy, including backward skew.* The observable is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:191|   the designated block's header timestamp — the chosen chain-time proxy
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:192|   for burial, not a measurement of when depth k was reached in wall-clock
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:193|   time. Median-time-past rules allow a block mined after a real-time
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:194|   deadline to carry an in-window timestamp (the mirror of the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:195|   forward-skew griefing above). The predicate is well-defined on the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:196|   proxy; wall-clock burial lateness is not what it measures.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:197| - *Header provenance.* The conjunct's verdict is only as trustworthy as
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:198|   the headers it is evaluated over. Bundled headers form a candidate
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:199|   chain segment, not proof of canonicity: a privately-mined in-window
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:200|   fork presented in a bundle, or a lying header store, yields false
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:201|   acceptance under naive stateless evaluation. Header authentication
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:202|   against the canonical chain — proof-of-work validity, cumulative-work
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:203|   or checkpoint anchoring, store identity pinned in declared verifier
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:204|   policy, bundle/store conflict rules — is part of the A2.2 evidence
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:205|   obligation; its full specification is deferred to that obligation's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:206|   discharge, not silently assumed here.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:207| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:208| **Model-convention pin (off-by-one, fixed here so it cannot drift).**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:209| P5c's `depth` variable counts blocks mined *after* inclusion (`depth = 0`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:210| at inclusion), so `depth ≥ DepthK` corresponds to `c ≥ DepthK + 1`. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:211| correspondence mapping instantiates **`DepthK = k − 1`** (for the strict
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:212| default k = 6: `DepthK = 5`). δ, ε, k remain ratified (or revised, on the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:213| record) at Band 0 exit, as registered; δ's 72-hour sizing already included
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:214| aggregation-to-confirmation lag, so this amendment does not move it.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:215| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:216| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:217| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:218| ## A2.2 P5, amended: the strict temporal check gains a third conjunct
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:219| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:220| `VALID_STRICT` now requires all of:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:221| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:222|     declared_issue_time − ε  ≤  anchor_time                       (unchanged)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:223|     anchor_time              ≤  declared_issue_time + δ           (unchanged)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:224|     confirmed_at             ≤  declared_issue_time + δ           (new)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:225| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:226| Consequences, stated explicitly:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:227| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:228| - The **chain-late subclass** of the A2.0 abandoned-anchor artifact
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:229|   (`confirmed_at > declared + δ`) is **rejected outright** — its
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:230|   `confirmed_at` exceeds its own window. Within this system the conjunct
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:231|   rejects *only* such artifacts: strict issuance ships nothing that fails
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:232|   it (A2.1). An operationally abandoned but chain-valid artifact passes
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:233|   this conjunct and is governed instead by the A2.1/A2.4 standing rules
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:234|   (no protocol standing; closure of the two-receipts residue is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:235|   Amendment 3's obligation, per A2.0).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:236| - **Evidence obligation.** The verifier must evaluate `confirmed_at`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:237|   statelessly (P9): block headers `h … h + k − 1` are available either
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:238|   archived in the bundle or from the verifier-distributed header store the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:239|   anchor check already requires — the same trust-configuration pattern as
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:240|   A1.5's historical trust-anchor store. Header *authentication* rules
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:241|   (canonicity, work validation, store identity in declared policy,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:242|   bundle/store conflict resolution — the header-provenance residual of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:243|   A2.1) are part of this obligation. This joins the H1a evidence
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:244|   obligations.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:245| - **Waiver status.** Temporal-anchor consistency is already non-waivable
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:246|   (A1.2.1); the new conjunct is part of it. The P4 partition applies
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:247|   inside it: performed-and-failed → `INVALID`; unperformable (headers
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:248|   unavailable) → `UNVERIFIABLE`; neither is promotable.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:249| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:250| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:251| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:252| ## A2.3 The re-issue loop terminates: bounded attempts, fail-closed refusal
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:253| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:254| As registered, the P5 corollary's re-issue rule was an unbounded loop, and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:255| its dominant triggers — fee spikes, congestion, calendar outage — are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:256| *correlated across attempts*: retrying under the same conditions is not a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:257| fresh draw, so "re-issue until it works" can livelock. Fail-closed means
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:258| issuance must be able to end in refusal, not only in success.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:259| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:260| Amended: issuance makes at most **N attempts**. The expiry clock is the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:261| **wall clock** (A2.1 clock roles): an attempt expires when wall time
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:262| passes `declared + δ + S`, except that timely-latched eligibility
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:263| excludes expiry — eligible/finalizing, shipped, and expired/refused are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:264| mutually exclusive states (construction obligation, registered with the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:265| ruling). Exhausting them obligates
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:266| the implementation to terminate issuance in an **explicit refusal, durably
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:267| recorded; reporting is a delivery obligation to be registered in
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:268| Amendment 3** — a first-class protocol outcome, not an error path. N is a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:269| protocol constant ratified at Band 0 exit alongside δ, ε, k, and S
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:270| (working default **N = 3**; per the A2.1 clock-roles ruling each
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:271| attempt's lifecycle is wall-governed through δ + S, so N attempts give
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:272| a **nominal lifecycle budget** of N × (δ + S) — twelve days at the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:273| working defaults δ = 72 h, S = 24 h — a nominal budget, not a proven
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:274| wall-clock bound on the process; see the model note).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:275| [**Note:** refusal as a separate delivery obligation added 2026/07/21 per
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:276| review process/response.]
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:277| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:278| Model note: P5c's `MaxAttempts` is hereby promoted from a state-space
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:279| bound to protocol semantics. The refusal state is modeled by **atomic
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:280| entry** (the transition expiring the final attempt's window records the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:281| refusal in the same step; checked, with a broken companion red on
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:282| exactly the silent-deadlock invariant among the checked set — review
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:283| archived in
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:284| `docs/reviews/2026-07-20-codex-p5c-refusal-review.md`). Scope of proof
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:285| versus contract, per that review: the model proves the *conditional
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:286| safety half* — the refusal state is entered atomically and latches; it
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:287| does not prove the crossing occurs (no fairness is assumed), so
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:288| **termination is a contract obligation on the implementation, not a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:289| proven liveness property**. The unbounded "eventually ships" claim
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:290| likewise remains explicitly unproven. Storage durability, retrievability,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:291| and reporting of the refusal record are implementation/handoff
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:292| obligations to be registered in Amendment 3 (planned, not yet in force).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:293| [**Note:** model-note scope split added 2026/07/21, same review cycle.]
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:294| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:295| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:296| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:297| ## A2.4 Anchor identity and declared-time confinement
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:298| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:299| - **A receipt's anchor is the proof it ships with.** A shipped receipt
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:300|   contains exactly one anchor proof (the OTS proof over its canonical
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:301|   bytes) together with the anchor transaction's id, which serves as the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:302|   **identity handle** binding the receipt to its chain transaction. (An
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:303|   identity/coherence handle, not by itself a retrieval mechanism:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:304|   txid → transaction *availability* requires chain access — a node,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:305|   index, or archive — which is an implementation obligation under the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:306|   evidence discipline, joining A2.2's; the hash argument below covers
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:307|   identity, not availability.) Verification evaluates the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:308|   shipped proof and no other; an anchor not shipped inside a receipt
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:309|   confers **no validity, no priority, and no claimed anchor identity**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:310|   in verification or dispute — in particular, a discarded attempt's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:311|   transaction confirming later confers nothing toward any of the three.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:312|   (This confines *protocol standing*; it does not render such artifacts
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:313|   inadmissible as *evidence* — e.g., of issuer conduct — in dispute
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:314|   processes. The stand-alone anchor-standing property is Amendment 3's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:315|   to register; this clause is written to underdetermine it, not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:316|   pre-empt it.) The handle
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:317|   requires no new assumption: a txid is the double-SHA-256 of the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:318|   transaction, so txid → transaction → committed bytes rests on the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:319|   SHA-256 resistance already cited in Layer 2, and the OTS proof's merkle
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:320|   path binds the anchored bytes to the block independently of the handle.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:321|   (The txid necessarily lives in the bundle outside the signed bytes — the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:322|   anchor is computed over those bytes, so the txid exists only after them;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:323|   the wrapper discipline of P7 makes the containment tamper-evident.)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:324| - **Declared times are existed-by claims, and only that.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:325|   `declared_issue_time` asserts the artifact existed by that time;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:326|   re-declaration on re-issue moves it forward, which weakens and never
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:327|   falsifies. **No verifier policy, and no downstream marketplace rule, may
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:328|   order competing receipts by declared time** (first-to-file semantics):
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:329|   the re-issue mechanism necessarily gives the issuer discretion over
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:330|   declared times within the retry schedule, and priority ordering would
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:331|   convert that discretion into a manipulation surface. This confinement is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:332|   a design commitment in the P6 monotonicity style — assumed by the model,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:333|   enforced by policy, deliberately not filed under Layer 2.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:334|

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:340|   the A2.2 conjunct under the existing verifier-owns-tolerances
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:341|   discipline; a broken companion omitting the conjunct must accept the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:342|   the chain-late subclass — witnessing exactly the gap A2.0 records.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:356|   bridge **registers the absence** of a lifecycle guard in its `Ship` —

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:363| ## A2.6 What changed, and what did not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:364| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:365| This amendment **strengthens** P5 (a third strict conjunct), **adds**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:366| obligations (header evidence and authentication for stateless
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:367| confirmation checking, the attempt bound with recorded refusal —
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:368| reporting to be registered in Amendment 3, per A2.3 — the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:369| anchor-identity rule, the declared-time confinement commitment, new
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:370| conformance-vector cases), **registers** a correction that narrows
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:371| what the strict rule may be claimed to protect, **rules** the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:372| clock-roles question (chain time governs evidence, wall time governs
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:373| the attempt lifecycle with operational slack S — a new constant
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:374| joining δ, ε, k, N at Band 0 exit; the opportunity guarantee is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:375| conditional on the observable lag, and no hard backward-lag assumption
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:376| is registered), and **withdraws** the two-receipts closure claim,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:377| re-registering it as an Amendment 3 obligation.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:378| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:379| Stated in A1.1's terms, exactly: no A1.2 property is weakened; no proof
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:380| is demoted to an assumption; no declared A1.3 adversary capability is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:381| excluded; the construction remains dual-signature plus temporal anchor.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:382| The A1.1 falsifier is not triggered. In ordinary language, behavior
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:383| does change, and this amendment does not pretend otherwise: the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:384| permissive reading's acceptances are excluded by ratifying strict, a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:385| refusal outcome and attempt bound now exist, exactly one shipped anchor
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:386| carries protocol standing, and declared-time priority policies are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:387| prohibited — all registered strengthenings or confinements. One
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:388| acknowledged cost: the new evidence obligation adds an `UNVERIFIABLE`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:389| path (headers unavailable) where pre-A2 verification could return a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:390| verdict — an availability cost of the strengthened check, carried by
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:391| the P4 partition, not a weakening of any registered property. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:392| bands, hypotheses, hard invariants, and division of labor are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-2.md:393| unchanged.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:59| ## A3.1 What Tessera attests: the identity boundary
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:60| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:61| **Registered (author-ruled 2026-07-28, adopted 68b581c):** Tessera
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:62| attests the **identity of the framed bytes presented at an issuance
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:63| event** — computational identity under the declared construction and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:64| assumptions — and nothing more. Outside the attestation: meaning,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:65| truth, intended use, future interpretation, and the metaphysical
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:66| identity of the payload's referent.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:67| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:68| 1. **Replay.** Re-presenting a genuinely issued package preserves
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:69|    identity; P1 permits it. Whether a replay is appropriate in a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:70|    transaction is policy belonging to a context that must supply
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:71|    transaction identity, nonce, audience, or purpose. Tessera does not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:72|    invent that context. P1's symbolic statement is accordingly
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:73|    **existential issuance-event authenticity** (a non-injective
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:74|    correspondence), with replay and context scoped to caller policy.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:75| 2. **The headline precision repair (Sol finding 1).** The H0 headline
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:76|    "altering any part requires solving a computationally hard problem"
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:77|    is corrected to its operative form, which already coexists in the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:78|    pre-registration (§2, Layer 1): alteration is trivial; **surviving
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:79|    verification over altered bytes is what is hard** — no transition
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:80|    leads to an accepted receipt over altered bytes. This is a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:81|    claim-correspondence repair, not a construction change or weakening
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:82|    under A1.1: the operative form is the checkable claim the models
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:83|    already use.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:84| 3. **Coverage map obligation.** The repository shall carry a coverage
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:85|    map from package component to defending property — bytes → P1,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:86|    signature set → P2, type/wrapper → P7, manifest authority → P10,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:87|    anchor identity → A2.4, framing → P8 — **with open cells visible**.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:88|    An honest map with gaps beats an implied completeness.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:89| 4. **The relying-party story is a required artifact.** One page: a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:90|    person holds a receipt and a verdict; these are the decisions they
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:91|    may and may not make on it. It opens with the can/does-not-establish
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:92|    list recorded verbatim in the 2026-07-28 ruling doc ("Tessera can
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:93|    establish: this valid package reconstructs the same framed bytes
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:94|    recorded at issuance. Tessera does not establish: the payload is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:95|    true; the issuer understood it; …"). Registered as a Band 0 exit
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:96|    artifact.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:97| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:98| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:99| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:100| ## A3.2 Evidence floors: the A1.2.1 tightening
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:101| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:102| **Adopted core (2026-08-07, commit 68b581c — adoption route (b): the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:103| minimal requirement adopted, its normative security boundary supplied
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:104| here while the realizing mechanism remains open):**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:105| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:106| > Every valid verdict requires at least one continuous accepted
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:107| > evidentiary chain per independently evaluated attestation layer;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:108| > redundant paths may be waived, but the final complete chain may not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:109| > be.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:110| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:111| **Normative expansion (the mapping clause).** "Continuous accepted
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:112| evidentiary chain" means **exactly** the following witness chain, and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:113| nothing weaker:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:114| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:115| > accepted external authority evidence
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:116| > → the exact authority statement consumed from the manifest
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:117| > → issuer identity and signing key
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:118| > → proof of possession **by that same key**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:119| > → accepted signature verifying under that key
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:120| > → the exact framed bytes
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:121| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:122| Both forms are registered — the sentence is the property statement the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:123| relying-party story and the written proof carry; the chain is the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:124| proof obligation the capstone (§A3.3) discharges. The mapping clause
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:125| binds them: neither may drift from the other. (Author ruling
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:126| 2026-08-07: the two formulations are complementary altitudes, not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:127| rivals; the rationale — report what was done, defer interpretation to
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:128| future verifiers and their risk tolerance — is on the record in the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:129| 2026-07-28 ruling doc.)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:130| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:131| **Why linked, not counted (registered rationale).** Counted floors
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:132| ("≥1 accepted signature AND ≥1 accepted external evidence") admit the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:133| two-worlds attack: evidence supports manifest M′ while the accepted
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:134| signature claims authority from M; both counters pass with the chain
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:135| broken — the aTLS genus. And without any floor, the model's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:136| IssuanceEvent correspondence becomes privileged historical knowledge
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:137| unavailable to a real verifier: the proof would be of the wrong model.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:138| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:139| **Interaction with the A1.2.1 waiver lattice (tightening, stated
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:140| exactly):**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:141| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:142| 1. A1.2.1's waivable item "accepting fewer than all external
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:143|    manifest-authority evidences (P10)" is tightened to: **fewer, but
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:144|    never zero** — redundant members of the A1.5 evidence set may be
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:145|    waived; the final complete chain may not be broken or eliminated.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:146| 2. **Unavailability is not waiver.** If every external authority
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:147|    evidence for a layer is unavailable, unsupported, or otherwise
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:148|    unperformable, the layer's verdict is `UNVERIFIABLE` — never
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:149|    `VALID_DEGRADED`. Evidence that is present and whose validation is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:150|    performed but fails yields `INVALID`. The P4 partition applies
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:151|    inside the floor exactly as A1.2.1 already requires of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:152|    non-waivable checks.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:153| 3. **Proof of possession is chain-internal:** the possession proof
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:154|    must be by the same key whose signature is accepted (consistent
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:155|    with A1.5's rule that the self-signature is never an authority
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:156|    channel). An existential self-signature by another key in a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:157|    multi-key manifest does not close the chain.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:158| 4. **Per-layer quantification.** A wrapped package's inner and outer
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:159|    attestations are separately typed signed objects (P7); each layer
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:160|    contributing to a returned valid verdict carries its own complete
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:161|    chain, evaluated independently. The base assessment reports each
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:162|    layer's result without replacement by an aggregate judgment; a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:163|    higher-level relying-party policy may consume those results. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:164|    proof obligation quantifies over every contributing layer.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:165| 5. **No change to P4's partition.** The floors bound entry into the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:166|    two VALID states; they add no states and alter no verdict
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:167|    semantics. P4 remains correct but incomplete by abstraction.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:168| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:169| ### A3.2.1 The chain's first-link invariant
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:170| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:171| A1 §A1.5's two external authority evidences (the DNSSEC chain snapshot
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:172| and the anchored repository publication, both archived in the bundle)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:173| publish **issuer-key fingerprints**, not manifest digests. Registering
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:174| an exact-manifest-digest mechanism here would both narrow the design
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:175| space prematurely and risk a self-reference if the hashed manifest
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:176| itself carries the archived evidence.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:177| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:178| The requirement is therefore stated at the security boundary:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:179| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:180| > External authority evidence must unambiguously bind the exact
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:181| > authority statement the verifier consumes. Two manifests that differ
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:182| > in any authority-relevant fact must not be supportable by the same
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:183| > evidence; differences explicitly declared non-authoritative may remain
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:184| > outside that binding.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:185| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:186| The mechanism spike may realize this with a separately hashed manifest
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:187| core, an exact authorized tuple, or another construction. It must name
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:188| which manifest facts are authority-relevant and carry a broken companion
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:189| in which two authority-distinct manifests share evidence; the consuming
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:190| linkage query must fail. The mechanism is not registered until the spike
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:191| has supplied that evidence.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:192| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:193| `[AUTHOR DECISION — ratified - 2026-08-08]` **Override of adopted text,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:194| named.** The adopted record (the 07-28 ruling, Ruling 2 item 5)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:195| docketed exactly two options — digest publication or authorized
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:196| tuple — required A3 to choose between them, and stated that the exact
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:197| links are resolved in A3 before the spike. This section declines both
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:198| options in favor of the boundary invariant above and moves mechanism
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:199| selection after the spike. Rationale: each docketed option is a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:200| premature narrowing, and the digest option additionally risks
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:201| self-reference (verified against A1 §A1.5: the manifest carries the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:202| archived authority evidences). The invariant with its two-worlds
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:203| broken companion preserves the falsifiable content the docketed fork
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:204| existed to protect. The same ruling covers the chain's second link:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:205| this amendment's "exact authority statement consumed from the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:206| manifest" supersedes the ruling doc's "exact manifest" link, and the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:207| spike targets the chain as registered here.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:208| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:209| ---
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:210| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:211| ## A3.3 The symbolic suite and the capstone gate
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:212| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:213| **Registered obligation (requirement level; ruled in dialogue
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:214| 2026-07-28, restated and adopted 2026-08-07, commit 68b581c):**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:215| per-property ProVerif models over a shared theory library; every model
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:216| carries an explicit assumes-from-elsewhere ledger holding **two entry
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:217| kinds** — dischargeable cross-model obligations, and exposed Layer 2
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:218| assumptions.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:219| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:220| > Band 0 exit is gated on a capstone composition context in which
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:221| > every ledgered **cross-model** assumption — a fact one symbolic
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:222| > model assumes and another must establish — is discharged by a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:223| > machine-checked producer query and carries a broken companion that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:224| > **fails the query consuming the severed link**. Layer 2 assumptions
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:225| > (cryptographic primitive security, historical trust-anchor
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:226| > correctness, chain availability, implementation fidelity,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:227| > operational independence of authority channels) are explicitly
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:228| > exposed and unclaimed in the ledger — never discharged, never
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:229| > silently absorbed. Any termination-forced scoping is named in-module
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:230| > and disposed by amendment discipline, never silently.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:231| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:232| **Ledger conservation rule** (each entry records at least): consumer
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:233| property/query; assumed fact; producer module and event/query (or
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:234| "Layer 2 — unclaimed"); the shared term establishing correspondence;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:235| adversary capabilities at the join; and any residual Layer 2
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:236| assumption. A cross-model entry additionally records the broken
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:237| mutation and expected failing query; those fields do not pretend to
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:238| discharge a Layer 2 entry.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:239| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:240| **The mechanism spike precedes the suite scaffold** (design adopted
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:241| 2026-08-07): representative complexity first — the §A3.2 witness
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:242| chain, the structural worst case — ablating toward the break point on
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:243| failure; the drafted ledger interface is the spike's scaffolding (one
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:244| artifact); per-query timebox declared before running with three named
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:245| outcomes (query violation = counterexample; timeout = mechanism
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:246| failure, not property evidence; termination = evidence for the checked
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:247| abstraction only); predictions registered before running. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:248| transcription-pattern capstone is a non-binding implementation
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:249| candidate, subject to the spike.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:250| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:251| **Additional model obligations from this amendment:** the capstone's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:252| linkage query proves the §A3.2 chain (the links, not just
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:253| cardinalities, per-layer); the P4 model's unknown-algorithm transition
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:254| (§A3.6) carries its own companion; every symbolic lemma carries a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:255| prose mapping to its registered property (standing rule, reaffirmed).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-3.md:256|
