docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:29| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:30| ## What this amendment establishes
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:31| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:32| **The claim.** V1 is a dual-signed timestamp notary for Tessera's own domain, `wamason.com`. Provided the service's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:33| signing capability was not misused within the key's window, a V1 receipt lets anyone, with no network and no help
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:34| from Tessera, check four things: that particular bytes were presented to the Tessera V1 service; that both of the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:35| service's keys signed them; that two channels (DNSSEC, and a signed, timestamped git commit) said those keys
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:36| belonged to that domain and were allowed to issue during a stated window; and that the bytes *and both signatures*
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:37| existed no later than a time T fixed by Bitcoin. Against the window, the declared issue time is not earlier than
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:38| its not-before, and the verified chain-time T is not later than its not-after.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:39| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:40| **The adversary.** Anyone who tampers with, forges, strips, swaps, replays, reattributes or backdates receipts;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:41| anyone who captures authority-channel credentials while signing capability stays uncompromised (A8.3's sense of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:42| capture); and anyone who steals a key, gains signing capability, or breaks a signature algorithm *after* a receipt
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:43| was anchored. Against these, V1's verdicts hold under the registered cryptographic, key-use and chain assumptions.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:44| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:45| **The boundaries.** V1 does not say who submitted the bytes or what they mean. It does not evaluate revocation, or
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:46| whether an algorithm or key was still safe when it signed. It offers no standing, renewal, wrappers or degraded
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:47| verification, and no lower time bound or priority. It does not hold against an adversary who holds signing
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:48| capability for every required slot inside the window (capture of the issuing AWS account confers it for both
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:49| slots, C3); against whole-author-sphere capture (R-2.15); or against breaks of SHA-256, OpenTimestamps, Bitcoin
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:50| history deeper than k, or, in git's links, a second-preimage break of SHA-1 or attacker influence over committed
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:51| contents; or against compromise of the verifier's distribution, meaning its release and the trust configuration
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:52| compiled into it (an explicit external assumption, A9.5). Both keys are under one controller.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:53|

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:98| - *Key lifetimes.* The author: *"these become product side questions and guarantees. One way to protect keys is to
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:99|   limit their lifetime. That doesn't prevent compromise, but it does mitigate the potential damage."* The single
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:100|   window of at most 90 days (A9.6) is an owner decision implementing this.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:101| - *Signer preference.* The author: *"I think we should build our V1 with a PQ implementation"* (2026-10-12). The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:102|   conditional hybrid (A9.6) records this as his stated preference, not as a claim requirement.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:110| ## A9.1 V1's success definition, claim, profile and scenario mapping — OWNER DECISION (Q1), implementing A and C
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:111| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:112| **Success definition** (`docs/V1-SCHEDULE.md`, adopted here). V1 succeeds when:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:113| 1. An organisation can obtain a receipt, at a stated cost and latency, asserting that *these exact bytes were
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:114|    presented, signed by key K whose authority is evidenced by named channels, no later than time T*.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:115| 2. A relying party can verify that claim without Tessera running and without the authors' help. From V1's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:116|    documentation alone, it reaches the safe decision on every case of the registered mapping below, including the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:117|    cases whose answer is "not established": **zero unsafe accepts; false rejects only on d2 and h** (AUTHOR
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:118|    DECISION C; this replaces V1-SCHEDULE's "the prototype's scenario set"). *Evidence:* one human tester (n = 1,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:119|    recorded under the pseudonym "Aki Doe") who meets the independence criteria of `docs/V1-TESTER-BRIEF.md`: a CS
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:120|    background; no knowledge of attestation, timestamping, blockchains or this project; has not discussed Tessera
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:121|    with the author; and no help from the project during the test. The evidence is stated as one tester's result,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:122|    not as a result about relying parties in general.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:123| 3. V1 ships by 4 December 2026, or the project stops pursuing V1 by explicit decision at that point.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:124|

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:127| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:128| **Claim.** *Conditional on the registered cryptographic and key-use assumptions, a V1 receipt lets anyone holding it
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:129| establish, without Tessera, that the attested content was presented to the Tessera V1 service, whose own domain is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:130| D; that each of the service's two keys K = {K_kms, K_gpg} signed its own frame binding that content; that two named
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:131| channels authenticated these keys for D, with an issuance window the git channel committed, in chain order, before
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:132| the receipt's anchor, at the stated evidence times; that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:133| the signed frames and their exact signatures existed no later than T; and that the declared issue time is not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:134| earlier than the window's not-before and the verified chain-time T is not later than its not-after. Effective
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:135| revocation and historical algorithm and key safety are not evaluated, and the receipt attests neither the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:136| submitter nor the content's meaning. The verdict is typed and says what was not established.*

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:253| ## A9.4 Revocation and historical security: not evaluated — AUTHOR DECISION B; OWNER DECISION for historical security. A weakening under A1 §A1.1.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:254| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:255| - **Weakened.** For V1 bundles, `VALID_STRICT` evaluates neither P6 condition: `key_authorized(declared_issue_time)`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:256|   against effective revocation, and no revocation effective at or before `max(anchor_time, declared_issue_time)`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:257|   (A4.3). Every report carries `revocation: NOT_EVALUATED` next to the verdict. *Why:* under the registered text
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:258|   a verifier that cannot evaluate revocation returns `UNVERIFIABLE` for every receipt.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:259| - **Historical security.** Every report carries `historical_security: NOT_EVALUATED`. V1 does not evaluate whether
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:260|   a signing algorithm or key was safe when it signed. The documentation names what a later examiner must supply:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:261|   an authenticated safe-before cutoff per algorithm and per key, compared against T with A2.1's chain-time
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:262|   uncertainty (CODEX-REVIEW 8). A surviving PQ attestation slot prevents a P-256 break alone from supplying every
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:263|   required attestation signature. An ML-DSA-65 cutoff and the classical slot remain; historical authority, per-key
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:264|   custody and continuing commitment and history security remain assumptions. A PQ slot never removes the need for
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:265|   a theft cutoff.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:266| - **Issuer duty.** The V1 issuer never re-authorizes a key (R-5.24). V1 defines no revocation publication.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:267| - **Contract for later verifiers.** Missing status capture does not by itself invalidate a V1 receipt. A later
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:268|   verifier given a V1 bundle, under the same governing V1 specification, policy, trust configuration and other
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:269|   declared inputs, returns the same verdict and values in the stable field set (A9.1), and never a weaker verdict
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:270|   because of missing status capture. **Verdict stability** (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-13, `docs/V1-V2-COMPATIBILITY.md`): a V1
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:271|   bundle is always evaluated under its signed `common.spec`. Trust configurations are append-only (A9.5), so a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:272|   later configuration cannot turn a V1 verdict into `UNVERIFIABLE` by dropping a KSK, a header pin or a repository
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:273|   key. Later algorithm policy enters the separate historical-security assessment only as an authenticated
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:274|   per-algorithm cutoff compared with T, with A2.1's chain-time uncertainty; authenticated per-key theft cutoffs are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:275|   assessed separately there as well. It never overwrites the V1 verdict or its six stable fields, whether T is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:276|   before, equal to or after a cutoff. A receipt whose T precedes an algorithm's cutoff keeps its V1 verdict; that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:277|   comparison alone does not establish historical safety. Later revocation, standing, renewal and historical-security
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:278|   results are reported separately, together with later adverse evidence. The V1 verdict continues to apply the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:279|   algorithm policy registered for its governing V1 specification, including its original malformed, unsupported and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:280|   prohibited-identifier cases (A9.7 row 29). This
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:281|   binds later verifiers and profiles; it is not a property V1 itself demonstrates. **This is not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:282|   non-repudiation.** Evidence (C7): for an otherwise valid, fully performable bundle where missing status capture
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:283|   is the sole difference, a companion returning `INVALID` or `UNVERIFIABLE` must go red.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:284| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:285| ## A9.5 Strict-only, standalone; the receipt anchor — OWNER DECISIONS 2026-10-12 except where marked
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:286| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:287| - **Dispatch.** Out-of-profile input gives `UNVERIFIABLE / OUT_OF_PROFILE` at dispatch; A4.2 precedence holds inside.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:288| - **H1a's suite.** Forge, tamper, backdate, break-chain, strip-one-signature, out-of-profile, the A9.1 mapping.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:289|   Degradation and wrapper instances move to their capabilities.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:290| - **Receipt anchor.** OTS stamps `SHA256(A_sig)`, tag `tessera-v1/receipt-anchor-sig`, which commits to both frames
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:291|   and their exact detached signatures in manifest slot order (ENCODING-V1 §5, D-8, D-14). The verifier verifies the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:292|   committed signature bytes only. The frame-only layout is withdrawn, with no fallback.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:293| - **Issue order (D-15).** Fix manifest and metadata; build frames; sign; verify; **freeze** the signature bytes;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:294|   **stamp** `A_sig` (one stamp per receipt, R-3.42); obtain confirmation; ship. A signature made after T cannot fit
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:295|   the anchor. A retry that changes any committed byte needs a fresh stamp. Signature identifiers stay independent
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:296|   of signature bytes; the anchor digest may commit to them; nothing is normalized after stamping.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:297| - **Git stamp target (D-16).** The git channel's OTS stamp targets the **signed commit's object id**, never a tree,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:298|   blob or unsigned commit. The verifier recomputes the id, verifies `gpgsig`, follows commit→tree→blob, and checks
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:299|   the stamped id. SHA-1 linkage remains a stated residual. The git evidence names its object format, and V1
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:300|   accepts only `sha1`: the key-assertion repository stays in SHA-1 format at a host that supports it, whatever
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:301|   git's default becomes (the author, 2026-10-13: Git 3 moves to SHA-256 in 2027; GitHub does not support it).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:302|   The pre-freeze bundle schema (V1-PROFILE §2.1, G-26) defines the git-evidence member `object_format` as the string
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:303|   `"sha1"`. It is an evidence descriptor, not a new signed-frame or key-publication field. A missing descriptor gives
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:304|   `UNVERIFIABLE / GIT_OBJECT_FORMAT_MISSING`; an unsupported value gives `UNVERIFIABLE / GIT_OBJECT_FORMAT`. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:305|   verifier recomputes the SHA-1 object ids from the raw commit/tree/blob bytes, so this descriptor cannot override
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:306|   their interpretation. For V1 the stamped message is exactly 40 lowercase ASCII hex digits naming the signed commit
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:307|   id followed by one LF byte. The schema/check specification and conformance cases are fixed before the 30 Oct
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:308|   profile freeze; no P8 frame or key-publication vector changes are required.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:309| - **Root-KSK rule.** The root DNSKEY set is valid at the snapshot's anchored time **if some trusted KSK whose reliance
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:310|   period contains that time validates it**. Each KSK entry records signing-start, signing-end and a sourced reliance
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:311|   lifetime L, with the reliance interval [signing-start, signing-end + L]. L is the registered acceptance-policy
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:312|   value derived from the cited root DNSKEY RRSIG validity evidence; a largest observed lifetime is labelled observed,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:313|   not asserted to be a proven global maximum. A candidate must also satisfy cryptographic validation and the selected
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:314|   RRSIG's inception/expiration checks at the snapshot's own verified anchored time. This extension permits authentic
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:315|   pre-retirement evidence anchored later; it does not establish that signing occurred before retirement. A thief of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:316|   a retired KSK can manufacture eligible root evidence during the extension. Exposure is bounded by the reliance
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:317|   endpoint in snapshot chain time, not by a finite UTC duration under A2.1. Historical authority-key safety and the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:318|   continuing anchor/history assumptions remain necessary and are not evaluated by V1. **AUTHOR ADOPTED, 2026-10-13**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:319|   (`docs/reviews/v1-profile/` F2; kind CORRECT: the withdrawn cutoff claimed a protection DNSSEC itself does not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:320|   supply, since resolvers accept a retired KSK's signatures until they expire). The author: *"I'd argue that the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:321|   'narrowing of protection' wasn't a real narrowing, it was us admitting the real level of protection given the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:322|   constraints of the project."* The rule is existential and order-independent: a candidate that fails is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:323|   informational, and the result is computed once, after every eligible key has been tried (F1). A trusted KSK that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:324|   is published but did not sign is informational, never a failure. The trust configuration records signing and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:325|   reliance periods separately from publication and revocation dates.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:326| - **Trust-configuration authority** (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-14, after `docs/reviews/spec-sufficiency/` F04). The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:327|   trust configuration is authenticated independently of the bundle and of both authority-channel credentials. Each
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:328|   verifier release compiles in the hash of its configuration. Releases are authenticated by a key that neither the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:329|   DNS credential, the repository key nor the issuing AWS account can use; the dated custody record names that key
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:330|   and its access boundary. Capture of an authority-channel credential grants no ability to sign a release,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:331|   authorize a configuration hash, or replace the compiled trust root. CI is not the authenticity check. Compromise
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:332|   of the release key is distribution compromise, a stated boundary.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:333| - **Trust configuration is append-only** (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-13). Trust configuration entries are append-only: KSKs, header
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:334|   pins and repository keys are never removed, and finalized period endpoints never change. Repository trust entries
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:335|   name D, the key and an inclusive signing interval; the git assertion passes this trust check if some configured
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:336|   entry for D verifies gpgsig and its interval contains the signed commit's own verified anchored time. Repository
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:337|   entries have no KSK-style reliance extension. Unknown material cannot establish this required check. Append-only
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:338|   extensions preserve previously usable trust witnesses; newly covered evidence can improve an earlier UNVERIFIABLE
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:339|   result. Exact stable-field identity remains the contract for identical declared inputs. Closing an open period must
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:340|   not retrospectively exclude evidence previously accepted under that entry; the pre-freeze configuration records the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:341|   endpoint/update convention explicitly. **Rollover control:** a snapshot taken while one trusted KSK is published but not signing must pass
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:342|   (SPIKE-REPORT, KSK-2024 re-capture; without it every receipt from 2026-10-11 would be falsely rejected).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:343| - **Custody.** V1 offers no renewal. Long-horizon validity depends on the dependency manifest and on the holder
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:344|   keeping the exact bytes (a mirror that alters a signature byte breaks its copy, CODEX-REVIEW 5).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:345| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:346| ## A9.6 Signers, the issuance window, and what they guarantee — OWNER DECISIONS 2026-10-12
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:347| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:348| **Signer profile, conditional.** The hybrid records the author's stated preference (2026-10-12: *"I think we
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:349| should build our V1 with a PQ implementation"*). It is not a claim requirement: no sentence of C1–C7 needs it. It
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:350| is the first item cut if 30 Oct slips (A9.2).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:351| - **If the hybrid spike passes by 21 Oct:** slot `kms` is AWS KMS **ML-DSA-65** (FIPS 204, in KMS's HSMs), raw
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:352|   signature per ENCODING-V1 §5.2 rule R; slot `gpg` is **P-256** OpenPGP (rule O), signed by a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:353|   non-exportable, hardware-protected key in a separate technical key-custody domain outside the issuing AWS account
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:354|   (*slot-2 custody*, below), pulling from a queue with no inbound path.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:355|   One pair algorithm identifier names both slot schemes (`common.alg` is shared, R-3.12). This adopts for V1 the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:356|   hybrid A3 §A3.6 deferred.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:357| - *Pass condition* (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-12, fixed after an offline pre-spike, `prototype/spike-pq/`, which the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:358|   author commits, and before the KMS spike):
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:359|   - the pair identifier is registered with its mode and context;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:360|   - the mixed-format pairing passes R-3.12 and P3's model;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:361|   - a real KMS ML-DSA-65 signature over a V1 frame (external μ above 4 KB) verifies offline in two
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:362|     implementations;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:363|   - a real P-256 signature from the `gpg` slot as deployed verifies offline;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:364|   - the full selected byte profile is specified and tested: attestation **and manifest-possession** verification
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:365|     for both slots, slot key and fingerprint encodings, key-use assumptions appropriate to each slot (PROOF's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:366|     OpenPGP type-0x00 assumption does not describe the raw ML-DSA slot), and golden and rejection vectors with an
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:367|     agreement run for rule R.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:368| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:369|   All of it by 21 Oct, or the fallback is taken automatically. The offline pre-spike is feasibility evidence only
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:370|   (approximate JCS, no real KMS, a bare SLH-DSA portable slot rather than this pair); it does not satisfy the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:371|   condition.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:372| - **Registered fallback, otherwise:** both slots classical P-256 under P4': KMS-backed OpenPGP P-256, plus the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:373|   `gpg` slot under slot-2 custody. The signature-inclusive anchor and the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:374|   issuance window are retained unchanged.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:375| - **Slot-2 custody (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-13).** The `gpg`-slot key is generated non-exportable in hardware outside
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:376|   the issuing AWS account: a token on author-controlled hardware, or an HSM-backed key at a provider other than AWS.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:377|   The owner chooses between them, and records the choice, dated, in the profile before the 30 Oct freeze. The choice
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:378|   takes into account measured token throughput and issuance availability, and the author's concern about scalability
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:379|   (2026-10-13: *"Scalability is a real, legitimate, concern"*). Either choice satisfies the author's key-protection
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:380|   requirement (A9.0) and leaves C1–C7 unchanged. The key's authority is evidenced by the key-publication record in
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:381|   both cases.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:382|   - *Policy signer.* In either custody option, a queue-pulling policy signer outside the issuing AWS account
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:383|     validates the complete V1 frame and enforces the declared-time check using its own clock before requesting a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:384|     signature. The issuing AWS account can enqueue frames but cannot invoke the slot-2 key directly, change that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:385|     policy or clock, or obtain the policy signer's key-use credentials. The slot-2 key is dedicated to V1 tagged
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:386|     type-0x00 documents (attestation and manifest-possession). The dated custody record names this enforcement
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:387|     boundary and its access policy. Non-exportability protects against key export, not signing misuse through the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:388|     permitted queue path.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:389|   - *Deadline.* For the hybrid, the final custody implementation must have completed the deployed-slot
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:390|     pass-condition evidence by 21 Oct. The owner may defer selection until before 30 Oct only among custody
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:391|     implementations that each met that deadline; otherwise the registered fallback is taken. A custody selection
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:392|     changes neither rule O nor any claim, pass condition or exit obligation.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:393|   - *Limit.* Separate technical custody does not imply independent availability, independent signing fates,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:394|     separate control or independent approval of content; C3 applies to both options.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:395| - **Branch registration.** If the hybrid branch is taken, the owner registers, before the 30 Oct freeze, a dated
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:396|   **branch-registration supplement** bounded to the pair identifier with its mode and context, the ENCODING-V1 §5.2
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:397|   edit for rule R, and the completed pass-condition evidence, naming the exact ENCODING-V1 and specification
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:398|   hashes. The signing-commit baseline plus that supplement governs the hybrid branch. This amendment authorizes
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:399|   that supplement and nothing else in it; it needs no further amendment and no further author approval. Either
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:400|   way, the owner records the branch taken, dated, in ENCODING-V1 §5.2 and the profile before the freeze.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:401| - **Declared-time check (issuer side, not a verifier rule).** The `gpg`-slot signer refuses a frame whose
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:402|   `declared_issue_time` is outside ε (A9.2) of its own clock. Whoever controls the queue (an AWS takeover) still
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:403|   has signing capability for both slots; the check limits that to minting at the current time. For an HSM-backed key,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:404|   this refusal is enforced by the policy signer, not by the HSM's generic signing API. Separation of control stays a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:405|   V2 driver (A9.3).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:406| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:407| **Issuance window.** The key-publication record carries `issuance-not-before` and `issuance-not-after`, **both
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:408| mandatory**, identical in DNS and the git blob (ENCODING-V1 §7, §7.1, D-17).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:409| - **Registered invariant: `issuance-not-after − issuance-not-before ≤ 90 days`** (a record that violates it is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:410|   rejected, `DNS_WINDOW_LENGTH`). This amendment registers the first issuance window only; it does not yet
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:411|   authorize successor issuance. A future sequential-replacement registration may retain the frozen V1 byte/check
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:412|   profile: the same DNS owner and git path, new keys, and a new window with next.not-before > previous.not-after (both
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:413|   endpoints are inclusive). Each receipt carries its own historical snapshot and commit. Multiple TXT records at the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:414|   required owner fail `DNS_RRSET`; a substituted per-key owner name fails `DNS_OWNER`. The V1 verifier checks each
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:415|   receipt's window, not non-overlap between receipts. Before successor issuance, the owner records a dated rotation
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:416|   registration naming the two-window positive/negative vectors and the model, checked property and result
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:417|   establishing the intended issuance invariant. This future rotation evidence is not added to the 30 Oct
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:418|   first-window gate. Without that registration, issuance stops at the first window's end.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:419| - **Verifier rule (C4).** A receipt is `INVALID / ISSUANCE_WINDOW` unless the declared issue time is not earlier
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:420|   than not-before and the verified chain-time T is not later than not-after, with T as registered and no margin.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:421|   T itself is not compared with not-before.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:422| - **Issuer invariant.** An attempt whose T would exceed not-after is not shipped. The stop margin, the window's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:423|   actual dates and the rotation plan are operating numbers, not registered (`docs/V1-OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md`).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:424| - A published window cannot be shortened; detection changes no V1 verdict.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:425| - The relying-party documentation states: `ISSUANCE_WINDOW` can result from presenting a later proof; ask the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:426|   holder for the issuer's original proof.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:427| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:428| **Exit.** The exit procedure is not part of this instrument; it is in the operations runbook. No V1 verifier rule
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:429| consults any end-of-issuance statement (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-12).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:430| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:431| **The two product guarantees, stated conditionally (CODEX-REVIEW 7).** Guarantee 2 is the C4 window rule, stated
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:432| as a property; a finding against it is a C4 finding for the closure rule (A9.2). Guarantee 1 is not computed.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:433| 1. **Past receipts survive later compromise.** A receipt whose exact signatures are anchored by T cannot have
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:434|    signatures manufactured after an adversary gains signing capability for every required slot substituted into
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:435|    it, while SHA-256, the OTS commitment and the pinned chain history stay secure. Its historical authenticity also
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:436|    needs the signing and key-use assumptions to have held before T, authentic historical authority, and no relevant
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:437|    compromise before T; V1 does not evaluate these (`historical_security: NOT_EVALUATED`). A later key theft or
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:438|    algorithm break does not by itself invalidate such a receipt. It does not cure earlier theft, unauthorized
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:439|    signing before T, misissuance or whole-author-sphere capture, and does not prove that the issuer itself obtained
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:440|    the stamp or issued the bundle uniquely.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:441| 2. **Signing capability mints only inside the window, in chain time.** Even signing capability for every required
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:442|    slot cannot make a receipt pass V1 with verified T after its authenticated not-after, under continuing anchor
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:443|    and history assumptions and provided the authority channels are not also captured (republishing a window is a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:444|    new authority event; whole capture is R-2.15). Translating this into a finite UTC cutoff requires an additional,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:445|    explicit backward-skew assumption that V1 does not establish: A2.1 registers no finite bound on B − C, and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:446|    neither ε nor S is one. Inside the window, such an adversary mints receipts that pass; the window cannot be
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:447|    shortened, and detecting misuse is the B(ii) add-on, not V1.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:448| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:449| **C3 non-claim.** The two keys are *separate technical failure domains under a single controller; no separation of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:450| control or independent fates.* The `gpg` signer signs frames delivered by the AWS-side issuer, so capture of the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:451| issuing account confers signing capability for both slots; the non-exportable key prevents key export, not misuse.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:452| With the hybrid the slots differ in algorithm (lattice and elliptic curve) and custody (AWS KMS and the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:453| slot-2 custody); under the fallback a P-256 break defeats both slots.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:454|

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:519| ## A9.8 The number rule, for the V1 profile — OWNER DECISION (ENCODING-V1 D-1); supersedes rows 22–23
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:520|

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:36| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:37| ## In plain words
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:38| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:39| This amendment has two parts.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:40| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:41| **Part 1** corrects six wording problems in Amendment 9. The owner decided these corrections. They add no
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:42| mechanism. The verifier uses the same checks and gives the same verdicts. A review of the plain version of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:43| Amendment 9 found the six problems.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:44| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:45| Bitcoin is a public system that adds blocks to a chain. A block header states a chain time. This value is not a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:46| measurement of real time. The registered number k is six.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:47| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:48| - **A01.** Amendment 9 says that the content existed "no later than" T. T is a chain time, not real time. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:49|   correction says this in the claim and in the other sentences that use T in this way.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:50| - **A02.** Amendment 9 says, in its own words, that the keys "were allowed to issue during a stated window". The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:51|   verifier makes only two comparisons with the window. The correction states only those two comparisons.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:52| - **A03.** Amendment 9 excludes Bitcoin history "deeper than k". The correction defines the depth of a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:53|   reorganization. The exclusion then also includes a reorganization of exactly k blocks. The models already
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:54|   exclude that case.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:55| - **A04.** Amendment 9 does not say which receipts V1 protects after an attacker obtains authority-record
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:56|   credentials. The author chose option (e) on 18 October 2026. Part 2 describes it.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:57|   - The adopted text protects the frames and signatures that the service keys made honestly. This protection
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:58|     applies before and after the attacker obtains the credentials.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:59|   - Without the key list of Part 2, V1 does not prevent new receipts under the attacker's own keys.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:60|   - The service must publish its authority record. A third party can inspect a substituted key if that record is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:61|     public. The verifier does not check publication. V1 does not guarantee that an attacker publishes the record.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:62| - **A05.** Amendment 9 does not give the order of the steps that select a Bitcoin attestation. The correction
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:63|   gives the steps that the profile already uses.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:64| - **A06.** DNS (the Domain Name System) holds one authority record. Amendment 9 says "owner name D". The verifier
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:65|   must check the DNS owner name `_tessera-v1.wamason.com`. The correction names it.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:66| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:67| **Part 2** has three new items. The owner and Codex recommended them. Codex is a second AI system that reviews this
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:68| work. The author accepted all three on 18 October 2026. They add new mechanism to V1.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:69| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:70| **UTC: what U is.** UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) is the standard measure of real time. Amendment 9 states no
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:71| UTC time.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:72| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:73| - Under A-UTC, U is a UTC upper bound: the latest chain time of the six confirming blocks, plus two hours.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:74| - The claim is conditional: if A-UTC is true, the content and both signatures existed before U.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:75| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:76| **UTC: the assumption A-UTC.** A miner is a party that makes Bitcoin blocks.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:77| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:78| - A-UTC says: at least one of those six blocks states a chain time no more than two hours before its real
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:79|   production time.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:80| - A-UTC is false only if the miners of all six blocks state chain times more than two hours early.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:81| - Nothing in Bitcoin or in the verifier makes sure that A-UTC is true.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:82| - The author's signature accepts A-UTC as an assumption. The signature does not show that miners make A-UTC true.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:83| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:84| **UTC: the evidence.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:85| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:86| - The retained measurements cover 2015 to 2026. In each complete set of six, one recorded arrival was no later
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:87|   than chain time plus 1065 seconds.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:88| - The dataset rejects arrival times more than two hours from the chain time. It cannot show failures beyond that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:89|   limit.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:90| - Observer clocks can also be wrong. These measurements do not show that A-UTC was true.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:91| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:92| **UTC: the output.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:93| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:94| - The verifier reports U with its assumption identifier, `A-UTC-7200-6`, in `utc_assessment`.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:95| - U, conditional on A-UTC, is outside the six fields that later verifiers must reproduce. U does not change the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:96|   verdict.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:97| - Each statement of U must give the assumption A-UTC next to it.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:98| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:99| **UTC: the year 2106.** In 2106 the Bitcoin time field reaches its maximum. The calculation of U, whose UTC claim
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:100| depends on A-UTC, stays correct for the saved headers of older blocks. Bitcoin, not V1, must define the times of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:101| blocks after that point.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:102| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:103| **Key substitution: the problem.** An attacker with both authority-record credentials can make authority records
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:104| that name the attacker's own keys. Without a new mechanism, receipts under those keys can get VALID.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:105| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:106| **Key substitution: option (e).**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:107| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:108| - Option (e) adds a list of the service keys to the trust file. The release key authenticates the trust file.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:109| - The verifier gives INVALID or CANNOT VERIFY for a receipt whose keys are not on the list.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:110| - The release-key holder must not add keys to the list only because the two authority records name them.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:111| - The author chose option (e). He did not choose option (a), which has no list, or options (b) to (d).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:112| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:113| **Key substitution: the limits.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:114| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:115| - The protection applies only to a user whose verifier release is authentic and comes from an honest release-key
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:116|   holder.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:117| - It stops those users from accepting such receipts.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:118| - It does not make sure that anybody finds or publishes the attack.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:119| - An attacker who also has the release key can make a release that lists the attacker's keys.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:120| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:121| **Key substitution: time.** A release must list the exact keys and window before the receipt's Bitcoin anchor. To
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:122| check this after release-key theft, keep the first listing release and its proof, and authenticate the Bitcoin
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:123| history for both anchors independently of the stolen key. The release-key fingerprint alone cannot identify a forged
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:124| release history. Keep this evidence together with the receipt.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:125| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:126| **Release-key custody: the rule.** AWS means Amazon Web Services, the provider of the service's cloud account.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:127| Amendment 9 already requires these access limits:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:128| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:129| - The DNS credential and the repository key must not give access to the release key.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:130| - Access to the AWS account must not give access to the release key.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:131| - Hardware or offline software for the release key is acceptable only with a written procedure.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:132| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:133| The procedure has these contents:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:134| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:135| - The procedure must say who authorizes each release.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:136| - The procedure must say where the signing occurs.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:137| - The procedure must say how backups stay outside the systems that operate the service.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:138| - The procedure must say how a separate system checks each release before the signing.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:139| - The procedure must say how files move into and out of the signing system.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:140| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:141| **Release-key custody: when.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:142| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:143| - At the freeze, the rule, the release format and the contents of the procedure must be fixed.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:144| - After the freeze, the owner builds and tests the signing system.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:145| - A reviewer must check the procedure before the first public verifier release.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:146| - The target for that release is before 20 November 2026.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:147| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:148| **Release-key custody: test releases.** Each early release uses a separate test release key. Production checks
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:149| never accept this key. Users must authenticate the production release key before they rely on a release. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:150| service must not offer an early release for real use. A test must show that production checks refuse a release
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:151| with only a test signature.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:152| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:153| **Release-key custody: risks that the owner names.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:154| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:155| - The schedule risk moves later. The owner must start the preparation early.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:156| - The rules do not change after the freeze, because the release format is fixed at the freeze.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:157| - Production checks refuse an early release, because it has only a test signature.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:158| - The author accepts the use of his time in November. He wrote: "(4) is acceptable to me".
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:159| - The service does not offer an early release for real use.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:160| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:161| **Release-key custody: if independence fails.** The purchase of hardware alone does not make the key independent.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:162| If the owner cannot show independence before the first public verifier release, the author gets a NARROW-MODEL. That
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:163| model is a smaller protection against an attacker with authority-record credentials. The removal of the key list
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:164| does not repair this.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:165| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:166| Two other mechanisms are recorded as candidates only: time-stamp authorities and a witnessed public log. This
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:167| amendment does not require anybody to make them.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:168| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:169| Each change has a kind:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:170| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:171| - CLARIFY: the meaning does not change.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:172| - NARROW-CLAIM: the claim becomes smaller, so that it states only what the checks establish.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:173| - CORRECT: the wording disagreed with a registered rule or model. The correction follows that rule or model
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:174|   without reducing the claim.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:175| - BROADEN: the claim becomes larger. It adds a mechanism or a stated assumption.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:176| - GATE: the change adds or changes a prerequisite, a trigger, or a cut order. The row states any scope change that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:177|   follows.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:230| ## A10.1 "Existed no later than T" is chain time, not UTC — OWNER DECISION, NARROW-CLAIM (review A01)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:231| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:232| A9 says the bytes and signatures "existed no later than a time T fixed by Bitcoin" (A9:36-37; again at :114,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:233| :133 and in C5, :144). A9 also says that header times are chain-time proxies (C5) and that a finite UTC cutoff
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:234| "requires an additional, explicit backward-skew assumption that V1 does not establish" (:444-446). The ordinary
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:235| reading of "no later than T" is a real-time bound, which A9 does not support.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:236| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:237| **Reading adopted.** "No later than T" means chain order: the bytes and exact signatures existed before the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:238| selected Bitcoin block was mined, because that block commits to their SHA-256 hash (under the registered
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:239| cryptographic and chain assumptions). T is that block's header time, a chain-time value. It is not an upper bound
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:240| in UTC: A2.1 registers no finite bound on B − C, and neither ε nor S is one. A UTC reading needs the additional
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:241| backward-skew assumption that V1 does not establish. A10.1.1 recommends one such assumption, for a separate
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:242| assessment only; this section does not depend on it.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:243| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:244| **Other registered uses of the same bound.** The scenario mapping (:177, :186), the issue order (:294-295) and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:245| guarantee 1 (:433-439) use T as the same clock bound. Each is qualified the same way (rows 5–9 of A10.7). These
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:246| qualifications change the explanation of the safe decisions, not their verdicts, fixtures or case membership.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:247| Scenario i's parties' signature-checking duty and guarantee 1's `historical_security: NOT_EVALUATED` stay. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:248| issue-order case is concrete: a signature made after a backward-skewed header's nominal UTC time, but before the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:249| block is mined, can fit the block's anchor.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:250| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:251| **Assembled C5 claim cell** (rows 4 and 17 of A10.7 both point here):
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:252| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:253| > The frames **and their exact signatures** existed before the selected Bitcoin block was mined. T is that block's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:254| > header time, not a UTC upper bound. The selected block belongs to the qualifying Bitcoin attestation at the lowest
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:255| > block height in the presented OTS proof, under A10.5's stages; T and its confirmations come from that same
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:256| > attestation. The three-conjunct predicate holds at k = 6. Header times need not be monotone; selection uses chain
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:257| > order, not the least header time (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-14, F03).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:258| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:259| C5's non-claims stay, with the reorganization residual amended by A10.3 (row 14). Under A10.1.1 (author adopted
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:260| 2026-10-18), row 21 adds its conditional sentence after this cell; the cell itself does not change.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:261| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:262| **A1.6.** A1.6 (:485-505) contains older, compressed clock and depth language. A1 stays standing. This amendment is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:263| a V1 qualification of that inherited clock wording; the unchanged historical prose does not itself establish a UTC
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:264| bound. The changed sentences are rows 1–9 of A10.7.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:265| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:266| ### A10.1.1 A conditional UTC assessment — AUTHOR ADOPTED 2026-10-18 (recommended by the owner and Codex), BROADEN
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:267| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:268| Source: the decision memo, Part 1 (U1) and Part 3; its Codex review, F03, F04 and "Questions checked" 1; the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:269| tolerance evidence file. A10.1 stays as decided independently of this section.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:270| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:271| **Author ruling, 2026-10-18** (`docs/reviews/amendment-10-r4/AUTHOR-RULINGS.md`): *"That's it.  The other three
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:272| items, while dense, seem rational are accepted."* And, confirming the owner's reading that this adopts A10.1.1,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:273| A10.4 option (e) with A10.4.1 and A10.4.2: *"Yes. That's my understanding.  I focused on reading those sections of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:274| the document.  A 10.4.2 stood out because you disagreed, but even for those where you were in agreement, I read what
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:275| was proposed and accepted the recommendation as being "rationally based.""*
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:276| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:277| **Notation.** h* is the receipt proof's selected inclusion height (A10.5). A2.1 counts it as confirmation one, so
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:278| h*+5 is confirmation six. r(j) is the real (UTC) time at which block j was first produced.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:279| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:280| **Assumption A-UTC** (`assumption_id: "A-UTC-7200-6"`). *At least one of the six blocks h* … h*+5 has a header
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:281| time no more than 7200 s before it was actually mined*, that is, `nTime(j) ≥ r(j) − 7200 s` for some j in
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:282| [h*, h*+5]. A-UTC is an assumption of the UTC assessment only. It is not a Bitcoin consensus rule, the verifier
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:283| does not check it, and no bundle carries evidence of it. It is a sufficient one-sided assumption, not a minimal one.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:284| Δ = 7200 s and m = 6 are frozen in the governing specification's catalog, not in the mutable trust file, and are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:285| not shown to be optimal.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:286| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:287| **Recommended claim text**, added after the A10.1 claim it qualifies (rows 20–21):
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:288| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:289| > Under assumption A-UTC (at least one of the blocks h* … h*+5 has a header time no more than 7200 s before it was
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:290| > actually mined; an assumption of the UTC assessment, not a consensus rule, and not checked by the verifier), the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:291| > bytes and both signatures existed before U = max nTime(h* … h*+5) + 7200 s, in UTC. V1 reports U only in
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:292| > `utc_assessment`, beside its assumption identifier, outside the six stable fields. A2.1's refusal to bound the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:293| > observation lag B − C is unchanged.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:294| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:295| **Derivation** (memo, checked by Codex). (1) `A_sig` existed before r(h*), because h*'s merkle root commits to
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:296| `SHA256(A_sig)` under the registered commitment and history assumptions. (2) r(h*) ≤ r(j) for every j ≥ h*,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:297| because block j commits to a chain that contains h*. (3) A-UTC supplies j in [h*, h*+5] with r(j) ≤ nTime(j) + 7200.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:298| (4) So r(h*) ≤ r(j) ≤ nTime(j) + 7200 ≤ U. The chain-order claims of A10.1 rest on steps 1–2 only.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:299| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:300| **Output contract** (memo, F03). `utc_assessment` contains `assumption_id: "A-UTC-7200-6"` and `utc_upper_bound`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:301| (RFC 3339 string or null). It is computed from the receipt proof's selected h* and its six qualified headers. Its
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:302| bound is conditional on A-UTC and the existing commitment/history assumptions. It is null exactly when T is null.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:303| It does not change the six-field V1 stable result (A9:162, A9.4). Reporting a value with INVALID or UNVERIFIABLE
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:304| does not establish a valid service receipt or valid service signatures. U is never a stable field, and V1's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:305| documentation and relying-party text never state U without A-UTC beside it.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:306| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:307| **Arithmetic and the 2106 boundary** (memo, F04). Verification of a preserved V1 receipt does not consult the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:308| current clock. Each bundled nTime is the profile's unsigned epoch-seconds value, widened before arithmetic:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:309| `U_seconds = 7200 + max(uint64(nTime(h*)), …, uint64(nTime(h*+5)))`, encoded as an RFC 3339 UTC string without
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:310| reduction modulo 2^32 (for max nTime = 4294967295, U = `2106-02-07T08:28:15Z`, not a 1970 time). This 64-bit
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:311| arithmetic covers preserved headers. Timestamp representation for Bitcoin blocks produced after the 2106 rollover
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:312| of the 32-bit field is a Bitcoin protocol matter outside V1; the profile's serial-time unwrapping applies to DNSSEC
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:313| RRSIG fields only.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:314| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:315| **What the ruling and signature do and do not do.** By his 2026-10-18 ruling and his signature, the author adopts
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:316| A-UTC as a trust assumption. It does not establish that miners satisfy it, and nothing in V1 can.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:317| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:318| **Justification of the tolerance against the intended adversary**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:319| (`docs/decisions/2026-10-17-a-utc-tolerance-evidence.md`). The intended adversary is A9's backdater (A9:40): bytes
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:320| that exist only at real time e, presented with a receipt whose U is earlier than e.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:321| - **Failure condition.** A-UTC fails, and U can be wrong, only if the miners of all six confirming blocks set
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:322|   lagging timestamps: every block h* … h*+5 has a header time more than 7200 s before it was mined.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:323| - **A non-mining backdater** can choose only when to stamp and which proof to present. Lowest-height selection fixes
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:324|   the result within a presented proof, but does not eliminate choice among available presentations. The UTC
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:325|   assessment relies on A-UTC for the selected segment in every case. Over 559,718 retained complete six-block
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:326|   windows (heights 369,715–941,944, 2015–2026; Bitcoin Block Arrival Time Dataset, multiple observers, CC0), every
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:327|   window contained a block whose recorded arrival lag was at most 1,065 s. The minimum computed U minus the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:328|   inclusion block's recorded first-seen time was 6,135 s (median 9,908 s); U's UTC interpretation remains
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:329|   conditional on A-UTC. If the selected observer readings do not understate production time, these observations
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:330|   support A-UTC for the sampled windows. Observer clock error is not bounded here. The dataset's ±7200 s quality
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:331|   filter and excluded incomplete windows prevent an inference about the frequency of A-UTC failures outside the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:332|   retained sample. The largest single-block lag observed was 3,918 s; the median was 18 s. A mempool.space sample of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:333|   481 blocks (2024) and Bowden et al. (arXiv:1801.07447, 2018) are consistent with this.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:334| - **Consensus.** Consensus requires each timestamp to exceed the median of the preceding eleven header times. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:335|   evidence reproduces 545 windows in which every recorded first-seen-minus-MTP value exceeds 7200 s. These MTPs use
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:336|   the actual predecessor timestamps and the observer-clock qualification. The count does not bound a coalition
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:337|   changing the six timestamps, since changes within the window also change later MTPs. A majority coalition can
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:338|   sustain lagging timestamps; A-UTC is not consensus protection against that adversary.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:339| - **Limits of the evidence.** The dataset's own quality check rejects any arrival more than 7200 s from its header
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:340|   time, so it cannot show a lag above the threshold; its distribution below the threshold has no observation
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:341|   between 3,918 s and 7,200 s. Observer clock error is not separated. The data describe ordinary miner behaviour,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:342|   not a deliberate coalition.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:343| - Δ equals Bitcoin's node-local forward tolerance; that match does not validate it. m = 6 reuses the k = 6 headers
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:344|   that V1 already requires and pins, so U needs no new input.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:345| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:346| **Relation to A2.1 and guarantee 2.** A2.1 refuses to bound B − C, the service's observation lag, and keeps
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:347| SLA-style bounds out of the assumption set. A-UTC bounds a different quantity (production time versus header time),
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:348| and U never enters a verdict, the shipping predicate or S. Guarantee 2 keeps its chain-time meaning and is not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:349| translated to UTC (row 23).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:350| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:351| **Recorded, not obligations.** RFC 3161 tokens over `SHA256(A_sig)` from at least two independently operated
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:352| time-stamp authorities (U_TSA = max_i(genTime_i + a_i), memo U2) are a recorded candidate, with no V2 or later
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:353| obligation. Unresolved use requirements, also recorded only: whether a court or another examiner will accept A-UTC;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:354| whether a particular use needs qualified timestamps.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:355| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:356| The changed sentences are rows 20–24 of A10.7.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:357| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:358| ## A10.2 The window establishes two comparisons, not issuance "inside" it — OWNER DECISION, NARROW-CLAIM (review A02)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:359| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:360| A9's opening says the keys "were allowed to issue during a stated window" (:36), and guarantee 2's heading says
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:361| "Signing capability mints only inside the window, in chain time" (:441). The C4 verifier rule (:419-421) checks
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:362| only two comparisons, and says "T itself is not compared with not-before".
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:363| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:364| **Reading adopted.** The verifier establishes exactly two inclusive comparisons, with no margin:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:365| - the declared issue time is not earlier than `issuance-not-before`;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:366| - the verified chain-time T is not later than `issuance-not-after`.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:367| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:368| It does not establish that T is not earlier than not-before, that the declared issue time is not later than
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:369| not-after, or that any signing act occurred inside the interval. The review's two arithmetic witnesses satisfy the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:370| two window comparisons and all three A2 temporal comparisons. They are not executed receipt vectors or evidence
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:371| that an honest issuer ships those values. The checks do not change. The issuer invariant (:422, an attempt whose T
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:372| would exceed not-after is not shipped) stays an issuer duty, not a verifier comparison. "Issuance window" stays the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:373| name of the record's two values. The changed sentences are rows 10–12 of A10.7.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:374| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:375| ## A10.3 Reorganization depth, at k = 6 and `DepthK = k − 1` — OWNER DECISION, NARROW-CLAIM (review A03)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:376| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:377| A9 excludes "Bitcoin history deeper than k" (:49-50) and calls "Reorganization deeper than k" a residual (C5,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:378| :144). A9 also imports k = 6 under `DepthK = k − 1` (:105) and A2.1's count, in which the including block is the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:379| first confirmation.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:380| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:381| **Definition.** The depth of a reorganization is the number of blocks it removes from the tip of the chain. A
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:382| reorganization of depth d removes every block that has d or fewer confirmations when it occurs. At k = 6
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:383| confirmations, five blocks follow the anchor block; P5c's `depth` counts those five (`depth = c − 1`, so
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:384| `DepthK = 5`).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:385| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:386| **Correction.** The registered assumption is that anchors with k or more confirmations are permanent (A1.6:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:387| "anchors at depth ≥ k are treated as permanent"). P5c's `Reorg` action can orphan an anchor only while
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:388| `depth < DepthK`, that is, at five or fewer confirmations. So a reorganization of depth exactly k, which removes an
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:389| anchor with k confirmations, is outside both. A9's "deeper than k" read literally leaves that case inside the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:390| claim, with no evidence. The excluded residual is therefore **a reorganization of depth k or more**. This narrows
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:391| A9's literal prose claim at equality. It changes neither the model nor its permanence assumption, and withdraws no
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:392| checked model result. This does not affect C4's chain-order gap (`g + 5 < r`), which the review found correct. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:393| changed sentences are rows 13–14 of A10.7.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:394|
