docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:462| ### A10.4.1 Protection against key substitution (option (e)) — AUTHOR ADOPTED 2026-10-18 (recommended by the owner and Codex), BROADEN
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:463| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:464| Source: the decision memo, Part 2 and Part 3; its Codex review, F05, F07 and "Questions checked" 2–3. Mechanism
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:465| details are the memo's. Adopted by the author with option (e) on 2026-10-18 (A10.4, author ruling).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:466| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:467| **Mechanism.** The trust configuration gains `service_keys`, an array of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:468| `{domain, kms_fp, gpg_fp, not_before, not_after, sources}` entries. Endpoints are finite, with
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:469| not_before ≤ not_after. Fingerprints are canonical; entries are unique; the array has an explicit sort order.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:470| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:471| **Ordered classifier** (one new check; one new reason code, `SERVICE_KEYS_NOT_LISTED`; `TRUST_HORIZON` exists):
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:472| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:473| > First, an exact match on D, both canonical fingerprints and both inclusive window endpoints passes this check.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:474| > Otherwise, overlap with any listed window **or** not_before ≤ as_of yields INVALID / SERVICE_KEYS_NOT_LISTED.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:475| > Otherwise yield UNVERIFIABLE / TRUST_HORIZON. Overlap includes a shared endpoint. Overall verdict and reason use
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:476| > the registered failure precedence, not an early return from this check.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:477| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:478| **Authorization closure:**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:479| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:480| > The initial release independently authorizes and records the complete service-key schedule through as_of. Later
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:481| > releases retain every existing entry unchanged, introduce no overlapping interval, and add an entry only if its
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:482| > not_before is strictly greater than the previous as_of. Thus absence through a past horizon is permanently
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:483| > closed. Completeness concerns authorized entries, not arbitrary channel assertions. The release authority must
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:484| > not authorize a new service-key tuple solely because the two potentially captured channels assert it.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:485| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:486| **Issuer invariant.** No receipt ships under keys that are not listed in a published release.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:487| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:488| **Chain-order pre-commitment of the listing — OWNER DECISION 2026-10-18, BROADEN; narrowed before signing after
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:489| review r4 (NARROW-CLAIM of an owner proposal).** It is part of option (e), which the author adopted on 2026-10-18
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:490| (A10.4). The fourth Codex review (`docs/reviews/amendment-10-r4/CODEX-REVIEW.md`, R4-01 to R4-04) found the owner
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:491| proposal as first drafted too broad; its text below applies Codex's exact corrections. The narrowing was applied
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:492| after the author's ruling, and the author was told of it before signing. *Gap:* the listing is release-signed but
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:493| not tied to time. A release key stolen decades later can sign a forked, internally consistent release chain that
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:494| lists the thief's keys for a past window; authorization closure protects only along the authentic chain. *Rule,*
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:495| mirroring C4's git rule:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:496| - Every verifier release is OpenTimestamps-stamped over the SHA-256 of its trust configuration.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:497| - A receipt's service keys count as listed only if the release that **first** lists their exact entry has a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:498|   qualifying anchor (A10.5) at a lower height than the receipt's selected anchor: `h_release + 5 < h_receipt`, the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:499|   same convention as C4.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:500| - The bundle does not carry the release. The verifier receives the listing evidence with the installed trust file,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:501|   as the listing-evidence package below states.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:502| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:503| **Scope of the retrospective protection (R4-01).** The retrospective protection requires a conforming verifier and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:504| independently authenticated Bitcoin history for both selected anchors and their six-header segments. The receipt,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:505| listing, snapshot and git proofs must use the same independently authenticated history. For this theft protection,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:506| a signature under the possibly stolen release key is not sufficient pin authentication. Compare every used pin with
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:507| independently validated Bitcoin history, or with a previously retained, independently authenticated genuine release
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:508| that covers that height. An earlier release with no pin at the height supplies no witness. A party unable to
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:509| establish this history has not established the retrospective protection. Authenticating only the bootstrap
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:510| public-key fingerprint does not distinguish a fork signed with the stolen genuine key. An independently retained
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:511| genuine release/configuration commitment can distinguish such a fork to the extent of its recorded contents and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:512| ancestry. A9's separate distribution-compromise boundary stays: an attacker-signed executable can simply omit the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:513| rule. The historical check is evaluated by a trusted conforming verifier; it does not authenticate arbitrary newly
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:514| acquired code after release-key theft. A later release-key theft can still issue new bad releases.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:515| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:516| **Initial-window bootstrap (R4-02).** Initial-window bootstrap: publish the authenticated initial listing release C0
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:517| and stamp SHA256(C0). After its selected inclusion block and five successors exist, publish an append-only release
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:518| C1 whose configuration pins those six headers and whose installed listing evidence includes C0 and its completed
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:519| proof. Before issuing the first receipt, make that usable release/evidence available. The receipt must select a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:520| height strictly greater than h_C0+5. C1 retains the exact entry unchanged; its own later stamp is not the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:521| first-listing witness for that entry. This adds a confirmation wait, at least one pin-extension release for
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:522| bootstrap, and custody of the listing evidence. Under this sequence an honest first-window receipt can satisfy the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:523| rule. For later windows, an installed configuration with coverage of the first-listing stamp is required before
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:524| issuance; merely submitting or publishing a release stamp does not supply that coverage. The single-window and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:525| separately registered successor boundaries stay.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:526| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:527| **Listing-evidence package (R4-03).** An installed, archived listing-evidence package, outside the receipt bundle,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:528| contains:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:529| - The canonical first-listing configuration, its authenticated release/archive binding and signatures, its completed
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:530|   OTS proof, and raw headers for its selected six-header segment. A10.5's selection rules apply to this fourth proof
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:531|   using a specified installed header pool; the profile states how that pool combines with bundle headers and how
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:532|   conflicting duplicates are handled.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:533| - A release-authenticated manifest mapping each exact service-key/window tuple to the first-listing configuration's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:534|   SHA-256. The release checker establishes that reference against the authenticated predecessor chain, verifying
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:535|   that the entry is absent before its introducing release and retained unchanged afterward. The intervening
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:536|   configurations and authentication/key-transition evidence needed to reproduce that check are preserved; they are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:537|   never fetched implicitly from Tessera during offline verification.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:538| - Independently authenticated history/pin evidence as R4-01 requires, plus the independently retained bootstrap
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:539|   record identifying the production key and original genuine baseline. A signature freshly verifiable under the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:540|   stolen key is not historical provenance. The actual verifier/specification/catalog and current configuration used
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:541|   for the original verdict are retained, alongside the receipt bundle and its original three proofs/headers. Any
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:542|   separate safe-before/theft-cutoff assessment stays outside the stable six, as A9.4 requires.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:543| - *Declared inputs.* The exact listing-evidence manifest, proof/header bytes and independent-history inputs are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:544|   declared verification inputs. Their content hashes are recorded with the existing configuration/spec diagnostics.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:545|   Exact reproduction requires the same bytes and policy; replacing a proof, supplying missing headers or changing
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:546|   history witnesses is a declared-input change. No network lookup may silently affect the stable result.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:547| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:548| *Holder instruction* (relying-party text): preserve this package with the receipt, including the release that first
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:549| lists the exact entry and its proof. Failure to retain evidence is not evidence of fraud. These are required inputs
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:550| to the check, not a claim that dead-project reconstruction has been demonstrated.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:551| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:552| **Failure cases and reporting (R4-04).** The reporting insertion goes after existing row 15.2 and before 16.1 of the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:553| profile's total check order, preserving all existing rows' relative order: the tuple classifier first, then these
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:554| listing subchecks in this order.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:555| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:556| | Listing subcheck | Outcome |
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:557| |---|---|
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:558| | First-listing configuration/reference authentic and internally consistent | Provisioning prerequisite under the existing trust-authentication refusal rule; missing or invalid required configuration/manifest gives `TRUST_CONFIG_UNAUTHENTICATED`, no receipt verdict. This does not include the separately supplied OTS proof, whose absence is handled below. |

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:565| | h_release+5 < h_receipt | False with both heights available: `INVALID / LISTING_NOT_PRECOMMITTED`; otherwise blocked by the earlier unavailable input, with no invented order-failure reason |
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:566| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:567| Header rows 10.1–10.3 extend to the explicitly defined installed listing-header inputs, with deterministic
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:568| source/path ties for duplicate or conflicting evidence. Every new row has its necessary-input dependencies; the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:569| tuple match uses the parsed domain/fingerprints/window, not successful DNSSEC authentication, as a prerequisite. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:570| classifier's position is registered, so `SERVICE_KEYS_NOT_LISTED` is not unordered. The existing
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:571| first-failed/else-first-unperformable aggregation applies, and independent receipt-anchor evaluation continues to

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:573| bad listing order plus `ISSUANCE_WINDOW`; wrong listing digest; missing listing headers; and the first-window C0/C1

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:575| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:576| **Verdict stability.** Passes and both INVALID conclusions of the **tuple classifier** survive every allowed append.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:577| An UNVERIFIABLE result may later pass, as A9.5 permits. This does not extend to the height comparison: pin
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:578| extensions can qualify a previously nonqualifying earlier attestation and change the selected height. A9.4's contract
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:579| stays identical output for identical complete declared inputs, the configuration and listing evidence included, and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:580| pin extensions can still change selection, T and U across releases. Historical-security assessments stay separate.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:581| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:582| **V1's single window.** A9.6 registers one window. V1's configuration lists exactly one entry, authorized at the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:583| freeze. A successor window needs a release that lists it, authorized before it opens, in addition to A9.6's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:584| rotation registration.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:585| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:586| **Scope.** The protection covers relying parties who run an authentic verifier release whose trust configuration
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:587| lists D's service keys. "Authentic" means authenticated distribution plus trustworthy release-authority behaviour;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:588| uncompromised key storage alone does not validate an authorization decision. Within this scope, a captor of both
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:589| channel credentials who lacks release authorization cannot make a receipt under keys other than those listed pass
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:590| V1. Such a receipt is INVALID when its window overlaps a listed window or starts at or before the configuration's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:591| `as_of`, and UNVERIFIABLE otherwise.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:592| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:593| **Limits.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:594| - It prevents acceptance by those relying parties. It does not ensure that anyone detects or publicly exposes a
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:595|   capture. It provides no issuer detection and no public visibility.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:596| - A horizon result means the keys are not yet covered. It is not proof of a takeover.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:597| - Release-key compromise is distribution compromise, already a stated boundary. A captor with both channels and the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:598|   release key can ship a release that lists its own keys. A release delivered to one party is not detectable by
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:599|   others.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:600| - A stale trust file gives an honest new-window receipt `UNVERIFIABLE / TRUST_HORIZON`, a safe false reject until
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:601|   the relying party updates. This cannot occur in V1, which has one window.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:602| - A8.3 and A8.5 supply no evidence for this property, and no formal model run supports it. Its evidence is the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:603|   check's construction plus prospective vectors (memo, Part 3, row 5), which are exit evidence once registered.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:604| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:605| **Change accounting.** This is a BROADEN, not a wording correction. C4 gains a third authenticated source for the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:606| key set, the release. The adversary text gains a protection, within the scope above. The scenario mapping's
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:607| verdicts are unchanged; a fresh captor-key receipt is deliberately a newly rejected case. The signed bytes, the P8
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:608| encoding, `A_sig`, the existing two-channel checks and every existing reason code are unchanged. The specification
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:609| hash changes. Adding the listing to the cut order is a gate and scope change and is labelled as one (row 33). The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:610| changed sentences are rows 25–33 and 37–39 of A10.7.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:624| - **Prerequisite.** Independence of the release key from the DNS credential, the repository key and the issuing AWS
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:625|   account is an existing prerequisite of A9.5's trust-configuration authority (A9:326-332). It already protects
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:626|   V1's KSKs, repository trust and header pins against the channel captor, with or without the listing. It is still
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:627|   OPEN (profile §14.2 item 1; YubiKey 2 is not in hand).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:628| - **Custody form.** Hardware or offline-software custody of the release key is acceptable **only** with a written
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:629|   custody and release-authorization procedure. The procedure states who authorizes releases, where signing occurs,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:630|   and how backups stay outside the operational environment of the service. After the custody review it must also
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:631|   state (C01) the independent review-and-build environment that checks each candidate release against an approved
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:632|   baseline kept outside the operational environment and binds approval to the exact archive hash, and (C02) the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:633|   controlled media crossing into and out of the signing session. The dated custody record names the procedure.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:634| - **Hardware is not independence.** Buying hardware alone does not establish independence.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:635| - **When: the first public verifier release, not the freeze.** The custody review found that real independence
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:636|   needs an independent review-and-sign environment and a controlled media crossing (C01, C02), which cannot be ready
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:637|   by 30 Oct. The *first public verifier release* is the first verifier release signed by the production release key
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:638|   and offered to relying parties.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:639|   - **Frozen at the 30 Oct freeze:** this requirement; the release format (the release archive, the release-signature
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:640|     format, and how the trust-file hash binds to the release; profile §14.2 item 2), which must be frozen by 30 Oct;
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:641|     and the custody procedure's required contents (the bullet above).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:642|   - **After the freeze, before the first public verifier release** (target: before the 20 Nov issuance milestone):
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:643|     the environment is built and rehearsed, the written procedure is reviewed, and independence is established.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:644| - **Test releases.** Every verifier release made before that gate is signed with a separate TEST release key. Its
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:645|   public key is never published as the release key, never named in the freeze record or relying-party text, and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:646|   never introduced by a production release. A pre-gate TEST signature cannot authenticate a production release.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:647|   Production authentication must use the independently authenticated production release key and must reject TEST
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:648|   authority, including TEST provisioning overrides. This does not protect a user who skips authentication or
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:649|   acquires a substituted initial key.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:650|   - *Offering restriction.* No pre-gate artifact is offered for production reliance: pre-gate releases are offered
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:651|     only as TEST releases, never as releases on which relying parties may rely.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:652|   - *Required rehearsal.* Before the first public verifier release, a rehearsal must show that an otherwise correct
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:653|     archive with only a TEST signature is refused by the production acquisition and verification procedure,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:654|     including when the TEST key is supplied through the test interface (profile §3.5's provisioning override).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:655|     Missing or substituted bootstrap authority is not accepted as production merely because a signature verifies.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:656|   - Profile §3.5 binds no production release; it supplies no evidence that the production path excludes TEST
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:657|     provisioning. The rehearsal is that evidence.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:658| - **Risks and mitigations** (owner's proposal):
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:659|   1. *Schedule.* The schedule risk moves later. Mitigation: start preparing the environment and procedure early.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:661|   3. *Convenience release* (a release signed outside the procedure because the environment is not ready). Closed for

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:680| ## A10.5 Attestation selection, in stages — OWNER DECISION, CLARIFY (review A05)
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:681| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:682| C5 selects "the verified attestation at the lowest block height in the presented OTS proof" (:144). C6 says "A
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:683| selected anchor (C5) beyond the newest pin is `UNVERIFIABLE`", "Every supplied header must be pinned" and "An
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:684| unselected attestation without its headers supplies no fact and is not a failure" (:145). "Verified" can be read
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:685| with or without pin coverage. The profile already fixes one order (`docs/V1-PROFILE.md` §7.1–§7.2, OWNER
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:686| 2026-10-14, G05, G07, G23; precedence rows 10–11). This amendment states that order as A9's meaning.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:687| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:688| These stages explain qualification and selection within the existing verifier. They do not replace other
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:689| registered checks, their dependencies, or dispatch and reason-code precedence. A failure of an independently
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:690| performable required check takes precedence over an unperformable check under A4.2. The header-pool link checks,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:691| OTS grammar and stamp checks, and selected-height transaction/path checks remain unchanged. A stage's UNVERIFIABLE
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:692| entry is an unperformable-check result, not an early return that suppresses other checks.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:693| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:694| **Stages**, for each of the receipt, snapshot and git proofs:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:695| 1. **Header pool.** Every supplied header, used or not, is checked against the pins. A header at a height with no
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:696|    pin gives `UNVERIFIABLE / HEADERS_NOT_COVERED`; a header that differs from its pin gives `INVALID /
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:697|    HEADER_CONFLICTS_PIN`.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:698| 2. **Qualification ("verified").** A Bitcoin attestation at height h qualifies only if the bundled header at h has
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:699|    a merkle root equal to the attestation message, headers h … h+5 are all bundled, each equals its pin, and each
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:700|    links to the one before. Pin coverage is part of "verified". A pinned header at h whose merkle root contradicts
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:701|    the attestation gives `INVALID / OTS_MERKLE_MISMATCH`.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:702| 3. **Selection.** The selected anchor is the qualifying attestation at the lowest height h*. T and the confirmation
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:703|    count come from h*. A non-qualifying attestation, including one without headers or one beyond the newest pin,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:704|    is never selected; it supplies no fact and is not a failed check, except as stages 1–2 state. A failed check at
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:705|    h* never moves selection to a higher height.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:706| 4. **No qualifying attestation.** The check is unperformable (`HEADERS_MISSING`, or `ANCHOR_PENDING_ONLY` if only
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:707|    pending attestations; `SNAPSHOT_NOT_ANCHORED` and `GIT_NOT_ANCHORED` for those proofs). The overall verdict is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:708|    `UNVERIFIABLE` unless another independently performable required check fails, in which case it is `INVALID`
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:709|    under A4.2.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:710| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:711| **Cases**, each subject to A4.2 precedence over any other failed check. A qualifying path at h = 100 and a lower,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:712| headerless attestation at h = 90: h* = 100. A sole attestation beyond the newest pin, without headers: stage 4,
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:713| unperformable. The same with its headers supplied: stage 1, `HEADERS_NOT_COVERED`, unperformable. So C6's

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:715| stage 1 or stage 4. The assembled C5 claim cell is in A10.1. The changed sentences are rows 17–18 of A10.7.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:719| C4 says "DNSSEC (owner name D, …)" (:143). In DNS, the owner name is the complete name that owns the record. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:720| encoding A9 adopts (:149) requires the owner `_tessera-v1.<D>`, where D is `common.issuer` (ENCODING-V1 §7, :551 at

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:722| in the workspace). A9.6 (:414-415) already rejects a substituted per-key owner. Read
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:723| literally, "owner name D" names `wamason.com`, the wrong record. For V1 the owner is `_tessera-v1.wamason.com`. The
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md:724| changed sentence is row 19 of A10.7.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:21| ## A11.1 What went wrong
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:22| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:23| P3's assumption half (A1 §P3, `phase-0-prereg-amendment-1.md:144-148`) requires the verification profile to record
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:24| the *exact library and version, accepted signature encodings, public-key validation behavior, low-order-point
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:25| handling, cofactor equation variant, and negative test vectors for each*. Two of those fields name concepts of
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:26| Ed25519-style curves, which A1 used as its example (`:136`). V1 later registered OpenPGP P-256 and then, on
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:27| 2026-10-16, the hybrid ML-DSA-65 + P-256 (`formal/p8/HYBRID-REGISTRATION-RECORD.md`). Neither registration re-read the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:28| checklist.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:29| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:30| For ML-DSA, the two curve fields have no referent. The other four fields still apply in full. So the checklist
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:31| names nothing specific to ML-DSA's own verification pitfalls: it **demands too little**. Nothing had been accepted
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:32| on it. The assumption half was open (`formal/PROPERTIES.md:37`) and due after the freeze
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:33| (`formal/freeze-v1/FREEZE-RECORD.md:81`).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:34| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:35| The method's defect: **a registered decision can change what an earlier registered sentence refers to, and nothing
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:36| requires anyone to re-read that sentence.** §A11.4 adds that duty.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:37| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:38| ## A11.2 P3's verification profile: floor and duty
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:39| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:40| **The proofs are unchanged.** P3's model half assumes a verifier with stated behaviour. The assumption half is
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:41| bounded implementation evidence that the shipped verifier has that behaviour. It does not show that every model
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:42| assumption is preserved in general.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:43| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:44| 1. **Fields kept.** All six of A1's fields stay. For each algorithm in the governing specification they are read as
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:45|    follows:
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:46| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:47|    | A1 field | ECDSA P-256 (rule O) | ML-DSA-65 (rule R) |
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:48|    |---|---|---|
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:49|    | exact library and version | `cryptography` and its bundled OpenSSL, identified by wheel tag and native-library SHA-256 | same |
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:50|    | accepted signature encodings | OpenPGP v4 packet; MPI rules; r, s ∈ [1, n−1]; rule-O policy | exact 3309 bytes; strict hint and z encoding |
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:51|    | public-key validation | exact uncompressed point; coordinates < p; on the curve; checked before the library | exact SPKI; no algebraic validation exists |
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:52|    | low-order-point handling | cofactor 1: infinity rejected as a key and as the equation's result; invalid-curve points rejected | no referent. Replaced by: degenerate-key behaviour recorded |
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:53|    | cofactor equation variant | cofactor 1: a single variant; x(R) reduced mod n | no referent. Replaced by: the FIPS 204 interface (pure, empty context), with every other interface rejected |

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:56| 2. **Floor (registered).** The evidence is the files listed in
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:57|    `formal/p3-verification-profile/FLOOR-MANIFEST.sha256`, whose SHA-256 is fixed at signing. At this draft it is

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:61|      - **ML-DSA-65** runs end to end through the verifier. Two disagreements, tcId 3 and 4, are V1 policy (empty
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:62|        context only).

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:64|        the digest substituted. 219 non-strict DER cases are tested at library level only. 21 P1363 strings of the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:65|        wrong length reach neither interface. There are no disagreements.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:66| 3. **Discharge.** Adopting this floor is not discharging P3. P3's assumption half is discharged only when:

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:72|      discharge until it is fixed and re-tested.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:73| 4. **Operational duty (not a registered result).** The floor's checks, and the latest published vectors for each
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:74|    algorithm in use, are re-run on every verifier release, on every change to the signature library's version or
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:75|    build, on every new upstream vector commit, and at least quarterly. Each run is recorded with its date, inputs and
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:76|    outcome, and attested by the operator.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:77| 5. **What a later finding changes.**
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:78|    - **A security-policy finding** (an algorithm, parameter or key later judged weak) never rewrites a V1 verdict.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:79|      It reaches relying parties as a historical-security result, beside the verdict and its stable fields
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:80|      (A9.4, `phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:267-283`).
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:81|    - **An implementation-conformance defect** (the verifier disagrees with the governing specification, for example
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:82|      by accepting a malformed or prohibited case the specification rejects, A9:278) is not preserved as V1
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:83|      behaviour. It is fixed in a signed release, which names the affected releases and says what changed. A silent
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:84|      change to the verifier is never permitted.

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:96| ## A11.4 Dependency duty for registered decisions
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:97| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:98| When a registered decision changes a parameter (an algorithm, a custody form, a channel, a horizon, a scope, a key),
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:99| the owner sweeps the registered texts for sentences whose referent the change alters. Each one is recorded as
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:100| amended, superseded, still fitting or open, before the decision's change is treated as complete. An owner decision
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:101| that touches a registered parameter is checked against those texts before it is recorded.
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:102| 
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:103| ## A11.5 Results of the first sweep (2026-10-28)

docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:109| 1. **H3 (`phase-0-prereg.md:232-248`): not amended.** H3 is a hypothesis with a stated falsifier. Its examples are
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:110|    AWS-based, but they do not restrict it to AWS. It is measured over the whole deployed system, every provider
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:111|    included. A measurement protocol is recorded before measurement. It covers retained resources (including the
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:112|    compliance-locked trail bucket), defines the demonstration and idle periods, and reports the three numbers
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:113|    separately. A slot-2 signer and an issuer poller that run through the operating window conflict with "idle
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:114|    compute exactly $0". If that or another number fails, H3 is reported as falsified. The operating window is not
docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-11.md:115|    redefined as a demonstration to avoid this.
