formal/p8/PROOF.md:68| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:69| ## 1. The accepted domain, exactly
formal/p8/PROOF.md:70| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:71| Let **V** be the set of JSON values in E§1.1:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:72| - `null`, `true` and `false`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:73| - finite binary64 numbers other than −0;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:74| - strings of Unicode scalar values that contain no noncharacter, no code point unassigned in Unicode 16.0.0, and are
formal/p8/PROOF.md:75|   in NFC;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:76| - arrays;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:77| - objects with pairwise distinct names.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:78| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:79| Two values are **equal** when they are equal as mathematical structures:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:80| - numbers are equal as doubles;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:81| - strings are equal as scalar sequences;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:82| - arrays are equal as sequences;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:83| - objects are equal as finite maps from names to values. Member order is not part of an object.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:84| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:85| That is the sense in which injectivity is claimed. Two JSON *texts* that differ only in spelling denote one value,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:86| and E§1.2 says why that is intended.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:87| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:88| The accepted sets are:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:89| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:90| - **Payloads.** For a tag `t`, `Pay(t) = { JCS(v) : v ∈ V, Schema_t(v), depth(v) ≤ 64, |JCS(v)| ≤ 2^24 }`. Here
formal/p8/PROOF.md:91|   `Schema_attest` is E§3.2 together with E§3.3, and `Schema_manifest` is E§4.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:92| - **Frames.** `Frm(t) = { frame(t, p) : p ∈ Pay(t) }` for `t ∈ {attest, manifest}`, where
formal/p8/PROOF.md:93|   `frame(t, p) = [|t|] ‖ t ‖ 00 01 ‖ u32(|p|) ‖ p`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:94| - **Signature slots.** For an algorithm id `a` and a slot `i ∈ {0 (kms), 1 (gpg)}`, `Sig(a, i)` is the set of
formal/p8/PROOF.md:95|   byte strings accepted by the E§5.2 rule for `(a, i)`. It is always a set of **nonempty** strings of length at
formal/p8/PROOF.md:96|   most `cap(a, i)`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:97|   - Rule O: exactly one legacy-header v4 signature packet, with every inner length consumed exactly.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:98|   - Rule R: the strings of the parameter set's exact signature length.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:99|   - Opaque: every string of 1 to 65536 bytes.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:100| - **Anchor preimages.** `Anc = { A(F0, S0, F1, S1) : F_i ∈ Frm(attest), S_i ∈ Sig(alg(F_i), i) }`, where `alg(F)`
formal/p8/PROOF.md:101|   is the `common.alg` of `F`'s payload and
formal/p8/PROOF.md:102|   `A(F0, S0, F1, S1) = [29] ‖ "tessera-v1/receipt-anchor-sig" ‖ 02 ‖ u32|F0| ‖ F0 ‖ u32|S0| ‖ S0 ‖ u32|F1| ‖ F1 ‖ u32|S1| ‖ S1`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:103|   The withdrawn frame-only construction (tag `tessera-v1/receipt-anchor`) is not in the domain. Its tag is not in
formal/p8/PROOF.md:104|   T.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:105| - **Snapshot preimages.** `Snp = { S(s) : 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 2^24 }`, where `S(s) = [26] ‖ "tessera-v1/dnssec-snapshot" ‖ u32|s| ‖ s`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:106| - **Receipts.** A tuple `(F_M, F_0, S_0, F_1, S_1, A)` is an *accepted receipt* (codec level) when all of the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:107|   following hold:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:108|   - `F_M ∈ Frm(manifest)` decodes to a manifest `M`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:109|   - `F_0` and `F_1` are in `Frm(attest)` and decode to `(C_0, fp_0)` and `(C_1, fp_1)`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:110|   - `fp_0 = M.key_fp` and `fp_1 = M.sset[0]`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:111|   - `JCS(C_0) = JCS(C_1)`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:112|   - `C_0.manifest_sha256 = hex(SHA256(F_M))`, and `C_0.issuer` and `C_0.alg` equal those of `M`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:113|   - `S_i ∈ Sig(C_0.alg, i)` and `A = A(F_0, S_0, F_1, S_1)`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:114| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:115|   The receipt's structure is `(M, C, S_kms, S_gpg)`. It is **not** a function of `(M, C)` alone. The signer's
formal/p8/PROOF.md:116|   choices are inside `S`: the nonce, the creation time and the unhashed area. So one `(M, C)` has many accepted
formal/p8/PROOF.md:117|   receipts, and P8 claims nothing about which one an issuer produces.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:118| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:119| The decoders in E§1.4, E§3.1, E§4, E§5 and E§6 accept exactly these sets and reject everything else with the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:120| stated codes. Lemma 3 shows this for payloads, and Lemmas 5–8 (with 7a) for the rest.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:121| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:122| ## 2. Assumptions
formal/p8/PROOF.md:123| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:124| - **(N) Number formatting.** For every finite double `d`, `ES(d)` (ECMA-262 Number::toString, used by RFC 8785
formal/p8/PROOF.md:125|   §3.2.2.3) is a decimal literal whose round-half-even nearest double is `d`. Decimal-to-double conversion is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:126|   correctly rounded (IEEE 754). The ECMAScript specification requires both. The implementations rely on them
formal/p8/PROOF.md:127|   through `rfc8785` (A) and through `repr` and `float` (B).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:128| - **(H) SHA-256 collision resistance.** This is used **only** in Theorem part (iv), for the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:129|   hash-carried bindings and the anchor digest, which since 2026-10-12 also carries the exact signatures. Parts
formal/p8/PROOF.md:130|   (i)–(iii) are unconditional.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:131|   - **SHA-256 is the only hash function V1's encoding relies on.** Both fingerprint slots are SHA-256: of the SPKI
formal/p8/PROOF.md:132|     for kms, and of the OpenPGP v4 key-packet body for gpg.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:133|   - The git channel's object linkage is SHA-1, but that belongs to C4's dependency manifest, not P8 (E§7.2).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:134|   - An OpenPGP signature as GnuPG emits it carries OpenPGP's own SHA-1 issuer fingerprint in a subpacket. Those
formal/p8/PROOF.md:135|     bytes are committed in `A_sig` like the rest, but no V1 check reads them.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:136| - **(U) Unicode 16.0.0 tables.** These define V's string conditions. They bear on what is accepted, never on
formal/p8/PROOF.md:137|   injectivity.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:138| - **(K) Key use.** Each V1 slot key signs only V1 tagged strings, as OpenPGP type-0x00 documents. The repository
formal/p8/PROOF.md:139|   key and the DNSSEC keys are other keys. This is used only in Remark 10.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:140| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:141| P8 assumes nothing about whether signatures can be forged. That is P1 and P3. Nor does P8 assume anything about
formal/p8/PROOF.md:142| time: what an OTS proof establishes about when `SHA256(A_sig)` existed belongs to C5 and its chain-time
formal/p8/PROOF.md:143| residuals. Theorem (iv) states how the three compose, and keeps them apart.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:144| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:145| ---
formal/p8/PROOF.md:146| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:147| ## 3. Lemmas
formal/p8/PROOF.md:148| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:149| **Lemma 1 (strings).** Let `E(s)` be RFC 8785's escaping of a string `s` of scalar values (E§1.3), and let `Dec`
formal/p8/PROOF.md:150| be RFC 8259 string decoding, which pairs surrogate escapes. Then for every string `s` in V, decoding
formal/p8/PROOF.md:151| `"` E(s) `"` returns exactly `s`, consumes exactly those bytes, and stops at the closing quote.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:152| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:153| *Proof.* `E` maps each scalar `c` on its own:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:154| - `"` becomes `\"`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:155| - `\` becomes `\\`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:156| - a control character `c < 0x20` becomes its two-character escape where RFC 8785 defines one, and `\u00xx`
formal/p8/PROOF.md:157|   otherwise;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:158| - every other `c` becomes its UTF-8 encoding, which is defined because `s` contains no surrogates.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:159| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:160| None of the outputs contains an unescaped `"`. Every output that starts with `\` is a complete escape that `Dec`
formal/p8/PROOF.md:161| maps back to `c`. Every other output is a raw scalar `≥ 0x20`, other than `"` and `\`, which `Dec` copies.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:162| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:163| UTF-8 is prefix-free, so the concatenation splits uniquely into these units. The first unescaped `"` is therefore
formal/p8/PROOF.md:164| the closing quote. ∎
formal/p8/PROOF.md:165| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:166| **Lemma 2 (numbers).** Let `d` be a finite double other than −0. Then:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:167| - (a) `ES(d)` matches the RFC 8259 number grammar;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:168| - (b) parsing `ES(d)` gives `d`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:169| - (c) `ES(d)` passes the value-preserving rule E§1.2;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:170| - (d) in `JCS(v)`, `ES(d)` is followed by `,`, `]`, `}` or the end of input.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:171| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:172| *Proof.*
formal/p8/PROOF.md:173| - (a) `ES` produces only the forms `digits`, `digits.digits`, `0.0…digits` and `d[.ddd]e±n`, with an optional
formal/p8/PROOF.md:174|   leading `-`. Integer parts have no leading zero, except the single `0` of `0.`. All of these are grammatical.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:175| - (b) This is (N).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:176| - (c) Rule 1: `ES(d)` is never a negative zero, because `d ≠ −0` and `ES(+0) = "0"`. Rule 2: the nearest double
formal/p8/PROOF.md:177|   to `ES(d)` is `d` by (b), which is finite. Rule 3: `ES(d)` is the literal being tested, so its value equals the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:178|   value of `ES` of its nearest double, which is `ES(d)` again.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:179| - (d) JCS puts a number only before a separator or a closing bracket, or at the end of the text. None of those can
formal/p8/PROOF.md:180|   extend a number token, so a maximal-munch number scan over `JCS(v)` stops exactly at the end of `ES(d)`. ∎
formal/p8/PROOF.md:181| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:182| **Lemma 3 (canonical payload; P8's injectivity of `canonical()`).** For every `v ∈ V`, the strict parser applied
formal/p8/PROOF.md:183| to `JCS(v)` consumes exactly `JCS(v)` and returns `v`. Hence:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:184| - (a) `JCS` is injective on V;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:185| - (b) a byte string `b` passes `payload()` (E§1.4) if and only if `b = JCS(v)` for some `v ∈ V` within the limits,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:186|   and then `payload(b) = v`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:187| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:188| *Proof.* By induction on `v`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:189| - Literals are immediate.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:190| - Numbers follow from Lemma 2(b) and (d).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:191| - Strings follow from Lemma 1.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:192| - **Arrays.** `JCS([v1…vn]) = "[" JCS(v1) "," … "," JCS(vn) "]"`. By the induction hypothesis, each `JCS(vi)` is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:193|   parsed to `vi` and consumed exactly. The next byte is then `,` or `]`, and the RFC 8259 grammar is LL(1) on
formal/p8/PROOF.md:194|   that byte, so the element boundaries are forced.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:195| - **Objects.** The same argument applies to `"{" JCS(k1) ":" JCS(u1) "," … "}"`. The parser returns the member
formal/p8/PROOF.md:196|   list `[(k1,u1)…]`. Its names are distinct because `v` is an object in V, so it denotes the map `v`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:197| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:198| For (a): if `JCS(v) = JCS(w)`, then `v = parse(JCS(v)) = parse(JCS(w)) = w`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:199| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:200| For (b), the "if" direction. Parsing `JCS(v)` succeeds by the argument above. Its UTF-8 is valid by Lemma 1.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:201| Every check in E§1.4 passes:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:202| - depth: the parse is `v`, and `v` is within the limits;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:203| - names: `v`'s names are distinct;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:204| - strings: `v`'s strings are in V;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:205| - numbers: every literal in `JCS(v)` is some `ES(d)`, which passes by Lemma 2(c);
formal/p8/PROOF.md:206| - canonical: `JCS(parse(b)) = JCS(v) = b`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:207| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:208| For (b), the "only if" direction. If `payload(b)` succeeds with value `v`, then the checks put `v` in V within the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:209| limits, and the final check gives `b = JCS(v)`. ∎
formal/p8/PROOF.md:210| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:211| *Remark (no normalization at the verifier).* By Lemma 3(b), the verifier's accepted payload set is exactly the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:212| image `JCS(V)`. A byte string that is not canonical, such as `9.80`, `1E2`, `A`, extra whitespace or
formal/p8/PROOF.md:213| reordered members, is rejected (XF-23 to XF-30). It is not repaired. Normalization happens only at the issuer's
formal/p8/PROOF.md:214| `ingest`, and there by Lemma 2 and E§1.2 it changes spellings and never values.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:215| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:216| **Lemma 4 (headers are prefix-free; tag separation).** Let `T` be the four tags of E§2, and
formal/p8/PROOF.md:217| `header(t) = [|t|] ‖ t`. For distinct `t, t' ∈ T`, no byte string begins with both `header(t)` and `header(t')`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:218| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:219| *Proof.* If `|t| ≠ |t'|`, the two headers differ in byte 0. If `|t| = |t'|`, then `t ≠ t'` differ at some
formal/p8/PROOF.md:220| position `j < |t|`, so the headers differ in byte `1 + j`. Either way the difference falls at a position both
formal/p8/PROOF.md:221| headers cover (byte 0, or byte `1 + j < 1 + |t| = 1 + |t'|`). ∎ [OWNER 2026-10-19, P8F-06] *(Was: "within the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:222| first `1 + max(|t|, |t'|)` bytes, which both headers cover"; headers of unequal length do not both cover that.)*
formal/p8/PROOF.md:223| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:224| So the tag is read first (a length byte, then that many bytes), before any other field is interpreted. The decoder
formal/p8/PROOF.md:225| compares it with the expected construction and rejects a mismatch (`TAG_MISMATCH`) or a tag outside T
formal/p8/PROOF.md:226| (`TAG_UNKNOWN`).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:227| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:228| **Lemma 5 (frame codec; boundary-unambiguity).**
formal/p8/PROOF.md:229| - For `t ∈ {attest, manifest}` and `p ∈ Pay(t)`: `decode_frame(frame(t, p), t) = parse(p)`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:230| - For every `b` that `decode_frame(·, t)` accepts: `b = frame(t, JCS(decode_frame(b, t)))`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:231| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:232| So `frame(t, ·)` is a bijection from `Pay(t)`, and through Lemma 3 from the schema-valid part of V, onto `Frm(t)`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:233| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:234| *Proof (boundary-unambiguity).* Every field's start and end are fixed by the bytes before it:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:235| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:236| | Field | Bytes | Fixed by |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:237| |---|---|---|
formal/p8/PROOF.md:238| | tag length | [0, 1) | position |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:239| | tag | [1, 1+n) | byte 0 |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:240| | canonicalization version | [1+n, 3+n) | n |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:241| | length L | [3+n, 7+n) | n |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:242| | payload | [7+n, 7+n+L) | n and L |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:243| | end of input | at exactly 7+n+L | n and L; otherwise `TRUNCATED` or `TRAILING` |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:244| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:245| No boundary depends on the contents of a later field. In particular, the payload's own JSON structure never
formal/p8/PROOF.md:246| decides where the frame ends; the length does, which is A1 P8's "a parser cannot disagree about where the payload
formal/p8/PROOF.md:247| ends". The fields are then checked in order: tag in T and equal to `t` (Lemma 4); version equal to `0x0001`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:248| `L ≤ 2^24`; payload in `Pay(t)` (Lemma 3(b) plus the schema).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:249| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:250| For the first identity: given `frame(t, p)`, the decoder reads `n = |t|`, the tag `t`, `0x0001` and `L = |p|`. It
formal/p8/PROOF.md:251| finds exactly `L` bytes left, and those bytes are `p`. Then Lemma 3(b) applies.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:252| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:253| For the second identity: if `b` is accepted, every field equals the corresponding field of
formal/p8/PROOF.md:254| `frame(t, JCS(parse(payload)))`: the tag was checked to be `t`, the version is `0x0001`, `L` is the actual
formal/p8/PROOF.md:255| remainder, and Lemma 3(b) gives `payload = JCS(parse(payload))`. ∎
formal/p8/PROOF.md:256| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:257| **Lemma 6 (the two signer frames).** Let `(F_M, F_0, S_0, F_1, S_1, A)` be an accepted receipt with common value `C`. Then:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:258| - (a) **Common content is byte-identical.** `JCS(C)` occupies bytes `[34, 34 + |JCS(C)|)` of both `F_0` and `F_1`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:259|   This is A5 §A5.4 / R-3.12's "payload equal across signer slots", as a statement about bytes.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:260| - (b) **The frames are distinct.** `F_0 ≠ F_1`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:261| - (c) **Each frame's slot is a function of its bytes, and the slots are disjoint.** Under E§3.3, the attestation
formal/p8/PROOF.md:262|   frames whose `key_fp` starts `spki-sha256:` and those whose `key_fp` starts `gpg-sha256:` are disjoint sets. A
formal/p8/PROOF.md:263|   frame accepted in slot `kms` is never accepted in slot `gpg`, and the reverse.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:264| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:265| *Proof.*
formal/p8/PROOF.md:266| - (a) `Schema_attest` fixes the payload's names to `common` and `signer`, and `"common" < "signer"` in UTF-16 order.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:267|   So JCS writes `{"common":` (10 bytes) at payload offset 0, followed by `JCS(C)`. The payload starts at frame
formal/p8/PROOF.md:268|   offset 24 (1 + 17 + 2 + 4). Both frames carry the same `C`, because the receipt condition is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:269|   `JCS(C_0) = JCS(C_1)`, which by Lemma 3(a) is the same as `C_0 = C_1`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:270| - (b) The manifest schema forces `fp_0` to have the prefix `spki-sha256:` and `fp_1` the prefix `gpg-sha256:`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:271|   These differ in their first character, so the two payload values differ, so the payloads differ by Lemma 3(a),
formal/p8/PROOF.md:272|   so the frames differ by Lemma 5.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:273| - (c) The prefix is part of the frame's bytes, and the receipt condition ties slot `kms` to `M.key_fp` and slot
formal/p8/PROOF.md:274|   `gpg` to `M.sset[0]`, which have different prefixes.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:275| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:276| A swapped presentation fails `RECEIPT_SLOT`. So does the same frame presented twice (XR-01, XR-02). A splice that
formal/p8/PROOF.md:277| changes `C` in one slot fails `RECEIPT_COMMON_MISMATCH` (XR-03). ∎
formal/p8/PROOF.md:278| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:279| *Why the two frames share one tag.* A5 §A5.4 registers that object type is one of the six fields that are equal
formal/p8/PROOF.md:280| across slots. So separation between the two signers' frames is done by the fingerprint slot and the manifest's
formal/p8/PROOF.md:281| slot order, not by the tag. Lemma 6(c) is that separation.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:282| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:283| **Lemma 7a (signature slots).** For every `(a, i)`, the slot decoder accepts a byte string `s` of declared slot
formal/p8/PROOF.md:284| length `n` if and only if `s ∈ Sig(a, i)` and `|s| = n`. When it accepts, it returns `s` itself. The signature's
formal/p8/PROOF.md:285| end is fixed twice, and the two must agree:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:286| - by the slot's `u32` length;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:287| - by the signature's own extent: rule O's packet header, rule R's fixed length, or, for opaque, the slot length.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:288| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:289| *Proof.*
formal/p8/PROOF.md:290| - The slot length `n` is read first.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:291|   - `n = 0` gives `SIG_EMPTY`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:292|   - `n > cap(a, i)` gives `LENGTH_CAP`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:293|   - Otherwise exactly `n` bytes are taken.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:294| - **Rule O.** Byte 0 must be `0x88` or `0x89`. It fixes the width of the length field (1 or 2 bytes), and the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:295|   shortest-form condition makes that width a function of the body length `m`. So the header is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:296|   `h ∈ {2, 3}` bytes, and the packet ends at `h + m`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:297|   - `h + m < n` gives `TRAILING`. This includes a second packet.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:298|   - `h + m > n` gives `TRUNCATED`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:299|   - Inside the body, every field's extent is fixed by bytes before it: four fixed bytes; `u16` and the hashed
formal/p8/PROOF.md:300|     area; `u16` and the unhashed area; two bytes; and then each MPI's `u16` bit count with ⌈bits/8⌉ bytes.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:301|   - Each subpacket area must be consumed exactly by subpackets whose lengths are in shortest form. The body must
formal/p8/PROOF.md:302|     end exactly after the second MPI.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:303|   - Anything else gives `SIG_FORMAT`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:304|   - So the accepted set is exactly rule O's, and no accepted string has a proper prefix or extension that is also
formal/p8/PROOF.md:305|     accepted at the same slot length.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:306| - **Rule R.** The accepted strings are those of the exact parameter-set length.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:307| - **Opaque.** The accepted strings are those of the slot length.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:308| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:309| In every case the decoder returns the bytes it took, unchanged. It normalizes nothing: no re-framing, no low-s,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:310| no subpacket edits. ∎
formal/p8/PROOF.md:311| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:312| *Remark.* The decoder returns `s` unchanged, so the codec is injective on signatures trivially. What Lemma 7a
formal/p8/PROOF.md:313| adds is that a signature's boundaries are unambiguous, and that the accepted set is pinned. That second fact keeps
formal/p8/PROOF.md:314| an encoder from choosing among serializations, and it makes two verifiers agree on rejection.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:315| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:316| **Lemma 7 (anchor preimage; revised 2026-10-12).** `A(·,·,·,·)` is injective on ordered tuples
formal/p8/PROOF.md:317| `(F0, S0, F1, S1)` with `F_i ∈ Frm(attest)` and `S_i ∈ Sig(alg(F_i), i)`, and
formal/p8/PROOF.md:318| `decode_anchor(A(F0, S0, F1, S1)) = ((F0, S0), (F1, S1))`. Every byte string that `decode_anchor` accepts equals
formal/p8/PROOF.md:319| `A` of its decoded tuple. In particular, `A` of a tuple differs from `A` of any other tuple. That covers each of
formal/p8/PROOF.md:320| these changes:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:321| - the slots swapped;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:322| - the signatures swapped between slots;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:323| - any signature byte replaced;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:324| - one valid signature over a frame replaced by another valid signature over the same frame.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:325| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:326| *Proof.* The header comes first (Lemma 4). Then come the fixed count byte `02`, and for each slot `i` in order:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:327| 1. the length `u32 L_i`, then exactly `L_i` bytes, decoded as a whole frame (Lemma 5). That decode determines
formal/p8/PROOF.md:328|    `alg(F_i)`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:329| 2. the length `u32 M_i`, then exactly `M_i` bytes, decoded by the rule for `(alg(F_i), i)` (Lemma 7a).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:330| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:331| Then the end of input. Each boundary is fixed by bytes already read. The choice of signature rule depends only on
formal/p8/PROOF.md:332| the frame just decoded and the slot position, both already read. No later byte influences an earlier boundary or
formal/p8/PROOF.md:333| rule. So the decoder is a left inverse of `A` on the domain, and `A` is injective. Conversely, an accepted string
formal/p8/PROOF.md:334| is rebuilt exactly by `A` from its decoded tuple, since each field is copied verbatim and each length prefix is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:335| the length of the field after it. ∎
formal/p8/PROOF.md:336| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:337| *Corollary (no fallback).* The withdrawn frame-only preimage begins with `header("tessera-v1/receipt-anchor")`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:338| That tag is not in T, so the decoder rejects it at its header (Lemma 4, `TAG_UNKNOWN`), before any length is read
formal/p8/PROOF.md:339| (XA-09, XR-09).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:340| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:341| **Lemma 8 (snapshot preimage).** `S(·)` is a bijection from snapshot bodies of 1 to 2^24 bytes onto `Snp`. The
formal/p8/PROOF.md:342| proof is Lemma 5's with an opaque body.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:343| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:344| **Lemma 9 (the OpenPGP hash input splits uniquely; narrowed 2026-10-19, P8F-01).** For a v4 OpenPGP signature of
formal/p8/PROOF.md:345| type 0x00 over document `F`, the hashed input is `F ‖ T`, where `T = 04 00 pa ha ‖ u16 h ‖ sub ‖ 04 FF ‖ u32(6 + h)`
formal/p8/PROOF.md:346| (E§3.5) and `|sub| = h`. The map `(F, T) ↦ F ‖ T` is injective over valid trailers: if `F ‖ T = F' ‖ T'` for valid
formal/p8/PROOF.md:347| trailers `T` and `T'`, then `F = F'` and `T = T'`. In particular, for the trailer `T` that a signature packet fixes,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:348| `F ‖ T = F' ‖ T` implies `F = F'`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:349| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:350| *Proof.* A valid trailer ends with `u32(6 + h)`, where `6 + h` is the length of its hashed header `04 00 pa ha ‖ u16
formal/p8/PROOF.md:351| h ‖ sub`. The whole trailer is that header, the two bytes `04 FF` and the four length bytes, so `|T| = 12 + h`:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:352| the final u32 plus six. Two decompositions `F ‖ T = F' ‖ T'` share their last four bytes, so `6 + h = 6 + h'` and
formal/p8/PROOF.md:353| `|T| = |T'|`. Both trailers are then the same-length suffix of one string, so `T = T'` and `F = F'`. (Corrected
formal/p8/PROOF.md:354| 2026-10-19, P8F-05: the final u32 is the hashed-header length, not the trailer's own length; the split is the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:355| final u32 plus six.)
formal/p8/PROOF.md:356| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:357| Type 0x01 is excluded because text mode rewrites line-ending bytes, and those bytes occur in frame headers and
formal/p8/PROOF.md:358| lengths. ∎
formal/p8/PROOF.md:359| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:360| *What Lemma 9 does not say (NARROW-CLAIM, P8F-01).* Until 2026-10-19 this lemma also claimed that if one signature
formal/p8/PROOF.md:361| packet verifies for `F` and for `F'`, then under (H) `F' = F`. That does not follow: verification does not
formal/p8/PROOF.md:362| establish that the two hashes are equal. The falsification review built two distinct accepted attestation frames
formal/p8/PROOF.md:363| whose SHA-256 digests of `F ‖ T` differ (agreeing only in OpenPGP's left 16 bits) and one rule-O packet that
formal/p8/PROOF.md:364| verifies over both under one chosen P-256 key (`prototype/p8-falsify/lemma9-witness.json`). Whether one signature
formal/p8/PROOF.md:365| can verify over two different documents is a property of the signature scheme and of how the key was generated
formal/p8/PROOF.md:366| (P1, P3), not of the encoding. P8 does not claim it. Theorem (ii) uses only the split above; Theorem (iv) never
formal/p8/PROOF.md:367| used Lemma 9, and (iv)(c) already leaves verification to P1 and P3.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:368| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:369| **Remark 10 (no confusion with foreign formats).** Every V1 tagged string begins with a byte in 0x11–0x1d, which
formal/p8/PROOF.md:370| is below 0x20. Each of the following begins with a printable byte:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:371| - a git commit object (`tree …`, 0x74);
formal/p8/PROOF.md:372| - a TXT value of E§7 (`v=`, 0x76);
formal/p8/PROOF.md:373| - RFC 8785 text (`{`, `[`, `"`, a digit, `-`, `t`, `f` or `n`).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:374| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:375| So no V1 tagged string is byte-equal to any of them: a V1 signed document is never also a commit, a DNS value or
formal/p8/PROOF.md:376| RFC 8785 text. (K) keeps the slot keys off those formats. [OWNER 2026-10-19, P8F-01, NARROW-CLAIM] *(Was: "With (K)
formal/p8/PROOF.md:377| this is not needed, but it means that a key reused by mistake still could not have one of its V1 signatures read as
formal/p8/PROOF.md:378| a signature over a commit or a DNS value, or the reverse." Different documents do not by themselves prevent one
formal/p8/PROOF.md:379| signature from verifying over both; that is a signature-scheme property (Lemma 9's note), not P8's.)*
formal/p8/PROOF.md:380| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:381| **Lemma 11 (DNS record).** The unambiguity of the E§7 record is argued in E§7 itself, because it lies outside the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:382| frame domain. In summary:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:383| - the accepted values form a fixed-order regular language over alphabets that exclude the separators, so parsing
formal/p8/PROOF.md:384|   inverts encoding;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:385|   - this includes, since 2026-10-12, the mandatory `issuance-not-before` and `issuance-not-after` (the first was
formal/p8/PROOF.md:386|     optional until the Amendment 9 disposition), whose values are `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`, one spelling per instant;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:387|   - `DNS_WINDOW` (not-after ≤ not-before) and `DNS_WINDOW_LENGTH` (not-after − not-before > 90 days) are checks on
formal/p8/PROOF.md:388|     parsed values and play no part in the split;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:389| - one RR with one character-string removes concatenation choices;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:390| - the owner name is compared as a sequence of labels, without regard to ASCII case.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:391| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:392| ---
formal/p8/PROOF.md:393| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:394| ## 4. Theorem (P8 for `tessera-v1-strict`)
formal/p8/PROOF.md:395| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:396| Let the accepted sets be as in §1.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:397| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:398| - **(i) Injectivity.** These maps are injective:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:399|   - `canonical = JCS` on V;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:400|   - `frame(t, ·)` on `Pay(t)`, and so `v ↦ frame(t, JCS(v))` on the schema-valid values;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:401|   - `A` on ordered (frame, signature) tuples `(F_kms, S_kms, F_gpg, S_gpg)` (Lemmas 7, 7a);
formal/p8/PROOF.md:402|   - `S` on snapshot bodies.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:403| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:404|   Each decoder is the exact inverse of its encoder on the accepted set: `Dec ∘ Enc = id` on accepted structures,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:405|   and `Enc ∘ Dec = id` on accepted bytes. *(Lemmas 3, 5, 7, 7a, 8.)*
formal/p8/PROOF.md:406| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:407|   So the map from an accepted receipt's structure `(M, C, S_kms, S_gpg)` to `(F_M, F_kms, F_gpg, A_sig)` is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:408|   injective outright:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:409|   - `F_M` determines `M`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:410|   - `F_kms` determines `C`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:411|   - `A_sig` determines `S_kms` and `S_gpg`, byte for byte.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:412| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:413|   The receipt is not determined by `(M, C)` alone (§1).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:414| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:415| - **(ii) Boundary-unambiguity.** In every accepted byte string, each field's extent is a function of the bytes
formal/p8/PROOF.md:416|   before it. The end of input is required to fall exactly where the last length prefix says. The JSON payload is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:417|   delimited by the frame's length, never by its own syntax. A signature's extent is fixed by its slot length, and
formal/p8/PROOF.md:418|   it must agree with the signature's own extent. *(Lemmas 5, 7, 7a, 8; Lemma 9 for the split of the OpenPGP hash
formal/p8/PROOF.md:419|   input into frame and trailer.)*
formal/p8/PROOF.md:420| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:421| - **(iii) Type and domain separation.** The accepted sets `Frm(attest)`, `Frm(manifest)`, `Anc` and `Snp` are
formal/p8/PROOF.md:422|   pairwise disjoint (Lemma 4). A decoder for one construction rejects every member of the others (`TAG_MISMATCH`).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:423|   The withdrawn frame-only anchor layout is rejected by every decoder (`TAG_UNKNOWN`; Lemma 7's corollary).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:424| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:425|   Inside `Frm(attest)`, the `kms` and `gpg` slot frames are disjoint, each frame's slot is fixed by its own bytes,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:426|   and an accepted receipt's two frames are distinct and byte-identical on `JCS(C)` (Lemma 6).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:427| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:428|   The DNS value and foreign formats are disjoint from all of these (Remark 10).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:429| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:430| - **(iv) Computational binding, under (H)** *(revised 2026-10-12)*. Each of the following binds only under SHA-256
formal/p8/PROOF.md:431|   collision resistance.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:432|   - A frame's signed bytes determine the manifest frame, the specification, the conformance vectors and the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:433|     preamble, through their SHA-256 values.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:434|   - The OTS-stamped digest `SHA256(A_sig)` determines the ordered tuple `((F_kms, S_kms), (F_gpg, S_gpg))`,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:435|     through Lemma 7: the frames **and the exact signature bytes**, in slot order.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:436| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:437|   So two different such objects bound by one accepted frame or anchor digest yield a SHA-256 collision. This is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:438|   the only place P8 for V1 rests on a cryptographic assumption.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:439| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:440|   **Four statements, kept apart** (finding 10). P8 proves (a) and (b). (c) and (d) are not P8's, and P8 does not
formal/p8/PROOF.md:441|   claim them.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:442|   - **(a) Codec injectivity** (unconditional). `A_sig` decodes to exactly one tuple and is re-encoded from it
formal/p8/PROOF.md:443|     (Lemma 7). A different signature byte string, even a valid one over the same frame, gives a different
formal/p8/PROOF.md:444|     preimage.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:445|   - **(b) Digest binding** (under (H)). A digest determines that tuple. A second tuple with the same digest is a
formal/p8/PROOF.md:446|     SHA-256 collision.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:447|   - **(c) Unforgeability** (P1 and P3, not P8). Whether `S` verifies over `F` under the slot key is a separate
formal/p8/PROOF.md:448|     check. It is made on the committed bytes (E§5.3). Whether a verifying `S` was produced by the key holder
formal/p8/PROOF.md:449|     rests on the signature scheme's security and on key custody.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:450|   - **(d) Temporal composition** (C5, not P8). Suppose valid OTS and Bitcoin evidence shows that
formal/p8/PROOF.md:451|     `SHA256(A_sig)` existed before the selected Bitcoin inclusion block was mined. Then by (b), the exact bytes
formal/p8/PROOF.md:452|     `S_kms` and `S_gpg` existed before that block was mined, under that evidence's own chain-order residuals. Its
formal/p8/PROOF.md:453|     header time T is not a UTC upper bound (A10.1); any UTC statement is separate and conditional on A-UTC
formal/p8/PROOF.md:454|     (A10.1.1), and P8 makes none. [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-01, NARROW-CLAIM]
formal/p8/PROOF.md:455|     - Hence a signature first produced after that block was mined, for example once a key is stolen or the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:456|       algorithm broken, cannot be substituted into this receipt while (H) and the temporal evidence hold.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:457|     - It does **not** follow that the signatures were produced honestly before that block was mined. That needs
formal/p8/PROOF.md:458|       the historical signing, custody and authority assumptions of CODEX-REVIEW findings 7 and 8, which V1 reports
formal/p8/PROOF.md:459|       as not evaluated.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:460|     - *(Was: "existed by time T", "existed by T", "first produced after T", "produced honestly before T"; a
formal/p8/PROOF.md:461|       signature made after a backward-skewed header's nominal UTC time, but before mining, can fit the anchor,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:462|       A10:248-249.)*
formal/p8/PROOF.md:463| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:464| ∎ (from the lemmas)
formal/p8/PROOF.md:465| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:466| **What is not claimed.** P8 does not claim any of the following:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:467| - that signatures are unforgeable, or that keys are bound to identities (P1, P3);
formal/p8/PROOF.md:468| - that a signature verifying over one document cannot also verify over another (Lemma 9's note; P1, P3)
formal/p8/PROOF.md:469|   [OWNER 2026-10-19, P8F-01];
formal/p8/PROOF.md:470| - that a stamp's time bound makes signing honest (iv)(d);
formal/p8/PROOF.md:471| - that the values have any meaning (A3 §A3.1);
formal/p8/PROOF.md:472| - that any value outside V is accepted. It is rejected with the code its first failing check names.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:473| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:474| ---
formal/p8/PROOF.md:475| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:476| ## 5. Evidence: the vectors, and the two-implementation check
formal/p8/PROOF.md:477| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:478| `vectors/gen.py` is implementation A: standard library plus `rfc8785` 0.1.4 for serialization. `vectors/check.py`
formal/p8/PROOF.md:479| is implementation B: standard library only, with its own UTF-8 decoder, JSON parser, ECMAScript number formatter,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:480| JCS serializer and every decoder. Since 2026-10-12, B also has its own OpenPGP signature-packet parser and its
formal/p8/PROOF.md:481| own ECDSA P-256 verifier. The two share no code. They share only Python's Unicode 16.0.0 tables, `float`/`repr`
formal/p8/PROOF.md:482| and `hashlib`'s SHA-256.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:483| - A also uses `hmac` (RFC 6979 nonces, pinned by RFC 6979 A.2.5) and SHA-1, both only to *make* the vector
formal/p8/PROOF.md:484|   signatures.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:485| - SHA-1 fills OpenPGP's issuer-fingerprint subpacket. No check reads it, and B never computes it.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:486| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:487| | Lemma | Golden vectors | Rejection vectors |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:488| |---|---|---|
formal/p8/PROOF.md:489| | 1 (strings) | C-04, C-05, C-06 | XC-13 to XC-22, XC-28, XC-29 |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:490| | 2 (numbers) | N-01 to N-22 (RFC 8785 Appendix B), C-03, C-10, C-N01 to C-N22 | XC-03 to XC-12, XC-31 to XC-33, XF-27 |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:491| | 3 (canonical payload) | C-01 to C-09 | XC-01, XC-02, XC-23 to XC-27, XC-30, XF-23 to XF-30, XF-48 |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:492| | 4, 5 (tags, frames) | F-01 to F-03, M-01 | XF-01 to XF-22, XF-31 to XF-47, XF-49 to XF-51 |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:493| | 6 (signer frames) | F-01/F-02, R-01 | XR-01 to XR-05 |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:494| | 7 (anchor) | A-01, A-02, R-01 | XA-01 to XA-10, XA-30, XR-06 to XR-09, XR-15 |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:495| | 7a (signature slots) | SIG-01, SIG-02, A-01, A-02 | XA-11 to XA-29, XA-31, XA-32 |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:496| | (iv)(a) negative controls | R-01 | XR-10 to XR-14: a valid signature that is not the committed one fails the anchor check |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:497| | E§5.3 verification stage (P3, not P8) | R-01 | XR-16 (`SIG_INVALID`), XR-17 (`KEY_MISMATCH`) |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:498| | 8 (snapshot) | S-01 | XS-01 to XS-04 |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:499| | 11 (DNS) | DNS-01 to DNS-03; K-01, K-02 (fingerprints) | XD-01 to XD-33 |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:500| | E§7.1 issuance window (C4 rule, not P8) | W-01 (T = not-after), W-02 (declared = not-before); DNS-02 (window exactly 90 days) | XW-01 (T = not-after + 1 s), XW-02, XW-03; XD-23, XD-24 (`DNS_WINDOW`), XD-25, XD-26 (not-after missing), XD-31 (not-before missing), XD-32 (90 days + 1 s), XD-33 (one year) (`DNS_WINDOW_LENGTH`) |
formal/p8/PROOF.md:501| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:502| **Counts:** 71 golden vectors and 173 rejection vectors. On 2026-10-09 they were 66 and 126. The changes:
formal/p8/PROOF.md:503| - golden: SIG-01, SIG-02 and A-02 are added, and so are W-01 and W-02 (the window follow-up);
formal/p8/PROOF.md:504| - rejection: XA-09 to XA-32 and XR-09 to XR-17 are added, and so are XD-23 to XD-30 and XW-01 to XW-03 (the
formal/p8/PROOF.md:505|   window follow-up);
formal/p8/PROOF.md:506| - DNS-01 to DNS-03, XD-03, XD-05, XD-16 and XD-22 are regenerated for the window grammar;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:507| - for the 90-day single window (Amendment 9 disposition): XD-31 to XD-33 are added; DNS-01 to DNS-03, W-01, W-02,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:508|   XW-01 to XW-03 and the XD vectors built on the canonical value are regenerated; XD-30 (fractional seconds) no
formal/p8/PROOF.md:509|   longer fits one character-string and is now `DNS_STRINGS`;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:510| - A-01, R-01 and every vector built from the anchor are regenerated for `A_sig`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:511| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:512| **Golden anchor digests.**
formal/p8/PROOF.md:513| - A-01 = R-01's anchor = `06caaf1a462b150f7f5b4a02691da1216259a5a080ad77dcfe1ffefd16ec64e4`. A-01 is 1932 bytes
formal/p8/PROOF.md:514|   and holds two 119-byte signatures. The frame-only A-01 of 2026-10-09 was `2d1e760f…4771427`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:515| - A-02 (canary) = `1d9f006cfca4e80eb87bd88eb20944b8dba2e5256ffe996f38f9ab27cfd91583`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:516| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:517| The output is deterministic: RFC 6979 nonces, and regeneration reproduces both files byte for byte.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:518| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:519| **Signatures.** The signatures are real ECDSA P-256 signatures in OpenPGP v4 packets.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:520| - The keys are public test keys: d = 1 (G, slot kms) and d = 2 (2G, slot gpg), as in K-01 and K-02.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:521| - The packet layout is the one GnuPG 2.4.4 emits.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:522| - A signs. A and B each verify with their own ECDSA code: A uses affine coordinates and B Jacobian, and each
formal/p8/PROOF.md:523|   builds its own OpenPGP hash input.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:524| - **External cross-check** (2026-10-12, by hand in a scratch GnuPG home, not part of the scripts). GnuPG 2.4.4
formal/p8/PROOF.md:525|   reported "Good signature" for SIG-01, SIG-02 and all five negative-control signatures: XR-10 (a second
formal/p8/PROOF.md:526|   nonce), XR-11 and XR-14 (`(r, n − s)`), XR-12 (an edited unhashed area) and XR-13 (signed five years later).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:527|   It reported "BAD signature" for a gpg-slot signature checked over the kms frame. A signature that GnuPG made
formal/p8/PROOF.md:528|   with its own fresh key also passes rule O.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:529| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:530| **Result** (2026-10-12; rerun after the 90-day window change, same day).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:531| - A self-checks every vector. Each negative control is asserted at generation: the presented signature verifies,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:532|   and its anchor digest differs from the stamped one.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:533| - B round-trips all **71/71** golden vectors. That includes re-parsing and re-verifying SIG-01 and SIG-02, and
formal/p8/PROOF.md:534|   verifying both committed signatures of R-01.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:535| - B rejects all **173/173** rejection vectors **with the same reason code as A**.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:536|   - B's window check uses its own days-from-civil arithmetic, not `datetime`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:537|   - It matched `datetime` on 20,000 random instants (a manual check).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:538| - B independently confirms the **5/5** negative controls: the signature verifies, and the anchor check fails.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:539| - `vectors/fuzz.py` runs 60,000 seeded differential cases, and **there were 0 disagreements** in verdict, reason
formal/p8/PROOF.md:540|   code, canonical bytes or decoded anchor tuples.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:541|   - Stages 1 and 2 (40,000 cases: JSON and frames) are unchanged from 2026-10-09. Their verdict histogram
formal/p8/PROOF.md:542|     reproduces that run exactly.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:543|   - Stage 3 adds 20,000 composite-anchor cases: byte edits biased to the signature slots and length prefixes,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:544|     and structural substitutions, duplications, truncations, re-framings and swaps. Its verdicts: 3858 accepted;
formal/p8/PROOF.md:545|     the rest rejected across 13 reason codes, including `SIG_EMPTY`, `SIG_PACKET`, `SIG_FORMAT`, `LENGTH_CAP`,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:546|     `TRUNCATED` and `TRAILING`.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:547| - *Sensitivity check* (by hand, on scratch copies). Two planted defects in B were each caught by the agreement
formal/p8/PROOF.md:548|   run: accepting a non-minimal `0x89` header (XA-20), and skipping signature verification (XR-16).
formal/p8/PROOF.md:549| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:550| **Falsification pass repairs** (2026-10-19, P8F-02 to P8F-04). The review found three places where B did not match
formal/p8/PROOF.md:551| E§1: an uncaught `ValueError` on accepted literals whose exponent exceeds Python's integer digit limit (`0e` and 4301
formal/p8/PROOF.md:552| nines); `JSON_SYNTAX` for a BOM followed by invalid UTF-8, where E§1.4 requires `JSON_ENCODING`; and no size cap in
formal/p8/PROOF.md:553| the standalone `payload_value`. B now clamps exponents of more than 18 significant digits (within the payload-size bound, no
formal/p8/PROOF.md:554| nonzero literal with such an exponent rounds to a finite, nonzero binary64 value; zero-valued literals are handled
formal/p8/PROOF.md:555| separately) [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-13] *(was: "no nonzero such literal is finite or nonzero as a double, and zero is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:556| decided first")*, decodes UTF-8 before the BOM check, and rejects a
formal/p8/PROOF.md:557| standalone payload above 2^24 bytes with `LENGTH_CAP`. The owner found the same three defects in A and repaired
formal/p8/PROOF.md:558| them the same way; A's old direct-decision bound (|exponent| > 100000) also wrongly rejected value-preserving
formal/p8/PROOF.md:559| literals such as `1` + 200000 zeros + `e-200000`, and now applies only above 18 exponent digits.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:560| `vectors/test_check.py` pins each reproduction for A and B. The rerun after the repair: B 71/71, 173/173 and 5/5
formal/p8/PROOF.md:561| baseline, 35/35, 63/63, 1/1 and 6/6 hybrid; A regenerates all four vector files byte for byte (checked in a
formal/p8/PROOF.md:562| scratch copy); `fuzz.py` 60,000 + 90,400 cases, 0 disagreements. No vector changed.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:563| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:564| The fuzz found one real defect in A before the 2026-10-09 vectors were frozen. A raised an uncaught `decimal`
formal/p8/PROOF.md:565| error on literals with exponents beyond about 10^18. A now decides those directly, and XC-31, XC-32 and C-10 pin
formal/p8/PROOF.md:566| the case.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:567| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:568| **Reproduce:**
formal/p8/PROOF.md:569| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:570| ```
formal/p8/PROOF.md:571| uv run --no-project --with rfc8785==0.1.4 python formal/p8/vectors/gen.py
formal/p8/PROOF.md:572| python3 formal/p8/vectors/check.py
formal/p8/PROOF.md:573| uv run --no-project --with rfc8785==0.1.4 python formal/p8/vectors/fuzz.py
formal/p8/PROOF.md:574| ```
formal/p8/PROOF.md:575| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:576| Python 3.14 is needed, for its Unicode 16.0.0 tables.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:577| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:578| ## 6. Limits of this evidence
formal/p8/PROOF.md:579| 
formal/p8/PROOF.md:580| - The proof is prose. A reader checks it lemma by lemma, and nothing has machine-checked it. Lean was judged
formal/p8/PROOF.md:581|   unnecessary: every lemma is a decoder-inverts-encoder argument over a fixed grammar.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:582| - "Two implementations agree" is weaker than independence. Both come from one author instance on one runtime, and
formal/p8/PROOF.md:583|   they share the Unicode tables and float conversion. The V1 build is the registered second encoder (V1-DERIVATION
formal/p8/PROOF.md:584|   §5), and it must reproduce these bytes.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:585| - (N) is assumed, not tested exhaustively. N-01 to N-22 check it against RFC 8785's own Appendix B values.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:586| - The golden fingerprints (K-01 `spki-sha256`, K-02 `gpg-sha256`) use the P-256 points G and 2G, and the spec,
formal/p8/PROOF.md:587|   vector, preamble and snapshot bytes are marked ILLUSTRATIVE. The real values come from the real keys and
formal/p8/PROOF.md:588|   documents at the freeze. The layouts do not change.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:589| - The vector signatures are mathematically real, but their private keys are 1 and 2, so anyone can forge them.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:590|   They show encoding, binding and the negative control. They say nothing about unforgeability, which is (iv)(c)
formal/p8/PROOF.md:591|   and not P8 in any case.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:592| - Rule R (raw FIPS 204/205) has no vectors and is not implemented in either codec, because no PQ id is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:593|   registered. It must get golden and rejection vectors, and an agreement run, when one is. *[OWNER 2026-10-19
formal/p8/PROOF.md:594|   annotation: superseded for the hybrid branch by HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT §8 (registered 2026-10-16): the pair id is
formal/p8/PROOF.md:595|   registered, both codecs implement rule R, and `vectors/hybrid-golden.json` (35) and `vectors/hybrid-reject.json`
formal/p8/PROOF.md:596|   (63) pass the agreement run. The bullet is kept as baseline text, as the supplement directs.]*
formal/p8/PROOF.md:597| - The GnuPG cross-check is a manual record, not a scripted step.
formal/p8/PROOF.md:598| - Number rule D-1 is registered by A9.8 for `tessera-v1-strict` (ENCODING-V1 §9), so Lemma 2(c) is stated against
formal/p8/PROOF.md:599|   the registered rule. [OWNER 2026-10-19, G38] *(Was: "Number rule D-1 is not registered yet … If the author keeps
formal/p8/PROOF.md:600|   the literal rule instead, Lemma 2(c) fails as stated …"; the contingency no longer arises.)*

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:21| ## What this document is for, and what it is not
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:22| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:23| This is the one place an implementer of the V1 verifier or issuer can read what V1 requires. It lists the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:24| requirements, and each one points to where it was decided (source section and rule name; line numbers are
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:25| locators only, section 0). Together with A9 and ENCODING-V1 it is intended to be **sufficient with the frozen
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:26| catalog, the authenticated trust configuration and the pinned normative dependencies**; those external immutable
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:27| inputs do not disappear. [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F17, r2-14.2] *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: previously "each one
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:28| points to the line where it was decided"; that overstated it where a requirement points only to a later owner tag.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:29| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:30| It is mostly an extraction. Where a rule is already decided, the source is tagged. Where it is not, the gap is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:31| marked `OPEN` and says what must be decided. It also records a small number of **new** choices that no source makes;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:32| each is labelled `OWNER PROFILE DECISION 2026-10-13`, is listed in section 0.1, and is not an A9 citation. It does not restate the byte encoding: for that, read
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:33| `formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md`. It does not hold operating numbers (window dates, stop margins, hardware): those are in
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:34| `docs/V1-OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md` and are not profile rules. It is not the 2929-line spec, which stays as the design
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:35| reference and is synced after V1.

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:96| ## 1. Profile identity
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:97| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:98| - **Profile id:** `tessera-v1-strict`. It appears in the signed bytes as `common.profile` and in the DNS and git
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:99|   record as `profile=`. [ENC §3.2:264; ENC §7:569; A9:148]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:100| - **Spec binding:** `common.spec.id` is `tessera-v1-strict/verification-spec/1` and `common.spec.sha256` is the hash
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:101|   of the specification bytes. [ENC §3.2:265-266]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:102|   - `common.spec.id` other than that value gives `INVALID / SPEC_ID`. The verifier compiles in a **frozen spec
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:103|     catalog**; a `common.spec.sha256` not in it gives `UNVERIFIABLE / SPEC_UNKNOWN`. The signed `vectors_sha256` and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:104|     `preamble_sha256` must equal the catalog entry (`INVALID / SPEC_OBJECT_MISMATCH`), and the bundled `spec`,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:105|     `vectors`, `preamble` and `dependency_manifest` bytes must hash to their signed or catalog values
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:106|     (`INVALID / BUNDLE_OBJECT_HASH`). Bundled objects are hashed, never parsed as policy or executed. The spec and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:107|     vectors objects are assembled by the part format of section 15.8. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G13]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:108|   - **Comparison targets** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F12]. Bundled spec → signed `common.spec.sha256`; bundled vectors →
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:109|     signed `vectors_sha256`; bundled preamble → signed `preamble_sha256`, each independently of catalog lookup
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:110|     (`BUNDLE_OBJECT_HASH`). Signed `vectors_sha256` / `preamble_sha256` → catalog entry only if the spec lookup
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:111|     succeeds (`SPEC_OBJECT_MISMATCH`). Bundled dependency manifest → catalog entry only if the lookup succeeds;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:112|     otherwise that comparison is unperformable, never compared with an unrelated entry. Other independent failures
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:113|     still dominate `SPEC_UNKNOWN`. Bundled objects never become policy because their hashes are self-consistent.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:114|     *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: "must hash to their signed or catalog values" did not say which comparisons
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:115|     remain performable for an unknown spec hash.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:116|   - **Catalog entry** (one, for V1): the frozen object hashes; exactly one `alg` id (`OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:117|     under the fallback, or the registered pair id under the hybrid); `alg_prohibited` = `[]`; `binding_forms` =
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:118|     `["STMT_DIRECT"]`; D, δ, ε, k; the UTC-assessment constants Δ = 7200 s and m = 6 (section 7.4) [OWNER 2026-10-19,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:119|     A10.1.1; A10:284-285; A10 row 22]; DNSSEC algorithms {8, 13} and DS digest types {2, 4}. A well-formed `common.alg`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:120|     other than the catalog id, including the branch not taken, gives `UNVERIFIABLE / ALG_UNKNOWN`. The catalog is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:121|     independent of the bundle and of trust-configuration updates, and later verifiers apply it unchanged to V1
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:122|     bundles (A9.4, A9.7 row 29). [OWNER 2026-10-14, G12]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:123|   - **Codec-known versus policy-supported** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F01]: "Each frame is decoded with E §5.2's codec
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:124|     registry, including any authorized supplement, using its own alg and slot. A codec-known but unselected branch
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:125|     still uses its specified codec; an id absent from that registry uses the opaque codec. Signature/possession
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:126|     verification semantics are performed only for the catalog-supported id. Receipt/manifest alg equality is checked
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:127|     independently for every syntactically valid id. M5's catalog-alg condition is performable only for a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:128|     policy-supported id; unsupported ids contribute ALG_UNKNOWN, not an additional SCHEMA failure." The incorporated
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:129|     codec baseline and its vectors are unchanged.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:130|   - **Branch-not-taken id before registration.** Until a dated branch-registration supplement registers the hybrid
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:131|     pair id, that id (or any stand-in for it) is absent from the codec registry: its frames use the opaque codec and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:132|     the outcome is `UNVERIFIABLE / ALG_UNKNOWN`, with signature and possession semantics unperformable and M5's alg
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:133|     condition contributing `ALG_UNKNOWN`, not `SCHEMA`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, EA-09]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:134|   - **Baseline.** The governing baseline is the frozen spec object hash in the catalog. A9 incorporates ENCODING-V1 at
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:135|     its signing commit; a frozen edited ENCODING-V1 replaces it only with authorized change accounting.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:136|     [OWNER 2026-10-14, G37]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:137| - **Encoding:** `formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md` at the signing commit, including D-1 to D-17. If the hybrid signer
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:138|   branch is taken, the signing-commit baseline plus the dated branch-registration supplement governs. [A9:149-150;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:139|   A9:395-400]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:140| - **Mode:** strict only. One layer. No wrappers, no renewal, no TLR, no waiver policy. `VALID_DEGRADED` is never

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:142| - **Claim and sub-claims:** C1 to C7 as in A9:128-146. This document does not restate them.

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:147|   N and S govern the issuer only. δ, ε and k are frozen catalog constants, not trust-configuration data.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:148|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, G12]

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:156| ## 2. Bundle format
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:157| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:158| ### 2.1 Members
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:159| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:160| A V1 bundle carries these twelve members. Nothing is taken from outside the bundle except the trust configuration
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:161| (section 5). The last column is the container member that carries each one (section 15.1). [OWNER 2026-10-14, G14,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:162| G17]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:163| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:164| | # | Member | Source | Container member |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:165| |---|---|---|---|
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:166| | 1 | Unsigned profile label (read first, for dispatch) | [ENC §8:742-743] | top-level `profile` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:167| | 2 | The receipt tuple `(F_kms, S_kms, F_gpg, S_gpg)`, or `A_sig`, which encodes it | [ENC §5.3:493-497] | `a_sig` only (one tuple route) |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:168| | 3 | The manifest frame `F_manifest` and each key's possession signature over it | [ENC §4:362-369; A9:364-366] | `manifest`, `possession` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:169| | 4 | The two public keys, checked against the manifest fingerprints | [ENC §5.3:509] | `keys` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:170| | 5 | The DNSSEC snapshot (envelope per ENC §6) and its own OTS proof | [ENC §6:536-542; DD:94] | `dns` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:171| | 6 | The git key-assertion evidence: raw signed commit object, the tree objects on the path, the blob, and the OTS proof stamped on the commit id | [ENC §7.2:706-710; A9:297-299] | `git` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:172| | 7 | The receipt's OTS proof and the anchor transaction id | [SPEC R-3.42:679-682] | `receipt_anchor` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:173| | 8 | Bitcoin block headers needed by the proof, each of which must be in the pinned set | [A9:156; DD:99] | `headers` (one pool) |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:174| | 9 | The verification specification bytes (content-addressed) | [A9:158-159; ENC §3.2:281] | `spec` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:175| | 10 | The conformance vector bytes (content-addressed) | [A9:158-159; ENC §3.2:281] | `vectors` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:176| | 11 | The plain-language purpose preamble, bound by hash in the signed bytes | [A9:159; ENC §3.2:281] | `preamble` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:177| | 12 | The dependency manifest (section 9) | [A9:159-160] | `dependency_manifest` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:178| | — | Observed anchor delay and issue-time policy version (R-3.46), optional diagnostics | [SPEC R-3.46:698-700] | `issuer_record` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:179| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:180| - Members 9, 10 and 11 are bound by SHA-256 of their raw bytes, inside the signed common bytes. They are never signed
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:181|   or anchored on their own. [ENC §0:71-72; ENC §3.2:281]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:182| - The OTS proof, txid, headers and confirmation evidence are outside `A_sig`. [ENC §5:402-405]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:183| - The txid sits in the bundle outside the signed bytes. [SPEC R-3.43:685-687]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:184| - **Container.** One canonical JCS JSON text, no JSON numbers, top level exactly
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:185|   `{"layers":[L],"profile":"tessera-v1-strict"}`, with the closed layer schema of section 15.1. ~~A required member
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:186|   that is absent, at any nesting level, gives `UNVERIFIABLE / MEMBER_MISSING:<path>`; this rule precedes the generic
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:187|   schema rule.~~ *(Withdrawn 2026-10-14, r2-F03: it contradicted the `object_format` and `issuer_record`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:188|   exceptions and left a null parent ambiguous.)* **Absence and presence** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F03]: "A missing
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:189|   required evidence member contributes UNVERIFIABLE/MEMBER_MISSING:<path>, except git.object_format, which
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:190|   contributes GIT_OBJECT_FORMAT_MISSING. A present parent of the wrong type contributes CONTAINER_SCHEMA; do not
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:191|   synthesize missing descendants beneath it. Absence of issuer_record is allowed; any defect in a present
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:192|   issuer_record, including absent internal fields, contributes INVALID/CONTAINER_SCHEMA. Absence and schema failures
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:193|   are collected independently; INVALID still dominates. Nested absence is inspected only beneath correctly typed
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:194|   parents." `<path>` is the layer-relative dotted schema path (`git`, `git.ots`, `keys.gpg`; array members by
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:195|   numeric index); several missing paths are compared in JCS key order with array indices numeric. A present
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:196|   `git.object_format` that is a JSON string other than `"sha1"` is A9.5's unsupported value (`UNVERIFIABLE /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:197|   GIT_OBJECT_FORMAT`); a present non-string value, `null` included, is a schema failure (`INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:198|   CONTAINER_SCHEMA`), not absence (**owner choice**, fail-closed; the honest issuer emits `"sha1"`). A present
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:199|   nonconforming member or an unnamed member gives `INVALID / CONTAINER_SCHEMA`. The receipt
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:200|   tuple is taken only by decoding `a_sig`. Re-indenting a container makes it `INVALID / JSON_NONCANONICAL`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:201|   (a visible custody restriction: keep the bytes, do not reformat). [OWNER 2026-10-14, G14, G17] *(Was:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:202|   "`OPEN (other):` the container and transport encoding, member names and member order", 2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:203| - **Observed delay and policy version** are carried in the optional `issuer_record` member: unsigned diagnostics.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:204|   Absence never affects the verdict; a present record is schema-checked (`INVALID / CONTAINER_SCHEMA`); its values
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:205|   never alter verification parameters and are not authenticated observations. The honest issuer always emits it.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:206|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, G33] *(Was: "`OPEN (other):` where the observed anchor delay and the issue-time policy version
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:207|   are recorded", 2026-10-13.)*

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:213| ## 3. Verifier dispatch, stages and precedence
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:214| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:215| ### 3.1 Dispatch
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:216| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:217| 1. The verifier reads the bundle's unsigned profile label first. An unrecognized label gives
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:218|    `UNVERIFIABLE / OUT_OF_PROFILE`, and nothing else is evaluated. [ENC §8:742-743; A9:287]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:219| 2. Out-of-profile layer structure or request gives the same result without evaluation. [DD:70; A9:287]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:220|    Cases c (two-layer transplant) and h (renewal wrapper) land here. [A9:179, 185]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:221| 3. **Dispatch reads exactly three things**, in order, and nothing else [OWNER 2026-10-14, G17]:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:222|    - **D1.** The bytes are not strict JSON (ENC §1.4 checks 1–5), or exceed 2^27 bytes: `UNVERIFIABLE /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:223|      OUT_OF_PROFILE`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:224|    - **D2.** Top-level `profile` absent or not exactly `tessera-v1-strict`: same.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:225|    - **D3.** `layers` not an array of length 1: same (cases c and h).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:226|    - **D4.** The request policy is a **verifier input**, never a bundle member; its only value is `strict`. Any other
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:227|      request: `UNVERIFIABLE / OUT_OF_PROFILE`, detail `REQUEST_UNSUPPORTED`, with no evaluation (case d1's waiver
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:228|      refused).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:229|    *(Was: "`OPEN (step 8):` what exactly dispatch inspects … Decide the fields dispatch reads, and where the request
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:230|    type lives", 2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:231| 4. Once dispatched to `tessera-v1-strict`, every codec rejection is `INVALID`. That includes a signed `profile` other
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:232|    than `tessera-v1-strict`, an unknown tag and an unknown canonicalization version. [ENC §8:744-746]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:233| 5. The one **codec-level** in-profile `UNVERIFIABLE` that concerns the bytes is a well-formed unknown `alg`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:234|    [ENC §8:747-748; SPEC R-2.37:308] The profile adds further in-profile `UNVERIFIABLE` outcomes (missing members,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:235|    unknown spec hash, binding forms, and the evidence outcomes below); they are not turned `INVALID` by this
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:236|    sentence. [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-contra] *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: previously "The one in-profile
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:237|    `UNVERIFIABLE` …", repeating ENC §8's stale wording, which G01 already requires to say "codec-level".)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:238| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:239| ### 3.2 Stages
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:240| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:241| The stage names follow the spec's. The spec registers no order between stages, only that the verdict does not
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:242| depend on evaluation order. [SPEC:1237-1248; SPEC R-5.16:1250] There are ten stages after dispatch. The
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:243| table presents ENC/SPEC material; it is not a newly fixed execution order (section 0.1, item 6).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:244| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:245| | Stage | What V1 does | Source |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:246| |---|---|---|
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:247| | (a) Parse | Decode every frame, the manifest and `A_sig` under ENC §1 to §5. Reason codes are reported in ENC's order. | [ENC §1.4:172-190; ENC §3.1:241-248; ENC §5:385-394] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:248| | (b) Type | Tag must be in T and be the expected one: `TAG_UNKNOWN`, `TAG_MISMATCH`. No wrapper stage: one layer only. | [ENC §2:215-218; A9:161] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:249| | (c) Algorithm | A well-formed unknown `common.alg` gives `UNVERIFIABLE`. A malformed, missing or substituted id gives `INVALID`. | [ENC §3.2:276; SPEC V13-V15:1282-1284] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:250| | (d) Key binding | Each presented key hashes to its slot's manifest fingerprint (`KEY_MISMATCH`). `manifest_sha256` equals the hash of the manifest frame. | [ENC §5.3:509; ENC §3.2:280] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:251| | (e) Authority | DNS channel and git channel (section 6), the issuance window, possession proofs. | [A9:143; A9:419-421] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:252| | (f) Signature set | Both slots are required, from the signed manifest, never from what the bundle presents. Common bytes are byte-equal across slots. | [SPEC V28-V31:1327-1330; ENC §3.4:303-320] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:253| | (g) Integrity | `SHA256(A_sig)` is the digest the OTS evidence attests. Each committed `S` verifies over its committed `F`. Any difference from the committed tuple gives `RECEIPT_ANCHOR_MISMATCH`; a bad signature gives `SIG_INVALID`. | [ENC §5.3:498-511] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:254| | (h) Temporal | The three-conjunct predicate at k = 6, plus the T rule (section 7). | [A9:144; SPEC V33-V36:1342-1346; SPEC R-5.19:1352] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:255| | (i) Revocation | Not evaluated. The report says so. | [A9:255-258] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:256| | (j) Partition | Section 3.3. | [SPEC R-5.25:1368] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:257| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:258| - The issuance-window check is part of stage (e) (C4). [A9:419-421; ENC §7.1:636-643]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:259| - **Reported reason.** The reported reason is the first failed check in the **total check order** of section 15.7;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:260|   if none failed, the first unperformable check in that order. The order is a reporting order, not an execution
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:261|   order. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G31] *(Was: "`OPEN (step 8):` which reason code is reported when several different
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:262|   checks fail", 2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:263| - **`DNS_*` record class.** A TXT RRset that is present is run through ENC §7's fifteen-step order; every failure is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:264|   `INVALID` with ENC's code, whether or not DNSSEC was performable. An absent TXT group is `UNVERIFIABLE /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:265|   DNS_EVIDENCE_MISSING`. ENC's `DNS_RRSET` zero case stays a codec vector, unreachable from a V1 container.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:266|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, G24] *(Was: "`OPEN (step 8):` the verdict class of the `DNS_*` record rejections", 2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:267| - **Size gates.** An empty snapshot body or a payload over its cap gives `LENGTH_CAP`, before the JSON categories.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:268|   The gates are exact and separate: container 2^27 bytes, payload per ENC §1, snapshot body 2^24. [OWNER 2026-10-14,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:269|   G30] For an empty snapshot body this profile governs over ENC §6's `1 ≤ len` wording and over
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:270|   `formal/p8/vectors/gen.py` (`decode_snapshot`, which reports `SCHEMA`): the outcome is `INVALID / LENGTH_CAP`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:271|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, EA-20]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:272| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:273| ### 3.3 Precedence and verdicts
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:274| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:275| - Order of decision: any required check failed gives `INVALID`; else any required check unperformable gives
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:276|   `UNVERIFIABLE`; else `VALID_STRICT`. There is no waiver set, so the degraded branch never applies. [SPEC
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:277|   R-5.25:1368; A9:161]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:278| - `INVALID` dominates `UNVERIFIABLE`. [A9:182; SPEC R-5.26:1370; SPEC R-2.33:300] Case d3 depends on it.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:279| - The unperformable rule applies to required checks only. [SPEC R-2.32:298]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:280| - A verdict is never a bare boolean. `UNVERIFIABLE` is never promoted. [SPEC R-2.34:302; SPEC R-5.38:1394]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:281| - No fallback, negotiation or normalization during verification. [SPEC R-5.18:1266; ENC §1.2:156-158]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:282| - **Aggregation.** Physical evaluation order is unrestricted, but reporting uses the fixed total check order (section
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:283|   15.7). Early termination is permitted only when every earlier-priority reportable check is settled and every
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:284|   stable field, including T, is determined. A failure prevents only checks whose own necessary input cannot be
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:285|   obtained; it does not suppress independent receipt-anchor evaluation needed for T. Derived checks are unperformable
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:286|   when necessary inputs cannot be obtained, and never pass by default. ~~An unknown `alg` routes the slot as opaque
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:287|   (Lemma 7a)~~: signature and possession semantics under an `alg` other than the catalog-supported id are
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:288|   unperformable; independent schema and hash checks still run. Codec routing is section 1's codec-known versus
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:289|   policy-supported rule. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G26; r2-F01] *Dated correction 2026-10-14: the resolutions draft's "a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:290|   verifier may stop early only on a failed check" is withdrawn; it let two schedules report different stable
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:291|   fields. Dated correction 2026-10-14 (r2-F01): "an unknown `alg` routes the slot as opaque" is withdrawn; it
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:292|   conflicted with ENC's codec selection for a codec-known but unselected id.*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:293| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:294| ### 3.4 Output
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:295| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:296| Every report carries these six fields, and they are the stable set that later verifiers must reproduce: the verdict,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:297| its reason code, T, `revocation`, `historical_security` and standing. [A9:162; A9:268-283]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:298| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:299| - `revocation: NOT_EVALUATED`. [A9:255-258]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:300| - `historical_security: NOT_EVALUATED`. The documentation names what a later examiner must supply: an authenticated
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:301|   safe-before cutoff per algorithm and per key, compared with T and A2.1's chain-time uncertainty. [A9:259-265]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:302| - Standing: `ABSENT/NOT_ISSUED_IN_PROFILE`, reported separately and never folded in. [A9:172-173; SPEC R-1.16:163]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:303| - No aggregate checkmark. [SPEC R-5.47:1419]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:304| - **Report encoding.** The stable-output object is the JCS object `{"historical_security":"NOT_EVALUATED",
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:305|   "reason","revocation":"NOT_EVALUATED","standing":"ABSENT/NOT_ISSUED_IN_PROFILE","T","verdict"}`; the success
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:306|   reason is `OK`. T is the RFC 3339 string of nTime(h*) when the receipt proof parses, its file digest equals SHA256
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:307|   of the presented `a_sig` bytes, no attestation in it is contradicted, and it has a qualifying attestation;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:308|   otherwise `null`. T is reported whatever the verdict. Diagnostics (trust-config version and hash, spec hash,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:309|   per-check list) go in a separate wrapper object, outside the stable six. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G32]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:310| - **UTC assessment** (outside the stable field set) [OWNER 2026-10-19, A10.1.1; A10:300-305; A10 row 22]. Every
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:311|   receipt-verdict report, including a D1–D4 terminal report, contains the object `utc_assessment` =
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:312|   `{"assumption_id":"A-UTC-7200-6","utc_upper_bound":U}`, defined in section 7.4. For D1–D4 its `utc_upper_bound`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:313|   is null. Startup refusals produce no receipt-verdict report. [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-03] *(Was: "Every report
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:314|   reached after dispatch also carries the object …", which left D1–D4 reports undecided.)* It is never a member of the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:315|   stable-output object, never one of the six stable fields, never enters the verdict, the reason code or the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:316|   section 15.7 check order, and later verifiers are not bound to reproduce it as a stable field. It is reported
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:317|   with every verdict, `INVALID` and `UNVERIFIABLE` included; a value reported with `INVALID` or `UNVERIFIABLE` does
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:318|   not establish a valid service receipt or valid service signatures (A10:303-304). Documentation and relying-party
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:319|   text never state U without the A-UTC identifier and the assumption beside it (A10:304-305).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:320| - **T for dispatch-terminal outcomes.** A D1–D4 outcome (section 3.1) evaluates nothing, the receipt proof
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:321|   included, so its T is `null`; this holds for D4 too, even when the same bundle bytes under a strict request would
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:322|   give a T. "T is reported whatever the verdict" applies to every outcome reached after dispatch.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:323|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, EA-05] Its `utc_upper_bound` is likewise `null` (section 7.4).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:324|   [OWNER 2026-10-19, A10.1.1]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:325| - Relying-party text must say that a U reported with `INVALID` or `UNVERIFIABLE` is not evidence of a valid service
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:326|   receipt, and must state A-UTC beside every U. [OWNER 2026-10-19, A10.1.1; A10:303-305]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:327| - Relying-party text must say that a T reported with `INVALID` is not evidence of a valid service receipt.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:328|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, G32]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:329| - Relying-party text must say that `INVALID / ISSUANCE_WINDOW` can come from presenting a later proof, and that the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:330|   holder should be asked for the issuer's original proof. [A9:425-426]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:331| - Relying-party text must say that the verifier cannot check public publication of the git commit. [A9:495-500]

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:333| ### 3.5 Verifier CLI and release-provisioning interface (instrument level)
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:334| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:335| **Interface convention, not a verdict rule.** This subsection records how the conformance suite and the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:336| differential harness drive a verifier under test. It changes no verdict, reason or T, binds no production release,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:337| and gives way to the release artefact and release-signature format when those are decided (section 14.2 items 1,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:338| 2). Both implementations of differential run 1 used it. [OWNER 2026-10-14, interface convention from diff-1,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:339| EA-01/EA-02/EA-03/EA-12] *The release format is now section 15.9. The TEST provisioning below is an instrument
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:340| interface only: it is never a release, and an installed production verifier refuses it (section 15.9 R4).*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:341| [OWNER 2026-10-19, §14.2 item 2, `docs/V1-FREEZE-OPEN.md` §3]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:342| - **Invocation and compiled-in inputs (EA-01).** `CMD --trust <config> --bundle <bundle>`. The compiled-in trust
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:343|   configuration hash and catalog (section 1, section 5) are provisioned for TEST by environment: the TEST release
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:344|   record from `TESSERA_V1_TEST_RELEASE`, authenticated by the public key in `TESSERA_V1_TEST_RELEASE_KEY`, and the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:345|   catalog from `TESSERA_V1_TEST_CATALOG`. A config whose hash is not the one compiled by an authentically signed
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:346|   release is refused (`TRUST_CONFIG_UNAUTHENTICATED`, no verdict).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:347| - **Request (EA-02).** The request (D4) is `strict` by default; `--request <value>` supplies any other value.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:348| - **Output and refusal (EA-03).** A verdict is one JSON object on stdout carrying the six stable fields, either at
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:349|   top level or under `stable`, `result` or `report`; diagnostics may accompany it. *Instrument convention
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:350|   [OWNER 2026-10-19, A10.1.1]:* the independent verifier prints `{"stable":<stable-output object>,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:351|   "utc_assessment":<section 7.4 object>}`; the conformance runner compares `utc_assessment` only where a case's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:352|   `expected.json` carries one. A startup refusal is a nonzero
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:353|   exit with the refusal code on stdout or stderr and no six-field object.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:354| - **Release checker (EA-12).** `CMD --previous <config> --next <config>` prints `ACCEPT` or `REJECT` for the release
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:355|   invariants of section 5.
