docs/V1-PROFILE.md:357| ## 4. Issue order (issuer side, binding on the build)
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:358| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:359| 1. Fix the manifest and common metadata, including `declared_issue_time`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:360| 2. Build both frames.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:361| 3. Sign each frame.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:362| 4. Verify both signatures with the exact bytes to be committed.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:363| 5. Freeze the signature bytes. Any re-framing happens before this point.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:364| 6. Build `A_sig` and stamp its SHA-256. One stamp per receipt.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:365| 7. Obtain and validate the confirmation and time evidence.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:366| 8. Ship the complete receipt.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:367| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:368| [ENC §5.4:515-525; A9:293-296] That is eight steps in both sources. A retry that changes any committed byte needs a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:369| fresh stamp. The frame-only anchor is withdrawn, with no fallback. [A9:292; ENC §5.1:407-414]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:370| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:371| Issuer duties that are not verifier rules: an attempt whose T would exceed not-after is not shipped [A9:422-423]; the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:372| `gpg` signer refuses a frame whose `declared_issue_time` is more than ε from its clock [A9:401-405]; the issuer never
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:373| re-authorizes a key [A9:266]; public publication of the commit stays an issuer duty [A9:495-500]; the issuer
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:374| re-captures the DNSSEC snapshot before shipping if it fails the snapshot rule [DD:94].
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:375| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:376| Further issuer duties [OWNER 2026-10-14]:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:377| - **Chain-order pre-commitment.** Do not issue in a window until the key-assertion commit's stamp has k = 6
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:378|   confirmations and the receipt will anchor at a higher height (A9 C4). Before honest issuance the issuer obtains and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:379|   validates the git assertion's k = 6 proof. A receipt stamped after the issuer has observed h_git + 5 anchors above
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:380|   it, so it passes the verifier's `h_git + 5 < h_receipt` rule (section 6.3). [G02; RB §5]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:381| - **Snapshot c3.** Check all three conjuncts on the snapshot's own proof before shipping; recapture or retry if they
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:382|   fail. A snapshot stamped before the receipt need not confirm before it. [G06]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:383| - **DNSSEC support.** Validate the snapshot under this profile's algorithm set (section 6.1); do not ship a receipt
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:384|   whose chain would be `DNSSEC_ALGORITHM_UNSUPPORTED`. [G16]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:385| - **Snapshot body.** Convert to the section 15.3 body before stamping. [G19]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:386| - **Signature output.** Both OpenPGP adapters emit signatures that satisfy the rule-O policy of section 8 before
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:387|   signing is final and before stamping. [G11]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:388| - **Canonical container.** Emit the container as canonical JCS (section 15.1). [G17]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:389| - **Pre-ship checks for the 2026-10-14 r2 completions** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F07, r2-F08, r2-F09, r2-F10]: the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:390|   snapshot body carries no RRSIG with fewer Labels than its owner (section 15.3); the selected path of each of the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:391|   three proofs (receipt, snapshot, git) satisfies the transaction-shape subset and the conventional merkle suffix
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:392|   (section 15.2), else the proof is re-stamped or the attempt abandoned; both OpenPGP adapters and the repository
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:393|   signer emit type-16/type-33 subpackets only in the shapes section 8 allows. All 352 Bitcoin paths in the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:394|   repository's 129 proofs satisfy the shape and suffix rules (owner check, 2026-10-14); this is evidence, not a rule.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:395| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:396| ## 5. Trust configuration
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:397| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:398| It ships with the verifier and is never read from the bundle. [A9:154; SPEC R-5.8:1217; SPEC R-2.17:262] It holds:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:399| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:400| | # | Item | Source |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:401| |---|---|---|
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:402| | 1 | Root KSK-2017 | [A9:154-155; DD:66] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:403| | 2 | Root KSK-2024 | [A9:154-155; DD:66] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:404| | 3 | Repository entries: D = `wamason.com`, the repository key, an inclusive signing interval | OWNER PROFILE DECISION 2026-10-13 (section 6.3); A9.5 repository entries; [A9:68-69] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:405| | 4 | A versioned set of pinned mainnet header hashes, authenticated by the release allowlist | [A9:155; DD:66]; A9.5 trust-configuration authority |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:406| | 5 | ~~The parameters δ, ε, k~~ | moved to the frozen spec catalog (section 1) [OWNER 2026-10-14, G12] |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:407| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:408| *Dated correction 2026-10-14:* item 5 previously read "The parameters δ, ε, k [A9:217; SPEC R-5.8:1217]". A
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:409| trust-configuration release can be extended, so verdict-deciding parameters now live in the frozen spec catalog,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:410| which cannot. Item 3 previously read "The pair (D, repository root key)"; A9.5's repository entries also carry a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:411| signing interval.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:412| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:413| - **Authority: independent release allowlisting** (A9.5 "Trust-configuration authority", OWNER DECISION 2026-10-14).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:414|   The trust configuration is authenticated independently of the bundle and of both authority-channel credentials.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:415|   Each verifier release compiles in the SHA-256 of exactly one trust configuration; the config file itself carries no
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:416|   signature. Releases are signed by the **release key**, which neither the DNS credential, the repository key nor the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:417|   issuing AWS account can use; the dated custody record names that key and its access boundary. Capture of any
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:418|   authority-channel credential grants no ability to sign a release, authorize a configuration hash, or replace the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:419|   compiled trust root or policy catalog. CI is not the authenticity check. Compromise of the release key is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:420|   distribution compromise, a stated boundary (A9 "The boundaries"). [OWNER 2026-10-14, G08]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:421|   - A config whose SHA-256 is not the compiled hash, or that fails the section 15.5 schema, makes the verifier refuse
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:422|     to run with exit error `TRUST_CONFIG_UNAUTHENTICATED`: no verdict.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:423|   - Bootstrap: the production release key's full v4 fingerprint is published through at least two channels
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:424|     independent of the operational environment and recorded in the dated first-production-release bootstrap record
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:425|     (section 15.9 R5; A10.4.2). The freeze record does not contain it. Initial bootstrap authenticates the first
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:426|     production key. A successor is authenticated by a conforming release verified under the currently authenticated
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:427|     key and naming the successor fingerprint; subsequently acquired successor key material must match that
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:428|     fingerprint. Loss recovery starts a separately authenticated release lineage and does not establish continuity
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:429|     with the old lineage (section 15.9 R5). [OWNER 2026-10-19, §14.2 item 2; A10.4.2 "Bootstrap record"; OWNER
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:430|     2026-10-19, PR-05] *(Was, 2026-10-19: "A new release key is introduced only by a release signed by the current
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:431|     one", which recovery contradicted.)* *(Was: "the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:432|     release public key is published with the verifier's documentation and relying-party text, and its fingerprint is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:433|     in the freeze record.")*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:434|   - `version` starts at `"1"` and increases by 1; `previous_sha256` is 64 zeros for version 1, else the prior config's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:435|     hash. Every report carries the config version and hash as diagnostics; reproducing a verdict exactly (A9.4) uses
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:436|     the release that compiled that hash.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:437|   - Required test: a captured repository signer (and, separately, a captured DNS credential and the issuing AWS
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:438|     account) signs a config adding its own KSK, repository key and pins; the verifier refuses it.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:439|   - **OPEN:** release-key custody, holder and access boundary (section 14.2 item 1; gate: the first public verifier
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:440|     release, A10.4.2). The release artefact and release-signature format are section 15.9. [OWNER 2026-10-19,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:441|     §14.2 item 2]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:442|   - *Dated correction 2026-10-14:* the 2026-10-13 resolutions draft proposed a dedicated trust-config key giving the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:443|     config a detached rule-O signature, with append-only enforced in CI. Withdrawn: key inequality does not establish
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:444|     independence, and CI cannot stop an attacker who bypasses it (`CODEX-REVIEW-RESOLUTIONS.md` F04).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:445| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:446| - **Root KSKs, three periods each.** The trust configuration records each KSK's signing and reliance periods
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:447|   separately from its publication and revocation dates. [A9:154-155; A9:324-325] The instrument spike found that
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:448|   conflating signing with publication falsely rejected every snapshot from 2026-10-11. [SR:73-78]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:449| - **Root rule.** The root DNSKEY set is valid at the snapshot's anchored time if some trusted KSK whose **reliance
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:450|   period** contains that time validates it. Each KSK entry records signing-start, signing-end and a sourced reliance lifetime L; the reliance
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:451|   interval is [signing-start, signing-end + L]. L is an acceptance-policy value from cited RRSIG validity evidence,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:452|   labelled observed, not a proven global maximum. The extension admits authentic pre-retirement evidence anchored
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:453|   later and does not prove signing before retirement: a thief of a retired KSK can manufacture eligible evidence
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:454|   during it (A9.5; AUTHOR ADOPTED 2026-10-13, kind CORRECT). *Dated correction 2026-10-13: the earlier wording
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:455|   ("maximum validity … it made"; "usable for that long and no longer") overclaimed provenance and is withdrawn.* The rule is existential and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:456|   order-independent: a candidate that fails is informational, and the result is computed once, after every eligible
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:457|   key has been tried. A trusted KSK that is published but did not sign is informational, never a failure.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:458|   [A9.5, A9:309-325, OWNER DECISION 2026-10-13 after `docs/reviews/v1-profile/` F1, F2]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:459| - **Rollover control (required vector).** A snapshot taken while one trusted KSK is published but not signing must
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:460|   pass. [A9:341-342] Further required vectors (`docs/reviews/v1-profile/` F1, F2 dispositions): a failing trusted
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:461|   candidate listed before a validating one, in both trust-list orders, must pass; an honest old root signed before
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:462|   retirement and anchored after retirement but within reliance must pass, and the same evidence after reliance must
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:463|   not.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:464|   - **Both orders.** `root_ksks` is sorted (section 15.5), so a conforming configuration has one order. "Both
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:465|     trust-list orders" is met by the failing trusted candidate sorting first and, separately, sorting second in the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:466|     canonical candidate order (G35), which also covers both snapshot-body RRSIG orders. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:467|     from diff-1, EA-08]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:468|   - **Expected reason after reliance.** Only a time-valid candidate is in the finalized-interval class. With L at
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:469|     least the RRSIG validity (L = 21 days observed), pre-retirement evidence anchored after reliance always has an
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:470|     expired RRSIG, so the "must not pass" vector reports the time class, `INVALID / RRSIG_NOT_VALID_AT_EVAL_TIME`;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:471|     `KSK_OUTSIDE_RELIANCE_PERIOD` needs an RRSIG window longer than L. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:472|     EA-14]

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:474|   removed 2027-03-22. [DD:66; SR:70-71] **OWNER PROFILE DECISION 2026-10-13** (values under the A9.5 rule):
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:475|   - KSK-2017 signing period ends **2026-10-11T00:00:00Z**: IANA, the root zone begins using KSK-2024 on 2026-10-11

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:479|   - Observed root DNSKEY RRSIG validity, used as L: **21 days** (observed, not a proven maximum), from the archived captures. `prototype/spike/out/dns-snapshot.json`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:480|     (captured 2026-10-09): the KSK-2017 RRSIG runs 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-10-22T00:00:00Z (21 d), the only

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:484|   - KSK-2017 reliance period ends **2026-11-01T00:00:00Z** (= 2026-10-11T00:00:00Z + 21 d). KSK-2024's reliance end
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:485|     stays open until its signing end is recorded.

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:490| - **No usable trusted KSK — OWNER PROFILE DECISION 2026-10-13** (under R-2.26; repaired after
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:491|   `docs/reviews/v1-profile/` F1, F3). Each candidate signature is classified separately, and only after every trusted
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:492|   KSK has been tried:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:493|   - a signature that verifies under a trusted KSK, is within its own RRSIG window, and whose KSK's reliance period
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:494|     contains the snapshot's anchored time: the set is valid, whatever the other candidates show;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:495|   - otherwise, a signature that **verifies** but whose KSK's reliance period excludes that time:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:496|     `INVALID / KSK_OUTSIDE_RELIANCE_PERIOD`;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:497|   - otherwise, a signature that verifies but is outside its own inception/expiration window at that time: `INVALID`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:498|     (`RRSIG_NOT_VALID_AT_EVAL_TIME` in the instrument);
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:499|   - otherwise, a signature bearing a trusted KSK's tag that does not verify: `INVALID`

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:501|     forged tag never produces the reliance reason;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:502|   - otherwise (signed only by keys the trust configuration does not hold, or the RRset, RRSIG or message missing):
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:503|     `UNVERIFIABLE / NO_TRUSTED_KSK_USABLE`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:504|   - **Superseding precedence** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F04]. The list above is replaced by one candidate
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:505|     classification used for both root and repository checks (section 6.3). Each candidate is first classified:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:506|     *eligible pass*; *horizon-unperformable* (verifies cryptographically, its RRSIG window and edge checks pass, and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:507|     it is limited only by an open entry with T_snap > `as_of`); *finalized interval failure* (verifies, time-valid,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:508|     reliance period of a finalized entry excludes the time); *time failure* (verifies; window or G27 edge failure);
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:509|     *crypto failure* (a trusted KSK's selector, does not verify); *no configured candidate*. Then: "Any eligible
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:510|     validating candidate passes. Otherwise a cryptographically validating, time-valid candidate limited only by an
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:511|     open horizon gives TRUST_HORIZON. Otherwise use finalized interval failure, time failure (including G27), crypto
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:512|     failure, then no configured candidate, in that order. Multiple reasons within one class use the G35 canonical
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:513|     candidate order." Codes: `UNVERIFIABLE / TRUST_HORIZON`; `INVALID / KSK_OUTSIDE_RELIANCE_PERIOD`; `INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:514|     RRSIG_NOT_VALID_AT_EVAL_TIME`, `RRSIG_TIME_AMBIGUOUS` or `RRSIG_INTERVAL_REVERSED`; `INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:515|     TRUSTED_KSK_SIGNATURE_INVALID` (these are now the profile's codes, not only the instrument's); a candidate
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:516|     bearing a trusted KSK's tag whose supported RDATA is malformed or whose non-temporal metadata is inconsistent is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:517|     a crypto-class failure reported as `DNSSEC_FORMAT` / `DNSSEC_RRSIG_METADATA` (section 6.1); `UNVERIFIABLE /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:518|     NO_TRUSTED_KSK_USABLE`. Horizon is claimed only after the key and signature are authenticated. Within the time
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:519|     class the edge reason follows section 15.7 (candidate G35 tuple, then endpoint inception before expiration,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:520|     then ambiguous / reversed / window). This is an owner selection of Codex's proposed precedence: it keeps A9.5's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:521|     existential rule, under which a failing extra candidate is informational while a validating one may still

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:631| ## 6. Authority channels
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:632| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:633| Both channels must pass (n = 2). Neither commits to any receipt. [A9:143, 153] Both carry the same issuance
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:634| window. [A9:407-408; ENC §7.1:630-634]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:635| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:636| ### 6.1 DNS channel
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:637| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:638| - Owner name is `_tessera-v1.<D>`. The verifier rebuilds it from the signed `issuer` and compares label by label,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:639|   ignoring ASCII case. Anything else is `DNS_OWNER`. [ENC §7:551-556] This is the owner-name check (G-21 / M2).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:640| - One TXT RRset, one RR, one character-string. The value grammar, the fifteen-step rejection order and the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:641|   exact-255-byte rule are in ENC §7. [ENC §7:557-612]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:642| - The record carries `kms`, `gpg`, `profile`, `issuance-not-before` and `issuance-not-after`, all mandatory, in a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:643|   fixed order. [ENC §7:569-579]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:644| - The DNSSEC chain is validated against the root rule (section 5) at the snapshot's own anchored time (section 7.3).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:645|   [A9:143; A9:309-310]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:646| - **Root rule first.** The root RRset passes only under A9.5: a byte-matching configured KSK, usable in its reliance
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:647|   interval at T_snap, verifies a selected RRSIG valid at T_snap. The algorithm profile below never replaces that
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:648|   eligibility condition. Candidate aggregation is existential and order-independent; extra candidates are
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:649|   informational after any eligible supported path passes. Root outcomes and their precedence are section 5's.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:650|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, G16]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:651| - **Supported DNSSEC set (NARROW-CLAIM, visible owner scope choice).** DNSKEY and RRSIG algorithms 8 (RSA/SHA-256,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:652|   RFC 5702, key per RFC 3110) and 13 (ECDSA P-256/SHA-256, RFC 6605); DS digest types 2 (SHA-256, RFC 4509) and 4
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:653|   (SHA-384, RFC 6605). The DNSKEY used has the Zone Key flag set, REVOKE clear, protocol 3. Validation is RFC 4035
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:654|   §5.3.1–5.3.3 at T_snap with RFC 4034 §6 canonical form. DS is signed by a key in the parent's validated DNSKEY
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:655|   set; a child DNSKEY RRset is self-signed by a key matching a validated DS; the TXT is signed by a key in its zone's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:656|   validated DNSKEY set. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G16]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:657| - **Outcomes for each non-root required RRset**, computed once after every candidate is tried [OWNER 2026-10-14,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:658|   G16]:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:659|   1. some supported path (matching authenticated DS → DNSKEY → RRSIG) validates at T_snap: pass;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:660|   2. else the RRset or the witness RRSIG it needs is missing: `UNVERIFIABLE / DNS_EVIDENCE_MISSING`;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:661|   3. else an unsupported algorithm or digest type could supply the path: `UNVERIFIABLE /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:662|      DNSSEC_ALGORITHM_UNSUPPORTED`;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:663|   4. else (every possibility supported and checked) a candidate verifies but its window excludes T_snap, or its
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:664|      times are edge failures (section 7.3): `INVALID / RRSIG_NOT_VALID_AT_EVAL_TIME` (or that edge reason);
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:665|   5. else a supported candidate fails cryptographically: `INVALID / DNSSEC_SIGNATURE_INVALID`;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:666|   6. else no child DNSKEY matches a validated DS: `INVALID / DNSKEY_DS_MISMATCH`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:667| - **Complete candidate table** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F05]. Supersedes the six rows above where they differ. DS →
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:668|   DNSKEY matching (DNSKEY RRsets) is separate from RRset → RRSIG → DNSKEY matching (DS and TXT RRsets, and each
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:669|   DNSKEY RRset's self-signature). Each candidate takes the first failing RFC 4035 §5.3.1 precondition below; the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:670|   RRset outcome is computed once, after every candidate:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:671|   1. some supported eligible path validates at T_snap: pass;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:672|   2. else the RRset, its witness RRSIG, or the signer zone's DNSKEY RRset is absent: `UNVERIFIABLE /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:673|      DNS_EVIDENCE_MISSING`;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:674|   3. else a **potentially usable unsupported path** exists: `UNVERIFIABLE / DNSSEC_ALGORITHM_UNSUPPORTED`. Defined
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:675|      by authenticated DS metadata and matching selectors only: for a DNSKEY RRset, an authenticated DS of
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:676|      unsupported digest type or algorithm whose key tag and algorithm match a child DNSKEY; for any RRset, an RRSIG
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:677|      of unsupported algorithm whose signer name, algorithm and key tag match a DNSKEY in the signer zone's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:678|      authenticated set. An unrelated unsupported RR does not qualify;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:679|   4. else the parent's authentication is blocked (the parent RRset's outcome is unperformable) and some candidate is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:680|      locally valid (well-formed, metadata consistent, verifies under a supplied matching DNSKEY of its signer zone,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:681|      window contains T_snap): the authenticated-path check is unperformable and carries no reason of its own (the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:682|      parent's reason is earlier in section 15.7);
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:683|   5. else, `INVALID`, by the most-progressed failing candidate, in this order: verifies but window or edge failure
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:684|      (`RRSIG_NOT_VALID_AT_EVAL_TIME`, `RRSIG_TIME_AMBIGUOUS`, `RRSIG_INTERVAL_REVERSED`); supported candidate fails
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:685|      cryptographically (`DNSSEC_SIGNATURE_INVALID`); present supported witness with no matching eligible DNSKEY
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:686|      (signer name, algorithm and key tag matching a DNSKEY with Zone Key set, protocol 3, REVOKE clear) in the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:687|      signer zone's set (`DNSSEC_KEY_MISMATCH`); no child DNSKEY matches a validated DS (`DNSKEY_DS_MISMATCH`);
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:688|      Labels greater than the owner's label count, or other non-temporal metadata mismatch (`DNSSEC_RRSIG_METADATA`);
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:689|      malformed supported DNSKEY or RRSIG RDATA (`DNSSEC_FORMAT`). Ties within a class: G35 candidate order.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:690|   Locally obtainable checks (framing, TXT grammar, signature mathematics against supplied keys) run whether or not
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:691|   the parent is authenticated; under row 4 they become reportable failures (row 5) only when no candidate of that
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:692|   RRset is locally valid, which preserves the existential rule. This is the bridge from RFC 4035's failures to the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:693|   V1 partition, not a claim that RFC 4035 is unspecified. **Owner choice (fail-closed):** an unmatched selector is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:694|   `INVALID / DNSSEC_KEY_MISMATCH`, not insufficient evidence; the honest issuer validates the chain before
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:695|   shipping. *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: the six rows above gave no outcome for an unmatched key tag, Labels
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:696|   defects, bad flags/protocol or malformed supported RDATA, and "an unsupported algorithm could supply the path" did
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:697|   not define which candidates count.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:698|   - **Unrelated unsupported witness only.** An RRSIG of an unsupported algorithm whose signer name, algorithm and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:699|     key tag match no DNSKEY in the signer zone's set is neither a potentially usable unsupported path (row 3) nor a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:700|     supported witness (row 5's `DNSSEC_KEY_MISMATCH`). If it is the only RRSIG covering the RRset, the RRset has no
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:701|     usable witness: `UNVERIFIABLE / DNS_EVIDENCE_MISSING` (row 2). The fail-closed unmatched-selector choice above
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:702|     applies to supported-algorithm witnesses only. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, EA-11]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:703|   - **RSA signature width.** An algorithm-8 RRSIG whose signature field is not exactly the modulus length of the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:704|     DNSKEY it is checked against is malformed supported RRSIG RDATA, `INVALID / DNSSEC_FORMAT`, not
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:705|     `DNSSEC_SIGNATURE_INVALID`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, A13]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:706| - **Relying-party text (visible limit).** A chain that moves to an algorithm outside {8, 13} (for example Ed25519,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:707|   algorithm 15) makes new snapshots `UNVERIFIABLE` under this frozen spec; the issuer does not ship such receipts.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:708|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, G16]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:709| - **No wildcards (NARROW-CLAIM).** A TXT RRSIG whose Labels field is less than the owner's label count gives
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:710|   `INVALID / DNS_WILDCARD`. The issuer publishes an explicit record. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G19]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:711|   - **Owner choice: a global body restriction, not witness eligibility** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F07]. The rule
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:712|     above is a **transport restriction on the snapshot body** (the "no-wildcard body restriction"), separate from
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:713|     witness eligibility: any RRSIG anywhere in the body whose Labels field is less than its owner's label count
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:714|     gives `INVALID / DNS_WILDCARD`, even beside a valid explicit-owner witness. Accordingly the promise that extra
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:715|     candidates are informational after an eligible path passes (above, and section 7.3) does **not** cover such an
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:716|     RRSIG. Chosen as the fail-closed reading; the honest issuer publishes an explicit record and checks the body
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:717|     before stamping (section 4). *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: the bullet left open whether an extra wildcard
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:718|     candidate beside a valid explicit witness rejects the snapshot; it now does. It previously named only TXT
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:719|     RRSIGs.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:720| - **Inherited residual.** An ancestor zone (root, `com`) can sign data for names below it; V1 inherits that DNSSEC
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:721|   trust, and the git channel (n = 2) guards against it. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G19]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:722| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:723| ### 6.2 Issuance window (C4 verifier rule)
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:724| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:725| - The window `issuance-not-after − issuance-not-before` is at most 90 days. A record that violates it is rejected
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:726|   (`DNS_WINDOW_LENGTH`). V1 has one window and no overlap. [A9:409-411; ENC §7:578-580]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:727| - A receipt is `INVALID / ISSUANCE_WINDOW` unless `issuance-not-before` ≤ declared issue time and T ≤
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:728|   `issuance-not-after`. Both bounds are inclusive. T is compared as registered, with no margin. T is not compared
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:729|   with not-before. [A9:419-421; ENC §7.1:636-643, 662-663]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:730| - The guarantee is in chain time. A UTC cutoff would need a backward-skew bound V1 does not establish. [A9:441-447;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:731|   ENC §7.1:661-671]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:732| - A published window cannot be shortened. [A9:424]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:733| - The window, its dates and the stop margin are operating facts, not profile rules. [A9:422-423; RB §2]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:734| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:735| ### 6.3 Git channel
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:736| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:737| The OTS stamp targets the signed commit's object id, never a tree, blob or unsigned commit. [A9:297-299; ENC
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:738| §7.2:685-691] The verifier does four things:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:739| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:740| 1. Recomputes the commit id from the presented raw commit object.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:741| 2. Verifies `gpgsig` over the object without that header, under the pinned repository key.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:742| 3. Follows commit, then tree, then blob, down the fixed path below.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:743| 4. Checks that the stamped bytes name that id.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:744| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:745| [ENC §7.2:706-710] SHA-1 linkage (the commit id and the commit-tree-blob links) is a stated residual. [A9:299;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:746| ENC §7.2:712-718]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:747| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:748| ENC §7.2 says the blob's path and any byte framing around the value are "not P8's" (ENC:680-682). These three owner
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:749| profile decisions fill that gap (section 0.1, items 1 and 2). Reference implementation, instrument only:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:750| `prototype/tessera_proto/real/gitchannel.py` (`verify_key_path`; `verify_profile_key_assertion` pins the fixed path
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:751| and compares the blob with the validated DNS TXT value byte for byte), tests in `prototype/tests/test_gitpath.py`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:752| Coverage limit: the instrument does not yet verify `gpgsig` under the pinned key, the commit's OTS stamp, or signed
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:753| issuer == pinned D together with the path (`docs/reviews/v1-profile/` F7).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:754| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:755| - **Closed git grammar** (OWNER CHOICE, supported-path limit): commit headers, armor, canonical trees, the path,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:756|   SHA-1 with collision detection, and the P-256 repository key, exactly as section 15.4. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G25]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:757| - **Repository signer.** If some repository entry for D verifies `gpgsig` and its interval contains T_git, the check
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:758|   passes; if one verifies but its interval excludes T_git, `INVALID / GIT_SIGNER_OUTSIDE_INTERVAL`; if none verifies,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:759|   `UNVERIFIABLE / GIT_SIGNER_NOT_CONFIGURED`. [A9.5; OWNER 2026-10-14, G25]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:760|   - **Candidate precedence** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F04]: section 5's classification, with repository entries as
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:761|     candidates: any entry for D that verifies with T_git in its interval passes; otherwise a verifying entry
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:762|     limited only by an open interval with T_git > `as_of` gives `UNVERIFIABLE / TRUST_HORIZON`; otherwise a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:763|     verifying finalized entry whose interval excludes T_git gives `INVALID / GIT_SIGNER_OUTSIDE_INTERVAL`;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:764|     otherwise `UNVERIFIABLE / GIT_SIGNER_NOT_CONFIGURED`. Multiple entries in a class are ordered by (signing_start,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:765|     key bytes). *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: an open entry verifying at T_git > `as_of` was both
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:766|     `GIT_SIGNER_OUTSIDE_INTERVAL` here and `TRUST_HORIZON` in section 5.)* A verifying entry with T_git before its
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:767|     `signing_start` is `INVALID / GIT_SIGNER_OUTSIDE_INTERVAL`, open entries included: the open horizon covers
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:768|     only T_git > `as_of`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, A08]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:769|   - **Git signature mapping** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F11]: every armor, codec and rule-O policy violation of the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:770|     `gpgsig` value is `INVALID / GIT_SIG_FORMAT` (the exception to section 8's generic `SIG_POLICY`); failed
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:771|     mathematics, including a hash-prefix mismatch, is "none verifies" above (`GIT_SIGNER_NOT_CONFIGURED`).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:772| - **Descriptor and stamp.** `object_format` absent gives `UNVERIFIABLE / GIT_OBJECT_FORMAT_MISSING`, a value other
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:773|   than `"sha1"` gives `UNVERIFIABLE / GIT_OBJECT_FORMAT` (A9.5). The proof's file digest is SHA256 of the 40
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:774|   lowercase hex commit id plus LF, else `INVALID / GIT_STAMP_MISMATCH`. The V1 verifier checks each receipt's own
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:775|   window and does not check non-overlap between receipts; successor registration is an issuance duty. [A9.5, A9.6;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:776|   OWNER 2026-10-14, G39]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:777| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:778| - **OWNER PROFILE DECISION 2026-10-13 (path).** The key-assertion blob is at the fixed path `tessera-v1/key-assertion` in the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:779|   issuer repository. One window per record (A9:409-411) means one path is enough. A rotation mechanism, if one is ever
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:780|   registered, must define its own paths. [ENC §7.2:680-682 for the gap; A9:409-411]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:781| - **OWNER PROFILE DECISION 2026-10-13 (framing).** None. The blob's bytes equal the ENC §7 canonical value byte for byte. A
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:782|   trailing LF or any other byte is rejected. The leaf tree entry mode must be 100644 and each intermediate entry must
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:783|   be 40000. [ENC §7:566-586; ENC §7.2:679-682] A blob that is the DNS value plus a trailing LF (or any other extra
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:784|   or differing byte) is rejected by row 15.2 as `INVALID / CHANNEL_VALUE_MISMATCH`, not as `GIT_PATH`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:785|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, EA-21]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:786| - **OWNER PROFILE DECISION 2026-10-13 (issuer domain D in the git channel).** The ENC §7 value does not carry D, so D is not
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:787|   extracted from the blob. D comes from the verifier's trust configuration, which pins the pair (D, repository root
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:788|   key). The git channel is accepted only for the pinned D. The verifier checks that the D bound in the receipt's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:789|   signed bytes (`common.issuer`) equals the pinned D. [ENC §7:566-575; ENC §3.2:279]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:790|   - **Correction.** This supersedes the derivation draft's "exact extraction of D and the key set" (DD:94). The key
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:791|     set is still taken from the blob, parsed with the ENC §7 grammar. D is not.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:792| - The git value and the DNS value must be identical, window included. [A9:408; ENC §7.2:679-681]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:793| - **One pinned-D gate for both channels.** Before either channel, `common.issuer` must be exactly `wamason.com`,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:794|   the profile constant D, which must also equal the trust configuration's `issuer_domain`; otherwise
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:795|   `INVALID / ISSUER_NOT_PINNED`. With git evidence absent and another D, the result is `INVALID`, not
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:796|   `UNVERIFIABLE`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G34] *(Was: "`OPEN (step 8):` whether the pinned-D equality check also gates the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:797|   DNS channel", 2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:798| - **Git time relation.** Let T_git and h_git be the git proof's T and selected height (section 7.1 rule on the git
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:799|   proof), and h_receipt the receipt proof's selected height. The git assertion must satisfy:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:800|   - T_git lies in some configured repository-key interval for D (A9.5);
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:801|   - **chain-order pre-commitment: h_git + 5 < h_receipt**, else `INVALID / GIT_NOT_PRECOMMITTED` (A9 C4 as revised
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:802|     2026-10-14, OWNER DECISION, BROADEN);
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:803|   - no upper bound from δ.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:804| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:805|   The same window value is authenticated by the anchored git assertion and by DNSSEC at the snapshot's own anchored
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:806|   time. No clock comparison between T_git and the declared issue time is made. *(Owner 2026-10-14: the `T_git ≤ declared_issue_time` check was dropped. Chain order carries the protection, and the clock check only added an nTime false-reject hazard on the honest path.)* Before
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:807|   honest issuance the issuer obtains and validates the git assertion's k=6 proof. The chain-order rule establishes
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:808|   that the window was confirmed at k = 6 in the chain before the receipt was anchored; pre-commitment is chain order,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:809|   not UTC (A2.1), and DNSSEC evidence establishes no publication before issue. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G02] *(Was:

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:856| ## 7. Time
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:857| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:858| ### 7.1 The T rule
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:859| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:860| - T is the time of the verified attestation at the **lowest block height** in the presented OTS proof; both T and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:861|   its confirmations come from that attestation. It is presentation-sensitive: a different presentation of the same
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:862|   receipt can select a different T. [A9 C5 as revised 2026-10-14; DD:56, 98-99; OWNER 2026-10-14, G03] *Dated
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:863|   correction 2026-10-14: this bullet previously read "T is the time of the earliest verified attestation", A9's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:864|   earlier wording. "Earliest" means chain order, not least nTime: header times are not monotone, and the two
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:865|   selection rules can give different verdicts on the same proof.*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:866| - No lower bound and no priority. Header times are chain-time proxies. [A9:144]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:867| - The three conjuncts at k = 6 (`DepthK = k − 1 = 5`): `declared − ε ≤ anchor_time`; `anchor_time ≤ declared + δ`;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:868|   `confirmed_at ≤ declared + δ`. All three are evaluated together. [SPEC R-4.41:985; SPEC R-5.19:1352; SPEC
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:869|   V33-V36:1342-1346; A9:105-106]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:870| - A real proof carries several attestations hours apart and nothing in the proof names T (M3). [FT:20; DD:98]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:871| - **T ≡ `anchor_time`.** For the receipt proof, T = `anchor_time` = nTime(h*), where h* is the lowest qualifying
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:872|   height. The same value feeds conjuncts 1 and 2, the C4 window rule and the reported T. Two qualifying attestations
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:873|   at the same height give the same T. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G03] *(Was: "`OPEN (step 8):` one sentence stating whether
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:874|   T is the `anchor_time` of the three conjuncts", 2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:875| - **`confirmed_at`** = nTime(h* + 5): the including block plus five successors, k = 6 (SPEC R-3.45, R-4.42). A
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:876|   failure gives `INVALID`: `TIME_BEFORE_DECLARED_EPSILON`, `TIME_AFTER_DECLARED_DELTA` or `CONFIRMATION_LATE`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:877|   Nonmonotone header times can give `confirmed_at` < T; that is not a failure, and there is no monotonicity check.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:878|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, G04]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:879| - **Qualifying ("verified") attestation.** A Bitcoin attestation at height h qualifies if and only if (a) the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:880|   bundled header at h exists and its merkle root equals the attestation message; (b) headers h … h+5 are all
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:881|   bundled; (c) each equals its pin, `hex(reverse(SHA256d(header))) = pin[height]`; (d) for i = h+1 … h+5,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:882|   `header_i.prev = SHA256d(header_{i−1})`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G05] *(Was: "`OPEN (step 8):` what 'verified' means
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:883|   for an attestation", 2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:884| - **Selection.** Attestation selection is existential over qualifying branches. A syntactically valid Bitcoin
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:885|   attestation without a complete h..h+5 segment is nonqualifying, not a required failed check. It supplies no time or
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:886|   trust fact. All supplied headers, including unused ones, are independently checked against pins (section 7.2).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:887|   The selected anchor, rather than every unverified attestation, is the referent of "anchors beyond the newest pin"
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:888|   (A9 C6 as revised 2026-10-14). [OWNER 2026-10-14, G05]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:889| - **Proof outcomes.** A pinned bundled header at h whose merkle root ≠ the attestation message: `INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:890|   OTS_MERKLE_MISMATCH` (a contradicted branch fails the proof). No qualifying attestation: `UNVERIFIABLE /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:891|   HEADERS_MISSING` if any Bitcoin attestation is present, `UNVERIFIABLE / ANCHOR_PENDING_ONLY` if only pending ones;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:892|   the snapshot uses `SNAPSHOT_NOT_ANCHORED` and git `GIT_NOT_ANCHORED`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G05]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:893| - **Time arithmetic.** Times are integer seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z without leap seconds; nTime is the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:894|   header's uint32; RFC 3339 fields convert by days-from-civil (proleptic Gregorian); comparisons are inclusive.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:895|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, G03]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:896| - **OTS and txid encoding**: section 15.2. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G20]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:897| - **txid scope and selected-height aggregation** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F08]: "§15.2's transaction-shape and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:898|   txid-equality check applies only to receipt_anchor. The snapshot/git proofs use the closed OTS grammar and header
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:899|   qualification, with no txid comparison. Select h* before the receipt txid check; any satisfying qualifying path at
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:900|   exactly h* passes that check. Never switch to a higher height merely to find a matching txid." **Owner choice
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:901|   (fail-closed), stated separately:** the **transaction-shape and merkle-suffix subset** (section 15.2, parts 1, 2
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:902|   and 4, without part 3's txid comparison) also applies to the selected height of the snapshot and git proofs; a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:903|   failure there is `INVALID / OTS_TX_SHAPE`, and any qualifying path at exactly that proof's h* satisfying the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:904|   subset passes. No receipt txid is compared with the snapshot or git proof; the three proofs normally anchor in
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:905|   different transactions. *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: section 15.7's "OTS (as 11 …)" imported the receipt's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:906|   txid check into proofs that carry no txid.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:907| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:908| ### 7.2 Header pins
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:909| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:910| - Every bundle header must be in the pinned set. Otherwise the verdict is `UNVERIFIABLE / HEADERS_NOT_COVERED`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:911|   There is no retarget logic, because the pins cover every accepted header. [A9:156; DD:99]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:912| - **Conflict.** A supplied header at a pinned height with a different hash gives `INVALID / HEADER_CONFLICTS_PIN`:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:913|   it is contradictory evidence. A9.1's "a bundle header outside the pins" is read as a header **at a height the pins
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:914|   do not cover**. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G23] A10.5 stage 1 (signed 2026-10-18) registers this reading as A9's meaning:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:915|   no pin at the height gives `UNVERIFIABLE / HEADERS_NOT_COVERED`, a header differing from its pin gives `INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:916|   HEADER_CONFLICTS_PIN`. [OWNER 2026-10-19, Levadura contested 2] *(Was: "`OPEN (step 8):` the verdict for a header that … conflicts with a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:917|   pin", 2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:918| - **Coverage.** Required: headers h* … h*+5 of the selected attestation of each of the three proofs (receipt,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:919|   snapshot, git), all in the shared `headers` pool. Every supplied header, used or not, is checked against the pins.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:920|   A `headers` entry that fails row 2.4 is not a supplied header: it contributes `CONTAINER_SCHEMA` only, and rows
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:921|   10.x, 11.x, 13.4 and 14.6 use the remaining entries [OWNER 2026-10-14, diff-1 F-3].
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:922|   For each pair of supplied headers at consecutive heights, a prev-hash mismatch gives `INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:923|   HEADER_CHAIN_BROKEN`; a missing intermediate height is not a broken link. No PoW, nBits or retarget check: a hash
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:924|   equal to a pin implies all of it. At an unselected height, a pinned header with missing successors is ignored,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:925|   while an unpinned header blocks the bundle (`HEADERS_NOT_COVERED`). [OWNER 2026-10-14, G07, G05] *(Was: "`OPEN
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:926|   (step 8):` which heights the pins must cover for a given proof", 2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:927| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:928| ### 7.3 The DNSSEC snapshot rule
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:929| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:930| - The issuer anchors the DNSSEC snapshot with its own OTS proof. The envelope is ENC §6 under the tag
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:931|   `tessera-v1/dnssec-snapshot`. [DD:94; ENC §6:536-542]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:932| - The verifier checks that the snapshot's anchored time lies inside every RRSIG window in the chain and within
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:933|   [declared − ε, declared + δ]. The issuer re-captures before shipping if it does not. [DD:94] This is an owner
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:934|   decision carried in, not routed. [A9:104-106]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:935|   - "declared" is the receipt's signed `declared_issue_time`, not the snapshot's capture time. Capture-to-anchor
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:936|     latency is a separate observation, not this predicate. (`docs/reviews/v1-profile/` F6, accepted 2026-10-13.)
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:937|   - "every RRSIG window in the chain" means the one witness signature selected to authenticate each required RRset,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:938|     not every signature offered: an extra expired or invalid signature beside a valid one neither fails the RRset
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:939|     nor narrows the joint window. The instrument's selection order is (key tag, inception, expiration, signature
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:940|     bytes), first that validates. (`docs/reviews/v1-profile/` F5, accepted 2026-10-13.) Exception: an RRSIG
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:941|     with fewer Labels than its owner fails the body restriction wherever it appears (section 6.1).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:942|     [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F07]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:943|   - **Frozen witness rule.** The selected witness is the **first eligible validating** candidate in (key tag,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:944|     inception, expiration, signature bytes, canonical RRSIG RDATA, canonical key RDATA) order. For the root, reliance
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:945|     eligibility precedes selection. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G35] *(Previously described only as the instrument's order.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:946|   - Conjunct 3 (`confirmed_at` of the snapshot ≤ declared + δ) is a new owner acceptance restriction, fail-closed. A
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:947|     failure of any conjunct gives `INVALID / SNAPSHOT_TIME`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G06]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:948| - The chain is evaluated at the snapshot's anchored time, not at T of the receipt. [A9:143]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:949| - Why: the joint RRSIG window measured 1.6 days, shorter than δ (M8). [DD:93]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:950| - **Snapshot body.** A fixed-order sequence of uncompressed RFC 1035 wire RRs in RFC 4034 §6.2 canonical form,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:951|   section 15.3. Framing violations are `INVALID / SNAPSHOT_FORMAT`; a syntactically complete body lacking a required
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:952|   RRset or its witness RRSIG is `UNVERIFIABLE / DNS_EVIDENCE_MISSING` (root: `NO_TRUSTED_KSK_USABLE`). The conversion
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:953|   from resolver messages happens before stamping and changes S, so each snapshot needs a fresh stamp; earlier
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:954|   stamped JSON snapshots cannot be reused. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G19] *(Was: "`OPEN (step 8):` the snapshot body
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:955|   format", 2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:956| - **Snapshot time.** T_snap = T of the snapshot's own proof under the section 7.1 rule, at the same depth k = 6, and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:957|   `confirmed_at`(snapshot) likewise. DNSSEC is evaluated at T_snap only; no capture time, receipt T or wall clock is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:958|   ever used. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G06] *(Was: "`OPEN (step 8):` how the snapshot's anchored time is derived",
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:959|   2026-10-13.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:960| - **RRSIG time arithmetic.** Inception and expiration are 32-bit values v, each resolved to the unique absolute
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:961|   second t with t ≡ v (mod 2^32) and |t − T_snap| < 2^31 (RFC 4034 §3.1.5, RFC 1982). If v − T_snap ≡ 2^31 (mod 2^32)
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:962|   the candidate fails with `RRSIG_TIME_AMBIGUOUS`; if resolved inception > expiration it fails with
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:963|   `RRSIG_INTERVAL_REVERSED`; inception = expiration is allowed. These are candidate failures under the existential
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:964|   rule, ranked with `RRSIG_NOT_VALID_AT_EVAL_TIME`. The witness check is inception ≤ T_snap ≤ expiration, never "now",
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:965|   including in 2106. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G27]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:966| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:967| ### 7.4 The UTC assessment [OWNER 2026-10-19, A10.1.1]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:968| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:969| A10.1.1 (AUTHOR ADOPTED 2026-10-18, BROADEN; A10 rows 20–24) adds one reported assessment and one named assumption.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:970| Nothing in this subsection changes T, a verdict, a reason code, the check order or the stable field set.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:971| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:972| - **Assumption A-UTC** (`assumption_id` `"A-UTC-7200-6"`). At least one of the six blocks h* … h*+5 has a header
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:973|   time no more than 7200 s before it was actually mined: `nTime(j) ≥ r(j) − 7200 s` for some j in [h*, h*+5], where
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:974|   r(j) is the real (UTC) time block j was first produced. It is an assumption of the UTC assessment only, not a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:975|   Bitcoin consensus rule; **the verifier does not check it** and no bundle carries evidence of it. It is sufficient,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:976|   not minimal. [A10:280-285]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:977| - **Constants.** Δ = 7200 s and m = 6 are frozen catalog constants (section 1), not trust-configuration data, and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:978|   are not shown to be optimal. m = 6 is the same six-header segment h* … h*+5 that section 7.1 already requires and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:979|   pins (k = 6), so U needs no new input. [A10:284-285; A10 row 22; A10:343-344] *Instrument note: the TEST catalog
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:980|   wire object (section 3.5; `prototype/differential/ADAPTER.md` T2) does not yet carry Δ and m; both instruments
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:981|   compile them in. Adding them to the frozen catalog object is owner work before the freeze.*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:982| - **h\*** is the receipt proof's selected inclusion height (section 7.1, A10.5); it counts as confirmation one, so
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:983|   h*+5 is confirmation six. [A10:277-278]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:984| - **Definition.** `U_seconds = 7200 + max(uint64(nTime(h*)), uint64(nTime(h*+1)), …, uint64(nTime(h*+5)))`, the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:985|   maximum over the receipt proof's selected h* and its six qualified headers (section 7.1 items (a)–(d)). Header
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:986|   times need not be monotone: the maximum is taken over all six, not nTime(h*+5) and not T. Each nTime is the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:987|   header's unsigned 32-bit little-endian field (section 7.1 "Time arithmetic"), widened to 64 bits **before** the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:988|   addition; the sum is never reduced modulo 2^32. [A10:287-293; A10:307-311]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:989| - **Encoding.** `utc_upper_bound` is the RFC 3339 UTC string of U_seconds in the form used for T
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:990|   (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, days-from-civil, no leap seconds). For max nTime = 4294967295, U = 4294974495 =
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:991|   `2106-02-07T08:28:15Z`, not a 1970 time. [A10:309-311]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:992| - **Null rule.** `utc_upper_bound` is `null` exactly when T is `null` (section 3.4), including every D1–D4
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:993|   dispatch-terminal outcome; otherwise it is computed from the same selected h* that gives T. Every receipt-verdict report,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:994|   including a D1–D4 terminal report, contains `utc_assessment`, with `assumption_id`. For D1–D4 its
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:995|   `utc_upper_bound` is null. Startup refusals produce no receipt-verdict report. [A10:300-302; OWNER 2026-10-19,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:996|   PR-03] *(Was: "The object `utc_assessment`, with `assumption_id`, is present on every report reached after
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:997|   dispatch.")*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:998| - **No verdict effect.** U never enters a verdict, reason code, stable field, the shipping predicate or S; a value
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:999|   is reported whatever the verdict, and with `INVALID` or `UNVERIFIABLE` it does not establish a valid service
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1000|   receipt or valid service signatures. [A10:302-305; A10:347-348; A10 row 21]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1001| - **Clock.** Verification does not consult the current clock; the arithmetic covers preserved headers. Timestamp
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1002|   representation for Bitcoin blocks produced after the 2106 rollover of the 32-bit field is a Bitcoin protocol
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1003|   matter outside V1. Section 7.3's serial-time unwrapping applies to DNSSEC RRSIG fields only, never to nTime.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1004|   [A10:307-313; A10 row 24]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1005| - **Claim, as registered** (A10:289-293): under A-UTC, the bytes and both signatures existed before U, in UTC. A2.1's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1006|   refusal to bound the observation lag B − C is unchanged; guarantee 2 keeps its chain-time meaning (A10 row 23).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1007|   A-UTC is false exactly when every one of the six blocks has a header time more than 7200 s before its production;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1008|   then the conditional UTC guarantee is unavailable, though the computed value need not itself be false (A10 row
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1009|   24).

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1060|   independent fates. [A9:142; A9:449-453]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1061| - Each slot's signature is exactly one detached signature in the serialization its rule pins. [ENC §5.2:429-436]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1062| - **Transported keys.** `keys.gpg` is the bare v4 public-key packet body, exactly the `gpg-sha256` preimage (no
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1063|   `0x99` prefix, packet header, user IDs, subkeys or armour). gpg must parse as the specified v4 P-256 public-key
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1064|   body. kms must parse as P-256 DER SPKI under the fallback, or as the exact ML-DSA-65 SPKI specified by the dated
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1065|   branch supplement under the hybrid. The rule is selected by the installed governing spec and slot, never by key
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1066|   bytes alone. Otherwise `INVALID / KEY_FORMAT`; a key not hashing to its slot fingerprint is `INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1067|   KEY_MISMATCH`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G21] Under the fallback, any `keys.kms` that is not a P-256 DER SPKI,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1068|   including an ML-DSA-65 SPKI (OID 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.18), is `INVALID / KEY_FORMAT`; this outcome does not depend
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1069|   on the hybrid supplement's exact SPKI encoding. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, EA-24]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1070|   **Scope of the key-format rule (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-14, EA-31; supersedes the literal reading of the sentences
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1071|   above where they conflict).** The installed-spec key rule applies only when the receipt's `common.alg` is the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1072|   installation's catalog-supported id (row 7.1). For a well-formed but unsupported alg, key format, key/fingerprint
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1073|   semantics, signatures and possession are not evaluated (r2-F01), and the outcome is `UNVERIFIABLE / ALG_UNKNOWN`,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1074|   not `KEY_FORMAT`. So a genuine hybrid receipt shown to a fallback installation, or a fallback receipt shown to a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1075|   hybrid installation, is "cannot evaluate", never "invalid". Rationale: an examiner holding the wrong installation
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1076|   must not be told that an honest receipt is forged. EA-24 still holds when the receipt's alg IS the fallback id
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1077|   and its kms key is ML-DSA: that is a malformed fallback receipt.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1078|   **Branch taken: HYBRID (registered 2026-10-16, A9.6).** Pair id `KMS-MLDSA65-PURE-GPG-OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256`;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1079|   supplement `formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md`; record `formal/p8/HYBRID-REGISTRATION-RECORD.md`; ENCODING-V1 §5.2
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1080|   edited per supplement §7. The V1 installation's catalog alg is this id.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1081|   **Codec registry per installation (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-14, differential run 4).** An installation's codec
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1082|   registry is the ENCODING-V1 baseline plus only the supplement(s) that installation registered. A fallback
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1083|   installation, which has no hybrid supplement, does not know the hybrid pair id: frames bearing it use the opaque
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1084|   codec (its length cap), and semantics give `UNVERIFIABLE / ALG_UNKNOWN`. A hybrid installation knows both ids,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1085|   because the classical id is in the baseline: the classical id uses rule O, then `ALG_UNKNOWN` for semantics (case
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1086|   (b)). Knowing an id's codec is a property of the installation, never of the verifier's source code.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1087| - **Rule-O signature policy** (attestation, possession and git signatures; OWNER CHOICE, supported-path limit)
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1088|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, G11]:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1089|   - ENC §5.2's grammar holds.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1090|   - Hashed area: exactly one signature-creation-time subpacket (type 2) with exactly four data octets, critical or
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1091|     not, never compared with anything; no signature-expiration subpacket (type 3), critical or not; issuer key ID
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1092|     (16) and issuer fingerprint (33) accepted critical or not and never read (no SHA-1 key binding, D-6); any other
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1093|     type ignored if not critical and a failure if critical.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1094|   - Unhashed area: ignored entirely, critical bits included (ENC §3.5: the unhashed area carries no meaning).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1095|   - ECDSA per FIPS 186-5 with r, s ∈ [1, n−1]; low-s not required.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1096|   - **Out-of-range r or s.** An r or s outside [1, n−1] is a policy failure, `INVALID / SIG_POLICY` (rows 9.1, 9.4;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1097|     git: `GIT_SIG_FORMAT`, section 6.3), not `SIG_INVALID`, except that an r or s of zero fails ENC §5.2's MPI
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1098|     grammar (1 to 256 bits) first and is `SIG_FORMAT` (git: `GIT_SIG_FORMAT`). [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1099|     diff-1, EA-23/A11]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1100|   - Policy failure: `INVALID / SIG_POLICY`. Failed verification: `SIG_INVALID`, or `POSSESSION_INVALID` for the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1101|     manifest possession signatures. Possession proofs use the same per-slot rule over `F_manifest` (rule R for kms
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1102|     under the hybrid). No revocation or current-time checks.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1103|   - **Advisory metadata, structural validation (owner choice, fail-closed)** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F10]. Codex's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1104|     proposal treated types 16 and 33 as opaque advisory octets; the owner instead selects exact structural
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1105|     validation, in the hashed area: at most one type-16 subpacket, with exactly 8 data octets; at most one type-33
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1106|     subpacket, with exactly 21 data octets whose first octet is `04` (v4 fingerprint); if both are present, the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1107|     type-16 value equals the last 8 octets of the type-33 fingerprint. Otherwise `INVALID / SIG_POLICY`. A
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1108|     zero-data critical type 33 is therefore `SIG_POLICY`. Their values are never compared with the transported
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1109|     key and confer no key-selection authority; critical bits are recognized and confer nothing. Other unhashed
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1110|     contents are semantically ignored after structural parsing under ENC (subpacket framing still holds). This
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1111|     overrides generic OpenPGP metadata interpretation for V1 and is not a claim of full RFC metadata conformance;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1112|     no keyring library decides it. GnuPG's output (hashed type 33 of 21 octets, type 16 unhashed) satisfies it.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1113|     *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: "accepted critical or not and never read" left payload length, repetition and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1114|     cross-field consistency unspecified.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1115|   - **Hash prefix** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F10]: the two hash-prefix octets must match the first two octets of
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1116|     SHA256(document ‖ ENC trailer), else `SIG_INVALID` / `POSSESSION_INVALID` (git: its signature-verification
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1117|     outcome, section 6.3).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1118|   - **Public-key validity** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F10]: every P-256 key (transported `gpg`, fallback `kms`, the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1119|     repository key) must be a finite on-curve P-256 point passing FIPS 186-5 / SP 800-186 public-key validation for
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1120|     P-256, checked by the verifier, not by library default; otherwise `INVALID / KEY_FORMAT`. A configuration key
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1121|     that fails is a startup refusal (`TRUST_CONFIG_UNAUTHENTICATED`).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1122|   - **Possession code mapping** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F11]: a possession signature's codec failures take ENC's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1123|     exact codes (`SIG_EMPTY`, `SIG_PACKET`, `TRUNCATED`, `TRAILING`, `LENGTH_CAP`, `SIG_FORMAT`, in ENC order) with
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1124|     the slot as diagnostic, then `SIG_POLICY`, then `POSSESSION_INVALID`. Receipt signature codec failures are
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1125|     reported only at `a_sig` decoding (section 15.7 row 3).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1126|   - *Dated correction 2026-10-14:* the resolutions draft's "no subpacket in either area has the critical bit set" is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1127|     withdrawn. RFC 9580 rejects only unknown critical subpackets and recommends a critical creation time; the blanket
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1128|     ban rejected conforming signatures.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1129| - **Subpacket lengths.** RFC 9580 §5.2.3.7: first octet < 192, one octet; 192–254, two octets
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1130|   `((o1−192)<<8)+o2+192` (192–16319); 255 followed by a four-octet big-endian value (five octets total). The length
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1131|   counts the type octet and is ≥ 1. V1 accepts the shortest form only (a V1 rule, not an RFC ban); a longer form is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1132|   `SIG_FORMAT`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G28; r2-F14] *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: "255, four octets" misdescribed the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1133|   five-octet form.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1134| - Revocation is not evaluated. Loss or theft handling is operations. [A9:255-258; RB §1]

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1190| ## 10. Number rule
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1191| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1192| Accept a number exactly when RFC 8785's canonical serialization preserves its value. Reject otherwise. The three
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1193| conditions (not negative zero, finite after round-half-even, exact decimal value of `ES(d)` equals the literal) and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1194| the accepted and rejected examples are in ENC §1.2. [A9:519-524; ENC §1.2:118-148; ENC D-1:752-755] Proof:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1195| `formal/p8/PROOF.md` Lemma 3. Vectors: `formal/p8/vectors/`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1196| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1197| This replaces the literal "exactly representable as an IEEE 754 double" rule for this profile only. [A9:486-487;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1198| A9:521-524] The stale "needs an author sentence" remarks in ENC (ENC:147-148, D-1) and PROOF §6 are superseded by
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1199| A9.8. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G38; the ENC and PROOF wording edits are done, OWNER 2026-10-19]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1200| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1201| **`ES` recipe.** `ES(d)` is ECMA-262 NumberToString (7.1.12.1, Note 2) of the 10th edition (June 2019), the edition RFC 8785 cites
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1202| (edition, section and digest in the dependency manifest; later editions rename it Number::toString with the same
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1203| output) [OWNER 2026-10-19, item 15; source formal/dependency-sources/MANIFEST.md]. If d is +0 or −0: `"0"`. If d < 0: `"-"` ‖ ES(−d). Otherwise let n, k, s be integers with
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1204| k ≥ 1, 10^(k−1) ≤ s < 10^k, s × 10^(n−k) = d as a double, and k as small as possible; if several s qualify, choose
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1205| the one for which s × 10^(n−k) is closest in value to d, and if two are equally close, the even one. Then: if
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1206| k ≤ n ≤ 21, the k digits followed by n−k zeros; if 0 < n ≤ 21, the first n digits, `.`, the remaining k−n digits;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1207| if −6 < n ≤ 0, `0.`, −n zeros, the digits; otherwise the first digit, then `.` and the remaining digits if k > 1,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1208| then `e`, `+` or `-`, and abs(n−1) in decimal. Any formatter must reproduce N-01…N-22 and C-N01…C-N22; Python's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1209| `repr` is not ES. Unicode tables must be 16.0.0, identified by the UCD file digests in the dependency manifest; a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1210| runtime may use bundled pinned tables, and one whose tables do not match refuses to run (no verdict).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1211| [OWNER 2026-10-14, G29]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1212| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1213| **Field grammars.** `utc` years run 0001–9999 (proleptic Gregorian, seconds 00–59). LDH labels match
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1214| `[a-z0-9-]{1,63}` with no leading or trailing hyphen; all-numeric labels, the top label included, are allowed; at
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1215| least two labels; at most 241 bytes. This is what both P8 codecs already do. [OWNER 2026-10-14, G18; the ENC §3.2
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1216| and §7 wording edit is done, OWNER 2026-10-19]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1217|
