docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1501| ## 15. Evidence formats and check order [OWNER 2026-10-14]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1502| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1503| ### 15.1 Container [OWNER 2026-10-14, G14, G17, G33]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1504| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1505| A bundle is one UTF-8 JSON text that passes ENC §1.4 checks 1–5 and 7 and is canonical JCS. It contains no JSON
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1506| numbers. Heights and durations are decimal strings matching `0|[1-9][0-9]*` with value at most 4294967295. Binary
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1507| values are RFC 4648 §4 base64 with padding that round-trips (no non-zero pad bits, no line breaks). Size cap 2^27
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1508| bytes. Top level: exactly `{"layers":[L],"profile":"tessera-v1-strict"}`. After dispatch (section 3.1): a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1509| non-canonical container is `INVALID / JSON_NONCANONICAL`; then the absence rule (section 2.1) and A9.5's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1510| `git.object_format` outcomes; then any other schema failure is `INVALID / CONTAINER_SCHEMA`. Absence is inspected
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1511| only beneath correctly typed parents, a present non-string `object_format` is `CONTAINER_SCHEMA`, and a present
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1512| `issuer_record` with an absent internal field is `CONTAINER_SCHEMA` (section 2.1). [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F03]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1513| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1514| **Numbers.** JSON numbers are admitted syntactically at dispatch (D1's strict-JSON checks do not exclude them, and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1515| D2/D3 read only `profile` and the length of `layers`) and rejected after dispatch by the container schema: a JSON
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1516| number anywhere in the layer is `INVALID / CONTAINER_SCHEMA` (row 2.4, after row 2.1), never `OUT_OF_PROFILE`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1517| [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, A10]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1518| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1519| Layer `L` (closed; each member exactly once; all values base64 unless marked):
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1520| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1521| | Member | JSON type and content | Invariants |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1522| |---|---|---|
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1523| | `a_sig` | string: `A_sig` bytes | decoded by ENC §5 |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1524| | `manifest` | string: `F_manifest` | decoded by ENC §4 |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1525| | `possession` | object `{"gpg","kms"}`: detached signature over `F_manifest` per slot rule | both present |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1526| | `keys` | object `{"gpg","kms"}` (section 8) | both present |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1527| | `receipt_anchor` | object `{"ots","txid"}`; `txid` 64 lowercase hex, display order | |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1528| | `headers` | object `{"<height>":"<160 lowercase hex>"}` (80-byte raw header) | height grammar; nonempty; shared pool |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1529| | `dns` | object `{"ots","snapshot_body"}` | body per 15.3 |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1530| | `git` | object `{"blob","commit","object_format","ots","trees"}`; `trees` array of exactly 2 strings [root, sub]; `object_format` string | A9.5 |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1531| | `spec`, `vectors`, `preamble`, `dependency_manifest` | string: raw bytes | hashed only |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1532| | `issuer_record` | optional object `{"observed_anchor_delay_s","policy_version"}`; delay in the decimal grammar (seconds); `policy_version` matches `tessera-v1-issue-policy/(0|[1-9][0-9]*)` | diagnostics only |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1533| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1534| ### 15.2 OTS proofs and the txid [OWNER 2026-10-14, G20]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1535| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1536| OWNER CHOICE (supported-path limit). python-opentimestamps 0.4.5 is the reference reader, not normative.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1537| - **Header.** Magic `00 4f70656e54696d657374616d7073 0000 50726f6f66 00 bf89e2e884e89294`, varuint major version 1,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1538|   file-hash op `08` (SHA-256 only), the 32-byte digest, one Timestamp, end of input.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1539| - **Timestamp.** `Timestamp := (ff Item)* Item`; `Item := 00 Attestation | Op Timestamp`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1540| - **Ops.** `08` (sha256), `f0 varbytes` (append), `f1 varbytes` (prepend). Arguments 1–4096 bytes; every message and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1541|   result at most 4096 bytes.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1542| - **Attestations.** `tag(8) varbytes(payload)`, payload at most 8192 bytes. Bitcoin `0588960d73d71901`: payload is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1543|   exactly one varuint height. Pending `83dfe30d2ef90c8e`: payload varbytes(URI ≤ 1000), URI ignored.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1544| - **Wire completion** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F09]. `varbytes := varuint byte_count || exactly byte_count octets`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1545|   Both the pending and the Bitcoin payloads must be consumed exactly (the pending payload's inner URI framing
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1546|   included); otherwise `OTS_FORMAT`. A Bitcoin attestation whose message is not exactly 32 bytes is `INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1547|   OTS_FORMAT`, independently of header availability. Timestamp depth: the root Timestamp has depth 0, each Op →
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1548|   Timestamp step adds 1, `ff` siblings do not add. Op and attestation counts are of serialized items, duplicates
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1549|   included; duplicates are semantically inert only within those limits.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1550| - **Varuint.** LEB128, shortest form only, value ≤ 2^32 − 1. (python-opentimestamps 0.4.5 accepts redundant groups;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1551|   V1 does not.)
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1552| - **Bounds.** Depth ≤ 256; ≤ 65536 ops and ≤ 4096 attestations per proof; proof ≤ 2^20 bytes. Duplicate identical
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1553|   branches are permitted and have no effect.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1554| - **Rejections.** Any other op or tag, or any grammar or bound violation: `INVALID / OTS_FORMAT`. File digest must be
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1555|   SHA256(`A_sig`) for the receipt (`RECEIPT_ANCHOR_MISMATCH`), SHA256 of the ENC §6 envelope for the snapshot
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1556|   (`SNAPSHOT_STAMP_MISMATCH`), SHA256 of `<40-hex commit id>\n` for git (`GIT_STAMP_MISMATCH`).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1557| - **Merkle link.** A Bitcoin attestation's message is 32 bytes and equals bytes 36–68 of the bundled header at that
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1558|   height.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1559| - **Header fields** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F09]. In a raw 80-byte header: prev = `header[4:36]`, merkle root =
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1560|   `header[36:68]`, nTime = `uint32le(header[68:72])`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1561| - **txid (supported-proof subset).** On the path to the **selected** attestation, let the first two consecutive
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1562|   sha256 ops have input P, and let m be the message immediately before the maximal run of append/prepend ops that
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1563|   precedes them. Required: (1) P parses exactly, consuming every byte, as a non-witness Bitcoin transaction —
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1564|   version (4), compact-size input count ≥ 1, inputs (32 + 4 + compact-size script length + script + 4), compact-size
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1565|   output count ≥ 1, outputs (8 + compact-size length + script), locktime (4); no SegWit marker; compact sizes
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1566|   shortest form; (2) m is 32 bytes and some output script is exactly `6a 20 ‖ m`; (3) `hex(reverse(SHA256d(P)))`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1567|   equals `receipt_anchor.txid`. Otherwise `INVALID / ANCHOR_TXID_MISMATCH`. Any one path to the selected height may
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1568|   satisfy this. (All 344 Bitcoin paths in the repository's 127 proofs had this shape when RES G20 was written; the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1569| later owner check of 2026-10-14 under part (4) below counts 352 paths in 129 proofs, all conforming. Evidence, not a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1570| rule. [OWNER 2026-10-19, Levadura contested 6])
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1571| - **CompactSize and transaction fields** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F09]. A first byte < 253 is the value; `fd` then u16le,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1572|   `fe` then u32le, `ff` then u64le; shortest form only; a length or count exceeding the remaining bytes is rejected
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1573|   before allocation. Version, value and locktime are parsed as their fixed-width bytes (4, 8, 4) and not
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1574|   interpreted. Consensus validity and script execution are supplied by authentic pinned history, not revalidated
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1575|   here.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1576| - **(4) Merkle suffix (owner choice, fail-closed)** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F09]. After the two sha256 ops that
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1577|   produce the txid, the path to the selected attestation consists only of zero or more repetitions of (append or
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1578|   prepend of exactly 32 bytes, sha256, sha256); an empty suffix is a one-transaction block. Otherwise `INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1579|   ANCHOR_TXID_MISMATCH` for the receipt. Without it, arbitrary allowed operations could follow the identified
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1580|   transaction. All 352 Bitcoin paths in the repository's 129 proofs have this suffix (owner check 2026-10-14;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1581|   evidence, not a rule). This is a missing structural definition, not a demonstrated forged timestamp.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1582| - **Scope** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F08]. Parts (1), (2) and (4) apply at the selected height of the receipt, snapshot
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1583|   and git proofs; part (3), the txid equality, applies to `receipt_anchor` only. Snapshot or git failure of (1), (2)
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1584|   or (4) at every qualifying path at its h*: `INVALID / OTS_TX_SHAPE`. h* is selected first (section 7.1); a failing
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1585|   path never moves selection to a higher height.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1586| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1587| ### 15.3 DNSSEC snapshot body [OWNER 2026-10-14, G19, G24, G30]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1588| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1589| A concatenation of RRs, each in RFC 1035 §3.2.1 wire format, uncompressed, in RFC 4034 §6.2 canonical form (owner
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1590| name and every domain-name field inside RDATA, including the RRSIG signer name, lowercase and uncompressed).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1591| 1. **Groups, in order:** the root DNSKEY group; then for each zone z below the root down to the TXT's signer zone, a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1592|    DS group at z and a DNSKEY group at z; last the TXT group at `_tessera-v1.<D>`. A group is a maximal run of RRs
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1593|    with the same owner, CLASS IN, and TYPE t (the RRset) or TYPE RRSIG with Type Covered t (its witnesses). The RRset
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1594|    comes first, in RFC 4034 §6.3 canonical RDATA order without duplicates, then zero or more RRSIGs in (key tag,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1595|    inception, expiration, signature bytes) order. Each z is a proper descendant of the previous zone. Signer names:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1596|    the parent for DS, z for DNSKEY, the root for the root group, the last z for TXT.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1597|    - **Serialization ties and duplicates** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F07]. Canonical RRSIG RDATA is the final body
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1598|      serialization sort key: RRSIGs sort by (key tag, inception, expiration, signature bytes, canonical RRSIG
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1599|      RDATA). A duplicate is an RR identical in owner, class, type and RDATA (`SNAPSHOT_FORMAT`); TTL consistency
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1600|      within an RRset is checked separately (point 2).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1601|    - **Raw time fields in sort keys.** Inception and expiration in these sort keys, and in the G35 candidate tuple
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1602|      (section 7.3), are the raw 32-bit unsigned RRSIG field values compared numerically (equivalently, as
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1603|      big-endian bytes), not the absolute times resolved by section 7.3's serial arithmetic; the two orders differ
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1604|      only across the 2^32 wrap. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, EA-13]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1605|    - **Too-short RRSIG.** An RRSIG whose RDATA (within a consistent RDLENGTH) is too short for RFC 4034 §3.1's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1606|      fixed fields and signer name is attributed to the group of the immediately preceding RRs at the same owner,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1607|      not treated as a framing failure, and is malformed supported RRSIG RDATA: `INVALID / DNSSEC_FORMAT`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1608|      (section 6.1). [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, A06]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1609|    - **Chain skeleton, recovery grammar** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F06]. The root is the initial zone. The ordered zone
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1610|      skeleton is constructed from the supplied DS and DNSKEY owners and the RRSIG signer names: each names a zone,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1611|      and the zones, ordered by descent, must form one chain from the root. Omitted DS, DNSKEY, root DNSKEY or TXT
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1612|      groups are admitted as missing evidence (`UNVERIFIABLE / DNS_EVIDENCE_MISSING`; root:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1613|      `NO_TRUSTED_KSK_USABLE`); omission alone is never a format failure. Direct signing of the TXT by the root, or
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1614|      by any ancestor zone in the skeleton, is permitted (section 6.1 retains ancestor signing authority); "the last
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1615|      z" is the TXT RRSIG's signer zone, which is the root when no below-root zone is supplied. Conflicting supplied
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1616|      transitions or signer names (names not forming one descent chain, a DS group not signed by its parent zone in
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1617|      the skeleton, a DNSKEY group not signed by its own zone, a group after the TXT group) are `INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1618|      SNAPSHOT_FORMAT`. A supplied final TXT owner is checked by ENC §7's `DNS_OWNER`, even when wrong; its existence
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1619|      does not itself constitute an "outside-chain" framing failure. *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: the grammar did
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1620|      not say whether a skipped zone was omission or inconsistency, and "the last z" was undefined for a TXT signed
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1621|      by the root.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1622| 2. **Fields.** CLASS IN. TTL equal within an RRset and otherwise uninterpreted; validation uses the RRSIG's Original
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1623|    TTL.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1624| 3. **Framing versus completeness.** A truncated RR encoding, forbidden RR type, duplicate RR, inconsistent
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1625|    owner/type within a group, or misordered supplied group is `INVALID / SNAPSHOT_FORMAT`. Among RDATA defects,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1626|    RR boundary/RDLENGTH truncation and any domain-name field inside RDATA that is not in the canonical form above (an
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1627|    uppercase ASCII letter or a compression pointer, including in the RRSIG signer name) are `INVALID /
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1628|    SNAPSHOT_FORMAT`, whatever other witnesses the body carries; TXT's internal character-string parsing uses ENC's
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1629|    `DNS_RDATA` / `DNS_STRINGS`, and other malformed supported DNSKEY/RRSIG RDATA is `DNSSEC_FORMAT` (section 6.1).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1630|    [OWNER 2026-10-14, diff-1 F-1: the earlier wording let a non-canonical RRSIG beside a valid witness reach
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1631|    `VALID_STRICT` in one implementation and `INVALID` in another; fail-closed chosen.]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1632|    A defect in an RR's owner-name wire encoding is `SNAPSHOT_FORMAT`; a defect of the RRSIG signer-name field
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1633|    other than the non-canonical forms just named (which are `SNAPSHOT_FORMAT` under diff-1 F-1) and other than a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1634|    recovery-grammar conflict is malformed supported RRSIG RDATA, `DNSSEC_FORMAT`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1635|    diff-1, A12]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1636|    [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F06, r2-F05] A syntactically complete
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1637|    sequence lacking a required RRset or its witness RRSIG is `UNVERIFIABLE / DNS_EVIDENCE_MISSING` (root:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1638|    `NO_TRUSTED_KSK_USABLE`). Missing groups alone are not order violations. Forbidden: any type other than DNSKEY, DS,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1639|    TXT and RRSIG, and any RR at a name outside the chain (the final TXT group excepted, see the recovery grammar);
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1640|    CNAME and DNAME are not followed. An empty body is `LENGTH_CAP`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1641| 4. **Wildcards:** `INVALID / DNS_WILDCARD` (section 6.1). This is the global no-wildcard body restriction: any
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1642|    RRSIG in the body with Labels less than its owner's label count, whatever other witnesses the body carries.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1643|    [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F07] The Labels octet is read, and this restriction applied, whenever an RRSIG's RDATA
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1644|    has at least 4 bytes (Type Covered, Algorithm, Labels), however malformed the rest of that RDATA is.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1645|    [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, A07]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1646| 5. **Envelope:** ENC §6, `header ‖ u32 len ‖ body`, 1 ≤ len ≤ 2^24.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1647| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1648| ### 15.4 Git evidence [OWNER 2026-10-14, G25]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1649| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1650| OWNER CHOICE (supported-path limit) plus SHA-1DC (BROADEN).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1651| - **Commit body** (without `commit <len>\0`): `tree <40 lhex>LF`, `(parent <40 lhex>LF)*`, `author <bytes>LF`,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1652|   `committer <bytes>LF`, exactly one `gpgsig <line>LF` with `( <line>LF)*` continuations, `LF`, message. Repeated
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1653|   `parent` headers with distinct ids are allowed (merges); a repeated identical id, any other header (`encoding`,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1654|   `mergetag`, `gpgsig-sha256`, unknown), or a second `tree`, `author`, `committer` or `gpgsig` gives
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1655|   `INVALID / GIT_COMMIT_FORMAT`. Author and committer are not interpreted. The signed payload is the commit without
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1656|   the `gpgsig` line and its continuations (gitformat-signature(5)).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1657|   - **Empty identity values.** The `<bytes>` of `author` and of `committer` are nonempty: `author` or `committer`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1658|     followed by an empty value is `INVALID / GIT_COMMIT_FORMAT`. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, A09]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1659| - **Signature value** (continuations joined by LF, one leading space stripped from each): `-----BEGIN PGP
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1660|   SIGNATURE-----` LF, one empty line, one or more base64 lines of 1–76 RFC 4648 characters (`=` padding only at the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1661|   end of the last), an optional CRC line `=` plus 4 base64 characters, `-----END PGP SIGNATURE-----`, no trailing LF.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1662|   No armor headers, no other blank lines, no whitespace inside lines. A present CRC-24 must match. Dearmored bytes
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1663|   satisfy rule O's grammar and policy (section 8) with type 0x00. Otherwise `INVALID / GIT_SIG_FORMAT`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1664|   The concatenated base64 lines obey strict RFC 4648 round-trip and padding (no nonzero pad bits), as in section
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1665|   15.1; CRC presence and validity remain as above. Every armor, codec and policy violation is `GIT_SIG_FORMAT`, the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1666|   stated exception to section 8's `SIG_POLICY`; failed mathematics is `GIT_SIGNER_NOT_CONFIGURED` (section 6.3).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1667|   [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F10, r2-F11]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1668| - **Trees.** Entries `mode SP name NUL id20`; modes {40000, 100644, 100755, 120000, 160000} without leading zero;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1669|   names nonempty, no `/` or NUL, not `.` or `..`; strictly sorted in git order (trees compare as `name/`), no
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1670|   duplicates, body consumed exactly. Otherwise `INVALID / GIT_TREE_FORMAT`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1671| - **Path.** Root entry `tessera-v1` (40000), then `key-assertion` (100644), the blob; `git.trees` is exactly
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1672|   [root, sub]. Otherwise `INVALID / GIT_PATH`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1673|   - A commit whose `tree` header names an id other than the SHA-1 id of `git.trees[0]` is `INVALID / GIT_PATH`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1674|     (row 14.5); there is no dedicated code. [OWNER 2026-10-14, codified from diff-1, EA-22]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1675| - **Ids.** SHA-1 of `"<type> <len>\0" ‖ body` with collision detection (SHA-1DC); a detection is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1676|   `INVALID / GIT_SHA1_COLLISION`. SHA-1DC is a pinned detection implementation and version named in the dependency
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1677|   manifest, with its prescribed collision-return behaviour, not whatever a library calls SHA-1 (section 14.2 item
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1678|   15). [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F14]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1679| - **Repository key.** v4 ECDSA P-256 public-key body, rule O (signer outcomes in section 6.3).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1680| - **Not checked:** that the commit introduced the blob.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1681| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1682| ### 15.5 Trust configuration [OWNER 2026-10-14, G08, G09, G22]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1683| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1684| One RFC 8785 JSON object, no numbers, every key required; authenticated only by the release allowlist (section 5).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1685| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1686| **Closure and grammar** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F14]. The schema is closed recursively: every object at every level
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1687| (top level, KSK entries, repository entries, `sources` items) has exactly the listed keys. Parsing is strict UTF-8
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1688| and JCS with no JSON numbers; binary values are canonical base64 (section 15.1); times use the `utc` grammar of
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1689| section 10; decimal strings are canonical unsigned decimals (`0|[1-9][0-9]*`) with per-field ranges: `version` 1 to
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1690| 4294967295; `key_tag` 0 to 65535; `algorithm` 0 to 255; `reliance_lifetime_s` 1 to 2592000 (**owner choice**,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1691| fail-closed: at most 30 days; the observed value is 1814400); heights as in section 15.1. `root_ksks` is sorted by
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1692| (`signing_start`, numeric `key_tag`, `dnskey_rdata` bytes); `repository_keys` by (`signing_start`, `key` bytes).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1693| `root_ksks`, `repository_keys` and every `sources` array are nonempty, and every key in them valid (section 8). An
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1694| entry with `signing_end` null must have `signing_start` ≤ `as_of`. A schema failure is a startup refusal
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1695| (`TRUST_CONFIG_UNAUTHENTICATED`, no verdict), never a bundle `INVALID`. Cross-release invariants stay in the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1696| release checker; the offline verifier never fetches a previous config. *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: "every key
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1697| required" did not say closed at every level, and the sort and decimal rules were less concrete than section 15.1.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1698| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1699| | Key | Type and grammar | Invariants |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1700| |---|---|---|
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1701| | `format` | `"tessera-v1-trust/1"` | |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1702| | `profile` | `"tessera-v1-strict"` | |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1703| | `version` | decimal string ≥ 1 | prior + 1 |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1704| | `previous_sha256` | 64 lowercase hex | 64 zeros for version 1; else the prior config's hash |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1705| | `as_of` | RFC 3339 `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` | nondecreasing |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1706| | `issuer_domain` | `"wamason.com"` | equals D |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1707| | `header_pins` | object height-string → 64 lowercase hex (display order) | nonempty; one per height; immutable |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1708| | `root_ksks` | array of KSK entries, sorted by (`signing_start`, `key_tag`) | unique `dnskey_rdata` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1709| | `repository_keys` | array of `{"domain","key","signing_end","signing_start","sources"}` | `domain` = D; `key` base64 v4 P-256 body; `signing_end` nullable; start ≤ end; unique `key` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1710| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1711| KSK entry (strings unless marked):
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1712| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1713| | Field | Type | Invariant |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1714| |---|---|---|
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1715| | `name` | e.g. `"KSK-2017"` | unique |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1716| | `key_tag` | decimal string 0–65535 | equals RFC 4034 App. B tag of `dnskey_rdata` |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1717| | `algorithm` | decimal string | equals the RDATA algorithm; in {8, 13} |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1718| | `dnskey_rdata` | base64 of RFC 4034 §2.2 RDATA | flags 257, REVOKE clear, protocol 3 |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1719| | `ds_sha256` | 64 lowercase hex | SHA-256 over root owner wire `00` ‖ RDATA |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1720| | `signing_start`, `signing_end` | RFC 3339; `signing_end` nullable | start ≤ end |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1721| | `reliance_lifetime_s` (L) | decimal string | immutable |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1722| | `publication`, `revocation` | RFC 3339 or null | informational |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1723| | `sources` | nonempty array of `{"description","sha256","uri"}` | `sha256` of the archived source |
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1724| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1725| ### 15.6 Dependency manifest [OWNER 2026-10-14, G15]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1726| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1727| A closed JCS object, exactly `{"entries":[…],"format":"tessera-v1-deps/1"}`; `entries` sorted by `id`, unique. Each
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1728| entry has all of: `id` (`[a-z0-9-]+`), `title`, `edition`, `sections` (nonempty array of strings), `errata`,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1729| `digest_sha256` (64 lowercase hex, or null where no canonical bytes exist), `retrieval`, `redistribution`,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1730| `failure_consequence`; strings unless marked. The entry list is section 9's, one entry per document (section 9 lists
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1731| concepts and several RFCs per line; the correspondence is in `formal/dependency-sources/MANIFEST.md`).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1732| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1733| **Multi-file sources** [OWNER 2026-10-19, item 15; source formal/dependency-sources/MANIFEST.md]: where the canonical bytes are several files (Bitcoin Core source, git, SHA-1DC),
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1734| `digest_sha256` is the sha256 of a `SHA256SUMS` listing (`sha256sum` format, `<hex>  <relative path>` per file, one
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1735| line per file), which is kept beside the files. Where only an HTML and a PDF form exist (ECMA-262), the digest is of
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1736| the PDF and the HTML digest is in `retrieval`. `digest_sha256` is null when exact source bytes were not obtained,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1737| with that limitation and its reason stated in `retrieval` (IEEE 754: not fetched). Redistribution restrictions alone
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1738| do not require a null digest. [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-10] *(Was: "A source with no redistributable bytes (IEEE 754)
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1739| has `digest_sha256` null.")*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1740| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1741| **Normative, informative, distributed** [OWNER 2026-10-19, item 15; source formal/dependency-sources/MANIFEST.md]: the format has no separate field. The manifest as built marks
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1742| informative entries in free text (the word "informative" in `errata` or `sections`; RFC 9102, RFC 5480, BIP 144),
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1743| and `redistribution` states whether the source is distributed with the verifier, archived with the spec sources, or
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1744| retrieved by reference. Entries not so marked are normative. Only SHA-1DC is distributed with the verifier.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1745| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1746| ### 15.7 Total check order for the reported reason [OWNER 2026-10-14, G31, G26; r2-F11]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1747| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1748| **Numbered check table** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F11; incorporates r2-F02–F10 and r2-F12]. The reported reason is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1749| the first **failed** row in (row id, tie key) order; if no row failed, the first **unperformable** row. A row whose
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1750| necessary input cannot be obtained because of an earlier row's failure or unperformability is unperformable and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1751| contributes no reason of its own; the table is ordered so that every such dependency points to an earlier row.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1752| Rows 11.1–11.4 are evaluated whatever else fails, because they determine T (section 3.4). Slot order is kms, then
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1753| gpg. Candidates are ordered by the G35 tuple (section 7.3), never by their position in a transport array; members
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1754| and missing paths by JCS key order with numeric array indices; heights ascending. The verdict rule (section 3.3) is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1755| unchanged: INVALID over UNVERIFIABLE, and no early exit before every earlier-priority row and every stable field,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1756| including T, is settled.

docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1849| ### 15.8 Spec and vectors object assembly [OWNER 2026-10-14, G13]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1850| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1851| Each object is one or more parts. A part is the ASCII line `tessera-v1-part <path> <length>` LF, then exactly
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1852| `<length>` bytes (decimal, no leading zeros), then LF. `<path>` is repository-relative UTF-8 without spaces. Parts are
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1853| in bytewise-sorted path order; file bytes verbatim as committed. The spec object holds the frozen
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1854| `docs/V1-PROFILE.md` and `formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md` (plus the branch-registration supplement under the hybrid). The
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1855| vectors object holds every file under `formal/p8/vectors/` and the non-P8 conformance vectors (RES §L). The vectors
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1856| may embed the spec hash; the spec never embeds the vectors' hash.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1857| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1858| **Canonical recipe** [OWNER 2026-10-14, r2-F13]. Supersedes the header and inventory sentences above where they
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1859| differ.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1860| - **Header grammar.** `tessera-v1-part` SP `<path>` SP `<length>` LF, with fixed single literal spaces. `<path>` is an
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1861|   ASCII repository-relative path matching `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+`, with no empty, `.` or `..` component, no leading
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1862|   slash, and unique within the object; `<length>` matches `0|[1-9][0-9]*`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1863| - **Bytes.** Only tracked regular-file **blob bytes** from a named freeze commit: no newline conversion, no symlink
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1864|   following, no generated caches, no working-tree overlay.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1865| - **Inventory.** The freeze record publishes the exact sorted path inventory of each object, including the non-P8
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1866|   conformance vector files (RES §L names cases, not paths), with an assembler and an independent byte-agreement
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1867|   check.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1868| - **A9 is a part (owner choice).** The spec object also carries the governing A9 bytes
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1869|   (`docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md` at its signing commit) as a part, so the object is the complete archival
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1870|   spec; this was chosen over distributing A9 separately with a bound digest.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1871| - **A10 and the current proof are parts** [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-08]. The spec object also carries, as parts, the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1872|   signed A10 bytes (`docs/phase-0-prereg-amendment-10.md`, signed by the author's commit `9ade764`; this includes
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1873|   A10.4.2's required custody-procedure contents) and the current repaired `formal/p8/PROOF.md`, each taken at the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1874|   freeze commit, whose A9 and A10 bytes must equal those at their signing commits. The "complete archival spec"
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1875|   sentence above holds only with these parts. HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT §9's table records the older baseline proof hash
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1876|   (`06910a5f…`); the current proof's SHA-256 is recorded in the freeze record, beside that baseline, outside every
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1877|   included part.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1878| - **Hashes live outside.** Actual spec, vectors and catalog hashes are recorded in a separate release/freeze record
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1879|   **outside** the frozen spec parts; recording them inside an included file would be self-reference.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1880| - The part format is a new packaging choice, not an inherited P8 construction or a proven archival format. Once
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1881|   exact catalog hashes exist, runtime hash checks are unique; runtime never parses these objects as policy.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1882|   *(Dated correction 2026-10-14: "repository-relative UTF-8 without spaces" admitted LF, CR, tab, absolute and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1883|   dot paths and duplicates; "every file under formal/p8/vectors/" did not select tracked regular files; "the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1884|   non-P8 conformance vectors (RES §L)" named cases, not files.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1885| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1886| ### 15.9 Release format [OWNER 2026-10-19, §14.2 item 2]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1887| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1888| Source: `docs/V1-FREEZE-OPEN.md` §3 (proposal R1–R6) as adjusted by its "Owner decisions" (2026-10-19); A10.4.2
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1889| (rows 34 and 36); the custody draft `docs/V1-RELEASE-KEY-CUSTODY-DRAFT.md` §2–§3. **Frozen at the 30 Oct freeze:** the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1890| envelope below (archive, release manifest, signature, TEST/production rules, bootstrap rule). **Not frozen:** the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1891| verifier's code bytes and its inventory, which each release binds (owner decision 1), and the production key,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1892| ceremony, bootstrap record and rehearsal, which come after the freeze and before the first public verifier release
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1893| (A10.4.2). None of this is a bundle-verifier rule.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1894| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1895| **R1. A release is one archive.**
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1896| - One file, `tessera-verifier-v1-<n>.parts` (production) or `tessera-verifier-v1-TEST-<n>.parts` (TEST); `<n>` is the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1897|   canonical decimal release number.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1898| - Its bytes are the section 15.8 part format (header grammar, sorted paths). Every part except `RELEASE.json` is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1899|   copied from the named **source commit** (verbatim tracked regular-file blob bytes). `RELEASE.json` is generated
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1900|   deterministically from those bytes and the declared release metadata; `source_commit` identifies their source
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1901|   commit. The independent assembler reproduces the complete archive, including that generated manifest, and it is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1902|   compared by hash [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-02] *(Was: "verbatim tracked regular-file blob bytes at one named source
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1903|   commit. Nothing is generated during assembly; the archive is rebuilt from the source commit and compared by
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1904|   hash", which required `RELEASE.json`, a tracked file, to name the commit containing it)* (the section 15.8 assembler and independent byte-agreement check), which is the input the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1905|   custody procedure's review-and-build step (A10.4.2 C01) needs.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1906| - Required parts: `RELEASE.json` (R2); `trust.json`, the exact section 15.5 bytes; `catalog.json`, the exact frozen
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1907|   catalog bytes; `release_constants.py` (R2); the dependency lock (R6); the vendored SHA-1DC source with
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1908|   `SHA1DC-PIN.md`; `install.sh`; the relying-party text; the verifier code. No other part carries authority.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1909| - The archive is unpacked only after R3 succeeds. Scripts run as `bash install.sh`, so no file mode is needed.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1910|   *(The custody draft's `.tar` is replaced: the part format has one byte string per file set.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1911| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1912| **R2. The release manifest and how the trust configuration and catalog bind.**
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1913| - `RELEASE.json` is one closed JCS object with exactly these keys: `format` (`"tessera-v1-release/1"`), `namespace`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1914|   (`"PRODUCTION"` or `"TEST"`), `release` (= `<n>`), `profile` (`"tessera-v1-strict"`), `source_commit` (40 lowercase
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1915|   hex), `trust_config_sha256`, `trust_config_version`, `catalog_sha256`, `freeze_record_sha256`, `parts` (an object
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1916|   mapping every other part's path to the 64-lowercase-hex SHA-256 of its bytes, exactly the archive's other paths),
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1917|   and `release_key_successor` (40 uppercase hex v4 fingerprint, or null). All values are strings except `parts` (an
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1918|   object of strings) and a null successor. `parts` is how a release binds its verifier code (owner decision 1).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1919| - **Binding equalities**, checked before signing and again by `install.sh`; any failure means no installation:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1920|   every `parts` entry equals the hash of that part and the path sets are equal; SHA-256(`trust.json`) =
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1921|   `trust_config_sha256` = `release_constants.TRUST_SHA256`; SHA-256(`catalog.json`) = `catalog_sha256` =
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1922|   `release_constants.CATALOG_SHA256`, and `release_constants.CATALOG_BYTES` equals `catalog.json`; the `version`
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1923|   inside `trust.json` = `trust_config_version`; `release_constants.NAMESPACE` = `namespace`. Under `PRODUCTION`,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1924|   `catalog_sha256` equals the catalog hash in the freeze record whose SHA-256 is `freeze_record_sha256`.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1925| - Run time is unchanged: a `--trust` file whose hash is not `TRUST_SHA256`, or that fails section 15.5, is
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1926|   `TRUST_CONFIG_UNAUTHENTICATED`, no verdict. Each new release's `trust.json` passes the release checker (section 5
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1927|   release invariants, EA-12) against the previous release's.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1928| - **No machine-specific facts in the signed archive.** `release_constants.py` holds only `NAMESPACE`,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1929|   `TRUST_SHA256`, `CATALOG_SHA256`, `CATALOG_BYTES` and `UNICODE_VERSION` (`"16.0.0"`), all independent of the build
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1930|   machine. Facts about one installation (the interpreter's `unicodedata` file hash, whether SHA-1DC built) are
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1931|   written by `install.sh` into a per-installation record `install.json`, outside the archive and unsigned; the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1932|   verifier checks them at start (Python 3.14, Unicode 16.0.0, SHA-1DC present, else the existing startup refusals)
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1933|   and reports the SHA-256 of `install.json` as a diagnostic. `install.json` carries no authority. *(Closes the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1934|   triage's departure: `build_release.py` wrote `UNICODE_MODULE_SHA256` and `SHA1DC_AVAILABLE` from the build
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1935|   machine into the release.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1936| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1937| **R3. The release signature.**
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1938| - A **detached, binary (unarmored) OpenPGP v4 signature of type 0x00** over the exact archive bytes, file
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1939|   `<archive>.sig`, ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256, satisfying rule O's grammar and policy (section 8). The signing session
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1940|   checks it against rule O before it leaves the session.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1941| - The release key is **one v4 ECDSA P-256 primary key with no subkeys**, identified by its full v4 fingerprint. A
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1942|   signature by any other key, or by a subkey, authenticates nothing.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1943| - The signature covers the whole archive, code included. The key never signs a hash written as text.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1944| - **Acceptance.** Accept only if a trusted acquisition-side checker first validates exactly one unarmored
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1945|   signature against rule O's grammar and section 8 policy, confirms the authenticated primary-key identity (the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1946|   currently authenticated production key under R5: the bootstrapped key or an authenticated successor), and the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1947|   pinned `gpgv` verifies the exact archive bytes with a keyring holding **only** that key. Installation then
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1948|   requires R2's equalities. The checker must be available before executing the acquired archive. [OWNER
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1949|   2026-10-19, PR-04, PR-05] *(Was: "Accept iff the pinned `gpgv` exits 0 on `<archive>.sig <archive>` with a keyring
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1950|   holding only the production key whose full fingerprint was obtained by R5"; `gpgv` also exits 0 on a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1951|   new-format-header signature, on two concatenated signatures and on armored signatures, which rule O rejects.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1952|   The manifest entry `gpgv` pins the upstream GnuPG 2.4.4 source (digest of the tarball) [OWNER 2026-10-19, item 15; source formal/dependency-sources/MANIFEST.md]. It does not certify
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1953|   distribution builds (the owner machine's Ubuntu `2.4.4-2ubuntu17.6` is patched; its bytes differ). A distribution
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1954|   build is acceptable only if it reproduces the upstream behaviour (exit status) on the release-format test vectors.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1955|   **The pin is upstream GnuPG 2.4.4** [OWNER DECISION 2026-10-23, E9 packet E9-05]. [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-12, superseded] *(Was: "The version is the one observed;
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1956|   R3/R6 have not yet fixed it, so it remains an owner choice", beside an unqualified pin.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1957| - **TEST releases use this same format** with a TEST key over the whole TEST archive, code included. The
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1958|   `tessera-v1-test-release/1` record (two hashes, raw r‖s, SPKI-hash signer) is withdrawn as a release: it did not
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1959|   cover the verifier code. It survives only as the section 3.5 instrument interface for the conformance and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1960|   differential harnesses, which is never a release and which an installed verifier refuses (R4). *(Closes the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1961|   triage's departure on TEST signature coverage.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1962| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1963| **R4. Production is the default; TEST is explicit.**
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1964| - Every release before the first public verifier release is a **TEST release**: `namespace` `"TEST"`, a `TEST` file
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1965|   name, signed by a TEST release key in the R3 format. TEST keys are throwaway v4 P-256 keys and may live on the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1966|   operational computer. A TEST public key is never published as the release key, never named in the freeze record,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1967|   the bootstrap record or relying-party text, and never named in any `release_key_successor` (A10 row 36).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1968| - The production key signs only `"PRODUCTION"`; a TEST key signs only `"TEST"`. The signing session checks this.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1969| - **Production refusal is by key, not by label.** A TEST signature fails R3 because the production keyring holds only
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1970|   the production key. The label prevents honest mistakes; it is not a security check.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1971| - **Mode comes from the installed archive, never from the command line.** There is no `--production` flag. An
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1972|   installed verifier whose `NAMESPACE` is not exactly `"TEST"` is a production verifier: it refuses
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1973|   `--test-release`, `--test-release-key` and every `TESSERA_V1_TEST_*` variable with `TEST_AUTHORITY_REFUSED` and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1974|   no verdict, whatever else the command line or environment says. Omitting a flag can therefore never select TEST.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1975| - **The explicit TEST provisioning path** is one of: (a) an installed TEST archive (`NAMESPACE = "TEST"`),
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1976|   acquired by R3 against a TEST keyring the operator names explicitly; or (b) the section 3.5 instrument interface,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1977|   usable only from a source checkout with no installed release, where the TEST release, TEST key and catalog must
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1978|   all be supplied; with none supplied it refuses (`TRUST_CONFIG_UNAUTHENTICATED`). *(Closes the triage's departure:
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1979|   production mode was a CLI flag, so an invocation without it accepted TEST provisioning.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1980| - **Rehearsal (A10 row 36), before the first public verifier release:** an otherwise correct archive signed only by
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1981|   a TEST key is refused by the R3/R5 acquisition procedure, including when the TEST public key is offered as the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1982|   key; and an installed production verifier refuses the section 3.5 interface.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1983| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1984| **R5. Out-of-band authentication of the production key** (owner decision 2).
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1985| - The relying party's root of trust is the production key's **full v4 fingerprint**, obtained before and apart from
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1986|   any release. A key or fingerprint that arrives with a release, on the same page as a release, or from the
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1987|   operational environment authenticates nothing. The operational environment is assessed by actual roles,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1988|   credentials and release authorization, not by provider names; it includes at least the operational computer
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1989|   (the NUC), this repository, DNS, the issuing AWS account and the GCP project that holds the slot-2 key, and
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1990|   another provider's name does not by itself establish independence [AUTHOR COMMENT 2026-10-23, E9 row 6]. Such a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1991|   key or fingerprint authenticates nothing, except a
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1992|   successor fingerprint named by a conforming release verified under the currently authenticated key (Rotation,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1993|   below). [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-05]
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1994| - **Frozen rule:** the fingerprint is published through **at least two channels independent of the operational
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1995|   environment**, named in the custody record before the first public verifier release (A10.4.2). The channels are
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1996|   the author's to name. *(Owner recommendation for then, not frozen: a Zenodo record under the author's ORCID plus
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1997|   one offline printed copy.)* A relying party who did not obtain the fingerprint this way relies on authenticated
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1998|   first acquisition as an assumption, which the relying-party text states (A10.4.2: "does not protect a user who …
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:1999|   acquires a substituted initial key").
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2000| - The fingerprint is recorded in the dated **first-production-release bootstrap record**, which names the freeze
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2001|   record by hash and the production key, and is published and OpenTimestamps-stamped. Publication and stamping give
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2002|   a dated public record; they are not authentication. The freeze record does not contain the fingerprint.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2003| - **Initial bootstrap and rotation** [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-05]. Initial bootstrap authenticates the first
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2004|   production key. A successor is authenticated by a conforming release verified under the currently authenticated
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2005|   key and naming the successor fingerprint in `release_key_successor`; subsequently acquired successor key material
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2006|   must match that fingerprint. The next release is signed by the successor.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2007| - **Loss or compromise.** V1 has no assured recovery. New releases stop. Loss recovery starts a separately
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2008|   authenticated release lineage, with new out-of-band publication under this rule and a new dated bootstrap record,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2009|   and does not establish continuity with the old lineage. Genuine old releases stay available. [OWNER 2026-10-19,
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2010|   PR-05] *(Was: "a replacement key needs new out-of-band publication under this rule and a new dated bootstrap
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2011|   record", which read as a second way to introduce a key in the same lineage.)*
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2012| 
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2013| **R6. Dependency pinning.**
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2014| - The archive carries a lock with exact versions **and SHA-256 hashes** for every Python package, installed with
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2015|   hash checking required; wheels are retrieved at install time, not distributed.
docs/V1-PROFILE.md:2016| - Python 3.14 with Unicode 16.0.0 tables is checked at install and at start; SHA-1DC is built from the vendored,
