formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:86| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:87| ## 0. What V1 encodes, and the encoding map (O-79)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:88| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:89| V1 signs, hashes or publishes eight byte strings. Nothing else in the bundle is signed or anchored directly, except
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:90| the git channel's stamped message (the signed commit's 40-hex id plus LF, A9.5), through which row 8's git copy is
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:91| anchored (§7.2). [OWNER 2026-10-19, Levadura C6]
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:92| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:93| | # | Byte string | Constructed as | Signed / hashed by | Section |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:94| |---|---|---|---|---|
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:95| | 1 | Attestation frame, slot `kms` | frame, tag `tessera-v1/attest` | KMS key; committed byte for byte in the anchor preimage | §3 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:96| | 2 | Attestation frame, slot `gpg` | frame, tag `tessera-v1/attest` | gpg key; committed byte for byte in the anchor preimage | §3 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:97| | 3 | Detached signature `S_kms` over frame 1 | one signature in the serialization §5.2 pins for `(alg, kms)` | committed byte for byte in the anchor preimage; verified over frame 1 from those committed bytes (§5.3) | §5.2 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:98| | 4 | Detached signature `S_gpg` over frame 2 | one signature in the serialization §5.2 pins for `(alg, gpg)` | committed byte for byte in the anchor preimage; verified over frame 2 from those committed bytes (§5.3) | §5.2 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:99| | 5 | Manifest frame (map-v1 tuple) | frame, tag `tessera-v1/manifest` | both keys (possession proofs); its SHA-256 is `manifest_sha256` | §4 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:100| | 6 | Receipt-anchor preimage `A_sig` | tagged, tag `tessera-v1/receipt-anchor-sig` | SHA-256, stamped by OpenTimestamps | §5 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:101| | 7 | DNSSEC-snapshot preimage | tagged, tag `tessera-v1/dnssec-snapshot` | SHA-256, stamped by OpenTimestamps (C4 snapshot rule) | §6 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:102| | 8 | Key-publication value (keys + issuance window) | ASCII record at `_tessera-v1.<D>`; the same value in the git key-assertion blob | the zone's DNSSEC keys; the repository key via the signed, anchored commit | §7, §7.1, §7.2 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:103| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:104| Rows 3 and 4 are new as of 2026-10-12. A signature is the signer's output, not a construction of P8. P8 fixes only
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:105| its serialization and its place in `A_sig`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:106| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:107| The spec, conformance-vector and preamble objects are content-addressed: their SHA-256 values sit inside the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:108| signed common bytes (§3.2), and they are never signed or anchored on their own.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:109| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:110| **Where each of the seven symbolic bindings lives** (A5 §A5.4; A7 §A7.9; R-3.12a):
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:111| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:112| | Binding (`framed(...)` argument) | Lives in | Equal across slots? |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:113| |---|---|---|
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:114| | object type `objType` | the envelope's `type_tag` = `tessera-v1/attest` | yes (one tag for both slots) |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:115| | canonicalization version `canonVer` | the envelope's `canonicalization_version` = `0x0001` | yes |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:116| | algorithm `alg` | the payload's `common.alg` (A3 §A3.6.1: in the canonical payload) | yes |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:117| | issuer identity `issuerId` | the payload's `common.issuer` = D | yes |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:118| | manifest hash `manifestHash` | the payload's `common.manifest_sha256` = hex(SHA256(manifest frame)) | yes |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:119| | payload | the payload's `common` member: the requester's `content` plus the common metadata | yes, **byte-equal** |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:120| | key fingerprint `kfp` | the payload's `signer.key_fp`, the **only** signer-specific member | no |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:121| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:122| **Requester content versus signer metadata.** The requester's content is exactly `common.content`. All other
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:123| `common` members are common metadata, written by the issuer and equal for both signers. `signer` holds the only
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:124| signer-specific field. That makes A5 §A5.4's "payload equal across signer slots" a statement about bytes (§3.4).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:125| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:126| ---
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:127| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:128| ## 1. Canonical payload bytes: RFC 8785 over the accepted domain
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:129| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:130| ### 1.1 The accepted value domain V
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:131| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:132| A JSON value is in V if and only if all of the following hold.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:133| - **Literals.** `null`, `true` and `false`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:134| - **Numbers.** A finite IEEE 754 binary64 value other than −0. *Reason: this is exactly what RFC 8785 can
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:135|   serialize without loss.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:136| - **Strings, including member names.** A sequence of Unicode scalar values with:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:137|   - no surrogate code point (U+D800 to U+DFFF), and so no lone `\uD8xx` escape;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:138|   - no noncharacter (U+FDD0 to U+FDEF, and U+xFFFE or U+xFFFF in every plane). *Reason: RFC 7493 §2.1 (I-JSON); G-04.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:139|   - no code point that is unassigned (General_Category `Cn`) in **Unicode 16.0.0**. *Reason: this pins the NFC test
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:140|     (next item) to one table. Under Unicode's stability policy, a string built from characters assigned in 16.0.0
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:141|     that is NFC under 16.0.0 stays NFC under every later version. An unassigned code point carries no such
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:142|     guarantee, so two verifiers on different Unicode versions could disagree about it.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:143|   - the string already in NFC. It is **rejected, never normalized**. *Reason: R-3.4, "inputs relying on Unicode
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:144|     normalization assumptions"; G-05 kept.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:145| - **Arrays.** Arrays of members of V.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:146| - **Objects.** Objects with pairwise distinct member names, compared after unescaping. *Reason: R-3.4's duplicate
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:147|   names; G-04.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:148| - **Depth.** Nesting depth is at most **64** for a whole payload. Each array or object adds 1. The requester's
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:149|   `content` sits at depth 3, so it may nest at most **62** levels. *Reason: this pins a limit that real parsers
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:150|   otherwise set differently.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:151| - **Size.** A payload is at most **2^24 bytes** (16 MiB). *Reason: a fixed cap that both implementations
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:152|   enforce. No V1 payload comes near it.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:153| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:154| ### 1.2 The number rule: value-preserving (G-03 and G-56 resolved for V1)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:155| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:156| A number **literal** `L` (RFC 8259 grammar) in submitted JSON text is accepted if and only if:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:157| 1. L is not a negative zero: no `-` with zero value (`-0`, `-0.0`, `-0e5`). *Reason: the R-3.4 list.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:158| 2. `d` = the binary64 nearest to L's exact decimal value, under round-half-even, is finite. Overflow is rejected.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:159| 3. **The exact decimal value of `ES(d)` equals the exact decimal value of L.** `ES` is ECMAScript
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:160|    Number::toString, the serialization RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3 uses.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:161| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:162| Accepted: `9.8`, `9.80`, `1E2`, `1e21`, `5e-324`, `123456789012345680000` and `0e99999999999999999999`. Each keeps its
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:163| value, and only the spelling changes.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:164| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:165| Rejected, each with its reason:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:166| - `1e400`: overflow.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:167| - `1e-400`: nonzero, and rounds to 0.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:168| - `333333333.33333329` and `9007199254740993`: the value would change.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:169| - `0.1000000000000000055511151231257827021181583404541015625`: this is *exactly* a double, but RFC 8785 prints it as
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:170|   `0.1`, which has a different value.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:171| - `4.9e-324`: rounds to the smallest subnormal, which prints as `5e-324`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:172| - `-0`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:173| - `NaN` and `Infinity`: not JSON at all.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:174| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:175| Subnormals that survive rule 3 are accepted, so G-03b is reversed: RFC 8785 treats them as ordinary.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:176| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:177| **Why this rule and not the registered literal rule.** Read literally, "exactly representable as a double" does
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:178| not compose with RFC 8785. It *accepts* `0.1000000000000000055511151231257827021181583404541015625`, whose
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:179| canonical form `0.1` it then *rejects* when the verifier re-reads the payload. So under that reading,
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:180| `canonical()` maps its own domain outside itself. The value-preserving rule is the largest rule under which:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:181| - (a) canonicalization never changes a value; and
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:182| - (b) every canonical output is itself accepted.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:183| **This changes A1 P8's rejection item and prereg §4.3's wording. A9.8 registers it for `tessera-v1-strict`,
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:184| replacing both (A9.7 rows 22–23).** [OWNER 2026-10-19, G38] *(Was: "… and it needs an author sentence (§9, D-1). The
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:185| V1 derivation's profile line, 'registered number rule unchanged', must be reconciled with it either way." A9.8
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:186| supplied the sentence, and the derivation's line now states the value-preserving rule.)*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:187| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:188| What "never helpfully normalized" means here. The **issuer's ingestion** normalizes *spelling only*:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:189| - insignificant whitespace;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:190| - member order;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:191| - escape choice;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:192| - number spelling.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:193| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:194| It never changes a value. The **verifier normalizes nothing**: a payload must already equal `JCS` of its own
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:195| parse (§1.4, `JSON_NONCANONICAL`). Injectivity (PROOF.md) is stated over *values*. Two texts that differ only in
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:196| spelling are one value by definition, and they get one canonical byte string. That is intended.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:197| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:198| ### 1.3 Serialization
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:199| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:200| `canonical(v) = JCS(v)` (RFC 8785):
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:201| - UTF-8 output, with no insignificant whitespace;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:202| - object members sorted by the UTF-16 code units of their names;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:203| - numbers printed by `ES`;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:204| - strings escaped only for `"`, `\` and U+0000 to U+001F: `\b \t \n \f \r` where defined, `\u00xx` with
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:205|   lowercase hex otherwise. Every other scalar appears literally.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:206| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:207| *Reason: R-3.1 binds to RFC 8785. Vectors C-04 and C-05 pin the escape and the UTF-16 ordering traps, for example
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:208| U+1F600 sorting before U+E000.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:209| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:210| ### 1.4 Decoding, and the order in which rejections are reported
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:211| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:212| Two entry points.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:213| - `ingest(text)` takes requester JSON: whitespace is allowed, and the depth limit is 62.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:214| - `payload(bytes)` takes in-frame bytes: the depth limit is 64, and the bytes must be canonical. Before the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:215|   checks below it enforces §1.1's size limit: more than 2^24 bytes gives `LENGTH_CAP`, the code a frame's
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:216|   `payload_length` check gives for the same bytes (§3.1), so the standalone entry point and the frame agree.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:217|   [OWNER 2026-10-19, P8F-04]
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:218| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:219| Each runs these checks in this order and reports the **first category that fails**, scanning the whole value for
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:220| each category. *Reason: both implementations then agree on the reason code, not only on rejection.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:221| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:222| 1. `JSON_ENCODING`: the bytes are not strict UTF-8. Overlongs, encoded surrogates and values above U+10FFFF are
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:223|    rejected.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:224| 2. `JSON_SYNTAX`:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:225|    - a BOM; not exactly one RFC 8259 JSON text; trailing non-whitespace;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:226|    - a raw control character in a string; bad escapes; leading zeros; `+`; `.5`; `1.`; `NaN`; `Infinity`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:227| 3. `JSON_DEPTH`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:228| 4. `JSON_DUPLICATE_NAME`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:229| 5. `JSON_STRING`: a surrogate, a noncharacter, an unassigned code point, or text that is not NFC.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:230| 6. `JSON_NUMBER`: §1.2.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:231| 7. *(`payload` only)* `JSON_NONCANONICAL`: the bytes are not equal to `JCS` of the parsed value.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:232| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:233| ---
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:234| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:235| ## 2. The tagged byte strings: one header, four tags
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:236| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:237| Every byte string that a V1 slot key signs (attestation and manifest frames), and every receipt-anchor and snapshot
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:238| preimage that OTS stamps, begins with the same header. Two V1 byte strings carry no header: the git channel's
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:239| stamped message, which is exactly the 40 lowercase hex digits of the signed commit id followed by one LF (A9.5,
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:240| §7.2), and the key-publication value (§7), which the repository key and the DNSSEC keys sign through git and DNS.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:241| Neither is a frame (Remark 10 of PROOF.md). [OWNER 2026-10-19, Levadura C6] *(Was: "Every V1 byte string that a V1
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:242| key signs or that OTS stamps begins with the same header:", which the git stamped message contradicts.)*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:243| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:244| The header:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:245| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:246| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:247| header(t) = u8 len(t) || t                       t ∈ T (ASCII, no NUL)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:248| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:249| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:250| | Tag `t` | len | First bytes (hex) | Construction |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:251| |---|---|---|---|
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:252| | `tessera-v1/attest` | 17 | `11 74 65 73 …` | frame, §3 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:253| | `tessera-v1/manifest` | 19 | `13 74 65 73 …` | frame, §4 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:254| | `tessera-v1/receipt-anchor-sig` | 29 | `1d 74 65 73 …` | signature-inclusive anchor preimage `A_sig`, §5 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:255| | `tessera-v1/dnssec-snapshot` | 26 | `1a 74 65 73 …` | snapshot preimage, §6 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:256| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:257| `tessera-v1/receipt-anchor` (25, `19 …`), the frame-only anchor tag of the 2026-10-09 draft, is **withdrawn**. It
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:258| is not in T, so it is rejected with `TAG_UNKNOWN` (§5.1).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:259| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:260| - One string serves as both the domain-separation tag and the object type. R-3.11 lists the two as separate items,
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:261|   but A1 P8's four-field frame has a single slot. The prefix `tessera-v1/` does the domain separation, and the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:262|   suffix names the type (G-07 resolved).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:263| - A tag outside T is rejected with `TAG_UNKNOWN`. That includes P7 types V1 does not use (`tessera-v1/wrapper`)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:264|   and later versions (`tessera-v2/attest`). A tag in T that is not the expected one is rejected with
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:265|   `TAG_MISMATCH`. *Reason: these are the registered "type-tag mismatch" rejections, and the tag decides the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:266|   construction before any other byte is read.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:267| - The length byte makes T prefix-free as headers. The proof's Lemma 4 depends on that.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:268| - *Why ASCII tags:* a reader with no V1 software can see them in a hex dump. That helps C6.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:269| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:270| ---
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:271| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:272| ## 3. The attestation frame (one per signer)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:273| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:274| ### 3.1 Layout (the four registered fields, A1 P8 / A7 §A7.1)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:275| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:276| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:277| frame(t, p) = header(t) || u16 canonicalization_version || u32 payload_length || payload
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:278|             with canonicalization_version = 0x0001 and payload_length = len(payload) ≤ 2^24
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:279| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:280| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:281| | Offset | Width | Field | Value / rule | Reason |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:282| |---|---|---|---|---|
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:283| | 0 | 1 | tag length | `0x11` for attest | prefix-free tags |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:284| | 1 | 17 | `type_tag` | `tessera-v1/attest` | §2 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:285| | 18 | 2 | `canonicalization_version` | `0x0001` means RFC 8785 + §1's domain + §1.2's number rule. Any other value: `CV_UNKNOWN` | fixed width; G-02 resolved (u16, value 1) |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:286| | 20 | 4 | `payload_length` | the exact payload length, ≤ 2^24, else `LENGTH_CAP` | G-01 changed from u64 to u32. Four bytes cover the cap, and a smaller field is one less thing to get wrong |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:287| | 24 | L | `payload` | `JCS(value)`, §3.2 | A7 §A7.1: the canonical payload bytes |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:288| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:289| The frame ends **exactly** at offset 24 + L.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:290| - If fewer than L payload bytes remain, the result is `TRUNCATED`. Truncation inside the header also gives
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:291|   `TRUNCATED`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:292| - If more remain, the result is `TRAILING`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:293| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:294| The registered rejections "length-prefix mismatch" and "trailing bytes" are therefore one condition, reported by
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:295| its direction. Once the length is the only payload boundary, a short length and a trailing byte are the same
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:296| event.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:297| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:298| ### 3.2 The attestation payload
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:299| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:300| The payload is exactly this object. **No member may be missing or added** (`SCHEMA`). *Reason: a closed schema
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:301| means no unsigned or unknown field can carry meaning, which is R-3.39.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:302| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:303| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:304| {"common":{
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:305|    "alg":                 A,     ^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]{0,63}$          V1 issues the catalog id (see below)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:306|    "binding_forms":       [F…],  nonempty, strictly ascending, each ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,31}$
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:307|    "content":             <any value in V>                          the requester's content
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:308|    "declared_issue_time": "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ"                    a real UTC date and time, seconds 00–59
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:309|    "issuer":              D,     lowercase LDH name, ≥ 2 labels, labels 1–63, total ≤ 241
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:310|    "manifest_sha256":     hex64  hex(SHA256(manifest frame)), §4
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:311|    "preamble_sha256":     hex64  hex(SHA256(purpose-preamble bytes))
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:312|    "profile":             "tessera-v1-strict"                       exact
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:313|    "spec":{"id": S,  ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/-]{0,127}$                  V1: "tessera-v1-strict/verification-spec/1"
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:314|            "sha256": hex64}      hex(SHA256(specification bytes))
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:315|    "vectors_sha256":      hex64  hex(SHA256(conformance-vector bytes))
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:316|  },
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:317|  "signer":{"key_fp": FP}}        FP ∈ §3.3
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:318| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:319| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:320| `hex64` means exactly 64 **lowercase** hex digits. Members appear in JCS order, which is the order shown.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:321| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:322| - **The id V1 issues.** Under the registered hybrid branch (A9.6; HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT §1, registered 2026-10-16), V1
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:323|   issues the pair id `KMS-MLDSA65-PURE-GPG-OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256` (§5.2). The classical id
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:324|   `OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256` stays codec-known (rule O in both slots) and is policy-unsupported in the V1
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:325|   installation: `UNVERIFIABLE / ALG_UNKNOWN` (V1-PROFILE §1, §8). [OWNER 2026-10-19, Levadura C2] *(Was: `V1 issues
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:326|   "OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256"`, the fallback branch's id; the supplement's superseded-statement list omitted it.)*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:327| - **Field grammars** [OWNER 2026-10-19, G18; codifies what both codecs already do, no vector change].
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:328|   `declared_issue_time`: years 0001–9999, proleptic Gregorian, seconds 00–59. `issuer`: labels match
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:329|   `[a-z0-9-]{1,63}` with no leading or trailing hyphen; all-numeric labels, the top label included, are allowed; at
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:330|   least two labels; at most 241 bytes in total.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:331| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:332| | Field | Reason, and the G-id it resolves |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:333| |---|---|
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:334| | `alg`: any well-formed id, not only V1's | P8 accepts a well-formed unknown id, and stage (c) returns `UNVERIFIABLE`. The canary (R-3.53) needs this, and G-10b's failure mode is avoided. The id names the scheme: "a v4 OpenPGP binary-document signature whose document is the frame, ECDSA P-256, SHA-256" (G-57 kept). Its location inside the payload is A3 §A3.6.1's. G-11 is resolved for V1. |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:335| | `binding_forms`: a sorted, unique, nonempty array | R-3.37 says P8 "defines the set's canonical encoding, ordering, uniqueness and bounds". It sits in the attestation's signed bytes (G-17 kept). *Which* forms V1 requires is C4 profile work. The vectors use `["STMT_DIRECT"]` for illustration. |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:336| | `declared_issue_time`: second precision, `Z` | One spelling per instant. No leap second, because Unix time and Bitcoin time have none. G-16 kept. |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:337| | `issuer` = D, at most 241 characters | D is bound in the signed bytes for the owner-name check (C4, G-21). 241 keeps `_tessera-v1.<D>` within DNS's 255-octet name limit (§7). |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:338| | `manifest_sha256` over the manifest **frame** | The hash covers a tagged string, so it is domain-separated by construction. G-14 is resolved: the hash covers the frame of the tuple and nothing more. |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:339| | `spec`, `vectors_sha256`, `preamble_sha256` | R-3.50: the spec id and hash are in the signed bytes. The vectors and preamble are bound the same way. Each hash is over the object's raw bytes, so `sha256sum` reproduces it with no Tessera code. G-18 and G-47 are resolved as far as P8 goes: they are bound. Consuming them is verifier work. |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:340| | `profile` inside `common` | The signed bytes name their own profile (C6). Dispatch reads the bundle's unsigned profile label first (§8). |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:341| | `content` is arbitrary V | Any JSON value in V. A bare digest string is accepted (C-06 and F-03). |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:342| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:343| ### 3.3 Fingerprint slot encodings (G-10 resolved; owner ruling for the DNS record)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:344| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:345| | Slot | `key_fp` string | Definition |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:346| |---|---|---|
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:347| | `kms` | `spki-sha256:` + 64 hex | hex(SHA256(DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo)). For P-256 the SPKI is the 26-byte prefix `3059301306072a8648ce3d020106082a8648ce3d030107034200` followed by `04‖X‖Y` (91 bytes). This is what KMS `GetPublicKey` returns. |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:348| | `gpg` | `gpg-sha256:` + 64 hex | hex(SHA256(body)), where `body` is the v4 public-key packet body (RFC 9580 §5.5.2): `04` ‖ u32 creation ‖ `13` ‖ `08 2a8648ce3d030107` ‖ u16 `0x0203` ‖ `04‖X‖Y`. These are exactly the bytes that the v4 fingerprint hashes *after* its `0x99` ‖ u16 length prefix. That prefix is **not** included, and SHA-1 is not used. This is **not** the fingerprint gpg prints; a tool computes it from the exported key packet. |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:349| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:350| - The scheme prefix makes the two slots' strings differ in their first byte, so they can never be equal. It also
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:351|   makes the frame self-describing.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:352| - The DNS record (§7) carries the bare hex under the slot name. The verifier compares `kms=<h>` with
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:353|   `spki-sha256:<h>` and `gpg=<h>` with `gpg-sha256:<h>`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:354| - *Consequences to record:*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:355|   - V1 uses no SHA-1 for key binding. The gpg slot binds the whole key packet body, creation time included, under
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:356|     SHA-256.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:357|   - The KMS key's OpenPGP key-packet creation time is **not** covered by its `spki-sha256` fingerprint. This is
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:358|     **accepted**: for the KMS slot the verifier binds the SPKI (the key KMS actually holds), not the OpenPGP key
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:359|     packet. The OpenPGP wrapper's creation time therefore carries no meaning for that slot.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:360| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:361| ### 3.4 The two frames, as bytes (A5 §A5.4 and R-3.12 stated over bytes)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:362| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:363| For one receipt with common value `C`:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:364| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:365| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:366| F_kms = 11 'tessera-v1/attest' 0001 u32(L_kms) '{"common":' JCS(C) ',"signer":{"key_fp":' JCS(fp_kms) '}}'
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:367| F_gpg = 11 'tessera-v1/attest' 0001 u32(L_gpg) '{"common":' JCS(C) ',"signer":{"key_fp":' JCS(fp_gpg) '}}'
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:368| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:369| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:370| - `JCS(C)` occupies bytes **[34, 34 + |JCS(C)|)** of both frames and is byte-identical. That covers the requester
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:371|   content and every common binding.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:372| - The frames differ only in bytes 20–23 (the length) and in the `signer` member. In F-01/F-02 they first differ
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:373|   at offset 23, then from offset 745, and the lengths differ by 1 byte (the prefixes `spki-sha256:` and
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:374|   `gpg-sha256:`).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:375| - Payload-byte identity of `common` is therefore **not** frame equality. The two frames are never equal (C1).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:376| - No slot name is written: A5 §A5.4 says only the fingerprint differs. The slot comes from the manifest's order:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:377|   `key_fp` is slot `kms` and `sset[0]` is slot `gpg` (G-09 kept). A frame in the wrong slot gives
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:378|   `RECEIPT_SLOT`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:379| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:380| ### 3.5 What exactly is signed (OpenPGP trailer, PHASE3 finding 4)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:381| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:382| Under `alg = OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256`, each slot's signature is an OpenPGP v4 signature of **type 0x00
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:383| (binary document)** whose document is the frame. Its exact byte serialization is fixed by §5.2, rule O. A raw
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:384| FIPS 204/205 signer signs the frame itself (§5.2, rule R). For OpenPGP, the signed hash input is
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:385| `frame ‖ trailer`, where:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:386| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:387| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:388| trailer = 04 ‖ 00 ‖ pubalg ‖ hashalg ‖ u16 hlen ‖ hashed-subpackets ‖ 04 FF ‖ u32(6 + hlen)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:389| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:390| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:391| - The trailer's last four bytes give `6 + hlen`, the length of its hashed header (`04 ‖ 00 ‖ pubalg ‖ hashalg ‖
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:392|   u16 hlen ‖ hashed-subpackets`); the whole trailer is `12 + hlen` bytes, that value plus six. So `frame ‖ trailer`
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:393|   splits into frame and trailer reading from the end, and the frame's own `payload_length` then delimits the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:394|   payload. PROOF.md Lemma 9 covers this. [OWNER 2026-10-19, P8F-05] *(Was: "The trailer's last four bytes give its
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:395|   own length … PROOF.md Lemma 7 covers this.")*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:396| - **Signature type 0x01 (text) must be rejected:** text mode rewrites line endings, and frame headers and lengths
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:397|   can contain the bytes `0x0a` and `0x0d`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:398| - The unhashed subpacket area carries no meaning. Its exact bytes are nonetheless committed by `A_sig` (§5), as
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:399|   are all of the signature's bytes.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:400| - **Identifier rule (W1, revised 2026-10-12, finding 5).** No V1 semantic, standing or attempt identifier is
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:401|   derived from signature bytes. The anchor digest `SHA256(A_sig)` does commit to them, by design. It is an
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:402|   existence commitment for this receipt's exact bytes, not an identifier of the statement (§8).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:403| - **Malleability now means exact-copy integrity, not forgery.** A signature can be changed and still verify:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:404|   - ECDSA's `(r, n − s)`;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:405|   - an edited unhashed subpacket;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:406|   - another packet serialization;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:407|   - a fresh randomized signature over the same frame.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:408| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:409|   Any such change gives bytes that fail the stamped anchor (`RECEIPT_ANCHOR_MISMATCH`, negative controls XR-10
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:410|   to XR-14). So none of them lets a new signature inherit an old time bound.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:411|   - What remains is copy integrity. A mirror that alters a signature byte damages its copy, just as altering a
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:412|     frame byte would. Preservation must keep the committed bytes exactly.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:413|   - A later re-stamp of an altered copy gets a new anchor in a block mined later. It does not restore the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:414|     original one. Its header time need not be later (A10.1). [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-01] *(Was: "gets a new, later
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:415|     time bound.")*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:416|   - V1 does not require signatures to be unique, and it normalizes no signature (low-s or otherwise). Low-s would
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:417|     not cover OpenPGP serialization or unhashed-area changes, and any normalization after stamping would break the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:418|     anchor. Serialization choices are made before stamping (§5.4).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:419| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:420| ---
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:421| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:422| ## 4. The manifest frame (map-v1 tuple; G-08, G-14, G-22)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:423| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:424| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:425| F_manifest = frame("tessera-v1/manifest", JCS({"alg":A,"issuer":D,"key_fp":fp_kms,"sset":[fp_gpg],"ver":"map-v1"}))
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:426| manifest_sha256 = hex(SHA256(F_manifest))
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:427| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:428| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:429| - The schema is closed: `key_fp` must be a `spki-sha256:` string, and `sset` must hold exactly one `gpg-sha256:`
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:430|   string. `ver` is exactly `map-v1`. Anything else is `SCHEMA`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:431| - *Reason: this is the map-v1 tuple of R-3.36 in the slot order of the C-C2 trace (G-09). Each key's possession
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:432|   proof (R-3.38) is its OpenPGP signature over this same frame. The `tessera-v1/manifest` tag keeps that
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:433|   signature apart from the same key's attestation signature (P7).*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:434| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:435| ## 5. The receipt-anchor preimage `A_sig` (G-19 and G-59 resolved; K-2; revised 2026-10-12)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:436| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:437| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:438| A_sig = header("tessera-v1/receipt-anchor-sig") ‖ u8 0x02
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:439|         ‖ u32 len(F_kms) ‖ F_kms ‖ u32 len(S_kms) ‖ S_kms
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:440|         ‖ u32 len(F_gpg) ‖ F_gpg ‖ u32 len(S_gpg) ‖ S_gpg
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:441| anchor digest = SHA256(A_sig), the value OpenTimestamps stamps
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:442| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:443| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:444| - `S_x` is slot x's detached signature over `F_x`, exactly as §5.2 serializes it.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:445| - Slots appear in **manifest slot order**: `kms` is the manifest's `key_fp`, and `gpg` is `sset[0]`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:446| - The count byte is the number of slots. It must be 2 (`ANCHOR_COUNT`).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:447| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:448| **Decoding, slot by slot.** Each step's boundary is fixed by bytes already read.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:449| 1. `u32` frame length. Above 2^24 + 64 gives `LENGTH_CAP`. Then exactly that many bytes, decoded as one complete
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:450|    attestation frame (§3.1). That decode yields the frame's `common.alg`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:451| 2. `u32` signature length. 0 gives `SIG_EMPTY`. Above the cap of the rule for `(common.alg, slot)` gives
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:452|    `LENGTH_CAP`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:453| 3. Exactly that many bytes, decoded by that rule (§5.2).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:454| 4. After the second signature, any byte gives `TRAILING`. A slot running past the end of input gives
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:455|    `TRUNCATED`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:456| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:457| The rule for a slot is chosen from that slot's own frame and its position, both already read.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:458| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:459| *Reason.* One OTS proof must cover a receipt that has two signed frames (R-3.42 with reading (a)). It must commit
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:460| to the signatures, not only the frames: a stamp over unsigned frames proves only that the frames existed. It
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:461| leaves open signing them later, once signing capability for every required slot has been obtained (CODEX-REVIEW
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:462| finding 1; finding 2 for "every slot"). Length prefixes and whole, exactly consumed parts make the preimage
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:463| injective without any hash assumption (PROOF Lemma 7). The tag keeps it from being taken for a snapshot's proof.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:464| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:465| **Outside the preimage.**
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:466| - The outputs of anchoring: the OTS proof, txid, block headers and confirmation evidence. Including them would
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:467|   be circular (finding 4).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:468| - Transport decoration: armor, containers and the bundle format.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:469| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:470| ### 5.1 Why the tag changes (and the count byte does not)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:471| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:472| The 2026-10-09 frame-only layout used the tag `tessera-v1/receipt-anchor`. That tag is **withdrawn and removed
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:473| from T**. A frame-only preimage is therefore rejected at its header with `TAG_UNKNOWN` (XA-09). A fully signed
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:474| receipt presented with a frame-only anchor is rejected the same way (XR-09).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:475| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:476| There is **no fallback**. No verifier accepts a frame-only anchor under any profile label.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:477| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:478| Reasons:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:479| - **Separation by construction.** With a distinct tag, rejecting the old layout is PROOF Lemma 4: the header
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:480|   alone decides it. It does not depend on whether bytes in the old layout happen to fail a signature rule.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:481|   - Under the old tag, that dependence would be real. Under rule R, any byte string of the right length is a
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:482|     syntactically valid signature.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:483|   - XA-10 shows the same-tag case: the old layout is rejected today only because the gpg frame's first byte
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:484|     fails rule O's packet header.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:485| - **Readable dumps.** A hex dump names which construction it holds (C6).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:486| - **No migration cost.** Nothing was issued under the draft layout, so replacing it costs nothing.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:487| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:488| The count byte keeps its meaning (two slots), so it is not the place to carry the version.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:489| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:490| ### 5.2 Signature-slot rules (by algorithm identifier)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:491| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:492| Each slot's `S` is **exactly one detached signature** in the single serialization its rule pins.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:493| - `S` is **nonempty** and **at most the rule's cap**.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:494| - The decoder **consumes `S` exactly**. Bytes beyond the signature's own extent give `TRAILING`, which covers a
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:495|   second packet. Fewer bytes give `TRUNCATED`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:496| - **Never `S`:** ASCII armor, a display string, a keyring, or any container that can hold more than one
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:497|   signature.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:498| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:499| The rule is chosen by `(common.alg, slot)`:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:500| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:501| | `common.alg` | slot `kms` | slot `gpg` | Cap per `S` |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:502| |---|---|---|---|
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:503| | `OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256` (the classical V1 signers) | rule O | rule O | 1024 bytes |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:504| | `KMS-MLDSA65-PURE-GPG-OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256` (hybrid pair id; registered by the branch-registration supplement of 2026-10-16, A9.6) | rule R: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204), pure, empty context | rule O (OpenPGP P-256; slot-2 custody per A9.6) | `kms`: exactly 3309; `gpg`: 1024 |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:505| | any other well-formed id (§3.2) | opaque | opaque | 1 to 65536 bytes; no inner rule. Stage (c) gives `UNVERIFIABLE` (canary, A-02) |
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:506| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:507| **Rule O (OpenPGP v4 signature, ECDSA P-256, SHA-256; RFC 9580 §4.2, §5.2.3).**
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:508| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:509| *The packet header (`SIG_PACKET`).*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:510| - `S` is exactly one Signature packet (tag 2) with a **legacy-format header in its shortest form**:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:511|   - `0x88 ‖ u8 n` when the body has n ≤ 255 bytes;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:512|   - `0x89 ‖ u16 n` when 256 ≤ n ≤ 1021.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:513| - Each of these gives `SIG_PACKET`:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:514|   - any other first byte: an OpenPGP-format `0xC2` header, another packet tag, or ASCII armor's `-`;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:515|   - a longer length form than needed.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:516| - This also excludes partial and indeterminate lengths.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:517| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:518| *The packet body (`SIG_FORMAT`).* The body is, in order:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:519| 1. version `04`, type `00`, public-key algorithm `13` (19, ECDSA), hash algorithm `08` (SHA-256);
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:520| 2. `u16` hashed length, then the hashed subpackets;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:521| 3. `u16` unhashed length, then the unhashed subpackets;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:522| 4. two bytes: the left 16 bits of the digest;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:523| 5. MPI r;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:524| 6. MPI s.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:525| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:526| Each of the following holds, or the result is `SIG_FORMAT`:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:527| - each subpacket area is an exact sequence of subpackets, each at least 1 byte, with shortest-form lengths. The
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:528|   length forms are RFC 9580 §5.2.3.7's: first octet < 192, one octet; 192–254, two octets
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:529|   `((o1−192)<<8)+o2+192` (192–16319); 255, then a four-octet big-endian value (five octets in all). The length
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:530|   counts the type octet and is ≥ 1. A longer form than needed is `SIG_FORMAT`; this is a V1 rule, not an RFC ban.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:531|   [OWNER 2026-10-19, G28];
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:532| - each MPI is 1 to 256 bits, with an exact bit count;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:533| - the body ends exactly after s.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:534| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:535| Type `0x01` (text) is `SIG_FORMAT` (D-10). The codec does not interpret subpacket contents.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:536| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:537| *Reasons.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:538| - **The legacy header is what the gpg signer emits.** GnuPG 2.4.4 emits exactly this header for a detached
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:539|   P-256 signature: `88 75 04 00 13 08 …`, a 119-byte packet, observed 2026-10-12. Its output is therefore `S`
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:540|   unchanged.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:541|   - The KMS slot's packet is assembled by Tessera's own code, and it must emit the same form.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:542|   - A tool that emits an OpenPGP-format header must have its output re-framed **before stamping**. The header is
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:543|     not covered by the signature hash, so re-framing does not affect validity.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:544|   - A verifier never re-frames.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:545| - **The cap.** 1024 bytes is about 8× a GnuPG signature, and it still bounds the malleable unhashed area.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:546| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:547| **Rule R (raw FIPS 204 / FIPS 205 signature).**
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:548| - `S` is the raw signature byte string that the standard's signing algorithm outputs (the FIPS 204 `sigEncode`
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:549|   output; the FIPS 205 signature). It has no header and no wrapper.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:550| - Its length is **exactly** the parameter set's signature size. Any other nonzero length gives `SIG_FORMAT`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:551| - The signed message is the frame itself (`F_manifest` for a possession proof). No trailer, no transformation.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:552| - **Registered pair (branch-registration supplement of 2026-10-16, A9.6).** `KMS-MLDSA65-PURE-GPG-OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256`:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:553|   slot `kms` is ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) in pure mode with the empty context, so the FIPS 204 message representative is
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:554|   `0x00 ‖ 0x00 ‖ F`; slot `gpg` is rule O. `S_kms` is exactly 3309 bytes. Length 0 gives `SIG_EMPTY`, above 3309
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:555|   `LENGTH_CAP`, any other length `SIG_FORMAT`. The codec reads no byte of `S_kms`: a malformed hint encoding or an
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:556|   out-of-range `z` is a verification failure (`SIG_INVALID`; `POSSESSION_INVALID` for possession), not a codec code.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:557| - The issuer obtains `S_kms` (attestation and possession) from KMS with `MessageType EXTERNAL_MU` only, sending
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:558|   μ = SHAKE256(SHAKE256(pk, 64) ‖ 0x00 ‖ 0x00 ‖ F, 64), pk the raw 1952-byte key (RFC 9881 Appendix D). The result is
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:559|   an ordinary pure signature over `F`. The verifier never sees μ and verifies over `F`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:560| - The kms key under this id is the exact DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo with OID 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.18 and no parameters
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:561|   (22-byte prefix `308207b2300b0609608648016503040312038207a100`, then the 1952-byte key); anything else is
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:562|   `KEY_FORMAT` (RFC 9881 §§2, 4). Its fingerprint is §3.3's `spki-sha256`, unchanged. Key-use assumption (K-R) of
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:563|   the supplement replaces PROOF (K) for this slot; the supplement carries both definitions.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:564| - *Consequence to record:* `common.alg` is one value, equal across slots (§0), naming the pair in slot order.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:565| - Vectors: `vectors/hybrid-golden.json` and `vectors/hybrid-reject.json`; agreement run and differential fuzz as in
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:566|   PROOF §5 (supplement §8).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:567| - **Branch recorded:** hybrid, 2026-10-16 (A9.6).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:568| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:569| ### 5.3 Verification uses the committed bytes, and only those
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:570| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:571| The verifier first obtains the ordered tuple `(F_kms, S_kms, F_gpg, S_gpg)`, by either route below. The two are
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:572| the same by PROOF Lemma 7.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:573| - decode `A_sig`; or
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:574| - encode the presented tuple into `A_sig`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:575| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:576| It checks that `SHA256(A_sig)` is the digest the OTS evidence attests. It then verifies **each committed `S` over
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:577| its committed `F` under its slot's key**, using exactly those bytes.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:578| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:579| The verifier never does any of these:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:580| - verify a separately selected, re-serialized, normalized or reconstructed signature;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:581| - accept a receipt whose presented frames or signatures differ in any byte from the committed tuple
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:582|   (`RECEIPT_ANCHOR_MISMATCH`), even when the presented signature is itself valid (negative controls XR-10 to
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:583|   XR-14);
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:584| - accept a frame-only anchor.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:585| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:586| The vectors exercise the following verification-stage codes. They are reported after every codec code:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:587| - `KEY_MISMATCH`: the presented public key does not hash to its slot's manifest fingerprint;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:588| - `SIG_INVALID`: a committed signature does not verify (XR-16, signatures swapped between slots, anchor rebuilt);
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:589| - `UNVERIFIABLE` (`ALG_UNKNOWN`): the algorithm id is well-formed but is not the installation's catalog-supported
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:590|   id. Being codec-known (a row of §5.2's table) is not being policy-supported: under the hybrid branch the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:591|   classical id is codec-known and still `UNVERIFIABLE` (V1-PROFILE §1, "Codec-known versus policy-supported").
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:592|   [OWNER 2026-10-19, Levadura contested 5] *(Was: "the algorithm id is not registered", which used "registered" in
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:593|   two senses.)*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:594| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:595| These codes belong to the signature verification profile (P3), not to P8.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:596| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:597| ### 5.4 Issue order (finding 6)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:598| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:599| 1. Fix the manifest and the common metadata, including `declared_issue_time`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:600| 2. Build `F_kms` and `F_gpg`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:601| 3. Produce one detached signature per slot over its frame.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:602| 4. Verify both signatures over their frames under the slot keys, using the exact bytes to be committed.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:603| 5. **Freeze** `S_kms` and `S_gpg`. Any serialization step, such as rule O re-framing, happens before this
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:604|    point. Nothing changes a signature byte after it.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:605| 6. Build `A_sig` and stamp `SHA256(A_sig)` with OpenTimestamps: **one** stamp per receipt (R-3.42).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:606| 7. Obtain and validate the confirmation and time evidence.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:607| 8. Ship the complete receipt.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:608| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:609| - A signature never includes its own eventual anchor time or proof.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:610| - A retry that changes any frame or signature byte needs a fresh stamp, and it obeys the existing reissue and
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:611|   temporal rules.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:612| - There is no per-signer stamp, and no frame-only proof is kept alongside.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:613| - R-3.9 is clarified, not weakened. Signatures commit to frames, and the receipt anchor commits to frames plus
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:614|   signatures.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:615| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:616| ## 6. The DNSSEC-snapshot preimage
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:617| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:618| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:619| S = header("tessera-v1/dnssec-snapshot") ‖ u32 len(snapshot) ‖ snapshot        1 ≤ len ≤ 2^24
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:620| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:621| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:622| - The snapshot body's internal format belongs to the profile document (Track 3). P8 fixes only its envelope.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:623| - *Reason:* C4's snapshot rule gives the snapshot its own OTS proof. The tag keeps that proof from being
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:624|   presented as a receipt anchor, or the reverse.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:625| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:626| ---
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:627| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:628| ## 7. DNS key-publication record
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:629| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:630| C4(i) needs a DNSSEC-authenticated record that binds V1's two keys to D. Neither the spec nor wamason.com has one
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:631| yet (spike report; R-4.26 says only "DNSSEC records publishing the fingerprints").
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:632| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:633| **Owner name:** `_tessera-v1.<D>`, where D is `common.issuer`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:634| - The verifier rebuilds this name from the signed `issuer` and compares it, label by label and ignoring ASCII
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:635|   case, with the validated RRset's owner name. Anything else gives `DNS_OWNER`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:636| - *Reason:* the owner name itself is then the C4 owner-name check (G-21/M2). An underscore label cannot collide
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:637|   with a hostname, and the `-v1` suffix lets a later profile publish next to it.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:638| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:639| **Type:** TXT. **RRset:** exactly **one** TXT record at the owner name (`DNS_RRSET` if there are zero or more).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:640| **RDATA:** exactly **one** character-string (`DNS_STRINGS` otherwise). If a string's length byte runs past the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:641| RDATA, the result is `DNS_RDATA`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:642| - *Reason:* one string removes every question about how several strings concatenate. A provider that splits a
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:643|   value is non-conforming for V1.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:644| - Every canonical value is **exactly 255 bytes**, the limit for one string (DNS-02): each field has a fixed length
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:645|   and, since 2026-10-12, every field is mandatory. That leaves no room for another field. A later field needs a new
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:646|   record version.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:647| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:648| **Value grammar** (ABNF; the canonical form is the only accepted form):
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:649| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:650| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:651| value      = "v=tessera1" ";profile=tessera-v1-strict" ";kms=" 64LHEX ";gpg=" 64LHEX
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:652|              ";issuance-not-before=" utc ";issuance-not-after=" utc
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:653| LHEX       = %x30-39 / %x61-66                              ; lowercase hex only
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:654| utc        = 4DIGIT "-" 2DIGIT "-" 2DIGIT "T" 2DIGIT ":" 2DIGIT ":" 2DIGIT "Z"
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:655|              ; RFC 3339 UTC; a real Gregorian date and time, seconds 00-59, no fraction
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:656|              ; years 0001-9999, proleptic Gregorian [OWNER 2026-10-19, G18]
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:657| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:658| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:659| - `kms` is the hex of §3.3's `spki-sha256`. `gpg` is the hex of §3.3's `gpg-sha256`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:660| - `issuance-not-before` and `issuance-not-after` are both **mandatory** (since 2026-10-12; `issuance-not-before` was
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:661|   optional before). `not-after` must be strictly later than `not-before` (`DNS_WINDOW`), and
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:662|   `not-after − not-before` must be at most 90 days, 7 776 000 s (`DNS_WINDOW_LENGTH`; Amendment 9's single V1
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:663|   window). §7.1 gives their meaning.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:664| - `utc` is exactly the grammar of `declared_issue_time` (§3.2), so the window and the declared time compare
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:665|   without conversion. The record's previous grammar was a date only. A one-second boundary cannot be stated with
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:666|   a date, so the window uses the same time grammar as the signed bytes.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:667| - The 2026-10-09 optional `not-before=<date>` is replaced by `issuance-not-before` and is now `DNS_FIELD_UNKNOWN`
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:668|   (XD-29).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:669| - The value has no spaces and no trailing `;`. Field order is fixed. Bytes are printable ASCII from 0x21 to 0x7E.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:670| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:671| Example (DNS-02):
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:672| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:673| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:674| v=tessera1;profile=tessera-v1-strict;kms=5cd252fb…7cd3;gpg=5ecd7121…8fc3;issuance-not-before=2026-10-12T00:00:00Z;issuance-not-after=2027-01-10T00:00:00Z
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:675| ```
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:676| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:677| **Rejection order** (the first that applies):
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:678| 1. `DNS_OWNER`
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:679| 2. `DNS_RRSET`
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:680| 3. `DNS_RDATA`
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:681| 4. `DNS_STRINGS`
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:682| 5. `DNS_SYNTAX`:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:683|    - a byte outside 0x21–0x7E;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:684|    - a field that is not `key=value`, with key `[a-z][a-z-]*` and a nonempty value containing no `=`;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:685|    - an empty field.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:686| 6. `DNS_VERSION`: the first field is not `v=tessera1`, or `v` appears again.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:687| 7. `DNS_FIELD_UNKNOWN`: an extra field.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:688| 8. `DNS_SLOT_DUPLICATE` (`kms` or `gpg` appears twice) or `DNS_FIELD_DUPLICATE` (another field appears twice).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:689| 9. `DNS_SLOT_MISSING`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:690| 10. `DNS_FIELD_MISSING` (`profile`, `issuance-not-before` or `issuance-not-after`).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:691| 11. `DNS_ORDER`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:692| 12. `DNS_PROFILE`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:693| 13. `DNS_VALUE`: the hex or a time fails its grammar.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:694| 14. `DNS_WINDOW`: `issuance-not-after` ≤ `issuance-not-before`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:695| 15. `DNS_WINDOW_LENGTH`: `issuance-not-after − issuance-not-before` > 90 days (7 776 000 s).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:696| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:697| **Why the record is unambiguous** (outside PROOF.md's frame domain):
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:698| - The accepted values form a regular language. Every field begins with a fixed literal key, and every value
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:699|   comes from an alphabet without `;` or `=`, so splitting on `;` and then on the first `=` recovers the fields
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:700|   uniquely.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:701| - The field order is fixed, and every value has exactly one spelling: lowercase hex, and `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:702|   So the map from (kms, gpg, issuance-not-before, issuance-not-after) to value strings is injective, and its
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:703|   inverse is the parse. `:` is outside the separators, and `DNS_WINDOW` and `DNS_WINDOW_LENGTH` are checks on parsed
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:704|   values, so none of them affects the split.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:705| - One RR with one character-string removes concatenation ambiguity. The RDATA length byte delimits the string.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:706| - The owner name is compared as a label sequence, so `_tessera-v1.wamason.com` cannot match
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:707|   `_tessera-v1.wamason.com.evil.example` or `tessera-v1.wamason.com` (XD-12 to XD-14).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:708| - The value begins `v=` (0x76), while every tagged string in §2 begins with a byte from 0x11 to 0x1d. So a TXT
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:709|   value can never be a V1 frame, and a frame can never be a TXT value.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:710| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:711| ### 7.1 Pre-committed issuance window (owner decision 2026-10-12; single 90-day window per Amendment 9)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:712| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:713| The key-publication record carries the issuance window. For V1 there is one window, of at most 90 days
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:714| (`DNS_WINDOW_LENGTH`), with no overlapping successor: before it ends, either a rotation mechanism is registered or
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:715| issuance stops (Amendment 9, A9.6). It is the same canonical value in both channels: the DNS
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:716| TXT record, and the git key-assertion blob (§7.2). The same window value is authenticated by the anchored git
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:717| assertion and by DNSSEC at the snapshot's own anchored time. Its pre-commitment is **chain order**: the git
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:718| assertion's selected anchor height plus 5 is lower than the receipt's selected anchor height, so the window was
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:719| confirmed at k = 6 in the chain before the receipt was anchored (A9 C4; V1-PROFILE §6.3, `GIT_NOT_PRECOMMITTED`).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:720| That is chain order, not UTC (A2.1), and DNSSEC evidence establishes no publication before issue (A9 C4). [OWNER
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:721| 2026-10-19, G02 CORRECT; Levadura C1] *(Was: "The window is therefore fixed in DNSSEC-authenticated and anchored
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:722| authority evidence before any receipt that relies on it", which overstated both channels.)*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:723| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:724| **Verifier rule (C4).** A receipt passes C4 only if both of these hold:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:725| - `issuance-not-before` ≤ `declared_issue_time`;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:726| - **T ≤ `issuance-not-after`**, where T is the header time of the qualifying attestation at the **lowest block
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:727|   height** in the presented OTS proof (A9 C5; A10.5's stages; V1-PROFILE §7.1). Header times are not monotone, so
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:728|   selection is by height, never by least header time. [OWNER 2026-10-19, r2-contra; Levadura contested 1] *(Was:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:729|   "the time of the earliest verified attestation", A9's pre-2026-10-14 wording.)*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:730| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:731| Otherwise the verdict is `INVALID`, with reason `ISSUANCE_WINDOW`. Both bounds are inclusive: W-01 is
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:732| T = not-after, W-02 is declared time = not-before. XW-01 is T = not-after + 1 s, and XW-02 is a declared time
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:733| 1 s early.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:734| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:735| *Rationale, recorded.*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:736| - **A surviving or stolen key cannot mint a receipt that passes with T after the window.** Keys may outlive the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:737|   service's exit, or be stolen. Even signing capability for every required slot cannot produce a receipt that
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:738|   passes with verified T after `issuance-not-after`, under continuing anchor, history and authority assumptions. A fresh mint's `A_sig` (§5) can only
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:739|   be stamped at or after the moment it exists, and the anchor prevents claiming an earlier block; a later block's
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:740|   header time can still be earlier, which is why the claim is only about verified T [OWNER 2026-10-19, PR-01]
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:741|   *(was: "the anchor prevents claiming an earlier T")*. So every receipt
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:742|   whose verified T is after the window fails (XW-03). This is a statement in chain time, not in UTC (see the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:743|   residual below).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:744|   - A compromise *before* `not-after` is not covered. Within the window, a thief mints receipts that pass, subject
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:745|     to the historical-security caveats of CODEX-REVIEW findings 7 and 8.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:746| - **Key-format expiries are not relied on.**
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:747|   - OpenPGP key-expiration subpackets live in a self-signature. Any keyholder, a thief included, can re-issue that
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:748|     self-signature to extend them.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:749|   - A raw SPKI key, such as a KMS ML-DSA key, carries no expiry at all.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:750|   - The window is instead fixed in authority evidence that the keyholder alone cannot rewrite after the fact.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:751|     Rewriting it means re-publishing the record, which is a new authority event with its own evidence times.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:752| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:753| *Residual: chain time (A2.1).*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:754| - T is the **header-time-derived T as registered**. The verifier compares it with `issuance-not-after` directly,
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:755|   with no margin added or subtracted. That keeps one registered meaning of T.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:756| - A Bitcoin header's timestamp is not an exact UTC clock. Consensus constrains it only loosely: it must exceed the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:757|   median of the previous eleven blocks, and nodes accept it up to about two hours ahead of their own clock.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:758| - In the direction that matters here, a stamp actually made **after** `not-after` can carry a header time at or
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:759|   before `not-after`. Its receipt passes. A2.1 registers no finite bound on that backward skew, and neither ε nor S
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:760|   is one. So what this rule guarantees is "no receipt passes with verified T after `not-after`". Translating that
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:761|   into a finite UTC cutoff needs an additional, explicit backward-skew assumption that V1 does not establish
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:762|   (Codex review of Amendment 9, finding 2; an earlier draft of this paragraph claimed such a bound).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:763| - The opposite error, an honest stamp made just before `not-after` getting a later header time and failing, is
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:764|   the safe direction.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:765| - *Issuer invariant:* an attempt whose T would exceed `not-after` is not shipped. The stop margin that implements
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:766|   it is an operating number, not part of this encoding (`docs/V1-OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md`). The verdict reports the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:767|   comparison with T as registered.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:768| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:769| ### 7.2 Git channel: what its OTS stamp must cover (finding 9; added 2026-10-12)
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:770| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:771| - **The blob's content.** Since the issuance-window decision (§7.1), the git key-assertion blob carries the same
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:772|   canonical value as the TXT record, so both channels assert one byte string, window included.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:773| - **What P8 does not fix.** The blob's path, and any byte framing around the value: for example, whether a
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:774|   trailing LF is allowed. Those are not P8's.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:775| - **What P8 fixes here.** The blob's anchor target.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:776| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:777| - **The stamp targets the signed commit's object id.** That commit's tree contains the assertion blob at the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:778|   profile path (V1-PROFILE §6.3, `tessera-v1/key-assertion`), and it carries a `gpgsig` header that verifies under
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:779|   the repository key. Whether this commit introduced the blob is not checked (V1-PROFILE §15.4). [OWNER 2026-10-19,
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:780|   r2-contra; Levadura C4] *(Was: "That commit adds the assertion blob".)*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:781| - These stamp targets are **not acceptable**:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:782|   - the tree;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:783|   - the blob;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:784|   - an unsigned commit, including the unsigned payload that the commit signature covers.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:785| - *Why, from git's documented object format:*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:786|   - gitformat-signature(5) (git 2.43.0, "COMMIT SIGNATURES") gives a commit signature's payload as the commit
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:787|     object, embedded as the header entry `gpgsig`.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:788|   - gitglossary(7) says an object "is uniquely identified by the SHA-1 of its contents".
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:789|   - So a signed commit's id is computed over the object **including** its `gpgsig` header. The signature lies
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:790|     inside the anchored bytes.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:791|   - A stamp over the tree or blob covers no signature. A stamp over the unsigned commit is the receipt's own
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:792|     pre-stage-then-sign gap again.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:793| - *Checked 2026-10-12* (git 2.43.0, GnuPG 2.4.4, scratch repository):
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:794|   - the signed commit's id equals `SHA-1("commit " ‖ decimal size ‖ 0x00 ‖ raw object)`;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:795|   - the raw object contains the `gpgsig` header;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:796|   - `git hash-object -t commit` reproduces the id;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:797|   - the unsigned commit with the same tree had a different id, while its tree id was identical.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:798| - **Matching the repository's convention.** This repository stamps a file `timestamps/<id>` holding the commit's
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:799|   lowercase hex id and LF, after the commit exists. For a signed commit, that is this target.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:800| - **What the verifier does.** It:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:801|   1. recomputes the id from the presented raw commit object;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:802|   2. verifies `gpgsig` over the object without that header;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:803|   3. follows the commit to its tree and then to the blob;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:804|   4. checks that the stamped bytes name that id.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:805| - The git signature is ASCII-armored inside the commit header. §5.2's binary rule applies to receipt slots only.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:806| - **Residual, already recorded.** Two parts are SHA-1:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:807|   - the commit id itself;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:808|   - the commit → tree → blob linkage.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:809| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:810|   Both are in the dependency manifest (V1-DERIVATION's bundle contents and custody residual) and outside P8's
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:811|   SHA-256 scope (PROOF (H)). Anchoring a signed commit puts its signature inside the anchored bytes. It does not
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:812|   turn the SHA-1 links into SHA-256 bindings.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:813| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:814| ---

formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:829| **Identifier rule (finding 5).**
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:830| - No identifier in this table, and no semantic, standing or attempt identifier anywhere in V1, is derived from
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:831|   signature bytes.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:832| - The receipt-anchor digest `SHA256(A_sig)` commits to the signature bytes, by design. It is an existence
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:833|   commitment, not an identifier (§3.5).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:834| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:835| **Dispatch boundary (O-78, an owner decision):**
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:836| - The verifier dispatches on the bundle's **unsigned** profile label. An unrecognized label gives
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:837|   `UNVERIFIABLE / OUT_OF_PROFILE`, and nothing in this document is evaluated.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:838| - Once a bundle is dispatched to `tessera-v1-strict`, every rejection here is `INVALID`. That includes a signed
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:839|   `profile` other than `tessera-v1-strict`, an unknown tag and an unknown canonicalization version, because the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:840|   bundle claimed V1 and its signed bytes contradict that claim.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:841| - The single **codec-level** in-profile `UNVERIFIABLE` that concerns these bytes is a well-formed unknown `alg`
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:842|   (stage (c)), and P8 lets that through. The profile adds further in-profile `UNVERIFIABLE` outcomes on these bytes
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:843|   (for example `BINDING_FORM_UNSUPPORTED` and `SPEC_UNKNOWN`; V1-PROFILE §3.1 item 5). [OWNER 2026-10-19, G01;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:844|   Levadura C5] *(Was: "The single in-profile `UNVERIFIABLE` …".)*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:845| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:846| ## 9. Owner decisions taken here, for the author's record
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:847| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:848| D-1 **Number rule: value-preserving (§1.2).** This changes A1 P8's item "numbers not exactly representable as
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:849| IEEE 754 doubles" and prereg §4.3's "must be exactly representable". **A9.8 registers it** (A9.7 rows 22–23), as
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:850| Codex review 14 asked. The registered wording also fails to compose with RFC 8785 (§1.2). [OWNER 2026-10-19, G38]
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:851| *(Was: "It needs an A9 sentence. … The derivation's profile line, which says the rule is unchanged, must be revised
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:852| to match." Both are done.)*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:853| D-2 Unicode 16.0.0 is pinned. Unassigned code points are rejected, and text that is not NFC is rejected rather than
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:854| normalized.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:855| D-3 Limits: a payload of at most 2^24 bytes; depth 64 for the payload and 62 for content.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:856| D-4 Widths: a u8 tag length, a u16 canonicalization version equal to 1, and a u32 length (G-01 changed from u64).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:857| D-5 One tag for both signers' frames (A5 §A5.4). Slots are told apart by the fingerprint and the manifest order,
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:858| and no slot name is written.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:859| D-6 Fingerprint strings carry scheme prefixes: `spki-sha256` for kms and `gpg-sha256` for gpg.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:860| **Owner decision (2026-10-09): no SHA-1 in V1.** The gpg key is bound by SHA-256 over its OpenPGP v4 public-key
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:861| packet body, not by the v4 SHA-1 fingerprint, and this applies to the frame, the manifest and the DNS record. The
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:862| KMS key stays SHA-256 of its SPKI. Its OpenPGP creation time is unbound, and that is accepted because the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:863| verifier binds the SPKI for that slot (§3.3).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:864| D-7 `manifest_sha256` is computed over the manifest frame. Spec, vectors and preamble are bound by SHA-256 of their
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:865| raw bytes.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:866| D-8 *(revised 2026-10-12, findings 4 and 10)* The anchor preimage `A_sig` holds each slot's full frame and its
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:867| exact detached signature, in manifest slot order, with a count byte, under the new tag
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:868| `tessera-v1/receipt-anchor-sig`. The 2026-10-09 frame-only layout and its tag are withdrawn, with no fallback
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:869| (§5.1). The DNSSEC snapshot has its own tagged envelope.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:870| D-9 A closed schema. `declared_issue_time` has second precision with no leap second. D is at most 241 characters.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:871| `binding_forms` is a sorted array.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:872| D-10 OpenPGP signature type 0x00 only. Since 2026-10-12, the anchor codec enforces this (§5.2, rule O).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:873| D-11 The dispatch boundary in §8.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:874| D-12 The DNS record: one RR, one string, a fixed order, no spaces, and the owner name compared without regard to
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:875| case. Since 2026-10-12 every field is mandatory, so every canonical value is 255 bytes.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:876| D-13 Reason codes, and the order in which they are reported (§1.4, §3.1, §5, §7). "Trailing bytes" and
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:877| "length-prefix mismatch" are reported as `TRAILING` or `TRUNCATED`, and this now includes a signature's own
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:878| extent against its slot length. New in 2026-10-12:
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:879| - `SIG_EMPTY`, `SIG_PACKET` and `SIG_FORMAT` (§5.2);
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:880| - `LENGTH_CAP` for a signature above its cap;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:881| - the verification-stage codes of §5.3;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:882| - `DNS_WINDOW` (§7) and the C4 code `ISSUANCE_WINDOW` (§7.1);
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:883| - `DNS_WINDOW_LENGTH` (§7; Amendment 9 disposition, 2026-10-12).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:884| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:885| D-14 *(2026-10-12)* Signature-slot rules are chosen by `(common.alg, slot)`. Rule O is one legacy-header binary v4
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:886| packet of at most 1024 bytes. Rule R is raw FIPS 204/205 bytes of the exact parameter-set length. An unregistered
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:887| id gets opaque bytes, 1 to 65536 of them.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:888| D-15 *(2026-10-12, finding 6)* The issue order is: frames, sign, verify, freeze the signature bytes, then stamp
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:889| `A_sig` (§5.4).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:890| D-16 *(2026-10-12, finding 9)* The git channel's OTS stamp targets the signed commit's object id, never a tree, a
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:891| blob or an unsigned commit (§7.2).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:892| D-17 *(2026-10-12, follow-up owner decision)* The issuance window lives in the key-publication record, in both
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:893| channels. A receipt is `INVALID / ISSUANCE_WINDOW` unless not-before ≤ declared time and T ≤ not-after. T is the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:894| registered header-time-derived T, with no margin. Key-format expiries are not relied on (§7.1). *Revised
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:895| 2026-10-12 (Amendment 9 disposition):* both bounds are mandatory and the window is at most 90 days
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:896| (`DNS_WINDOW_LENGTH`).
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:897| 
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:898| **Out of P8's scope, and named so that nothing is dropped quietly:**
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:899| - the bundle's container format and transport encoding (G-26);
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:900| - where the observed anchor delay is recorded (G-40);
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:901| - the snapshot body's format;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:902| - the git blob path;
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:903| - the signature verification profile (P3 [assumption]). P8 now fixes each signature's *serialization* and its
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:904|   place in `A_sig` (§5.2). Whether a signature verifies, and what that proves, remains P3's question.
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:905| - the PQ algorithm id(s), the parameter set and the signing mode. They are registered only if the 21 Oct spike
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:906|   passes (§5.2, rule R); *[OWNER 2026-10-19 annotation: superseded for the hybrid branch by HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT §1–§2,
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:907|   registered 2026-10-16 (pair id, ML-DSA-65, pure, empty context). The bullet is kept as baseline text, as the
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:908|   supplement directs.]*
formal/p8/ENCODING-V1.md:909| - which binding forms V1 requires.
