formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:44| ## 1. The pair algorithm identifier, its mode and its context — OWNER-PROPOSED
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:45| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:46| ```
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:47| KMS-MLDSA65-PURE-GPG-OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:48| ```
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:49| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:50| - **Grammar.** It matches E§3.2's `^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]{0,63}$`: 47 characters, ASCII capitals, digits and `-`.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:51| - **Reading, in slot order.** Slot `kms`: ML-DSA-65, pure. Slot `gpg`: the classical id's scheme, spelled exactly as
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:52|   the classical id (`OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256`), so rule O keeps one name in both branches. *Reason:* `common.alg`
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:53|   is one value shared by both frames (R-3.12, §5). It must therefore name the **pair**, in manifest slot order. A
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:54|   reader with no V1 software can read both schemes off a hex dump (C6).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:55| - **Mode: pure ML-DSA.** FIPS 204 ML-DSA.Sign / ML-DSA.Verify (Algorithms 2 and 3), not HashML-DSA. Parameter set
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:56|   ML-DSA-65.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:57| - **Context: the empty octet string.** So the FIPS 204 message representative is
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:58|   `M' = 0x00 ‖ 0x00 ‖ F` (domain byte 0 for pure mode, context length 0, no context bytes). `F` is the frame (§2).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:59|   `PURE` in the id names the mode. The empty context is fixed by this registration, not spelled in the id; a
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:60|   non-empty context is a different scheme and needs a different id.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:61| - **External μ is a signer-side computation only, and it is the issuer's only path** (owner decision 6). AWS KMS refuses
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:62|   `MessageType RAW` over 4096 bytes (observed 2026-10-13: "Member must have length less than or equal to 4096").
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:63|   For one code path whatever the size, the issuer always computes
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:64|   `μ = SHAKE256(SHAKE256(pk, 64) ‖ 0x00 ‖ 0x00 ‖ F, 64)` from the slot's own public key and the frame, and sends `μ`
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:65|   with `MessageType EXTERNAL_MU`, signing algorithm `ML_DSA_SHAKE_256`, for **attestations and possession proofs
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:66|   alike**. `pk` here is the raw 1952-byte key, not the SPKI. The output is an ordinary pure ML-DSA-65 signature over
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:67|   `F` (FIPS 204 Algorithms 2, 3, 7, 8; RFC 9881 Appendix D on external μ).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:68|   - The verifier never sees `μ`, never receives a `MessageType`, and verifies over `F`. A signature checked over `μ`
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:69|     as if `μ` were the message fails (XM-05).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:70|   - Evidence for the selected path:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:71|     - SIG-G3 / R-G2 is the real KMS EXTERNAL_MU signature over a **genuine** 6753-byte V1 attest frame;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:72|     - SIG-H3 is made from `μ` by implementation A and is byte-identical to A's deterministic signature over the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:73|       frame itself;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:74|     - B recomputes `μ` for both.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:75|   - **RAW captures are comparative only:** SIG-G1 / R-G1 and P-G1 (genuine frames) and SIG-H5 (spike frame). They
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:76|     show that a verifier cannot tell the two KMS message types apart. They do not test the selected issuer path.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:77| - **Signing randomness.** Hedged and deterministic FIPS 204 signing both give valid signatures. Nothing in V1
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:78|   depends on which KMS uses: the anchor commits the exact bytes (E§5.3), and a second valid signature over the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:79|   same frame fails the anchor (negative control XHR-01).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:80| - **Catalog.** Under the hybrid branch the V1 catalog's single `alg` is this id (V1-PROFILE §1). The classical id
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:81|   stays codec-known (rule O for both slots) and becomes policy-unsupported: `UNVERIFIABLE / ALG_UNKNOWN`.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:82| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:83| ## 2. Rule R for the pair: raw ML-DSA-65 signature bytes — OWNER-PROPOSED
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:84| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:85| - `S_kms` is the FIPS 204 `sigEncode` output and nothing else: no header, length prefix, wrapper, DER, armor or
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:86|   base64.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:87| - **Length: exactly 3309 bytes.** That is `c̃` (λ/4 = 48 bytes) ‖ `z` (5 polynomials × 256 coefficients × 20 bits =
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:88|   3200 bytes) ‖ `h` (ω + k = 55 + 6 = 61 bytes). The cap for `(pair id, kms)` is also 3309.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:89| - **Codes, in E§5's order:** length 0 → `SIG_EMPTY`; length above 3309 → `LENGTH_CAP`; any other length below 3309 →
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:90|   `SIG_FORMAT`. Rule R reads no byte of `S`, so within an anchor the slot's `u32` length is the signature's only
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:91|   boundary: a trailing byte (3310) is `LENGTH_CAP` and a truncation (3308) is `SIG_FORMAT`, never `TRAILING` or
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:92|   `TRUNCATED` (XH-01 to XH-04).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:93| - **Internal malformation is a verification failure, not a codec failure (OWNER-PROPOSED).** Out-of-order or
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:94|   over-full hint indices, nonzero hint padding, and a `z` coefficient beyond the bound all make FIPS 204
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:95|   verification return false: `SIG_INVALID` for a receipt slot, `POSSESSION_INVALID` for a possession proof
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:96|   (XHR-04, XHR-05, XHR-12, XHR-16 to XHR-19; gate-off demonstrations in §8). *Reason:* this keeps PROOF Lemma 7a's accepted set for rule R exactly "the strings of
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:97|   the exact length", as the baseline proof already states it. Both codecs stay byte-blind for rule R, and the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:98|   boundary argument needs no FIPS 204 parser.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:99| - **The signed message is the frame `F` itself**, for the attestation slot, and `F_manifest` for the kms possession
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:100|   proof (R-3.38; V1-PROFILE §8: "Possession proofs use the same per-slot rule over `F_manifest` (rule R for kms
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:101|   under the hybrid)"). There is no trailer, so PROOF Lemma 9 has no rule-R counterpart to prove: the message *is*
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:102|   `F`.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:103| - **Rule O in the `gpg` slot is unchanged** (E§5.2, cap 1024, V1-PROFILE §8's rule-O signature policy).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:104| - **Malleability (E§3.5).** Under hedged signing one frame has many valid ML-DSA signatures. Exact-copy integrity is
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:105|   what the anchor gives, as for rule O; V1 normalizes nothing.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:106| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:107| ## 3. Slot `kms` key encoding and fingerprint under the pair id — OWNER-PROPOSED
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:108| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:109| **Key encoding: the exact DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo**, as AWS KMS `GetPublicKey` returns it, with the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:110| AlgorithmIdentifier `id-ml-dsa-65` (OID **2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.18**, NIST CSOR) and **parameters absent**. Source:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:111| **RFC 9881 §2** (the OID, parameters absent) and **§4** (the SubjectPublicKeyInfo and its public-key encoding).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:112| 1974 bytes: 22 fixed bytes, then the 1952-byte FIPS 204
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:113| public key `ρ (32) ‖ t1 (6 × 320)`:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:114| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:115| ```
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:116| 30 82 07 b2                          SEQUENCE, length 1970
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:117|    30 0b                             SEQUENCE (AlgorithmIdentifier), length 11
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:118|       06 09 60 86 48 01 65 03 04 03 12   OID 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.18 (id-ml-dsa-65); no parameters
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:119|    03 82 07 a1                       BIT STRING, length 1953
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:120|       00                             zero unused bits
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:121|       <1952 bytes>                   FIPS 204 pkEncode(ρ, t1)
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:122| prefix (hex): 308207b2300b0609608648016503040312038207a100
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:123| ```
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:124| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:125| - Checked against the real key: the KMS spike key's `GetPublicKey` bytes have exactly this prefix and length, and
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:126|   `cryptography` 50.0.2 re-exports the parsed key to the same 1974 bytes (K-H2).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:127| - **Fingerprint: unchanged scheme.** `key_fp = "spki-sha256:" + hex(SHA256(SPKI DER))`, as E§3.3 already defines for
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:128|   the kms slot. The manifest schema, the frame schema and the DNS record (`kms=<hex>`) are unchanged. The OID sits
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:129|   inside the hashed bytes, so a P-256 and an ML-DSA-65 key cannot share a fingerprint under (H).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:130|   - Real spike key: `spki-sha256:d1b35a0e5273912ee85c7f88ee97929cef311e7854ad30c58faa3e0250c4a7a4` (K-H2).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:131|   - Illustrative test key (public seed): `spki-sha256:576e49c28c431d6cf6679ff5a04a0a023ca7dd8d0da2a75881ff0b3dee6c5cb4`
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:132|     (K-H1).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:133| - **`KEY_FORMAT`.** Under the pair id, `keys.kms` that is not exactly this encoding is `INVALID / KEY_FORMAT`, before
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:134|   `KEY_MISMATCH` (V1-PROFILE §8, row 5.1 then 5.2). The rule is selected by the installed spec and the slot, never by
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:135|   the key bytes. That includes a P-256 SPKI, ML-DSA-44 or ML-DSA-87 SPKIs, the right OID with the wrong length,
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:136|   NULL parameters, a nonzero unused-bits octet, non-minimal or indefinite DER lengths, a truncation, a trailing byte,
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:137|   the bare 1952-byte key and PEM text (XK-01 to XK-12).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:138|   - A generic key loader is not a substitute: `cryptography` accepts the P-256, ML-DSA-44 and ML-DSA-87 SPKIs of
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:139|     XK-01 to XK-03 as valid keys of their own algorithms.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:140| - **No further public-key validation exists for ML-DSA.** Every 1952-byte string is a well-formed FIPS 204 public key:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:141|   ρ is arbitrary, and every 10-bit `t1` field is in range. So, unlike P-256's on-curve check, `KEY_FORMAT` for this
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:142|   slot is purely the encoding check.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:143| - **Under the fallback** nothing changes: an ML-DSA-65 SPKI in `keys.kms` is `KEY_FORMAT` (V1-PROFILE §8, EA-24).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:144| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:145| ## 4. Key-use assumptions for the raw slot (what replaces PROOF (K) for `kms`) — OWNER-PROPOSED
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:146| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:147| PROOF (K) reads: *"Each V1 slot key signs only V1 tagged strings, as OpenPGP type-0x00 documents."* Under the hybrid
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:148| that sentence still describes the `gpg` slot and does not describe the `kms` slot. Under the pair id, (K) is
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:149| replaced by two assumptions:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:150| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:151| - **(K-R), slot `kms`.** The ML-DSA-65 key signs only messages `F ∈ Frm(attest) ∪ Frm(manifest)` (V1 tagged strings),
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:152|   in pure mode with the empty context. Every issuer KMS `Sign` call on the key is `MessageType EXTERNAL_MU`, with
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:153|   `μ` computed by the issuer from such an `F` and this key's raw public key (§1; owner decision 6).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:154|   - The spike's `MessageType RAW` calls (message exactly `F`) are comparative captures, not the issuer path.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:155|   - They satisfy the same assumption, because the message is a V1 tagged string.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:156| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:157|   The key is used with no other context, never in HashML-DSA mode, and by no other protocol or service.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:158| - **(K-O), slot `gpg`.** Unchanged: V1 tagged strings, as OpenPGP type-0x00 documents, through the policy signer
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:159|   (A9.6, slot-2 custody).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:160| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:161| *Why the type-0x00 clause has no rule-R counterpart.* In rule O the signed hash input is `F ‖ trailer`, and type 0x00
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:162| is what excludes text mode's line-ending rewrite (E§3.5). Rule R signs `F` itself, with no transformation, so there
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:163| is nothing to exclude. Domain separation comes from the bytes:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:164| - every V1 tagged string begins with a tag-length byte in 0x11–0x1d (Lemma 4, Remark 10);
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:165| - pure mode's `M'` begins `0x00`, where HashML-DSA's begins `0x01` (FIPS 204's own separation, should the key ever
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:166|   be misused in that mode).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:167| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:168| PROOF uses (K) only in Remark 10, and Remark 10's argument holds unchanged with message = `F`.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:169| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:170| *What enforces (K-R), stated so it is not overread.*
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:171| - The HSM cannot check that a message is a V1 frame. Under EXTERNAL_MU it does not even see the message: whoever
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:172|   may call `kms:Sign` on the key can sign any message by computing `μ`.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:173| - So (K-R) is an issuer-code and IAM assumption: the key policy grants `kms:Sign` only to the issuer role, and the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:174|   issuer code builds only V1 frames. It is not an HSM property. The operations runbook carries the key policy.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:175| - This is the same single-controller position C3 already states. Capture of the issuing account confers signing
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:176|   capability for both slots.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:177| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:178| ## 5. R-3.12 for the mixed pair
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:179| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:180| R-3.12: *"the six non-fingerprint fields of every required signer's frame — object type, algorithm, identity,
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:181| manifest hash, canonicalization version, payload — are equal across signer slots; only the key-fingerprint field
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:182| differs."* What it requires of the mixed pair, and why it holds:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:183| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:184| 1. **One algorithm value in both frames.** `common.alg` is the pair id in both frames, and the manifest's `alg` is the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:185|    same id (E§4; `RECEIPT_MANIFEST_MISMATCH` otherwise). The slots' *schemes* differ, but the *field* is equal: the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:186|    verifier takes each slot's scheme from `(common.alg, slot)` (E§5.2), never from the frame, the key or the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:187|    signature bytes.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:188| 2. **Byte equality of `common` is unaffected.** PROOF Lemma 6(a) is unchanged: `JCS(C)` occupies bytes
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:189|    `[34, 34 + |JCS(C)|)` of both frames (F-H1/F-H2, F-H3/F-H4). Lemma 6(b) and (c) are unchanged too: the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:190|    fingerprint prefixes `spki-sha256:` and `gpg-sha256:` still differ in their first byte.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:191| 3. **Rule choice stays left-to-right.** Lemma 7 chooses each slot's rule from that slot's own frame and position,
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:192|    both already read. Lemma 7a already covers rule R ("the strings of the parameter set's exact length"); this
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:193|    supplement fixes that length at 3309.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:194| 4. **The failing shape is rejected.** M9 is the shape where each slot carries its own scheme's id (V1-DERIVATION:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:195|    "KMS ECDSA + gpg OpenPGP is `INVALID` under R-3.12"). Here the kms frame carries the pair id and the gpg frame the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:196|    classical id. That is `RECEIPT_COMMON_MISMATCH` (XHR-08), and it is why A9.6 requires one pair id.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:197| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:198| **Status: holds, by construction and by vector.** No model run is needed for R-3.12 itself. It is a byte condition
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:199| that the receipt check enforces, and both codecs agree on it.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:200| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:201| ## 6. P3's model: what "passes P3's model" requires, and the run
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:202| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:203| **What P3 is.** Key binding (anti-DSKS), `formal/PROPERTIES.md` row P3: `[model]+[assum]`, tool ProVerif, status
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:204| `checked`, artifact `formal/suite/s-p3/`. Its two-signer model is S-P3.Q5 (`sp3_q5_multikey_correct.pv`). Its
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:205| adversary holds the registered DSKS capability (theory library D-4). The case is degraded mode with the sole
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:206| authority channel compromised: the P3 hard case.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:207| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:208| **Why the existing models do not cover the pair.** Every S-P3 model signs every slot with the library's single
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:209| family `sign/checksign`, which carries one DSKS capability. The mixed pair has two schemes, chosen per slot by one
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:210| id. That is a different signature algebra, so "passes P3's model" needs a model run. Reading the old green results
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:211| across would not do.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:212| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:213| **The model change** (`formal/suite/s-p3/proverif/hybrid/`, derived from Q5 recut 3 and nothing else changed):
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:214| - slot A (= kms) signs possession and attestation with a second, model-local family `signR/checksignR`;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:215| - that family has **its own DSKS capability** `dsksR`, of the library's shape. This is conservative: ML-DSA is not
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:216|   assumed to resist key substitution;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:217| - slot B (= gpg) keeps the library family;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:218| - both frames and the tuple carry one value `algPair`;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:219| - the verifier accepts only `algPair`, and checks slot A with `checksignR` and slot B with `checksign`, for both the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:220|   possession proof and the attestation.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:221| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:222| Predictions were written into each model header before the first run of any of them.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:223|

formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:292| ## 8. Evidence: vectors, agreement run, fuzz, real signatures
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:293| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:294| **What kind of evidence this is (HS-04).** Implementations A (`gen.py`) and B (`check.py`) are **candidate-codec and
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:295| cryptographic-profile evidence**.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:296| - Both hard-code the classical id and the pair id in one codec registry.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:297| - Both treat registry membership as the condition for verifying signatures.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:298| - Neither has an input for the selected catalog id or for registration state.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:299| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:300| So they establish:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:301| - the rule R and rule O codecs;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:302| - the ML-DSA-65 and P-256 verification;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:303| - the key encodings;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:304| - R-3.12's byte checks.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:305| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:306| They do **not** establish the catalog and registration routing (V1-PROFILE §1 r2-F01, EA-09; §6.4 M5). Those claims
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:307| rest on the five profile-conformance cases (a)–(e) in `formal/p8/HYBRID-CONFORMANCE-CASES.md`, which are for
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:308| `prototype/conformance` and have not been run.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:309| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:310| **Files** (`formal/p8/vectors/`).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:311| - `gen.py` writes the hybrid vectors to `hybrid-golden.json` and `hybrid-reject.json`.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:312| - `golden.json` and `reject.json` regenerate **byte-identical** to the 2026-10-12 baseline (checked with `cmp`
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:313|   against copies taken before any edit).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:314| - `check.py` reports the two sets on separate lines.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:315| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:316| **Two ML-DSA-65 implementations, no shared local code.**
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:317| - **A** (in `gen.py`): KeyGen; Sign from the message or from μ; Verify from the message or from μ. It uses the
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:318|   butterfly NTT and big-integer bit packing. Checked by hand against dilithium-py 1.4.0 and cryptography 50.0.2:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:319|   from one seed, the identical public key and the identical deterministic signature.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:320| - **B** (in `check.py`): Verify only. It evaluates and interpolates at the roots ζ^(2·brv8(i)+1) directly, with no
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:321|   butterfly and no zeta table, and reads bit fields with a cursor. It parses the SPKI DER field by field, where A
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:322|   compares a prefix.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:323| - What they share: hashlib's SHA-256, SHAKE-128 and SHAKE-256 (plus the baseline's Unicode tables and float), and one
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:324|   author instance. "No shared code" means no shared local implementation, not independent authors or independent
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:325|   cryptographic backends (PROOF §6's limit).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:326| - **Demonstration switches (vectors only).** Both verifiers can switch off exactly one decoding gate at a time:
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:327|   `norm`, `order` or `padding`. This lets a vector show that it fails on that gate alone. The cumulative-count gates
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:328|   cannot be switched off, because without them the hint field is undecodable.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:329| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:330| **Golden vectors (35).**
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:331| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:332| *Illustrative test key (public seed):*
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:333| - fingerprint K-H1;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:334| - manifest M-H1;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:335| - frames F-H1 to F-H4 (F-H3/F-H4 are 5246 bytes);
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:336| - SIG-H1 (pure, deterministic) and SIG-H3 (made from external μ);

formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:372| **Results** (2026-10-14, after the HS revisions; Python 3.14.6):
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:373| - **A** self-checks every vector, its expected code, and each demonstration: the gate-off acceptance, and the

formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:378| - **Differential fuzz** (`fuzz.py`):
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:379|   - stages 1–3 reproduce the baseline histograms exactly (60,000 cases);
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:380|   - stages 4–6 add 30,400 hybrid cases, now drawing on the genuine anchors and signatures as well;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:381|   - **0 disagreements** in 90,400 cases;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:382|   - stage 4: 20,000 anchor mutations, 2481 accepted, the rest across 13 reason codes;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:383|   - stage 5: 10,000 SPKI mutations (`KEY_FORMAT` 9400, `KEY_MISMATCH` 596, OK 4);
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:384|   - stage 6: 400 verify pairs (347 false, 53 true).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:385| - **Sensitivity** (each defect planted in a scratch copy of B). Caught:

formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:387|   - skipped verification;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:388|   - NULL parameters accepted;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:389|   - a trailing SPKI byte accepted;
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:390|   - hint order unchecked (XHR-04/16 demonstrations);
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:391|   - padding unchecked (XHR-17);
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:392|   - z bound loosened (XHR-12);
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:393|   - μ computed without `00 00` (19 failures).
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:394| 
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:395|   Not catchable: removing the "count ≤ ω" bound. A count above 55 cannot form a consistent signature, so XHR-18 is
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:396|   a decoder-failure check, as HS-03 asks, not an acceptance demonstration.
formal/p8/HYBRID-SUPPLEMENT.md:397| - **External cross-check** (by hand). cryptography/OpenSSL and dilithium-py agree with A and B on:

formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:30| `run_sig` calls `parse_signature`, then `sig_policy`, then `signature_verifies` against one known-good key, and
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:31| `run_key` calls `public_key`. These are the functions behind bundle rows 3.1/9.3, 9.1/9.4, 9.2/9.5 and 5.1, but the
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:32| harness does not reproduce the bundle's order: a bundle evaluates keys (5.1) before signature policy (9.1) and
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:33| reports by row precedence. **Precedence is claimed only from the bundle tests** (B01..B08; B08 is a combined key and
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:34| policy failure, which reports `KEY_FORMAT`). `SIG_INVALID` in a vector reads as `POSSESSION_INVALID` for a possession
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:35| proof, because the same function serves both rows (`verify.py:216`, `verify.py:226`). There are 22 positive controls
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:36| across the three slot rules. `TestControls` fails if a file has no `ACCEPT` or only one outcome.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:37| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:38| ## 0. Scope
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:39| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:40| P3 concerns the issuer's signatures: the two receipt slots and the two possession proofs. V1's issuer signature
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:41| algorithms (V1-PROFILE §8; ENC §5.2) are:
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:42| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:43| - **slot `kms`, hybrid pair id** `KMS-MLDSA65-PURE-GPG-OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256`: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204), pure mode,
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:44|   empty context, raw 3309-byte signature (rule R). The key is the exact 1974-byte RFC 9881 SPKI.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:45| - **slot `gpg`** (both ids), and **slot `kms` under the classical fallback id** `OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256`: ECDSA
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:46|   P-256 / SHA-256 inside an OpenPGP v4 signature packet (rule O). The `gpg` key is the bare v4 public-key packet
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:47|   body; the fallback `kms` key is a 91-byte P-256 SPKI.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:48| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:49| The V1 installation's catalog alg is the hybrid id. The fallback is covered because it is codec-known.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:50| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:51| The same rule-O functions also verify the git commit signature against the trust configuration's repository key
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:52| (`policy.py:57`, `verify.py:278`), so F2/F3 apply to that key too (bundle test B07).
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:53| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:54| **Outside P3; listed, not profiled:**
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:55| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:56| | Verifier path | Algorithm | Call |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:57| |---|---|---|
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:58| | DNSSEC RRSIG (`dnssec.py:187-200`) | RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5/SHA-256 (alg 8), ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 (alg 13; key via the same `codec.point`) | `pub.verify(sig, data, padding.PKCS1v15(), hashes.SHA256())`; `pub.verify(encode_dss_signature(r, s), data, ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA256()))` |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:59| | TEST release stand-in (`release_auth.py:51-75`) | ECDSA over SHA-256 of the JCS body | `serialization.load_der_public_key(spki)` then `pub.verify(der, body, ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA256()))`. See DIVERGENCES.md D1 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:60|

formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:62| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:63| | Item | Value | Backed by |

formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:66| | Wheel | tag `cp311-abi3-manylinux_2_34_x86_64`; `cryptography/hazmat/bindings/_rust.abi3.so` SHA-256 `1e5d23fa66915204b9b67202a46993844d81cda56f6ad52cead2def37617ee29` | `test_installed_wheel_identity` (verifier venv) |

formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:73| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:74| The call tests require each call string to occur exactly once in `codec.py`. F1's "negative vector" is a tripwire:
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:75| a different library version, wheel binding, OpenSSL build, interpreter or call fails `TestF1Library`, and this
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:76| profile must then be re-recorded. A genuinely different supported build needs its own record.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:77| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:78| **Deployment tie.** The issuer Lambda runs the verifier from the zip that `service/issuer/package.py` builds. That
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:79| script resolves `cryptography==50.0.2` for `x86_64-manylinux_2_34` and prints the zip's SHA-256, and that zip is what
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:80| infra deploys as `lambda_zip`. The deployed verifier's library identity is tied to this record through the package
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:81| digest:
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:82| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:83| - `test_lambda_package_wheel_identity` runs `package.build()` into a fresh temporary directory and checks that the
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:84|   zip's `_rust.abi3.so` digest and wheel tag equal F1. It passed in this run, using uv's cache or the network; it
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:85|   skips with a stated reason if uv or the build is unavailable.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:86| - `test_deployed_zip_identity` checks a specific zip when `TESSERA_LAMBDA_ZIP` names it. It is skipped unless set.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:87|   Run it on the deployed artifact, whose digest matches the deployed `lambda_zip`.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:88| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:89| This is not a Lambda invocation. The record says which bytes are deployed, not that they were exercised on Lambda.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:90| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:91| `package.py` does not itself expose the cryptography binding digest; it was not edited. Suggested change, for the
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:92| issuer owner: have `build()` return or print the `_rust.abi3.so` SHA-256 and the dist-info `WHEEL` tag beside the
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:93| zip digest, and fail if they differ from `formal/p3-verification-profile/vectors/F1-library.json`. A package with a
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:94| different backend could then not be built silently.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:95| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:96| ## 2. F2: accepted signature encodings and rule-O policy
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:97| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:98| **Rule O encoding (gpg slot; fallback kms slot).** Accepted: exactly one legacy-format signature packet, `0x88 u8`
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:99| (body ≤ 255) or `0x89 u16` (256..1021), with a v4 body of type 0x00, algorithm 19, hash 8, shortest-form subpackets,
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:100| two prefix octets, then MPIs r and s of 1..256 bits each with exact bit counts; r, s ∈ [1, n−1].
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:101| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:102| - **Both low-S and high-S are accepted.** O-01 is low-S (s ≤ n/2). O-02 is its high-S twin (r, n−s). A test asserts
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:103|   which is which (`test_O01_is_low_s_and_O02_is_its_high_s_twin`).
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:104| - **DER is never an accepted input form.** The verifier builds the DER itself from the parsed MPIs. The analogue of
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:105|   non-canonical DER, a non-minimal MPI, is `SIG_FORMAT` (O-15).
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:106| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:107| | Rejected | Code | Vectors |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:108| |---|---|---|
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:109| | OpenPGP-format header, non-shortest header, bare DER, raw r‖s, armor | `SIG_PACKET` | O-04..O-08 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:110| | trailing / truncated | `TRAILING` / `TRUNCATED` | O-09, O-10 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:111| | v5, type 0x01, algorithm 22, hash 10, MPI with leading zero, 257-bit MPI, r = 0 | `SIG_FORMAT` | O-11..O-17 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:112| | r = n, s = n, r = 2²⁵⁶−1 | `SIG_POLICY` | O-18..O-20 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:113| | prefix octets wrong, other document, other key | `SIG_INVALID` | O-21..O-23 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:114| | rule-O packet in the hybrid kms slot | `SIG_FORMAT` | O-25 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:115| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:116| **Rule-O signature policy** (V1-PROFILE §8, "Rule-O signature policy" and "Advisory metadata, structural
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:117| validation"; `codec.sig_policy`). Every P vector is a correctly signed packet over its own hashed area.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:118| `TestRuleOPolicy::test_policy_vector_is_correctly_signed` checks that each one verifies when `sig_policy` is
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:119| skipped, so each `SIG_POLICY` outcome is the policy's doing.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:120| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:121| - **Hashed area:**
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:122|   - exactly one creation-time subpacket (type 2) with exactly 4 data octets, critical or not;
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:123|   - no signature-expiration subpacket (type 3), critical or not;
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:124|   - types 16 and 33 accepted, critical or not, with exact structure: at most one 16, of 8 octets; at most one 33, of
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:125|     21 octets with first octet 04; if both are present, 16 equals the last 8 octets of 33;
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:126|   - any other type is ignored if noncritical and a failure if critical.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:127| - **Unhashed area:** ignored entirely, critical bits included, after ENC's subpacket framing.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:128| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:129| | Case | Outcome | Vectors |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:130| |---|---|---|
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:131| | creation time critical; GnuPG shape (hashed 2 + 33, unhashed 16); hashed 16 + 33 consistent; 16 + 33 both critical; unknown noncritical hashed type | `ACCEPT` | P-01..P-05 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:132| | unhashed area holding a critical unknown, a critical expiration, malformed and inconsistent 16/33, and duplicate creation times | `ACCEPT` (ignored) | P-06 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:133| | creation time missing, duplicated, 3, 5 or 0 data octets | `SIG_POLICY` | P-10..P-14 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:134| | expiration, noncritical or critical | `SIG_POLICY` | P-15, P-16 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:135| | unknown critical type; RFC-known type 4 marked critical | `SIG_POLICY` | P-17, P-18 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:136| | type 16 of 7 octets; two type 16; type 33 of 20 octets; type 33 version 05; two type 33; 16/33 inconsistent; zero-data critical 33 | `SIG_POLICY` | P-19..P-25 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:137| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:138| **Rule R (hybrid kms slot).** Accepted: exactly 3309 bytes that pass the FIPS 204 HintBitUnpack and z-bound
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:139| conditions and verify under pure ML-DSA-65 with the empty context. Positive controls: a library `sign(F, context=b'')`
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:140| signature (R-01) and an `EXTERNAL_MU`-style `sign_mu` signature (R-02, the issuer's path).
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:141| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:142| | Rejected | Code | Vectors |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:143| |---|---|---|
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:144| | length 0 | `SIG_EMPTY` | R-03 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:145| | length 3308, ML-DSA-44 (2420) | `SIG_FORMAT` | R-04, R-06 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:146| | length 3310, ML-DSA-87 (4627) | `LENGTH_CAP` | R-05, R-07 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:147| | hint: nonzero padding, duplicate index, swapped indices (each decodes to the **same** h under a lax decoder), count ω+1, decreasing counts | `SIG_INVALID` | R-08..R-12 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:148| | z coefficient = ±(γ1−β) | `SIG_INVALID` | R-13, R-14 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:149| | z in range but wrong, c̃ flipped, other document, other key | `SIG_INVALID` | R-15..R-18 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:150| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:151| R-08..R-14 are rejected by the verifier's own gate before the library is called. `TestMLDSAGate` proves this with a
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:152| permissive mock backend, so rejection does not depend on library strictness. The library also rejects them without
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:153| the gate (LIB07), so with this build the gate is defence in depth.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:154| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:155| ## 3. F3: public-key validation behaviour
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:156| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:157| **P-256 (gpg packet; fallback kms SPKI; repository key).** The verifier requires:
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:158| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:159| - the exact encoding: the 82-byte v4 packet body with prefix `13 08 2a8648ce3d030107 0203`, or the 26-byte SPKI prefix
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:160|   plus 65 bytes;
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:161| - an **uncompressed** point `04‖X‖Y`.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:162| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:163| It then checks **X < p, Y < p and the curve equation itself, before the EC constructor is called**. All of the
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:164| following are `KEY_FORMAT`:
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:165| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:166| | Case | Vectors |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:167| |---|---|
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:168| | compressed point | K-05, K-17 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:169| | hybrid 06/07 encoding | K-06 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:170| | off-curve point | K-03, K-15 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:171| | non-canonical X = x+p | K-04, K-16 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:172| | non-canonical Y = y+p | K-36, K-37 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:173| | other curves | K-09, K-18, K-19 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:174| | wrong version, algorithm, MPI count or length | K-07, K-08, K-10..K-12 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:175| | cross-slot encodings | K-13, K-20, K-21 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:176| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:177| A bad repository key refuses the trust configuration (`TRUST_CONFIG_UNAUTHENTICATED`, B07).
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:178| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:179| **Ordering, tested (P3R-02).** `TestPointBeforeConstructor` replaces `codec.ec`, for the codec module only, with a
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:180| permissive stand-in whose constructor accepts anything:
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:181| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:182| - **Rejected without the constructor ever being called:** X ≥ p (K-04, K-16), Y ≥ p (K-36, K-37), curve membership
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:183|   (K-03, K-15, L-03, L-01), and representation (compressed, hybrid, leading 00 or 05).
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:184| - **Positive controls reach the constructor with the exact (x, y):** K-01, K-02, K-35, K-14.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:185| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:186| So the verifier's own checks decide these cases, not the library's defaults. This matters because the library alone
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:187| **accepts X ≥ p and Y ≥ p and reduces them** (LIB02, LIB09). Its DER loader also **accepts compressed-point SPKIs and
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:188| other curves** (LIB03). The library does reject off-curve points by itself (LIB01), so for curve membership the
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:189| verifier's check is shown, by the mock, to come first, but is redundant with this build.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:190| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:191| **ML-DSA-65 (hybrid kms).** The only check is the exact 1974-byte SPKI: OID 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.18, parameters
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:192| absent, zero unused bits, minimal DER (K-22 accepted; K-24..K-34 `KEY_FORMAT`). There is no further public-key
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:193| validation. Every 1952-byte string is a well-formed FIPS 204 key: the all-zero key is accepted (K-23), and the
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:194| library accepts it too (LIB06). That is decoding behaviour, not a security claim about such a key. The library's
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:195| generic DER loader would accept ML-DSA-44/-87 SPKIs as keys of their own parameter sets (LIB04); the verifier's
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:196| exact-prefix rule rejects them (K-28, K-29).
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:197| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:198| ## 4. Translation of A1's Ed25519 fields — OWNER READING, contestable
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:199| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:200| **Not decided here: the algorithm policy.** V1 *requires* both algorithms. The frozen catalog names only the hybrid
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:201| `KMS-MLDSA65-PURE-GPG-OPENPGP4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256` (registered 2026-10-16). Any other algorithm is `ALG_UNKNOWN`
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:202| (`verify.py:180`), and a receipt missing either signature fails (G3). This section decides only whether checking each
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:203| of the two algorithms against its own analogue of A1's Ed25519 checklist meets P3's registered words. Because both
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:204| signatures are required, a forgery must break both. A weakness noted below for one algorithm matters only if the
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:205| other algorithm also fails.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:206| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:207| The registered text names Ed25519 concepts. V1 does not verify Ed25519. The mapping below is the owner's reading and
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:208| is open to challenge: whether these analogues discharge the registered words is for the author to rule. (Codex
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:209| review: "a reasonable, explicitly contestable owner reading, not a concealed amendment"; its sufficiency still
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:210| needs the author's ruling.)
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:211| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:212| | A1 field (Ed25519 sense) | V1 analogue: ECDSA P-256 (rule O) | V1 analogue: ML-DSA-65 (rule R) |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:213| |---|---|---|
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:214| | Exact library and version | §1 | §1 |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:215| | Accepted signature encodings (canonical S < L, canonical R) | §2: OpenPGP v4 packet, exact-bit-count MPIs, r, s ∈ [1, n−1], rule-O policy. **High-S accepted**: ECDSA's (r, s)/(r, n−s) malleability is not removed, and the profile relies on the anchor's exact-copy commitment (ENC §3.5) | §2: exact 3309 bytes; strict HintBitUnpack and z bound, so one (c̃, z, h) has one encoding (R-08..R-10) |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:216| | Public-key validation (canonical A encoding, small-order A) | §3: exact uncompressed encoding, coordinates < p, on-curve, all before the constructor | §3: exact SPKI only. **No algebraic validation exists**, so this is "not applicable beyond encoding" |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:217| | Low-order-point handling (the 8-torsion of Curve25519) | P-256 has **cofactor h = 1**: every finite on-curve point has prime order n, and the only low-order element is the point at infinity. As a **public key** it cannot be received (L-01, L-02, L-06, L-08 `KEY_FORMAT`); as the **result of the verification equation** it is rejected (E-11). The live residue of the concern is **invalid-curve points**, including small-order points on other curves with the same a; the verifier's on-curve check rejects them before the constructor (L-03, an order-2 point of y² = x³ − 3x + 2; L-04, L-07). h = 1 is a property of the curve (SP 800-186), not something a test here derives | **Not applicable**: ML-DSA is lattice-based, with no group, cofactor or torsion. Degenerate keys (e.g. all-zero t1) are accepted (K-23); whether they weaken anything is not tested here |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:218| | Cofactor equation variant (cofactored [8]SB = [8]R + [8]kA vs cofactorless) | With h = 1 the cofactored/cofactorless distinction does not exist. The equation choices that remain, all tested: the message representative is SHA256(F ‖ v4 trailer), passed `Prehashed`, with no second hash and no plain SHA256(F) (E-01..E-03); the hash prefix is checked; **x(R) is reduced mod n before comparison with r**: E-10 is a constructed key with x(R) = n + 3, r = 3, s = 1, accepted, where an unreduced comparison would reject (`TestEquationConstruction` confirms x(R) ≥ n; LIB10 shows the library does the reduction); a verification result of infinity is rejected (E-11) | The variant question becomes **which FIPS 204 interface**. The verifier uses pure ML-DSA, empty context: M′ = 00 ‖ 00 ‖ F. A non-empty context (E-04, E-09), HashML-DSA (E-05, E-06), the internal interface with no domain prefix (E-07) and μ passed as the message (E-08) are all `SIG_INVALID` |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:219| | (P3's premise) the verification equation is not issuer binding | **Demonstrated**: from (F, S) alone, `p256.dsks_keys` computes a different valid P-256 key under which the honest signature verifies (D-02 `ACCEPT` at the function level). In a bundle that key is rejected by the signed fingerprint binding: `KEY_MISMATCH` (B02). Rewriting the manifest to match gives `RECEIPT_MANIFEST_MISMATCH` (B03). This concerns substitution into existing honest signed material, not receipts minted by an attacker who holds both channels | Not demonstrated either way. ML-DSA hashes tr = H(pk) into μ, which is the usual argument for its exclusive-ownership properties; no test here exercises it |
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:220| 
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:221| E-10 and E-11 follow Codex's construction (review scratch `probe.py`): choose an on-curve R with x(R) = n + r, then
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:222| Q = r⁻¹(R − eG) with s = 1. For E-11, Q = (−e/r)G, so eG + rQ = O.
formal/p3-verification-profile/PROFILE.md:223|

docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:17| 
docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:18| | Item | Resolution | By |
docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:19| |---|---|---|
docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:20| | S1 forms, representation, size | One form: the request body is the content, as raw bytes. The receipt carries them as canonical base64 in `common.content`; decoding recovers exactly the submitted bytes, and those bytes are what is attested. Client limit: **1 MiB** of content; the complete encoded payload stays under the 16 MiB cap. A client with larger content submits a digest (S6). | Owner |
docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:21| | S2 incomplete delivery | Every completed result carries the receipt's SHA-256. The client checks it, and can retrieve the result again as often as it likes while it is kept (S5). | Owner |
docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:22| | S3 unknown outcome; terminal refusal | The client resolves an unknown outcome by status lookup, using its own request key (S5). **A refusal is final:** a refused request is never completed later. To try again, the client sends a new request. | Owner |
docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:23| | S4 latency | **Stated, not guaranteed:** a receipt is usually complete within 3 hours of acceptance. A request not complete **24 hours** after acceptance ends as FAILED, with its reason. Start: the acceptance response. End: the status becoming COMPLETE. Window preparation happens before the window opens and does not count. Results are **retrieved by the client**, not pushed. | Owner |
docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:24| | S5 request lifecycle | The client supplies a **request key** (a UUID). The same key returns the same request and the same receipt, every time. The same content under a different key is a separate request with its own receipt. States: ACCEPTED, COMPLETE, REFUSED, FAILED. Acceptance is durable once the ACCEPTED response is sent. Only the client credential that made a request may look it up or retrieve it. No cancellation in V1. Lookup and identical-result retrieval last **30 days** after the request ends (COMPLETE, REFUSED or FAILED). After that, lookup returns EXPIRED. A content-free record of the key is kept until issuance closes, so an expired key cannot start a new issuance. | Owner |
docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:25| | S6 content exposure | Requests and results are readable only by the submitting client credential. Transport is encrypted. Refused content is not stored. Content and results are deleted 30 days after the request ends, copies included. Content is used for nothing but the request. A receipt the client hands to others exposes the content to them: that is the client's choice. | Owner |
docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:26| | S7 cost | **AUTHOR.** Recommendation: V1 charges nothing (trial service). It states the measured cost per receipt (H3) as the cost figure A9.1 asks for. | Author |
docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:27| | S8 availability | No target. Best effort, stated as such. | Owner |

docs/V1-SERVICE-RESOLUTIONS.md:42| | L1 window dates and closure | Both window endpoints are fixed and published before issuance preparation, at most 90 days apart. The actual dates stay OPEN until the dated operating record; a late first issuance does not extend the window. Signing stops 96 hours before the window ends (the runbook's operating margin, not a registered rule). Acceptance stops 120 hours before the end, so that every accepted request can complete or fail (S4) before signing stops. Only receipts that pass the registered window checks are shipped. Completed results stay retrievable for 30 days (S5). Closure is announced 14 days ahead on the service page. | Owner |
